一部内容丰富、不断向四面八方延展的思想史概览——戴维·夸曼（David Quammen）

A rich and endlessly reticulating survey through the history of ideas —DAVID QUAMMEN

《数学：确定性的丧失》最初于1980年出版，驳斥了一种神话：数学是关于物质世界的一套不可动摇的真理，数学推理则精确无误。正如莫里斯·克莱因所指出的，数学并没有一个得到普遍接受的概念，而是存在许多相互冲突的观念。

MATHEMATICS: THE LOSS OF CERTAINTY, originally published in 1980, refutes the myth that mathematics is a body of unshakable truths about the physical world and that mathematical reasoning is exact and infallible. As Morris Kline points out, there is not one universally accepted concept of mathematics— there are many conflicting ones.

然而，数学在描述和探索物理现象与社会现象方面的效力仍在不断增强。随着计算机科学的迅速发展，以及社会科学和生物科学对定量关系的探索，数学活动正空前繁荣。“我们是否正在用不完善的工具创造奇迹？”克莱因提出了这个发人深省的问题。

Yet the effectiveness of mathematics in describing and exploring physical and social phenomena continues to expand. Mathematical activity is flourishing as never before, with the rapid changes in computer science and the search for quantitative relationships in the social and biological sciences. “Are we performing miracles with imperfect tools?” Kline asks provocatively.

十九世纪的两项发展——非欧几里得几何与四元数——迫使数学家认识到，数学并不是由无误的推理产生的一系列关于自然的自明真理。例如，他们发现，几种不同的几何都同样符合空间经验，却不可能全都是真理。这一认识促使数学家研究其公理和“无懈可击”的推理的本质。令他们惊讶的是，公理既是任意的，又是不充分的，而证明则存在严重缺陷。

Two nineteenth-century developments—non-Euclidean geometry and quaternions—forced mathematicians to realize that mathematics is not a series of self-evident truths about nature produced by infallible reasoning. They found, for example, that several different geometries fit spatial experience equally well. All could not be truths—a realization that impelled mathematicians to investigate the nature of their axioms and “unassailable” reasoning. To their surprise, they found that the axioms were arbitrary and inadequate and their proofs were woefully defective.

为了重建数学的基础并解决这些矛盾，出现了四个思想流派，它们对于数学究竟是什么的看法截然不同。本书追溯数学如何从其不可动摇的崇高宝座上跌落，并探讨它何以仍然具有神秘的有效性。克莱因用非专业性的语言，解释了我们对“纯”数学及“应用”数学的理解所发生的剧烈变化，以及这些变化对科学乃至整个人类理性的意义。

To rebuild the foundations of mathematics and to resolve the contradictions, four schools of thought emerged—each differing radically in their views of what mathematics is. This book traces the history of mathematics’s fall from its lofty pedestal of unshakability and explores the reasons for its continuing mysterious effectiveness. Kline explains in nontechnical language the drastic changes that have taken place in our understanding of “pure” as well as “applied” math, and the implications for science and for human reason generally.

序言

Preface

本书探讨人类在理解数学的本质与作用时，被迫作出的根本改变。如今我们知道，数学并不具备过去为它赢得普遍尊敬和赞赏的那些品质。数学曾被视为精确推理的顶峰，其本身是一套真理，也是关于自然设计的真理。人类如何认识到这些价值判断是错误的，以及我们目前的认识究竟是什么，构成本书的主要主题。导论简要陈述了这些主题。其中有些材料可以从详尽的、技术性的数学史中搜集到。但主要关注那些戏剧性变化的人会发现，直接而非技术性的论述方式，能使这些变化更容易接近，也更容易理解。

This book treats the fundamental changes that man has been forced to make in his understanding of the nature and role of mathematics. We know today that mathematics does not possess the qualities that in the past earned for it universal respect and admiration. Mathematics was regarded as the acme of exact reasoning, a body of truths in itself, and the truth about the design of nature. How man came to the realization that these values are false and just what our present understanding is constitute the major themes. A brief statement of these themes is presented in the Introduction. Some of the material could be gleaned from a detailed technical history of mathematics. But those people who are interested primarily in the dramatic changes that have taken place will find that a direct, non-technical approach makes them more readily accessible and more intelligible.

许多数学家也许宁愿把数学现状的披露限制在自家人之中。把这些麻烦公之于众，可能显得不得体，就像公开自己的婚姻困境一样。然而，重视理智的人必须充分了解手头工具的效能。认识理性的局限以及能力，远比盲目信任更有益；盲目信任可能导致错误的意识形态，甚至导致毁灭。

Many mathematicians would perhaps prefer to limit the disclosure of the present status of mathematics to members of the family. To air these troubles in public may appear to be in bad taste, as bad as airing one’s marital difficulties. But intellectually oriented people must be fully aware of the powers of the tools at their disposal. Recognition of the limitations, as well as the capabilities, of reason is far more beneficial than blind trust, which can lead to false ideologies and even to destruction.

我谨向牛津大学出版社的工作人员致谢，感谢他们对本书的周到处理。我尤其感谢威廉·C.哈尔平先生和谢尔登·迈耶先生，感谢他们认识到开展这项普及工作的意义；也感谢利昂娜·凯普利斯女士和柯蒂斯·丘奇先生所提出的宝贵建议与批评。我的妻子海伦帮助我多次改进文字，并细心校对，我对此深怀感激。

导论：本书的论旨

Introduction: The Thesis

要预见数学的未来，真正的方法是研究它的历史与现状。

To foresee the future of mathematics, the true method is to study its history and its present state.

亨利·庞加莱

Henri Poincaré

有些悲剧是战争、饥荒和瘟疫造成的。但也有些思想上的悲剧，源于人类心智的局限。本书叙述的，是降临于人类最有效、无与伦比的成就，亦即人类运用理性最持久、最深刻的努力——数学——之上的种种灾难。

There are tragedies caused by war, famine, and pestilence. But there are also intellectual tragedies caused by limitations of the human mind. This book relates the calamities that have befallen man’s most effective and unparalleled accomplishment, his most persistent and profound effort to utilize human reason—mathematics.

换言之，本书以非技术性的方式探讨数学威严的兴衰。鉴于数学目前的规模如此庞大，数学活动不断增多乃至蓬勃发展，每年发表数千篇研究论文，人们对计算机的兴趣迅速增长，而且对定量关系的探索不断扩展，尤其是在社会科学和生物科学中，我们怎么能谈数学的衰落呢？悲剧究竟在哪里？要回答这些问题，我们必须先考察：什么样的价值为数学赢得了巨大的威望、尊重与荣耀。

Put in other terms, this book treats on a non-technical level the rise and decline of the majesty of mathematics. In view of its present immense scope, the increasing, even flourishing, mathematical activity, the thousands of research papers published each year, the rapidly growing interest in computers, and the expanded search for quantitative relationships especially in the social and biological sciences, how can we talk about the decline of mathematics? Wherein lies the tragedy? To answer these questions we must consider first what values won for mathematics its immense prestige, respect, and glory.

自古典时代的希腊人创立数学，使之成为独立的知识体系之日起，两千多年来，数学家一直在追求真理。他们的成就辉煌壮丽。关于数和几何图形的大量定理，本身就呈现出一幅看似几乎无穷无尽的确定性图景。

From the very birth of mathematics as an independent body of knowledge, fathered by the classical Greeks, and for a period of over two thousand years, mathematicians pursued truth. Their accomplishments were magnificent. The vast body of theorems about number and geometric figures offered in itself what appeared to be an almost endless vista of certainty.

在数学本身的领域之外，数学概念和推导又构成了诸多卓越科学理论的精髓。虽然数学与科学合作取得的知识运用了物理原理，但这些原理似乎与数学本身的原理一样可靠，因为天文学、力学、光学和流体动力学的数学理论所作的预测，与观察和实验惊人地精确吻合。因此，数学使人牢牢把握了自然的运行，这种认识消除了神秘，以规律和秩序取而代之。人能够自豪地审视周围世界，夸耀自己已经掌握了宇宙的许多奥秘，而这些奥秘本质上就是一系列数学规律。拉普拉斯曾说，牛顿是一个极其幸运的人，因为宇宙只有一个，而牛顿已经发现了它的规律；这句话集中体现了人们对于数学家正在获得真理的确信。

Beyond the realm of mathematics proper, mathematical concepts and derivations supplied the essence of remarkable scientific theories. Though the knowledge obtained through the collaboration of mathematics and science employed physical principles, these seemed to be as secure as the principles of mathematics proper because the predictions in the mathematical theories of astronomy, mechanics, optics, and hydrodynamics were in remarkably accurate accord with observation and experiment. Mathematics, then, provided a firm grip on the workings of nature, an understanding which dissolved mystery and replaced it by law and order. Man could pridefully survey the world about him and boast that he had grasped many of the secrets of the universe, which in essence were a series of mathematical laws. The conviction that mathematicians were securing truths is epitomized in Laplace’s remark that Newton was a most fortunate man because there is just one universe and Newton had discovered its laws.

为了取得奇妙而强有力的成果，数学依靠一种特殊方法，即从称为公理的自明原理出发进行演绎证明；我们至今仍学习这种方法，通常是在中学几何中。演绎推理的本性保证了：如果公理是真理，那么推导出的命题也是真理。数学家运用这种貌似清晰、无误而无懈可击的逻辑，得出了看来毋庸置疑、不可反驳的结论。数学的这一特点今天仍被人们引用。每当有人想举出推理的确定性与精确性的实例时，总会求助于数学。

To achieve its marvelous and powerful results, mathematics relied upon a special method, namely, deductive proof from self-evident principles called axioms, the methodology we still learn, usually in high school geometry. Deductive reasoning, by its very nature, guarantees the truth of what is deduced if the axioms are truths. By utilizing this seemingly clear, infallible, and impeccable logic, mathematicians produced apparently indubitable and irrefutable conclusions. This feature of mathematics is still cited today. Whenever someone wants an example of certitude and exactness of reasoning, he appeals to mathematics.

数学凭借其方法论取得的成功，吸引了最伟大的思想家。数学展示了人类理性的能力、资源与力量。他们问道：为什么不运用这种方法，在受权威、习俗和习惯支配的领域，如哲学、神学、伦理学、美学与社会科学中，获得真理呢？人类理性在数学与数学物理中显然如此有效，它当然也能成为这些其他领域中思想与行动的裁判，使它们获得真理之美与美之真理。于是，在被称为启蒙时代或理性时代的时期，数学方法论，甚至某些数学概念与定理，都被应用于人类事务。

The successes mathematics achieved with its methodology attracted the greatest intellectuals. Mathematics had demonstrated the capacities, resources, and strengths of human reason. Why should not this methodology be employed, they asked, to secure truths in fields dominated by authority, custom, and habit, fields such as philosophy, theology, ethics, aesthetics, and the social sciences? Man’s reason, so evidently effective in mathematics and mathematical physics, could surely be the arbiter of thought and action in these other fields and obtain for them the beauty of truths and the truths of beauty. And so, during the period called the Enlightenment or the Age of Reason, mathematical methodology and even some mathematical concepts and theorems were applied to human affairs.

洞见最丰富的源泉，是回顾过去。十九世纪初出现的奇异几何与奇异代数，迫使数学家勉强而不情愿地认识到，数学本身以及科学的数学规律并不是真理。例如，他们发现，几种不同的几何都同样符合空间经验。它们不可能全都是真理。显然，数学设计并非自然固有；即便自然具有这样的设计，人类的数学也未必是对它的描述。通向实在的钥匙已经丢失。这一认识，是降临于数学的第一场灾难。

The most fertile source of insight is hindsight. Creations of the early nineteenth century, strange geometries and strange algebras, forced mathematicians, reluctantly and grudgingly, to realize that mathematics proper and the mathematical laws of science were not truths. They found, for example, that several differing geometries fit spatial experience equally well. All could not be truths. Apparently mathematical design was not inherent in nature, or if it was, man’s mathematics was not necessarily the account of that design. The key to reality had been lost. This realization was the first of the calamities to befall mathematics.

这些新几何与新代数的创立，又使数学家受到另一种震动。他们深信自己正在获得真理，这一信念使他们如此着迷，以至于他们急切地奔向这些看似真理的结果，却牺牲了健全的推理。认识到数学并非一套真理，动摇了他们对自己创造物的信心，于是他们开始重新审查这些创造物。他们惊愕地发现，数学的逻辑状况十分糟糕。

The creation of these new geometries and algebras caused mathematicians to experience a shock of another nature. The conviction that they were obtaining truths had entranced them so much that they had rushed impetuously to secure these seeming truths at the cost of sound reasoning. The realization that mathematics was not a body of truths shook their confidence in what they had created, and they undertook to re-examine their creations. They were dismayed to find that the logic of mathematics was in sad shape.

事实上，数学一直以非逻辑的方式发展。这种非逻辑的发展，不仅包含错误的证明、推理中的失误，以及本可通过更加谨慎而避免的无心错误。这类失误确实多得很。非逻辑的发展还涉及对概念理解不足、未能认识到所需的全部逻辑原则，以及证明不够严密；也就是说，直觉、物理论证和对几何图形的诉诸，取代了逻辑论证。

In fact mathematics had developed illogically. Its illogical development contained not only false proofs, slips in reasoning, and inadvertent mistakes which with more care could have been avoided. Such blunders there were aplenty. The illogical development also involved inadequate understanding of concepts, a failure to recognize all the principles of logic required, and an inadequate rigor of proof; that is, intuition, physical arguments, and appeal to geometrical diagrams had taken the place of logical arguments.

然而，数学仍然是对自然的有效描述。而数学本身无疑是一套富有吸引力的知识；在许多人，尤其是柏拉图主义者看来，它也是实在的一部分，值得因其自身而珍视。因此，数学家决定补足缺失的逻辑结构，并重建有缺陷的部分。在十九世纪后半叶，通常被称为数学严格化的运动，成为最突出的活动。

However, mathematics was still an effective description of nature. And mathematics itself was certainly an attractive body of knowledge and in the minds of many, the Platonists especially, a part of reality to be prized in and for itself. Hence mathematicians decided to supply the missing logical structure and to rebuild the defective portions. During the latter half of the nineteenth century the movement often described as the rigorization of mathematics became the outstanding activity.

到1900年，数学家相信自己已经达到了目标。虽然他们不得不满足于把数学视为对自然的近似描述，许多人甚至放弃了自然具有数学设计的信念，但他们的确为重建数学的逻辑结构而洋洋自得。然而，他们还没有为自以为取得的成功举杯庆祝完毕，重建后的数学中就发现了矛盾。人们通常把这些矛盾称为悖论，这是一种委婉说法，回避了矛盾会破坏数学逻辑这一事实。

By 1900 the mathematicians believed they had achieved their goal. Though they had to be content with mathematics as an approximate description of nature and many even abandoned the belief in the mathematical design of nature, they did gloat over their reconstruction of the logical structure of mathematics. But before they had finished toasting their presumed success, contradictions were discovered in the reconstructed mathematics. Commonly these contradictions were referred to as paradoxes, a euphemism that avoids facing the fact that contradictions vitiate the logic of mathematics.

当时的主要数学家和哲学家几乎立即着手解决这些矛盾。实际上，他们构思、表述并推进了四种不同的数学进路，每一种都聚集了许多拥护者。这些基础学派不仅试图解决已知的矛盾，也试图保证永远不会出现新的矛盾，即确立数学的一致性。在奠定基础的努力中，又产生了其他问题。某些公理和演绎逻辑原则是否可以接受，也成为争论焦点，各学派对此采取了不同立场。

The resolution of the contradictions was undertaken almost immediately by the leading mathematicians and philosophers of the times. In effect four different approaches to mathematics were conceived, formulated, and advanced, each of which gathered many adherents. These foundational schools all attempted not only to resolve the known contradictions but to ensure that no new ones could ever arise, that is, to establish the consistency of mathematics. Other issues arose in the foundational efforts. The acceptability of some axioms and some principles of deductive logic also became bones of contention on which the several schools took differing positions.

直到1930年，数学家或许还可以满足于接受几种数学基础中的某一种，并宣称自己的数学证明至少符合该学派的原则。但灾难再次降临，这次是一篇库尔特·哥德尔的著名论文。除了其他意义重大而令人不安的结果，哥德尔还证明，各学派所接受的逻辑原则无法证明数学的一致性。哥德尔指出，若不引入一些如此可疑、以至于使所得成果本身都成为问题的逻辑原则，就无法做到这一点。哥德尔的定理造成了一场崩溃。后来的发展又带来了进一步的复杂情况。例如，就连过去被高度推崇为通向精确知识之途的公理—演绎方法，也被发现存在缺陷。这些新发展的总体结果，是增加了可能的数学进路，并使数学家分裂成数量更多、彼此不同的派别。

As late as 1930 a mathematician might perhaps have been content with accepting one or another of the several foundations of mathematics and declared that his mathematical proofs were at least in accord with the tenets of that school. But disaster struck again in the form of a famous paper by Kurt Godel in which he proved, among other significant and disturbing results, that the logical principles accepted by the several schools could not prove the consistency of mathematics. This, Godel showed, cannot be done without involving logical principles so dubious as to question what is accomplished. Godel’s theorems produced a debacle. Subsequent developments brought further complications. For example, even the axiomatic-deductive method so highly regarded in the past as the approach to exact knowledge was seen to be flawed. The net effect of these newer developments was to add to the variety of possible approaches to mathematics and to divide mathematicians into an even greater number of differing factions.

数学当前的困境在于：数学并非只有一种，而是有许多种；由于种种原因，每一种都不能令反对学派的成员满意。如今已很清楚，所谓普遍接受、永不出错的推理体系——1800年那庄严的数学、人类的骄傲——不过是一场宏大的幻觉。对数学未来的不确定与怀疑，取代了过去的确定与自满。对于这门“最确定”的科学之基础的分歧，既令人惊讶，又——说得轻些——令人不安。数学目前的状况，嘲弄了此前根深蒂固且广受赞誉的数学真理性与逻辑完美性。

The current predicament of mathematics is that there is not one but many mathematics and that for numerous reasons each fails to satisfy the members of the opposing schools. It is now apparent that the concept of a universally accepted, infallible body of reasoning—the majestic mathematics of 1800 and the pride of man—is a grand illusion. Uncertainty and doubt concerning the future of mathematics have replaced the certainties and complacency of the past. The disagreements about the foundations of the “most certain” science are both surprising and, to put it mildly, disconcerting. The present state of mathematics is a mockery of the hitherto deep-rooted and widely reputed truth and logical perfection of mathematics.

有些数学家相信，对于什么能够被接受为健全数学的不同看法，终有一天会得到调和。其中最著名的是一批以尼古拉·布尔巴基为笔名写作的法国杰出数学家：

There are mathematicians who believe that the differing views on what can be accepted as sound mathematics will some day be reconciled. Prominent among these is a group of leading French mathematicians who write under the pseudonym of Nicholas Bourbaki:

自最早的时代以来，对整个数学或其任何分支的原理所作的一切批判性修订，几乎总是在不确定的时期之后发生；在这些时期，矛盾确曾出现，并且必须加以解决。……如今，数学家纠正自己的错误，并由此看到自己的科学变得更丰富而非更贫乏的实践，已经持续了二十五个世纪；这使他们有权平静地展望未来。

Since the earliest times, all critical revisions of the principles of mathematics as a whole, or of any branch of it, have almost invariably followed periods of uncertainty, where contradictions did appear and had to be resolved. . . . There are now twenty-five centuries during which the mathematicians have had the practice of correcting their errors and thereby seeing their science enriched, not impoverished; this gives them the right to view the future with serenity.

然而，更多的数学家持悲观态度。本世纪最伟大的数学家之一赫尔曼·外尔于1944年说：

However, many more mathematicians are pessimistic. Hermann Weyl, one of the greatest mathematicians of this century, said in 1944:

数学的基础与最终意义问题仍悬而未决；我们不知道它将在什么方向上找到最终解决，甚至不知道究竟能否期待一个最终的客观答案。“数学化”很可能是人类一种具有根本独创性的创造活动，如同语言或音乐；其历史上的抉择，无法完全以客观理性加以解释。

The question of the foundations and the ultimate meaning of mathematics remains open; we do not know in what direction it will find its final solution or even whether a final objective answer can be expected at all. “Mathematizing” may well be a creative activity of man, like language or music, of primary originality, whose historical decisions defy complete objective rationalization.

用歌德的话说：“一门科学的历史，就是这门科学本身。”

In the words of Goethe, “The history of a science is the science itself.”

关于正确数学究竟是什么的分歧，以及彼此不同的多种基础，不仅严重影响数学本身，而且对物理科学的影响尤为关键。正如我们将会看到的，发展得最完善的物理理论完全是数学性的。（当然，这类理论的结论会被解释为可感知的或真正的物理对象；我们能从收音机中听到声音，尽管我们对于无线电波究竟是什么，丝毫没有物理上的理解。）因此，即使科学家本人并不研究基础问题，为了不把多年时间浪费在不健全的数学上，他们也必须关心究竟可以放心运用哪些数学。

The disagreements concerning what correct mathematics is and the variety of differing foundations affect seriously not only mathematics proper but most vitally physical science. As we shall see, the most well-developed physical theories are entirely mathematical. (To be sure, the conclusions of such theories are interpreted m sensuous or truly physical objects, and we hear voices over our radios even though we have not the slightest physical understanding of what a radio wave is.) Hence scientists, who do not personally work on foundational problems, must nevertheless be concerned about what mathematics can be confidently employed if they are not to waste years on unsound mathematics.

真理的丧失、数学与科学日益增加的复杂性，以及对于哪种数学进路才可靠的不确定，促使大多数数学家放弃了科学。他们带着“愿你们各家都遭瘟疫”的态度，退守到证明方法似乎安全的数学领域中的专门方向。他们还发现，相比自然提出的问题，人类自行编造的问题更有吸引力，也更容易处理。

The loss of truth, the constantly increasing complexity of mathematics and science, and the uncertainty about which approach to mathematics is secure have caused most mathematicians to abandon science. With a “plague on all your houses” they have retreated to specialties in areas of mathematics where the methods of proof seem to be safe. They also find problems concocted by humans more appealing and manageable than those posed by nature.

围绕何谓健全数学的危机与冲突，也使人们不愿把数学方法论应用于我们文化的许多领域，如哲学、政治学、伦理学与美学。发现客观、无误的规律和标准的希望已经消退。理性时代已经过去。

The crises and conflicts over what sound mathematics is have also discouraged the application of mathematical methodology to many areas of our culture such as philosophy, political science, ethics, and aesthetics. The hope of finding objective, infallible laws and standards has faded. The Age of Reason is gone.

尽管数学的状况不令人满意，存在多种进路，对于可接受的公理存在分歧，而且一旦发现新的矛盾，许多数学就可能失效，某些数学家仍在把数学应用于物理现象，并且确实把应用领域扩展到了经济学、生物学和社会学。数学持续有效这一事实，提示了两个主题。第一个是，可以把有效性用作正确性的标准。当然，这样的标准是暂时的。今天被视为正确的东西，在下一次应用中可能被证明是错误的。

Despite the unsatisfactory state of mathematics, the variety of approaches, the disagreements on acceptable axioms, and the danger that new contradictions, if discovered, would invalidate a great deal of mathematics, some mathematicians are still applying mathematics to physical phenomena and indeed extending the applied fields to economics, biology, and sociology. The continuing effectiveness of mathematics suggests two themes. The first is that effectiveness can be used as the criterion of correctness. Of course such a criterion is provisional. What is considered correct today may prove wrong in the next application.

第二个主题涉及一个谜。鉴于人们对什么是健全数学存在分歧，数学究竟为什么还能有效？我们是否正在用不完善的工具创造奇迹？如果人受到了欺骗，自然是否也能受到欺骗，屈从于人类数学的指令？显然不能。然而，我们成功登月以及对火星、木星的探索，不是证实了关于宇宙的数学理论吗？这些成就是技术所促成的，而技术本身又高度依赖数学。那么，我们怎么还能谈数学的人为性和多样性呢？当心智与精神困惑时，躯体还能继续生存吗？对于人，这当然是事实；对于数学也是如此。因此，我们理应弄清：尽管数学的基础不确定，尽管数学家的理论相互冲突，数学为什么仍被证明如此不可思议地有效。

The second theme deals with a mystery. In view of the disagreements about what sound mathematics is, why is it effective at all? Are we performing miracles with imperfect tools? If man has been deceived, can nature also be deceived into yielding to man’s mathematical dictates? Clearly not. Yet, do not our successful voyages to the moon and our explorations of Mars and Jupiter, made possible by technology which itself depends heavily on mathematics, confirm mathematical theories of the cosmos? How can we, then, speak of the artificiality and varieties of mathematics? Can the body live on when the mind and spirit are bewildered? Certainly this is true of human beings and it is true of mathematics. It behooves us therefore to learn why, despite its uncertain foundations and despite the conflicting theories of mathematicians, mathematics has proved to be so incredibly effective.

I 数学真理的起源

I. The Genesis of Mathematical Truths

三倍幸福的灵魂！他们得以登临 这样的真理，攀上星光灿烂的天空！ 遥远的星辰被他们带到最清晰的视野， 以思想的链条环绕以太。 如此才抵达天庭——不似古人骄傲地 妄图以山叠山，直上九霄。

Thrice happy souls! to whom ’twas given to rise To truths like these, and scale the spangled skies! Far distant stars to clearest view they brought, And girdled ether with their chains of thought. So heaven is reached—not as of old they tried By mountains piled on mountains in their pride.

奥维德

Ovid

任何名副其实的文明都曾追求真理。有思想的人不能不尝试理解各种自然现象，解开人类如何来到地球上居住的谜，辨明人生应当服务于何种目的，并探索人类的命运。在所有早期文明中，只有一个例外；其余文明都由宗教领袖回答这些问题，而这些答案普遍被接受。古希腊文明就是这个例外。希腊人所发现的——也是人类最伟大的发现——是理性的力量。正是古典时期的希腊人，认识到人具有智力，具有一种有时借助观察或实验就能发现真理的心智；这一时期在公元前600年至前300年间达到鼎盛。

Any civilization worthy of the appellation has sought truths. Thoughtful people cannot but try to understand the variety of natural phenomena, to solve the mystery of how human beings came to dwell on this earth, to discern what purpose life should serve, and to discover human destiny. In all early civilizations but one, the answers to these questions were given by religious leaders, answers that were generally accepted. The ancient Greek civilization is the exception. What the Greeks discovered—the greatest discovery made by man—is the power of reason. It was the Greeks of the classical period, which was at its height during the years from 600 to 300 B.C., who recognized that man has an intellect, a mind which, aided occasionally by observation or experimentation, can discover truths.

是什么引导希腊人作出这一发现，是一个不易回答的问题。最初提出把理性应用于人类事务与关切的人，生活在爱奥尼亚，即小亚细亚的一处希腊人聚居区。许多历史学家试图依据政治与社会条件解释那里发生的事情。例如，爱奥尼亚人可以较为自由地忽视支配欧洲希腊文化的宗教信仰。然而，我们对于约公元前600年以前的希腊历史所知如此零碎，以至于无法提出明确的解释。

What led the Greeks to this discovery is a question not readily answered. The initiators of the plan to apply reason to human affairs and concerns lived in Ionia, a Greek settlement in Asia Minor, and many historians have sought to account for the happenings there on the basis of political and social conditions. For example, the Ionians were rather freer to disregard the religious beliefs that dominated the European Greek culture. However, our knowledge of Greek history before about 600 b.c. is so fragmentary that no definitive explanation is available.

随着时间推移，希腊人把理性应用于政治制度、伦理、正义、教育，以及人类关注的许多其他问题。他们最主要的贡献，也是对后来所有文化产生决定性影响的贡献，是接受理性所面对的最宏伟挑战：认识自然规律。在希腊人作出这一贡献之前，他们和其他古代文明都把自然视为混乱无序、反复无常，甚至可怕的。自然的行为要么无法解释，要么被归于诸神的任意意志；而诸神只能通过祈祷、献祭和其他仪式来安抚。巴比伦人和埃及人早在公元前3000年就拥有显著的文明，确实注意到了太阳与月亮运动中的某些周期性，并且以这些周期性为基础制定历法，但他们并未在其中看出更深的意义。这些少数例外的观察，没有改变他们对自然的态度。

In the course of time the Greeks applied reason to political systems, ethics, justice, education, and numerous other concerns of man. Their chief contribution, and the one which decisively influenced all later cultures, was to undertake the most imposing challenge facing reason, learning the laws of nature. Before the Greeks made this contribution, they and the other civilizations of ancient times regarded nature as chaotic, capricious, and even terrifying. Acts of nature were either unexplained or attributed to the arbitrary will of gods who could be propitiated only by prayers, sacrifices, and other rituals. The Babylonians and Egyptians, who had notable civilizations as far back as 3000 b.c., did note some periodicities in the motions of the sun and moon and indeed based their calendars on these periodicities but saw no deeper significance in them. These few exceptional observations did not influence their attitude toward nature.

希腊人敢于直面自然。即使不是全体民众，至少他们的思想领袖拒绝了传统教义、超自然力量、迷信、教条，以及其他对思想的束缚。他们是最早考察自然那千变万化、神秘而复杂的运行，并试图理解它们的人。他们以心智迎战宇宙中纷乱而看似偶然的事件，着手以理性之光照亮这些事件。

The Greeks dared to look nature in the face. Their intellectual leaders, if not the people at large, rejected traditional doctrines, supernatural forces, superstitions, dogma, and other trammels on thought. They were the first people to examine the multifarious, mysterious, and complex operations of nature and to attempt to understand them. They pitted their minds against the welter of seemingly haphazard occurrences in the universe and undertook to throw the light of reason upon them.

他们怀有无法满足的好奇心与勇气，提出并回答了许多人想到、少数人着手解决、而只有智力最卓越者才能解答的问题。整个宇宙的运行背后，是否存在某种计划？植物、动物、人、行星、光与声音，只是物理上的偶然，还是宏伟设计的一部分？希腊人富于梦想，足以提出新的观点，因而塑造了一种宇宙观，支配了此后一切西方思想。

Possessed of insatiable curiosity and courage, they asked and answered the questions that occur to many, are tackled by few, and are resolved only by individuals of the highest intellectual caliber. Is there any plan underlying the workings of the entire universe? Are plants, animals, men, planets, light, and sound mere physical accidents or are they part of a grand design? Because they were dreamers enough to arrive at new points of view, the Greeks fashioned a conception of the universe which has dominated all subsequent Western thought.

希腊思想家对自然采取了全新的态度。这种态度是理性的、批判的、世俗的。他们摒弃了神话，也摒弃了诸神任凭一时兴致操纵人与物质世界的信念。这些思想家最终形成一种学说：自然井然有序，始终按照某种宏伟设计运行。从行星的运动到树叶的摇曳，一切感官可见的现象，都能纳入精确、连贯、可理解的模式。简言之，自然是依照理性设计的；虽然人的行动不能改变这种设计，但人的心智能够理解它。

The Greek intellectuals adopted a totally new attitude toward nature. This attitude was rational, critical, and secular. Mythology was discarded as was the belief that the gods manipulate man and the physical world according to their whims. The intellectuals eventually arrived at the doctrine that nature is orderly and functions invariably according to a grand design. All phenomena apparent to the senses, from the motions of the planets to the stirrings of the leaves on a tree, can be fitted into a precise, coherent, intelligible pattern. In short, nature is rationally designed and that design, though unaffected by human actions, can be apprehended by man’s mind.

希腊人不仅最早大胆设想纷乱现象中存在规律与秩序，也最早凭借才智揭示出自然显然遵循的某些深层模式。因此，他们敢于追问，并且发现了人类所见最壮观景象背后的设计：灿烂太阳的运行、色彩多变的月亮的盈亏、行星的光辉、群星穹幕中辽阔的光景，以及看似奇迹的日食与月食。

The Greeks were not only the first people with the audacity to conceive of law and order in the welter of phenomena but also the first with the genius to uncover some of the underlying patterns to which nature apparently conforms. Thus they dared to ask for, and found, design underlying the greatest spectacle man beholds, the motion of the brilliant sun, the changing phases of the many hued moon, the brightness of the planets, the broad panorama of lights from the canopy of stars, and the seemingly miraculous eclipses of the sun and moon.

最初尝试对宇宙的本性与运行作出理性解释的，同样是公元前六世纪的爱奥尼亚哲学家。这一时期的著名哲学家泰勒斯、阿那克西曼德、阿那克西美尼、赫拉克利特和阿那克萨戈拉，各自选定一种单一物质来解释宇宙的构成。例如，泰勒斯主张万物都由气态、液态或固态的水构成，并试图用水解释许多现象。这并非不合理的选择，因为云、雾、露、雨和冰雹都是水的形态，水又是生命所必需的，滋养庄稼，并维持众多动物的生命。甚至人体，如今我们知道，也有90%是水。

It was the Ionian philosophers of the sixth century b.c. who also made the first attempts to secure a rational explanation of the nature and functioning of the universe. The famous philosophers of this period, Thales, Anaximander, Anaximenes, Heraclitus, and Anaxagoras, each fixed on a single substance to explain the constitution of the universe. Thales, for example, argued that everything is made up of water in either gaseous, liquid, or solid state, and he attempted explanations of many phenomena in terms of water—a not unreasonable choice because clouds, fog, dew, rain, and hail are forms of water and water is necessary to life, nourishes the crops, and supports much animal life. Even the human body, we now know, is 90 percent water.

爱奥尼亚人的自然哲学，是一系列大胆的思辨、敏锐的猜测和卓越的直觉，而不是广泛、细致的科学研究的成果。这些人或许过于急切地想看到全貌，因而贸然得出宽泛的结论。但他们确实摒弃了旧日主要依靠神话的说法，代之以对宇宙设计与运行的唯物、客观的解释。他们以讲求理由的方法，取代幻想而未经批判的叙述，并用理性为自己的主张辩护。这些人敢于用心智来应对宇宙，拒绝依赖那些可能维持或扰乱自然现象的神、精灵、幽灵、魔鬼、天使以及其他神话中的力量。这些理性解释的精神，可以用阿那克萨戈拉的话来表达：“理性统治世界。”

The natural philosophy of the Ionians was a series of bold speculations, shrewd guesses, and brilliant intuitions rather than the outcome of extensive and careful scientific investigations. These men were perhaps a little over-eager to see the whole picture and so jumped to broad conclusions. But they did discard the older, largely mythical accounts and substituted materialistic and objective explanations of the design and operation of the universe. They offered a reasoned approach in place of fanciful and uncritical accounts and they defended their contentions by reason. These men dared to tackle the universe with their minds and refused to rely on gods, spirits, ghosts, devils, angels, and other mythical agents who might maintain or disrupt nature’s happenings. The spirit of these rational explanations can be expressed in the words of Anaxagoras: “Reason rules the world.”

驱散自然运行中的神秘、玄秘和表面混乱，并以可理解的模式取而代之的决定性一步，是应用数学。在这里，希腊人展现出的洞见，其深远意义与独创性，几乎不亚于发现理性的力量。宇宙按照数学设计，人能够通过数学深入理解这一设计。最先提出自然的数学方案的主要团体，是毕达哥拉斯学派；该学派由毕达哥拉斯（约公元前585—约前500年）领导，扎根于意大利南部。虽然他们确实从当时盛行的希腊宗教中汲取灵感和教义——这种宗教以净化灵魂、使其摆脱肉体的玷污与牢狱为中心——但毕达哥拉斯学派的自然哲学明确是理性的。他们注意到一个引人注目的事实：从质的角度看极不相同的现象，却表现出相同的数学性质。因此，数学性质必定是这些现象的本质。更具体地说，毕达哥拉斯学派在数与数的关系中发现了这种本质。数是他们解释自然的第一原理。一切物体都由物质的基本粒子，即“存在的单位”组成，其组合对应于各种几何图形。单位的总数，实际上就代表了物质对象。数既是宇宙的质料，也是宇宙的形式。由此产生了毕达哥拉斯学派的学说：“万物皆数。”既然数是一切对象的“本质”，便只能通过数来解释自然现象。

The decisive step in dispelling the mystery, mysticism, and seeming chaos in the workings of nature and in replacing them by an understandable pattern was the application of mathematics. Here the Greeks displayed an insight almost as pregnant and as original as the discovery of the power of reason. The universe is mathematically designed, and through mathematics man can penetrate to that design. The first major group to offer a mathematical plan of nature was the Pythagoreans, a school led by Pythagoras (c. 585-c. 500 b.c.) and rooted in southern Italy. While they did draw inspiration and doctrines from the prevailing Greek religion centering on purification of the soul and its redemption from the taint and prison of the body, Pythagorean natural philosophy was decidedly rational. The Pythagoreans were struck by the fact that phenomena most diverse from a qualitative point of view exhibit identical mathematical properties. Hence mathematical properties must be the essence of these phenomena. More specifically, the Pythagoreans found this essence in number and in numerical relationships. Number was the first principle in their explanation of nature. All objects were made up of elementary particles of matter or “units of existence” in combinations corresponding to the various geometrical figures. The total number of units represented, in fact, the material object. Number was the matter and form of the universe. Hence the Pythagorean doctrine, “All things are numbers.” Since number is the “essence” of all objects, the explanation of natural phenomena could be achieved only through number.

毕达哥拉斯学派早期的这一学说令人困惑，因为在我们看来，数是抽象的观念，而事物则是物理对象或物质。但我们对数作了一种抽象，而早期的毕达哥拉斯学派并没有这样做。对他们来说，数就是点或粒子。当他们谈论三角形数、正方形数、五边形数以及其他数时，他们想到的是排列成这些形状的点、石子或点状物的集合（图1.1—1.4）。

This early Pythagorean doctrine is puzzling because to us numbers are abstract ideas, and things are physical objects or substance. But we have made an abstraction of number which the early Pythagoreans did not make. To them, numbers were points or particles. When they spoke of triangular numbers, square numbers, pentagonal numbers, and others, they were thinking of collections of points, pebbles, or point-like objects arranged in those shapes (Figs. 1.1-1.4).

虽然零散的历史资料无法提供精确的年代信息，但毫无疑问，随着毕达哥拉斯学派发展并完善自己的学说，他们开始把数理解为抽象概念，而把对象仅仅视为数的具体实现。有了这一后来形成的区分，我们就能理解公元前五世纪著名的毕达哥拉斯学派成员菲洛劳斯的话：“如果没有数及其本性，任何存在的事物，无论就其自身，还是就它与其他事物的关系而言，对任何人都不会是清楚的。……你可以看到数的力量在发挥作用……在人类的一切行动与思想之中，在一切手工艺与音乐之中。”

Though historical fragments do not afford precise chronological data, there is no doubt that as the Pythagoreans developed and refined their own doctrines they began to understand numbers as abstract concepts, whereas objects were merely concrete realizations of numbers. With this later distinction we can make sense of the statement of Philolaus, a famous fifth-century Pythagorean: “Were it not for number and its nature, nothing that exists would be clear to anybody either in itself or in its relation to other things. . . . You can observe the power of number exercising itself ... in all the acts and the thoughts of men, in all handicrafts and music.”

例如，当毕达哥拉斯学派发现两个事实之后，他们就能够把音乐归结为数之间的简单关系：第一，拨动琴弦产生的声音取决于弦长；第二，张力相同、长度之比为整数之比的琴弦，会发出和谐的声音。例如，拨动两根张力相同、其中一根长度为另一根两倍的弦，便会产生和谐的声音。用我们的术语说，这两个音之间的音程是八度。另一种和谐的组合，由长度之比为3比2的两根弦构成；此时较短的弦发出的音，比第一根弦发出的音高五度。事实上，每一种和谐的拨弦组合，其相对弦长都可以表示为整数之比。毕达哥拉斯学派还发展了一种著名的音阶。虽然我们不打算用篇幅讨论希腊时期的音乐，但应当指出，许多希腊数学家，包括欧几里得和托勒密，都撰文论述过这个主题，尤其是声音的和谐组合与音阶的构造。

The reduction of music, for example, to simple relationships among numbers became possible for the Pythagoreans when they discovered two facts: first that the sound caused by a plucked string depends upon the length of the string; and second that harmonious sounds are given off by equally taut strings whose lengths are to each other as the ratios of whole numbers. For example, a harmonious sound is produced by plucking two equally taut strings, one twice as long as the other. In our language the interval between the two notes is an octave. Another harmonious combination is formed by two strings whose lengths are in the ratio 3 to 2; in this case the shorter one gives off a note, called the fifth, above that given off by the first string. In fact, the relative lengths in every harmonious combination of plucked strings can be expressed as a ratio of whole numbers. The Pythagoreans also developed a famous musical scale. Though we shall not devote space to music of the Greek period, we would like to note that many Greek mathematicians, including Euclid and Ptolemy, wrote on the subject, especially on harmonious combinations of sounds and the construction of scales.

毕达哥拉斯学派把行星的运动归结为数的关系。他们相信，在空间中运动的物体会产生声音。这或许是由系在绳端旋转的物体发出的嗖嗖声启发的。他们还相信，运动迅速的物体发出的音，比运动缓慢的物体更高。而按照他们的天文学，行星离地球越远，运动就越快。因此，行星产生的声音随其到地球的距离而变化，而且这些声音彼此和谐。然而，这种“天体音乐”如同一切和声一样，不过归结为数的关系，因而行星的运动也归结为数的关系。我们听不到这种音乐，是因为我们从出生起就已习惯了它。

The Pythagoreans reduced the motions of the planets to number relations. They believed that bodies moving in space produce sounds. Perhaps this was suggested by the swishing of an object whirled on the end of a string. They believed, further, that a body which moves rapidly gives forth a higher note than one which moves slowly. Now according to their astronomy, the greater the distance of a planet from the earth the more rapidly it moved. Hence the sounds produced by the planets varied with their distances from the earth and these sounds all harmonized. But this “music of the spheres,” like all harmony, reduced to no more than number relationships and hence so did the motions of the planets. We do not hear this music because we are accustomed to it from birth.

自然的其他特征也被“归结”为数。数1、2、3、4，即四元组（tetractys），尤其受到重视。据说，毕达哥拉斯学派的誓言是：“我以赐予我们灵魂的四元组之名起誓。永不停息的自然，其源泉与根本都包含在其中。”自然由各种四重结构组成，如点、线、面、体这四种几何元素，以及柏拉图后来强调的土、气、火、水这四种物质元素。

Other features of nature were “reduced” to number. The numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4, the tetractys, were especially valued. In fact, the Pythagorean oath is reported to be: “I swear in the name of the Tetractys which has been bestowed on our soul. The source and roots of the everflowing nature are contained in it.” Nature was composed of fournesses such as the four geometric elements, point, line, surface, and solid; and the four material elements Plato later emphasized, earth, air, fire, and water.

四元组中的四个数相加等于十，所以十是理想的数，代表宇宙。因为十是理想的，天上必定有十个天体。为了凑足所需数目，毕达哥拉斯学派引入了一个中央火体，地球、太阳、月亮以及当时已知的五颗行星都围绕它运行；他们还在中央火体的另一侧引入了一个反地球。我们看不到这个中央火体和反地球，是因为我们居住的地球区域背向它们。细节不值得继续追究；关键在于，毕达哥拉斯学派试图建立一种以数的关系为基础的天文学理论。

The four numbers of the tetractys added up to ten and so ten was the ideal number and represented the universe. Because ten was ideal there must be ten bodies in the heavens. To fill out the required number the Pythagoreans introduced a central fire around which the earth, sun, moon, and the five planets then known revolved and a counter-earth on the opposite side of the central fire. We do not see this central fire and the counter-earth because the area of the earth on which we live faces away from them. The details are not worth pursuing; the main point is that the Pythagoreans tried to build an astronomical theory based on numerical relationships.

由于毕达哥拉斯学派把天文学与音乐“归结”为数，音乐和天文学便与算术、几何联系起来，四门学科全被视为数学学科。这四门成为学校课程的一部分，甚至一直保留到中世纪，当时它们被称为“四艺”（quadrivium）。

Because the Pythagoreans “reduced” astronomy and music to number, music and astronomy came to be linked with arithmetic and geometry, and all four subjects were regarded as mathematical. The four became part of the school curriculum and remained so even into medieval times, where they were labelled the quadrivium.

亚里士多德在《形而上学》中概括了毕达哥拉斯学派把数与真实世界等同起来的观点：

Aristotle in his Metaphysics sums up the Pythagorean identification of number and the real world:

他们似乎在数中，比在火、土、水中，更多地看到了与存在和生成的事物的相似性（数的某种变化就是正义，另一种就是灵魂与理性，还有一种就是时机——同样，几乎其他一切都可以用数来表达）；又因为音阶的变化和比例能够用数表达；因此，既然其他一切事物在其整个本性上似乎都以数为范型，数又似乎是整个自然中最先存在的东西，他们便假定数的元素就是万物的元素，整个天宇就是一种音阶和一个数。

In numbers they seemed to see resemblances to things that exist and come into being—more than in fire and earth and water (such and such a modification of numbers being justice, another being soul and reason, another being opportunity—and similarly almost all other things being numerically expressible); since, again, that the modifications and the ratios of the musical scales were expressible in numbers;—since, then, all other things seemed in their whole nature to be modelled on numbers, and numbers seemed to be the first things in the whole of nature, they supposed the elements of numbers to be the elements of all things, and the whole heaven to be a musical scale and a number.

毕达哥拉斯学派的自然哲学谈不上扎实。审美考量与寻找数的关系的执念交织在一起，无疑使他们作出了超越观察证据的断言。他们也没有使物理科学的任何一个分支得到深入发展。完全可以说，他们的理论是肤浅的。然而，无论出于幸运还是直觉上的天才，他们确实抓住了后来被证明极其重要的两项学说：第一，自然按照数学原理构成；第二，数的关系是自然秩序的基础，并能统一和揭示这种秩序。事实上，现代科学也坚持毕达哥拉斯学派对数的重视；不过正如我们将看到的，现代学说是精密得多的毕达哥拉斯主义。

The natural philosophy of the Pythagoreans is hardly substantial. Aesthetic considerations commingled with an obsession to find number relationships certainly led to assertions transcending observational evidence. Nor did the Pythagoreans develop any one branch of physical science very far. One could justifiably call their theories superficial. But, whether by luck or by intuitive genius, the Pythagoreans did hit upon two doctrines which proved later to be all-important: the first is that nature is built according to mathematical principles; the second that number relationships underlie, unify, and reveal the order in nature. Actually modern science adheres to the Pythagorean emphasis on number, though, as we shall see, the modern doctrines are a much more sophisticated form of Pythagoreanism.

在时间上继毕达哥拉斯学派之后的哲学家，同样关心实在的本性及其深层的数学设计。留基伯（约公元前440年）与德谟克利特（约公元前460—约前370年）值得注意，因为他们最明确地肯定了原子论。他们共同的哲学是：世界由无穷多个简单、永恒的原子组成。这些原子在形状、大小、硬度、排列和位置上各不相同。每个物体都是这些原子的某种组合。虽然线段等几何量可以无限分割，但原子是最终的、不可分割的粒子。形状、大小以及刚才提到的其他性质，是原子的性质。味道、热和颜色等其他一切性质，并不在原子之中，而在于原子对感知者产生的效果。这种感性知识并不可靠，因为它随感知者而变化。和毕达哥拉斯学派一样，原子论者断言，物质世界不断变化的多样性背后的实在，可以用数学来表达。而且，这个世界中发生的事情，严格由数学规律决定。

The philosophers who chronologically succeeded the Pythagoreans were as much concerned with the nature of reality and the underlying mathematical design. Leuccipus (c. 440 b.c.) and Democritus (c. 460- c. 370 B.c.) are notable because they were most explicit in affirming the doctrine of atomism. Their common philosophy was that the world is composed of an infinite number of simple, eternal atoms. These differ in shape, size, hardness, order, and position. Every object is some combination of these atoms. Though geometrical magnitudes such as a line segment are infinitely divisible, the atoms are ultimate, indivisible particles. Properties such as shape, size, and the others just mentioned were properties of the atoms. All other properties such as taste, heat, and color were not in the atoms but in the effect of the atoms on the perceiver. This sensuous knowledge was unreliable because it varied with the perceiver. Like the Pythagoreans, the atomists asserted that the reality underlying the constantly changing diversity of the physical world was expressible in terms of mathematics. Moreover, the happenings in this world were strictly determined by mathematical laws.

在毕达哥拉斯学派之后，阐述并传播自然具有数学设计这一学说的最有影响力的团体，是当然由柏拉图领导的柏拉图学派。虽然柏拉图（公元前427—前347年）接受了某些毕达哥拉斯学派的学说，但他是一位大师，在意义重大的公元前四世纪支配着希腊思想。他在雅典创立了学园；这个中心吸引了当时的主要思想家，并延续了九百年。

After the Pythagoreans the most influential group to expound and propagate the doctrine of the mathematical design of nature was the Platonists, led, of course, by Plato. Though Plato (427-347 b.c.) took over some Pythagorean doctrines, he was a master who dominated Greek thought in the momentous fourth century b.c. He was the founder of the Academy in Athens, a center which attracted leading thinkers of his day and endured for nine hundred years.

柏拉图对宇宙理性的信仰，也许在他的对话《斐勒布篇》中表达得最为清楚：

Plato’s belief in the rationality of the universe is perhaps best expressed in his dialogue the Pkilebus:

普罗塔库斯：什么问题？ 苏格拉底：他们所说的这个宇宙中的一切，究竟是任由

Protarchus: What question? Socrates: Whether all this which they call the universe is left to the

非理性与偶然的杂乱来支配，还是相反，正如

guidance of unreason and chance medley, or, on the contrary, as

我们的先辈所宣称的，由奇妙的

our fathers have declared, ordered and governed by a marvellous

智力与智慧来安排和治理。 普罗塔库斯：这两种断言相差太远了，尊敬的

intelligence and wisdom. Protarchus: Wide asunder are the two assertions, illustrious

苏格拉底，因为您刚才对我说的那种看法，似乎

Socrates, for that which you were just now saying to me appears

是亵渎神明；而另一种断言，即心智安排一切

to be blasphemy, but the other assertion, that mind orders all

事物，则与世界、太阳、

things, is worthy of the aspect of the world, and of the sun, and

月亮、星辰以及整个天

of the moon, and of the stars and of the whole circle of the heav¬

穹的面貌相称；我决不会说出或想出相反的意见。

ens; and never will I say or think otherwise.

后期的毕达哥拉斯学派与柏拉图学派严格区分事物的世界和理念的世界。物质世界中的对象与关系难免不完美、变化与衰朽，因而不能代表终极真理；但另有一个理念世界，其中存在绝对而不变的真理。这些真理才是哲学家应当关注的。对于物理世界，我们只能有意见。可见的、可感的世界，只是理念世界模糊、黯淡而不完美的实现。“事物是理念投射在经验屏幕上的影子。”因此，实在应当在可感的物理对象的理念中寻找。柏拉图会说，一匹马、一座房子或一个美丽的女人，其中没有什么是真实的。实在存在于马、房子或女人的普遍类型或理念之中。只有关于纯粹理念形式，才能获得无误的知识。这些理念确实恒定不变，关于它们的知识也坚固而不可摧毁。

The later Pythagoreans and the Platonists distinguished sharply between the world of things and the world of ideas. Objects and relationships in the material world were subject to imperfections, change, and decay and hence did not represent the ultimate truth, but there was an ideal world in which there were absolute and unchanging truths. These truths were the proper concern of the philosopher. About the physical world we can only have opinions. The visible and sensuous world is just a vague, dim, and imperfect realization of the ideal world. “Things are the shadows of ideas thrown on the screen of experience.” Reality then was to be found in the ideas of sensuous, physical objects. Thus Plato would say that there is nothing real in a horse, a house, or a beautiful woman. The reality is in the universal type or idea of a horse, a house, or a woman. Infallible knowledge can be obtained only about pure ideal forms. These ideas are in fact constant and invariable, and knowledge concerning them is firm and indestructible.

柏拉图坚持，唯有通过理念世界的数学，才能理解物理世界的实在性与可理解性。这个世界具有数学结构，是毋庸置疑的。普鲁塔克记载了柏拉图的名言：“神永远在进行几何活动。”柏拉图在《理想国》中说：“几何所追求的知识，是关于永恒者的知识，而不是关于任何会消亡、转瞬即逝之物的知识。”数学规律不仅是实在的本质，而且永恒不变。数的关系也是实在的一部分，而事物的集合只是数的摹本。在早期毕达哥拉斯学派那里，数内在于事物；在柏拉图那里，数则超越事物。

Plato insisted that the reality and intelligibility of the physical world could be comprehended only through the mathematics of the ideal world. There was no question that this world was mathematically structured. Plutarch reports Plato’s famous, “God eternally geometrizes.” In the Republic, Plato said “the knowledge at which geometry aims is knowledge of the eternal, and not of aught perishing and transient.” Mathematical laws were not only the essence of reality but eternal and unchanging. Number relations, too, were part of reality, and collections of things were mere imitations of numbers. Whereas with the earlier Pythagoreans numbers were immanent in things, with Plato they transcended things.

柏拉图比毕达哥拉斯学派走得更远：他不仅希望通过数学理解自然，还希望以数学取代自然本身。他相信，只需对物理世界作几次深刻的观察，就能得到基本真理的启示，随后理性便可不借助外力继续前进。从此以后，就只剩数学。数学将取代物理研究。

Plato went further than the Pythagoreans in that he wished not merely to understand nature through mathematics but to substitute mathematics for nature herself. He believed that a few penetrating glances at the physical world would suggest basic truths with which reason could then carry on unaided. From that point on there would be just mathematics. Mathematics would substitute for physical investigation.

普鲁塔克在《马塞卢斯传》中记述，与柏拉图同时代的著名人物欧多克索斯和阿尔基塔斯，曾用物理论证来“证明”数学结果。但柏拉图愤怒地斥责这种证明败坏了几何，因为它们利用感性事实代替纯粹推理。

Plutarch relates in his “Life of Marcellus” that Eudoxus and Archytas, famous contemporaries of Plato, used physical arguments to “prove” mathematical results. But Plato indignantly denounced such proofs as a corruption of geometry; they utilized sensuous facts in place of pure reasoning.

柏拉图对天文学的态度，说明了他对应该追求何种知识的立场。他说，这门科学不关心可见天体的运动。天上星辰的排列及其视运动，确实壮丽而美不胜收；但仅仅观察并解释这些运动，还远远达不到真正的天文学。在达到这种真正的科学之前，我们“必须撇开天空”，因为真正的天文学研究的是数学天空中真实星辰的运动规律，可见天空不过是它不完美的表现。他鼓励人们献身于理论天文学：其中的问题使心智而不是眼睛感到愉悦，其对象由心智而不是视觉把握。天空呈现在眼前的各种图形，只应当用作帮助寻找更高真理的示意图。我们必须像对待几何一样，把天文学看作一系列仅由可见事物启发的问题。柏拉图对于天文学在航海、历法计算与计时中的用途毫无兴趣。

Plato’s attitude toward astronomy illustrates his position on the knowledge to be sought. This science, he said, is not concerned with the movements of the visible heavenly bodies. The arrangement of the stars in the heavens and their apparent movements are indeed wonderful and beautiful to behold, but mere observations and explanation of the motions fall far short of true astronomy. Before we can attain to this true science we “must leave the heavens alone,” for true astronomy deals with the laws of motion of true stars in a mathematical heaven of which the visible heaven is but an imperfect expression. He encouraged devotion to a theoretical astronomy whose problems please the mind and not the eye and whose objects are apprehended by the mind and not by vision. The varied figures the sky presents to the eye are to be used only as diagrams to assist the search for higher truths. We must treat astronomy, like geometry, as a series of problems merely suggested by visible things. The uses of astronomy in navigation, calendar-reckoning, and the measurement of time were of no interest to Plato.

亚里士多德虽是柏拉图的学生，并从他那里吸收了许多思想，但对于真实世界的研究，以及数学与实在的关系，他的看法颇为不同。他批评柏拉图脱离现实的倾向，以及把科学归结为数学的做法。亚里士多德是“物理学家”一词字面意义上的物理学家。他相信物质事物是实在的首要实体与来源。物理学乃至一般科学，都必须研究物理世界，从中获得真理。真正的知识通过直觉与抽象，从感官经验中取得。这些抽象物不具有独立于人类心智的存在。

Aristotle, though a student of Plato from whom he derived many ideas, had a quite different concept of the study of the real world and of the relation of mathematics to reality. He criticized Plato’s other-worldliness and his reduction of science to mathematics. Aristotle was a physicist in the literal sense of the word. He believed in material things as the primary substance and source of reality. Physics, and science generally, must study the physical world and obtain truths from it. Genuine knowledge is obtained from sense experience by intuition and abstraction. These abstractions have no existence independent of human minds.

亚里士多德确实强调共相，即从真实事物中抽象出的一般性质。他说，要得到这些性质，我们应“从我们能够认识和观察的事物出发，走向那些依其本性更清楚、更可知的事物”。他把对象明显的感性性质实体化，提升为独立的心智概念。

Aristotle did emphasize universals, general qualities that are abstracted from real things. To obtain these he said we “start with things which are knowable and observable to us and proceed toward those things which are clearer and more knowable by nature.” He took the obvious sensuous qualities of objects, hypostatized them, and elevated them to independent, mental concepts.

在亚里士多德的体系中，数学处于什么位置？物理科学是根本。数学通过描述形状和数量等形式性质，帮助研究自然。数学还为物质现象中观察到的事实提供理由。因此，几何可以解释光学与天文学提供的事实，算术比例可以为和声提供基础。但数学概念与原理明确是从真实世界中抽象出来的。正因为它们从世界中抽象出来，所以能应用于世界。心智具有一种能力，使我们从感觉中获得物理对象的这些理想化性质，而且这些抽象必然是真的。

Where was mathematics in Aristotle’s scheme of things? The physical sciences were fundamental. Mathematics helped in the study of nature by describing formal properties such as shape and quantity. Also mathematics provided the reasons for facts observed in material phenomena. Thus geometry could provide the explanation of facts provided by optics and astronomy, and arithmetical ratios could give the basis for harmony. But mathematical concepts and principles are definitely abstractions from the real world. Because they are abstracted from the world, they are applicable to it. There is a faculty of the mind which enables us to arrive at these idealized properties of physical objects from sensations and these abstractions are necessarily true.

以上对造就并塑造希腊思想世界的哲学家的简要概述，可以说明，他们都强调研究自然，以便认识、理解并欣赏深层的实在。而且，自毕达哥拉斯学派时代起，几乎所有哲学家都断言自然是按照数学设计的。到古典时期结束时，自然具有数学设计的学说已获确立，寻找数学规律的工作也已开展。虽然这一信念并非后来所有数学的动力，但它一经接受，大多数伟大数学家便依此行动，甚至包括那些未曾接触过这一信念的人。在希腊人思辨思想的一切胜利中，最具真正新意的，是他们认为宇宙依照人类思想能够发现的数学规律运行。

This brief survey of the philosophers who forged and molded the Greek intellectual world may serve to show that all of them stressed the study of nature for comprehension, understanding, and appreciation of the underlying reality. Moreover, from the time of the Pythagoreans practically all philosophers asserted that nature was designed mathematically. By the end of the classical period the doctrine of the mathematical design of nature was established and the search for mathematical laws had been instituted. Though this belief did not motivate all later mathematics, once accepted it was acted on by most of the great mathematicians, even those who had no contact with the belief. Of all the triumphs of the speculative thought of the Greeks, the most truly novel was their conception of the cosmos operating in accordance with mathematical laws discoverable by human thought.

因此，希腊人决意追求真理，尤其是关于自然数学设计的真理。人应当怎样寻找真理，并保证所得确为真理？在这一点上，希腊人也提供了方案。虽然这一方案在公元前600年至前300年间逐渐形成，虽然它最初由谁、何时提出尚有疑问，但到公元前300年，它已趋于完善。

The Greeks, then, were determined to seek truths and in particular truths about the mathematical design of nature. How does one go about seeking truths and guaranteeing that they are truths? Here, too, the Greeks provided the plan. Though this evolved gradually during the period from 600 to 300 b.c., and though there is some question as to when and by whom it was first conceived of, by 300 b.c. it was perfected.

从宽泛意义上说，即就运用数和几何图形而言，数学比古典时期希腊人的工作早了几千年。在这种宽泛意义上，数学一词包括许多古代文明的贡献，其中埃及与巴比伦最为突出。除希腊文明之外，在所有这些文明中，数学几乎算不上一门独立学科——它没有方法论，也不为直接实用目的之外的目标而研究。它是一种工具，一系列彼此无关的简单规则，使人们能够回答日常生活中的问题：历法计算、农业和商业。这些规则通过试错、经验和简单观察获得，许多仅仅近似正确。对于这些文明的数学，至多只能说，它虽未展示思想的严密性，却展示了一定的活力；它的毅力也胜过才华。这种数学可以用“经验性”一词来概括。巴比伦人和埃及人的经验数学，也为希腊人的工作拉开了序幕。

Mathematics in a loose sense of the term, in the sense of utilizing numbers and geometrical figures, antedates the work of the classical Greeks by several thousand years. In this loose sense the term mathematics includes the contributions of many bygone civilizations among which the Egyptian and Babylonian are most prominent. In all of these, except the Greek civilization, mathematics was hardly a distinct discipline— it had no methodology nor was it pursued for other than immediate, practical ends. It was a tool, a series of disconnected, simple rules which enabled people to answer questions of daily life: calendar-reckoning, agriculture, and commerce. These rules were arrived at by trial and error, experience, and simple observation, and many were only approximately correct. About the best one can say for the mathematics of these civilizations is that it showed some vigor if not rigor of thought and more perseverance than brilliance. This mathematics is characterized by the word empirical. The empirical mathematics of the Babylonians and the Egyptians also served as a prelude to the work of the Greeks.

虽然希腊文化并非全然不受外来影响——希腊思想家确实到过埃及和巴比伦旅行、学习——而且即使在希腊适宜的思想氛围中，现代意义上的数学也必须经历孕育时期，但希腊人的创造与他们继承的东西之间，差别犹如黄金与锡。

Though the Greek culture was not entirely free of outside influences—Greek thinkers did travel and study in Egypt and Babylonia— and though mathematics in the modern sense of the word had to undergo a period of gestation even in the congenial intellectual atmosphere of Greece, what the Greeks created differs as much from what they took over as gold from tin.

希腊人既然决定追求数学真理，就不能以其前辈，尤其是埃及人和巴比伦人所汇集的那些粗糙、经验性、有限、互不相连，而且往往只是近似的结果为基础。数学本身，即关于数和几何图形的基本事实，必须是一套真理；旨在获得物理现象——如天体运动——之真理的数学推理，必须产生毋庸置疑的结论。这些目标该如何达到呢？

Having decided to search for mathematical truths, the Greeks could not build upon the crude, empirical, limited, disconnected, and, in many instances, approximate results that their predecessors, notably the Egyptians and Babylonians, had compiled. Mathematics itself, the basic facts about number and geometrical figures, must be a body of truths, and mathematical reasoning, aimed at arriving at truths about physical phenomena, the motions of the heavens for example, must produce indubitable conclusions. How were these objectives to be attained?

第一条原则是，数学应当处理抽象对象。在塑造希腊数学的哲学家看来，真理按其含义，只能涉及永久、不变的实体与关系。幸运的是，人类智力受感性对象的印象激发而思考，能够上升到更高的概念；这些就是理念，是永恒的实在，也是思想真正的对象。偏爱抽象还有另一个理由。如果数学要具有力量，它就必须用一个抽象概念，涵盖该概念在物理世界中一切实例的本质特征。因此，数学直线必须涵盖拉紧的绳子、直尺的边缘、田地的边界以及光线的路径。相应地，数学的线不应具有厚度、颜色、分子结构或张力。希腊人明确宣称，他们的数学处理抽象对象。柏拉图在《理想国》中谈到几何学家时说：

The first principle was that mathematics was to deal with abstractions. For the philosophers who molded Greek mathematics, truth by its very meaning could pertain only to permanent, unchanging entities and relationships. Fortunately, the intelligence of man excited to reflection by the impressions of sensuous objects can rise to higher conceptions; these are the ideas, the eternal realities and the true object of thought. There was another reason for the preference for abstractions. If mathematics was to be powerful it must embrace in one abstract concept the essential feature of all the physical occurrences of that concept. Thus the mathematical straight line must embrace stretched strings, ruler’s edges, boundaries of fields, and the paths of light rays. Accordingly, the mathematical line was to have no thickness, color, molecular structure, or tension. The Greeks were explicit in asserting that their mathematics dealt with abstractions. Speaking of geometricians, Plato said in The Republic:

你不也知道吗？虽然他们运用可见的形状并推论它们，但他们所想的并不是这些形状，而是这些形状所类似的理念；并非他们画出的图形，而是绝对的正方形与绝对的直径……他们真正追求的是看见事物本身，而这些事物只能以心灵之眼看见。

Do you not know also that although they make use of the visible forms and reason about them, they are thinking not of these, but of the ideals which they resemble; not of the figures which they draw, but of the absolute square and the absolute diameter . . . they are really seeking to behold the things themselves, which can be seen only with the eye of the mind?

因此，数学首先要处理点、线、整数等抽象概念。三角形、正方形、圆等其他概念，随后可以用基本概念来定义；而如亚里士多德指出的，基本概念必须不加定义，否则便没有起点。希腊人的敏锐，体现在他们要求：经定义的概念，必须通过论证或作图，证明在实在中具有对应物。因此，不能只是定义一个三等分角的构造，再证明关于它的定理。它可能并不存在。事实上，希腊人未能在自己规定的作图限制下构造出三等分角的图形，所以没有引入这一概念。

Hence mathematics would deal first of all with abstract concepts such as point, line, and whole number. Other concepts such as triangle, square, and circle could then be defined in terms of the basic ones, which as Aristotle pointed out must be undefined or else there would be no starting point. The acuity of the Greeks is evident in the requirement that defined concepts must be shown to have counterparts in reality, either by demonstration or construction. Thus one could not define an angle trisector and prove theorems about it. It might not exist. And in fact, since the Greeks did not succeed in constructing an angle trisector under the limitations they imposed on constructions, they did not introduce this concept.

为了推论数学概念，希腊人从公理出发，即从如此自明、以至于无人能够怀疑的真理出发。这样的真理当然存在。柏拉图用回忆说，又称追忆说（anamnesis），为接受公理提供依据。正如前面指出的，在他看来，存在一个客观的真理世界。人在来到地球以前，曾以灵魂的形式在另一个世界获得经验；只需激发灵魂回忆先前的经验，就能知道几何公理是真理。无需地上的任何经验。亚里士多德则用另一种方式表述。公理是可理解的原理，向心智呈现得无可怀疑。亚里士多德在《后分析篇》中说，我们凭无误的直觉知道公理是真的。此外，我们必须拥有这些真理，作为推理的基础。如果推理反而运用一些尚不知为真的事实，就需要进一步推理来确立这些事实，而这一过程又必须无休止地重复。这样便会陷入无穷倒退。他把公理区分为共同概念与公设。共同概念在所有思想领域中都为真，包括“等量加等量，所得仍相等”这样的陈述。公设则适用于几何等特定学科，如“两点确定唯一一条直线”。亚里士多德确实说过，公设不必自明，但不自明时，必须由从它们推出的结果来支持。然而，数学家要求公设具有自明性。

To reason about the concepts of mathematics the Greeks started with axioms, truths so self-evident that no one could doubt them. Surely such truths were available. Plato justified acceptance of the axioms by his theory of recollection or anamnesis. There was for him, as we noted earlier, an objective world of truths. Humans had experience as souls in another world before coming to earth and the soul had but to be stimulated to recall its prior experience in order to kpow that the axioms of geometry were truths. No experience on earth was necessary. Aristotle put it otherwise. The axioms are intelligible principles which appeal to the mind beyond possibility of doubt. The axioms, Aristotle said in Posterior Analytics, are known to be true by our infallible intuition. Moreover, we must have these truths on which to base our reasoning. If, instead, reasoning were to use some facts not known to be truths, further reasoning would be needed to establish these facts and this process would have to be repeated endlessly. There would then be an infinite regress. Among the axioms, he distinguished common notions and postulates. Common notions are true in all fields of thought and include statements such as “Equals added to equals give equals.” Postulates apply to a specific subject such as geometry. Thus, “Two points determine a unique line.” Aristotle did say that postulates need not be self-evident but when not must be supported by the consequences which follow from them. However, self-evidency was required by the mathematicians.

应当通过推理从公理推出结论。推理有许多类型，例如归纳、类比和演绎。在这些类型中，只有一种能保证结论正确。因为发现一千个苹果是红的，便断定所有苹果都是红的，这属于归纳，因而并非绝对可靠。同样，认为约翰应该能够大学毕业，因为继承了相同能力的哥哥做到了，这属于类比推理，当然也不可靠。相反，演绎推理虽然有许多形式，却确实能够保证结论。因此，如果承认所有人都会死，而苏格拉底是人，就必须接受苏格拉底会死。这里涉及的逻辑原则，是亚里士多德所谓三段论推理的一种形式。在其他演绎推理规律中，亚里士多德还列入了矛盾律（一个命题不能既真又假）与排中律（一个命题必定非真即假）。

From the axioms, conclusions were to be derived by reasoning. There are many types of reasoning, for example, induction, reasoning by analogy, and deduction. Of the many types, only one guarantees the correctness of the conclusion. The conclusion that all apples are red because one thousand apples are found to be red is inductive and therefore not absolutely reliable. Likewise the argument that John should be able to graduate from college because his brother who inherited the same faculties did so, is reasoning by analogy and certainly not reliable. Deductive reasoning, on the other hand, though it can take many forms does guarantee the conclusion. Thus, if one grants that all men are mortal and Socrates is a man, one must accept that Socrates is mortal. The principle of logic involved here is one form of what Aristotle called syllogistic reasoning. Among other laws of deductive reasoning, Aristotle included the law of contradiction (a proposition cannot be both true and false) and the law of excluded middle (a proposition must be either true or false).

他和世人都毫不怀疑地接受：把这些演绎原则应用于任何前提，所得结论就与前提一样可靠。因此，如果前提是真理，结论也是真理。值得注意的是，尤其联系到我们后面将讨论的问题，亚里士多德是从数学家已经实践的推理中，抽象出演绎逻辑原则的。实际上，演绎逻辑是数学的孩子。

He and the world at large accepted unquestioningly that these deductive principles when applied to any premise yielded conclusions as reliable as the premise. Hence if the premises were truths, so would the conclusions be. It is worthy of note, especially in the light of what we shall be discussing later, that Aristotle abstracted the principles of deductive logic from the reasoning already practiced by mathematicians. Deductive logic is, in effect, the child of mathematics.

虽然几乎所有希腊哲学家都倡导演绎推理，认为它是获得真理的唯一可靠方法，但柏拉图的观点略有不同。他虽不反对演绎证明，却认为证明是多余的，因为数学的公理与定理存在于某个独立于人的客观世界之中；按照他的回忆说，人只需回忆它们，就能认识到它们毋庸置疑的真理性。用柏拉图本人在《泰阿泰德篇》中的比喻，定理就像鸟舍中的鸟。它们已经存在，人只需伸手便可抓住。学习不过是回忆的过程。在柏拉图的对话《美诺篇》中，苏格拉底通过巧妙提问，使一个年轻奴隶说出：在等腰直角三角形的斜边上作的正方形，其面积是在一条直角边上所作正方形的两倍。随后苏格拉底得意地断言，这个奴隶既然没有受过几何教育，就是在适当的提示下回忆起了这一事实。

Though deductive reasoning was advocated by almost all the Greek philosophers as the only reliable method of obtaining truths, Plato’s view was somewhat different. Though he would not object to deductive proof, he did regard it as superfluous, for the axioms and theorems of mathematics exist in some objective world independent of man, and in accordance with Plato’s doctrine of anamnesis, man has but to recall them to recognize their indubitable truth. The theorems, to use Plato’s own analogy in his Theaetetus, are like birds in an aviary. They exist and one has only to reach in to grasp them. Learning is but a process of recollection. In Plato’s dialogue Meno, Socrates by skillful questioning elicits from a young slave the assertion that the square erected on the diagonal of an isosceles right triangle has twice the area of a square erected on a side. Socrates then triumphantly concludes that the slave, since he was not educated in geometry, recalled it under the proper suggestions.

理解坚持演绎证明是多么激进，十分重要。假设一位科学家测量了一百个位置、大小和形状各不相同的三角形的内角和，发现在实验精度范围内，内角和都是180°。他当然会断定，任何三角形的内角和都是180°。但他的证明是归纳而非演绎，因而不能在数学上被接受。同样，人可以随意检验任意多个偶数，发现每一个都是两个素数之和。但这种检验不是演绎证明，所以所得结果不是数学定理。因此，演绎证明是一个非常严格的要求。尽管如此，大体上也是哲学家的希腊数学家，坚持只使用演绎推理，因为它能产生真理，产生永恒的真理。

It is important to appreciate how radical the insistence on deductive proof was. Suppose a scientist should measure the sum of the angles of a hundred different triangles in different locations and of different size and shape and find that sum to be 180° to within the limits of experimental accuracy. Surely he would conclude that the sum of the angles of any triangle is 180°. But his proof would be inductive, not deductive, and would therefore not be mathematically acceptable. Likewise, one can test as many even numbers as he pleases and find that each is a sum of two prime numbers. But this test is not a deductive proof and so the result is not a theorem of mathematics. Deductive proof is, then, a very stringent requirement. Nevertheless, the Greek mathematicians, who were in the main philosophers, insisted on the exclusive use of deductive reasoning because this yields truths, eternal verities.

哲学家偏爱演绎推理，还有另一个原因。哲学家关心关于人和物理世界的广泛知识。要确立诸如人性本善、世界是设计出来的、人生具有目的之类的普遍真理，从可接受的第一原理出发进行演绎推理，远比归纳或类比可行。

There is another reason that philosophers favor deductive reasoning. Philosophers are concerned with broad knowledge about man and the physical world. To establish universal truths such as that man is basically good, that the world is designed, or that man’s life has purpose, deductive reasoning from acceptable first principles is far more feasible than induction or analogy.

古典时期希腊人偏爱演绎的又一个原因，或许可以在其社会组织中找到。哲学、数学与艺术活动由较富裕的阶层从事。这些人不做体力劳动。奴隶、外侨（非公民）以及自由公民中的工匠，受雇从事商业与家务，甚至从事最重要的职业。受教育的自由人不动手劳动，也很少从事商业。柏拉图宣称，店主的职业有辱自由人的身份，并希望自由人从事这种职业会被当作犯罪惩罚。亚里士多德说，在完美国家中，没有公民（与奴隶相对而言）会从事任何机械技艺。在希腊部族之一的彼奥提亚人中，凡以商业玷污自己的人，十年内不得担任任何公职。对这种社会中的思想家来说，实验和观察是陌生的。因此，不会有科学或数学成果从这类来源得出。

Still another reason for the classical Greeks’ preference for deduction may be found in the organization of their society. Philosophical, mathematical, and artistic activities were carried on by the wealthier class. These people did no manual work. Slaves, metics (non-citizens), and free citizen-artisans were employed in business and in the household, and they even practiced the most important professions. Educated freemen did not use their hands and rarely engaged in commercial pursuits. Plato declared that the trade of a shopkeeper was a degradation to a freeman and wished that his engagement in such a trade be punished as a crime. Aristotle said that in the perfect state no citizen (as opposed to slaves) would practice any mechanical art. Among the Boeotians, one of the Greek tribes, those who defiled themselves with commerce were excluded from all state offices for ten years. To thinkers in such a society, experimentation and observation would be alien. Hence no results scientific or mathematical would be derived from such sources.

虽然希腊人坚持演绎证明有许多原因，但究竟是哪位哲学家或哪个哲学团体最先提出这一要求，仍有疑问。遗憾的是，我们对前苏格拉底哲学家的教导与著作所知零碎；虽然有人提出过各种答案，却没有一个得到普遍认可。到亚里士多德时代，这一要求肯定已经生效，因为他明确论述了严格性的标准，如需要不定义的术语以及推理规律。

Though there are many reasons for the Greeks’ insistence on deductive proof there is some question as to which philosopher or group of philosophers first laid down this requirement. Unfortunately our knowledge of the teachings and writings of the pre-Socratic philosophers is fragmentary and though various answers have been given there is no universally accepted one. By Aristotle’s time the requirement was certainly in effect, for he is explicit about standards of rigor such as the need for undefined terms and the laws of reasoning.

希腊人执行获得宇宙数学规律的计划，取得了多大成功？幸运的是，欧几里得、阿波罗尼奥斯、阿基米德和克劳狄乌斯·托勒密等人所创造的数学精华流传至今。按年代，这些人属于希腊文化的第二个伟大时期，即希腊化时期或亚历山大里亚时期（公元前300—公元600年）。公元前四世纪，马其顿国王腓力着手征服波斯人；他们控制着近东，向来是欧洲希腊人的敌人。腓力遇刺，其子亚历山大继位。亚历山大确实击败了波斯人，并把扩大后的希腊帝国的文化中心迁到一座新城市；他“谦逊地”以自己的名字命名这座城市。亚历山大于公元前323年去世，但他在埃及的继承者采用了托勒密这一王号，继续实施发展这个新中心的计划。

How successful were the Greeks in executing their plan of obtaining mathematical laws of the universe? The cream of the mathematics created by such men as Euclid, Apollonius, Archimedes, and Claudius Ptolemy has fortunately come down to us. Chronologically these men belonged to the second great period of Greek culture, the Hellenistic or Alexandrian (300 b.c.-a.d. 600). During the fourth century b.c. King Philip of Macedonia undertook to conquer the Persians, who controlled the Near East and had been traditional enemies of the European Greeks. Philip was assassinated and was succeeded by his son Alexander. Alexander did defeat the Persians and moved the cultural center of the enlarged Greek empire to a new city which he modestly named after himself. Alexander died in 323 b.c. but his plan to develop the new center was continued by his successors in Egypt who adopted the royal title of Ptolemy.

相当确定的是，欧几里得约于公元前300年住在亚历山大里亚，并在那里培养学生，不过他本人很可能是在柏拉图学园接受教育的。顺便说，这些信息几乎就是我们对欧几里得个人生活所知的全部。欧几里得的著作，以系统、演绎而宏大的形式，汇述了许多古典时期希腊人各自的发现。他的主要著作《几何原本》，给出了空间与空间中图形的规律。

It is quite certain that Euclid lived in Alexandria about 300 b.c. and trained students there, though his own education was probably acquired in Plato’s Academy. This information, incidentally, is about all we have on Euclid’s personal life. Euclid’s work has the form of a systematic, deductive, and vast account of the separate discoveries of many classical Greeks. His chief work, the Elements, offers the laws of space and figures in space.

《几何原本》绝非欧几里得对空间几何贡献的全部。他在一部今已失传的著作中研究了圆锥曲线。阿波罗尼奥斯（公元前262—前190年）出生于小亚细亚的帕加马，在亚历山大里亚学习数学；他继续研究抛物线、椭圆与双曲线，写成了这一主题的经典著作《圆锥曲线论》。

Euclid’s Elements was by no means all of his contribution to the geometry of space. Euclid took up the theme of conic sections in a book no longer extant, and Apollonius (262-190 b.c.), a native of Pergamum in Asia Minor who learned mathematics in Alexandria, carried on this study of the parabola, ellipse, and hyperbola and wrote the classic work on the subject, the Conic Sections.

阿基米德（公元前287—前212年）在亚历山大里亚受教育，但住在西西里。他以《论球和圆柱》《论锥状体和球状体》以及《抛物线求积》等著作，补充了这些纯几何知识。所有这些著作都涉及用一种由欧多克索斯（公元前390—前337年）引入、后来称为穷竭法的方法，计算复杂的面积与体积。今天，这些问题用微积分方法解决。

To this purely geometrical knowledge Archimedes (287-212 b.c.), who was educated in Alexandria but lived in Sicily, added several works, On the Sphere and Cylinder, On Conoids and Spheroids, and The Quadrature of the Parabola, all of which deal with the calculation of complex areas and volumes by a method introduced by Eudoxus (390- 337 b.c.) and later known as the method of exhaustion. Nowadays these problems are solved by the methods of the calculus.

希腊人为空间与空间中图形的研究，还增添了一项重大成果——三角学。这项工作的开创者是喜帕恰斯，他曾住在罗得岛与亚历山大里亚，约于公元前125年去世。墨涅拉俄斯（约公元98年）扩展了这项工作；在亚历山大里亚工作的埃及人克劳狄乌斯·托勒密（卒于公元168年），又给出了完整而权威的版本。他的主要著作是《数学汇编》，更常用的名称是其阿拉伯语书名《至大论》（Almagest）。三角学研究三角形各边与各角之间的数量关系。希腊人主要关心球面上的三角形，其边由大圆的弧组成（大圆的圆心位于球心），因为主要应用是研究行星与恒星的运动；在希腊天文学中，它们沿大圆运动。不过，同一理论经过转换，很容易应用于平面三角形，这也是今天学校中学习三角学的形式。三角学的引入，要求使用者掌握相当高级的算术和一些代数。希腊人究竟如何在这些领域中运算，将在后面讨论（第V章）。

The Greeks made one more major addition to the study of space and figures in space—trigonometry. The originator of this work was Hipparchus, who lived in Rhodes and in Alexandria and died about 125 b.c. It was extended by Menelaus (c. a.d. 98) and given a complete and authoritative version by the Egyptian Claudius Ptolemy (d. a.d. 168), who worked in Alexandria. His major work was Mathematical Composition, known more popularly by the Arabic title, Almagest. Trigonometry concerns the quantitative relationships among the sides and angles of a triangle. The Greeks were concerned mainly with triangles on the surface of a sphere, the sides of which are formed by arcs of great circles (circles with centers at the center of the sphere) because the major application was to the motion of planets and stars, which in Greek astronomy moved along great circles. However, the same theory, when translated, readily applies to triangles in a plane, the form in which trigonometry is approached in our schools today. The introduction of trigonometry required of its users rather advanced arithmetic and some algebra. Just how the Greeks operated in these areas will be a later concern (Chapter V).

随着这些创造，数学从晦暗、经验性、互不相连的片段，发展成辉煌、庞大、系统而深刻的思想创造。然而，欧几里得、阿波罗尼奥斯和阿基米德关于空间及空间中图形性质的经典著作——托勒密的《至大论》是个例外——似乎范围有限，几乎不显示其内容更广泛的意义。这些著作似乎与揭示自然运行的真理没有多少关系。实际上，它们只呈现形式化、经过润饰的演绎数学。在这方面，希腊数学著作与现代数学教科书、论著并无不同。这类书只求组织并呈现已经获得的数学结果，因而略去了数学的动机、定理的线索与启示，以及数学知识的用途。因此，许多论述古典希腊数学的作者断言，该时期的数学家只为数学本身而关心数学；他们通过援引当时两部最伟大的成果汇编——欧几里得的《几何原本》与阿波罗尼奥斯的《圆锥曲线论》——得出并捍卫这一断言。然而，这些作者的眼界太窄了。只看《几何原本》和《圆锥曲线论》，就像只看牛顿关于二项式定理的论文，便断定牛顿是纯数学家。

With these several creations mathematics emerged from obscure, empirical, disconnected fragments to brilliant, huge, systematic, and deep intellectual creations. However, the classics of Euclid, Apollonius, and Archimedes—Ptolemy’s Almagest is an exception—that deal with the properties of space and of figures in space seem to be limited in scope and give little indication of the broader significance of their material. These works seem to have little relation to revealing truths about the workings of nature. In fact, these classics give only the formal, polished deductive mathematics. In this respect Greek mathematical texts are no different from modern mathematical textbooks and treatises. Such books seek only to organize and present the mathematical results that have been attained and so omit the motivations for the mathematics, the clues and suggestions for the theorems, and the uses to which the mathematical knowledge is put. Hence many writers on classical Greek mathematics assert that the mathematicians of the period were concerned only with mathematics for its own sake and they arrive at and defend this assertion by pointing to Euclid’s Elements and Apollonius’s Conic Sections, the two greatest compilations of work in that period. However, these writers have narrowed their focus. To look only at the Elements and the Conic Sections is like looking at Newton’s paper on the binomial theorem and concluding that Newton was a pure mathematician.

真正的目标是研究自然。就研究物理世界而言，甚至几何真理也具有重大意义。希腊人清楚，几何原理体现在整个宇宙的结构中，而空间是宇宙的首要组成部分。因此，研究空间及空间中的图形，是对自然研究的重要贡献。几何实际上是更广泛的宇宙论研究的一部分。例如，球面几何的研究，是在柏拉图时代天文学数学化时开展的。事实上，对毕达哥拉斯学派而言，希腊语中表示球体的词就意味着天文学。而欧几里得研究球面几何的《天象论》（Phaenomena），明确旨在用于天文学。根据这些证据，加上我们对近代数学发展过程更充分的了解，可以肯定，科学研究必定提出过数学问题，数学是自然研究不可分割的组成部分。不过，我们无需猜测。只需考察希腊人在自然研究中取得了什么成果，以及参与者是哪些人即可。

The real goal was the study of nature. Insofar as the study of the physical world was concerned, even the truths of geometry were highly significant. It was clear to the Greeks that geometric principles were embodied in the entire structure of the universe, of which space was the primary component. Hence the study of space and figures in space was an essential contribution to the investigation of nature. Geometry was in fact part of the larger study of cosmology. For example, the study of the geometry of the sphere was undertaken when astronomy became mathematical, which happened in Plato’s time. In fact, the Greek word for sphere meant astronomy for the Pythagoreans. And Euclids’s Pbaenomena, which was on the geometry of the sphere, was specifically intended for use in astronomy. With such evidence and with the fuller knowledge of how developments in mathematics took place in more recent times, we may be certain that the scientific investigations must have suggested mathematical problems and that the mathematics was part and parcel of the investigation of nature. But we need not speculate. We have only to examine what the Greeks accomplished in the study of nature and who were the men involved.

在物理科学本身的领域中，最大的成功是在天文学中取得的。柏拉图虽充分了解巴比伦人和埃及人所作的数量惊人的天文观察，却强调他们没有基础性或统一性理论，也没有解释行星看似不规则的运动。欧多克索斯曾在学园学习，他的纯粹几何工作被纳入欧几里得《几何原本》第V卷与第XII卷；他着手研究“挽救现象”的问题。他的答案，是历史上已知第一个相当完整的天文学理论。

The greatest success in the field of physical science proper was achieved in astronomy. Plato, though fully aware of the impressive number of astronomical observations made by the Babylonians and Egyptians, emphasized that they had no underlying or unifying theory and no explanation of the seemingly irregular motions of the planets. Eudoxus, who was a student at the Academy and whose purely geometrical work is incorporated in Books V and XII of Euclid’s Elements, took up the problem of “saving the appearances.” His answer is the first reasonably complete astronomical theory known to history.

图1.5

Figure 1.5

我们不详细介绍欧多克索斯的理论，只指出它彻底是数学性的，涉及彼此相互作用的球体的运动。除了恒星“球”之外，这些球并非物质实体，而是数学构造。他也没有试图说明使球体按其描述旋转的力。他的理论精神完全是现代的，因为今天科学的目标是数学描述，而非物理解释。这一理论后来被另一理论取代；后者归功于欧多克索斯之后三位最伟大的理论天文学家，即阿波罗尼奥斯、喜帕恰斯和托勒密，并被纳入托勒密的《至大论》。

We shall not describe Eudoxus’s theory except to state that it was thoroughly mathematical and involved the rpotions of interacting spheres. These spheres were, except for the “sphere” of fixed stars, not material bodies but mathematical constructions. Nor did he try to account for forces which would make the spheres rotate as he said they did. His theory is thoroughly modern in spirit, for today mathematical description and not physical explanation is the goal in science. This theory was superseded by the theory credited to the three greatest theoretical astronomers after Eudoxus, namely, Apollonius, Hipparchus, and Ptolemy and incorporated in Ptolemy’s Almagest.

阿波罗尼奥斯没有留下现存的天文学著作。然而，希腊作者引用过他的贡献，包括托勒密在《至大论》（第XII卷）中对他的引用。他作为天文学家如此著名，以至于得到绰号ε（epsilon），因为他对月球运动做了大量研究，而ε是月亮的符号。喜帕恰斯的著作只有一部次要作品为人所知，但《至大论》也引用他，并承认他的贡献。

Apollonius left no extant work in astronomy. However, his contributions are cited by Greek writers including Ptolemy in his Almagest (Book XII). He was so famous as an astronomer that he was nicknamed ε (epsilon) because he had done much work on the motion of the moon and ε was the symbol for the moon. Only one minor work of Hipparchus is known but he, too, is cited and credited in the Almagest.

如今所谓托勒密天文学的基本模式，在欧多克索斯与阿波罗尼奥斯之间的时期，就已进入希腊天文学。在这一模式中，行星P以恒定速度沿以S为圆心的圆运动（图1.5），而S本身以恒定速度沿以地球E为圆心的圆运动。S所沿的圆称为均轮，P所沿的圆称为本轮。在某些行星的情形中，点S是太阳；在另一些情形中，它只是一个数学点。P的运动方向可以与S的运动方向相同，也可以相反。太阳和月亮属于后一种情形。托勒密还使用这一模式的一种变体，描述某些行星的运动。通过恰当选择本轮与均轮的半径、天体在本轮上的速度，以及本轮中心在均轮上的速度，喜帕恰斯和托勒密得以对运动作出与当时观察相当吻合的描述。从喜帕恰斯时代起，月食就可以预测到误差一两个小时以内，虽然日食的预测精度稍低。这些预测之所以可能，是因为托勒密运用了三角学；他说自己是为天文学而创立三角学的。

The basic scheme of what is now referred to as Ptolemaic astronomy had entered Greek astronomy between the times of Eudoxus and Apollonius. In this scheme a planet P moves at a constant speed on a circle (Fig. 1.5) with center S while S itself moves with constant speed on a circle with center at the earth E. The circle on which S moves is called the deferent while the circle on which P moves is called an epicycle. The point S in the cases of some planets was the sun but in other cases it was just a mathematical point. The direction of the motion of P could agree with or be opposite to the direction of motion of S. The latter was the case for the sun and moon. Ptolemy also used a variation on this scheme to describe the motion of some of the planets. By properly selecting the radii of the epicycle and deferent, the speed of a body on its epicycle, and the speed of the center of the epicycle on the deferent, Hipparchus and Ptolemy were able to get descriptions of the motions which were quite in accord with the observations of their times. From the time of Hipparchus an eclipse of the moon could be predicted to within an hour or two, though eclipses of the sun were predicted somewhat less accurately. These predictions were possible because Ptolemy used trigonometry, which he said he created for astronomy.

从追求真理的角度看，值得注意的是，托勒密像欧多克索斯一样，充分认识到他的理论只是一种符合观察的便利数学描述，未必是自然的真实设计。对于某些行星，他有几种模式可供选择，而他选择了数学上较简单的一种。托勒密在《至大论》第XIII卷中说，天文学应当寻找尽可能简单的数学模型。但基督教世界把托勒密的数学模型当作真理接受了。

From the standpoint of the search for truths, it is noteworthy that Ptolemy, like Eudoxus, fully realized that his theory was just a convenient mathematical description which fit the observations and was not necessarily the true design of nature. For some planets he had a choice of alternative schemes and he chose the mathematically simpler one. Ptolemy says in Book XIII of his Almagest that in astronomy one ought to seek as simple a mathematical model as possible. But Ptolemy’s mathematical model was received as the truth by the Christian world.

托勒密理论首次为自然的统一性与不变性提供了相当完整的证据，也是希腊人对于柏拉图提出的、将天体视运动理性化这一问题的最终回答。在整个希腊时代，没有其他成果能在对宇宙观的深刻影响方面与《至大论》相比；除欧几里得的《几何原本》外，也没有其他成果取得如此不容置疑的权威。

Ptolemaic theory offered the first reasonably complete evidence of the uniformity and invariability of nature and is the final Greek answer to Plato’s problem of rationalizing the apparent motions of the heavenly bodies. No other product of the entire Greek era rivals the Almagest for its profound influence on conceptions of the universe and none, except Euclid’s Elements, achieved such unquestioned authority.

这份对希腊天文学的简述，当然没有涵盖这一学科的许多其他贡献，也没有揭示即便是已讨论人物的工作之深度与广度。希腊天文学精湛而全面，运用了大量数学。而且，几乎每一位希腊数学家都曾投身这一学科，包括欧几里得和阿基米德这些大师。

This brief account of Greek astronomy does not of course cover many other contributions to the subject nor does it reveal the depth and extent of the work even of the men treated. Greek astronomy was masterful and comprehensive and it employed a vast amount of mathematics. Moreover, almost every Greek mathematician devoted himself to the subject, including the masters Euclid and Archimedes.

物理真理的获取并未止于空间数学与天文学。希腊人创立了力学。力学研究可以视为质点的物体的运动、有广延的物体的运动，以及造成这些运动的力。亚里士多德在《物理学》中建立的运动理论，是希腊力学的最高成就。如同他的全部物理学，他的力学以理性的、貌似自明的原理为基础，完全符合观察。虽然这一理论统治了近两千年，但我们不作回顾，因为它已被牛顿力学取代。对亚里士多德运动理论的重要补充，是阿基米德关于物体重心的研究和他的杠杆理论。在所有这些工作中，与我们有关的一点是，数学发挥了主导作用，从而加强了人们的确信：数学是深入理解自然设计的根本。

The attainment of physical truths did not end with the mathematics of space and astronomy. The Greeks founded the science of mechanics. Mechanics deals with the motion of objects that may be considered as particles, the motion of extended bodies, and the forces that cause these motions.
