In his Physics Aristotle put together a theory of motion which is the high point of Greek mechanics. Like all of his physics, his mechanics is based on rational, seemingly self-evident principles, entirely in accord with observation. Though this theory held sway for almost two thousand years, we shall not review it because it was superseded by Newtonian mechanics. Notable additions to Aristotle’s theory of motion were Archimedes’ works on centers of gravity of bodies and his theory of the lever. What is relevant in all of this work is that mathematics played a leading role and thereby added to the conviction that mathematics was fundamental in penetrating the design of nature.

除天文学与力学外，光学是最持久地受到研究的学科。这门数学科学也由希腊人创立。从毕达哥拉斯学派开始，几乎所有希腊哲学家都思考过光、视觉与颜色的本性。不过，我们关注的是这些领域中的数学成果。第一项成果，是阿格里真托的恩培多克勒（约公元前490年）依据先验理由断言光以有限速度传播；阿格里真托位于西西里。我们现有最早的系统光学著作，是欧几里得的《光学》与《反射光学》*。《光学》讨论视觉问题，以及如何利用视觉确定物体的大小。《反射光学》（镜子的理论）说明光线从平面镜、凹面镜和凸面镜反射时如何运动，以及这种运动对我们所见之物的影响。它像《光学》一样，从实际是公设的定义出发。定理1（在现代著作中是一条公理）是几何光学的基础，称为反射定律。它指出，从点P入射的光线与镜面所成的角A（图1.6），等于反射光线与镜面所成的角B。欧几里得还证明了光线射到凸面镜或凹面镜上的相应定律（图1.7）。在接触点，他以切线R代替镜面。这两部著作不仅内容完全是数学性的，组织形式也是如此。如同《几何原本》，定义、公理与定理占据主导地位。

Next to astronomy and mechanics optics has been the subject most constantly pursued. This mathematical science, too, was founded by the Greeks. Almost all of the Greek philosophers, beginning with the Pythagoreans, speculated on the nature of light, vision, and color. Our concern, however, is with mathematical accomplishments in these areas. The first was the assertion on a priori grounds by Empedocles of Agrigentum (c. 490 B.c.)—Agrigentum was in Sicily—that light travels with finite velocity. The first systematic treatments of light that we have are Euclid’s Optics and Catoptrica* The Optics is concerned with the problem of vision and with the use of vision to determine sizes of objects. The Catoptrica (theory of mirrors) shows how light rays behave when reflected from plane, concave, and convex mirrors and the effect of this behavior on what we see. Like the Optics it starts with definitions which are really postulates. Theorem 1 (an axiom in modern texts) is fundamental in geometrical optics and is known as the law of reflection. It says that the angle A that a ray incident from point P makes with a mirror (Fig. 1.6) equals the angle B which the reflected ray makes with the mirror. Euclid also proves the law for a ray striking a convex or a concave mirror (Fig. 1.7). At the point of contact he substitutes the tangent R for the mirror. Both books are thoroughly mathematical not only in content but in organization. Definitions, axioms, and theorems dominate as in Euclid’s Elements.

我们今天所见的版本，很可能是包括欧几里得著作在内的几部作品的汇编。

The version we have today is probably a compilation of several works including Euclid’s.

数学家兼工程师希罗（公元一世纪）从反射定律得出了一个重要结论。如果图1.6中的P和Q是直线ST同侧的任意两点，那么在从点P到达该直线、再到点Q的所有可能路径中，最短路径经过这样一个点R：线段PR与QR同该直线所成的角相等。而这恰好就是光线所走的路径。因此，光线从P经过镜面到Q时，采取最短路径。显然，自然十分熟悉几何，并充分利用它。这个命题见于希罗的《反射光学》，该书还讨论凹面镜、凸面镜以及镜子的组合。

From the law of reflection, the mathematician and engineer Heron (first century a.d.) drew an important consequence. If P and Q in Figure 1.6 are any two points on one side of the line ST, then of all the paths one could follow in going from point P to the line and then to point Q, the shortest path is by way of the point R such that the two line segments PR and QR make equal angles with the line. And this is exactly the path a light ray takes. Hence, the light ray takes the shortest path in going from P to the mirror to Q. Apparently nature is well acquainted with geometry and employs it to full advantage. This proposition appears in Heron’s Catoptrica which also treats concave and convex mirrors and combinations of mirrors.

图1.8

Figure 1.8

关于各种形状镜面对光的反射，希腊人写过许多著作。其中包括今已失传的阿基米德《反射光学》与阿波罗尼奥斯《论燃烧镜》（约公元前190年），以及现存的狄奥克勒斯《论燃烧镜》（约公元前190年）。燃烧镜是凹面镜，形状为球面的一部分、旋转抛物面（由抛物线绕其轴旋转形成），或旋转椭球面。阿波罗尼奥斯知道，狄奥克勒斯的书中也证明了：抛物面镜能把从焦点发出的光反射为平行于镜轴的光束（图1.8）。反过来，平行于轴入射的光线，经反射后会集中于焦点。太阳光这样集中后，在焦点产生高温，因此称为燃烧镜。据说，阿基米德正是利用抛物面镜的这一性质，把太阳光集中到围攻其家乡叙拉古的罗马舰船上，使它们起火。阿波罗尼奥斯还知道其他圆锥曲线的反射性质，例如从椭球面镜的一个焦点发出的所有光线，都会反射到另一个焦点。他在《圆锥曲线论》第III卷中给出了椭圆与双曲线的相关几何性质。

Any number of works were written on the reflection of light by mirrors of various shapes. Among these are the now lost works, Archimedes Catoptrica and Apollonius’s On the Burning Mirror (c. 190 B.C.), and the extant work of Diodes, On Burning-Mirrors (c. 190 b.c.). Burning mirrors were concave mirrors in the form of portions of a sphere, paraboloids of revolution (formed by revolving a parabola about its axis), and ellipsoids of revolution. Apollonius knew and Diodes’ book contains the proof that a paraboloidal mirror will reflect light emanating from the focus into a beam parallel to the axis of the mirror (Fig. 1.8). Conversely, rays coming in parallel to the axis will after reflection be concentrated at the focus. The sun’s rays thus concentrated produce great heat at the focus and hence the term burning mirror. This is the property of the paraboloidal mirror which Archimedes is reported to have used to concentrate the sun’s rays on the Roman ships besieging his home city Syracuse and to set them afire. Apollonius also knew the reflection properties of the other conic sections, such as that all rays emanating from one focus of an ellipsoidal mirror will be reflected to the other focus. He gives the relevant geometrical properties of the ellipse and hyperbola in Book III of his Conic Sections.

希腊人还创立了许多其他科学，尤其是地理学与流体静力学。昔兰尼的埃拉托色尼（约公元前284—约前192年）是古代最博学的人物之一，担任亚历山大里亚图书馆馆长。他多次计算了希腊人所知地球区域中重要地点之间的距离。他还作出了如今著名而相当准确的地球周长计算，并撰写《地理学》；书中除描述数学方法外，还解释了地表已发生变化的原因。

The Greeks founded many other sciences, notably geography and hydrostatics. Eratosthenes of Cyrene (c. 284-c. 192 b.c.), one of the most learned men of antiquity and director of the library at Alexandria, made numerous calculations of distances between significant places on the portion of our earth known to the Greeks. He also made a now famous and quite accurate calculation of the circumference of the earth and wrote his Geography, in which beyond describing his mathematical methods he also gave his explanation of causes for the changes which had taken place on the earth’s surface.

最全面的地理学著作，是托勒密八卷本的《地理学》。托勒密不仅扩展了埃拉托色尼的工作，还用我们今天使用的同样的经纬度，确定了地球上八千个地点的位置。他还给出了地图绘制方法，其中某些至今仍在使用，尤其是球极投影法。在所有这些地理学工作中，从公元前四世纪起就被应用的球面图形几何，是基础。

The most extensive work on geography was Ptolemy’s Geography, in eight books. Ptolemy not only extended Eratosthenes’ work but located eight thousand places on the earth in terms of the very same latitude and longitude we now use. Ptolemy also gave methods of mapmaking, some of which are still used, particularly the method of stereographic projection. In all of this work in geography the geometry of figures on a sphere, applied from the fourth century b.c. onward, was basic.

至于研究置于水中物体所受压力的流体静力学，阿基米德的《论浮体》是奠基之作。如同我们介绍的所有著作，它在研究方法与结果推导上完全是数学性的。它尤其包含如今所谓阿基米德原理：浸入水中的物体受到向上的浮力，其大小等于排开水的重量。因此，对于人在各种力都倾向于使其下沉的世界中如何保持漂浮的解释，应归功于阿基米德。

As for hydrostatics, the subject which deals with the pressure on bodies which are placed in water, Archimedes’ book On Floating Bodies is the foundational work. Like all of the works we have been describing it is thoroughly mathematical in approach and derivation of results. In particular it contains what is now known as Archimedes’ principle, that a body immersed in water is buoyed up by a force equal to the weight of the water displaced. Thus we owe to Archimedes the explanation of how man can remain afloat in a world of forces that tend to submerge him.

虽然数学的演绎方法与自然规律的数学表述，主导了希腊的亚历山大里亚时期，但应当指出，亚历山大里亚人不同于古典时期的希腊人，也诉诸实验与观察。他们继承并利用了巴比伦人在两千年间作出的异常准确的天文观察。喜帕恰斯编制了当时可见恒星的星表。发明——尤其是阿基米德与数学家兼工程师希罗的发明——包括日晷、星盘以及蒸汽与水力的应用。

Though the deductive approach to mathematics and the mathematical representation of the laws of nature dominated the Alexandrian Greek period, we should note that the Alexandrians, unlike the classical Greeks, also resorted to experimentation and observation. The Alexandrians took over and utilized the remarkably accurate astronomical observations which the Babylonians had made over a period of two thousand years. Hipparchus made a catalogue of the stars observable in his time. Inventions (notably by Archimedes and the mathematician and engineer Heron) included sun-dials, astrolabes, and uses for steam and water power.

特别著名的是亚历山大里亚的缪斯院，它由亚历山大在埃及的直接继承者托勒密·索特创建。缪斯院是学者的居所，拥有一座著名图书馆，藏书约四十万卷。由于无法容纳所有手稿，另有三十万卷存放在塞拉皮斯神庙。学者们还向学生传授知识。

Particularly famous was the Alexandrian Museum, which was started by Ptolemy Soter, the immediate successor of Alexander in Egypt. The Museum was a home for scholars and included a famous library of about 400,000 volumes. Since it could not house all the manuscripts an additional 300,000 were housed in the Temple of Serapis. The scholars also gave instruction to students.

希腊人以数学工作与诸多科学研究，为宇宙按照数学设计提供了实质证据。数学内在于自然；它是关于自然结构的真理，或者如柏拉图所说，是关于物理世界的实在。宇宙存在规律与秩序，而数学是理解这种秩序的钥匙。此外，人类理性能够深入这一方案，揭示其数学结构。

With their mathematical work and many scientific investigations, the Greeks gave substantial evidence that the universe is mathematically designed. Mathematics is immanent in nature; it is the truth about nature’s structure, or, as Plato would have it, the reality about the physical world. There is law and order in the universe and mathematics is the key to this order. Moreover, human reason can penetrate the plan and reveal the mathematical structure.

以逻辑和数学方法研究自然这一观念的推动力，主要应归于欧几里得的《几何原本》。虽然这部著作旨在研究物理空间，但它的组织、巧思与清晰性，启发人们把公理—演绎方法不仅用于数论等其他数学领域，还用于全部科学。通过这部著作，以数学为基础，将一切物理知识加以逻辑组织的观念，进入了思想世界。

The impetus for the conception of a logical, mathematical approach to nature must be credited primarily to Euclid’s Elements. Though this work was intended to be a study of physical space, its organization, ingenuity, and clarity inspired the axiomatic-deductive approach not only to other areas of mathematics such as the theory of numbers but to all of the sciences. Through this work the notion of a logical organization of all physical knowledge based on mathematics entered the intellectual world.

因此，希腊人建立了数学与自然设计研究之间的联盟，这一联盟此后成为现代科学的根基。直到十九世纪后期，寻找数学设计就是寻找真理。数学规律是关于自然的真理这一信念，把最深刻、最高尚的思想家吸引到数学之中。

Thus the Greeks founded the alliance between mathematics and the study of nature’s design which has since become the very basis of modern science. Until the latter part of the nineteenth century, the search for mathematical design was the search for truth. The belief that mathematical laws were the truth about nature attracted the deepest and noblest thinkers to mathematics.

II 数学真理的繁盛

II. The Flowering of Mathematical Truths

一切对外部世界的研究，其主要目标应当是发现上帝赋予世界的理性秩序与和谐；他以数学的语言向我们揭示了这种秩序与和谐。

The chief aim of all investigations of the external world should he to discover the rational order and harmony which has been imposed on it hy God and which He revealed to us in the language of mathematics.

约翰内斯·开普勒

Johannes Kepler

宏伟的希腊文明被几种力量摧毁。第一种是罗马人逐渐征服希腊、埃及与近东。罗马扩张政治权力的目标，并不是传播其物质主义文化。被征服地区成为殖民地，罗马通过征收与税赋从中榨取巨额财富。

The majestic Greek civilization was destroyed by several forces. The first was the gradual conquest by the Romans of Greece, Egypt, and the Near East. The Roman objective in extending its political power was not to spread its materialistic culture. The subjugated areas became colonies from which great wealth was extracted by expropriation and by taxation.

基督教的兴起，是对异教希腊文化的另一打击。虽然基督教领袖采用了许多希腊与东方的神话和习俗，以使基督教更容易为皈依者接受，但他们反对异教学术，甚至嘲笑数学、天文学与物理科学。尽管遭受罗马人的残酷迫害，基督教仍不断传播，变得如此强大，以至于罗马皇帝君士坦丁大帝在公元313年的《米兰敕令》中，承认基督教为帝国的官方宗教。后来，狄奥多西（公元379—396年在位）禁止异教，并于392年下令摧毁异教神庙。

The rise of Christianity was another blow to pagan Greek culture. Though Christian leaders adopted many Greek and Oriental myths and customs with the intent of making Christianity more acceptable to converts, they opposed pagan learning and even ridiculed mathematics, astronomy, and physical science. Despite cruel persecution by the Romans, Christianity spread and became so powerful that the Roman emperor Constantine the Great in his Edict of Milan of a.d. 313 recognized Christianity as the official religion of the Empire. Later, Theodosius (ruled a.d. 379-396) proscribed the pagan religions and in 392 ordered that their temples be destroyed.

罗马人与基督徒焚毁了数千部希腊书籍。公元前47年，罗马人纵火焚烧亚历山大里亚港中的埃及舰船；火势蔓延，烧毁了图书馆——古代规模最大的图书馆。在狄奥多西禁止异教的那一年，基督徒摧毁了亚历山大里亚的塞拉皮斯神庙，那里收藏着仅存的大规模希腊著作。还有许多写在羊皮纸上的作品，被基督徒擦除，以便用这些羊皮纸写他们自己的著作。

Thousands of Greek books were burned by the Romans and the Christians. In 47 b.c., the Romans set fire to the Egyptian ships in the harbor of Alexandria; the fire spread and burned the library— the most extensive of ancient libraries. In the year that Theodosius banned the pagan religions, the Christians destroyed the temple of Serapis in Alexandria, which housed the only remaining sizable collection of Greek works. Many other works written on parchment were expunged by the Christians so that they could use the parchment for their own writings.

罗马帝国的晚期历史也与此相关。皇帝狄奥多西把庞大的帝国分给两个儿子：霍诺里乌斯统治意大利与西欧，阿卡狄乌斯统治希腊、埃及与近东。西部于公元五世纪被哥特人征服，其后的历史属于欧洲中世纪史。东部保持了独立。由于东罗马帝国，又称拜占庭帝国，包括希腊本土与埃及，希腊文化和希腊著作在一定程度上得以保存。

The late history of the Roman Empire is also relevant. The Emperor Theodosius divided the extensive empire between his two sons, Honorius, who was to rule Italy and Western Europe, and Arcadius, who was to rule Greece, Egypt, and the Near East. The western part was conquered by the Goths in the 5th century a.d. and its subsequent history belongs to the history of medieval Europe. The eastern part preserved its independence. Since the Eastern Roman Empire, known also as the Byzantine Empire, included Greece proper and Egypt, Greek culture and Greek works were to some extent preserved.

对希腊文明的最后一击，是迅速崛起的穆斯林于公元640年征服埃及。剩下的书籍被销毁，理由正如阿拉伯征服者欧麦尔所说：“这些书要么包含《古兰经》中已有的内容，那我们就不必读；要么包含与《古兰经》相反的内容，那我们就不许读。”于是，整整六个月，亚历山大里亚的浴场都靠焚烧羊皮纸卷来加热。

The final blow to the Greek civilization was the conquest of Egypt by the upsurging Moslems in a.d. 640. The remaining books were destroyed on the ground that, as Omar, the Arab conqueror, put it, “Either the books contain what is in the Koran, in which case we don’t have to read them, or they contain the opposite of what is in the Koran, in which case we must not read them.” And so for six months the baths of Alexandria were heated by burning rolls of parchment.

穆斯林占领埃及之后，大多数学者迁往已经成为东罗马帝国首都的君士坦丁堡。虽然在拜占庭不友好的基督教氛围中，沿着希腊思想路线开展的活动不可能繁荣，但这些学者及其著作迁入相对安全之地，扩大了八百年后传入欧洲的知识宝库。

After the capture of Egypt by the Mohammedans the majority of scholars migrated to Constantinople, which had become the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire. Though no activity along the lines of Greek thought could flourish in the unfriendly Christian atmosphere of Byzantium, this inflow of scholars and their works to comparative safety increased the treasury of knowledge that was to reach Europe 800 years later.

印度与阿拉伯为数学活动的延续作出了贡献，并引入了后来将发挥更大作用的一些思想*。从公元200年至约1200年，印度人受到希腊著作的一定影响，在算术与代数方面作出了一些原创贡献。阿拉伯帝国在鼎盛时期覆盖地中海沿岸所有地区，并深入近东，包含了由伊斯兰教联结的许多民族。阿拉伯人吸收了希腊与印度的贡献，也取得了自己的某些进展。这些进展继承亚历山大里亚希腊人的精神，把演绎推理与实验结合起来。阿拉伯人对代数、地理学、天文学和光学都有贡献。他们还建立学院与学校，以传播知识。值得称赞的是，虽然阿拉伯人坚定信奉自己的宗教，却没有让宗教教义限制其数学与科学研究。

India and Arabia contributed to the continuity of mathematical activity and introduced some ideas that were to play a larger role later.* During the years from a.d. 200 to about 1200 the Hindus, influenced somewhat by the Greek works, made some original contributions to arithmetic and algebra. The Arabs, whose empire at its height extended over all the lands bordering the Mediterranean and into the Near East and embraced many races united by Mohammedanism, absorbed the Greek and Hindu contributions and also made some advances of their own. These, in the spirit of the Alexandrian Greeks, commingled deductive reasoning and experimentation. The Arabs contributed to algebra, geography, astronomy, and optics. They also built colleges and schools for the transmission of knowledge. It is to the credit of the Arabs that though they were firm adherents of their own religion, they did not allow religious doctrines to restrict their mathematical and scientific investigations.

尽管印度人和阿拉伯人都能得益于希腊人建立的宏伟基础，也推进了希腊数学与科学，但他们并不像希腊人那样，执着于理解宇宙结构。阿拉伯人广泛翻译并评论希腊著作，甚至作出批判性评论，却没有为已知真理增添特别重大或庞大的成果。到公元1500年，他们的帝国已因西方基督徒的进攻与东方的内部纷争而瓦解。

Despite the fact that both the Hindus and the Arabs were able to profit from the magnificent foundations erected by the Greeks and though they furthered Greek mathematics and science, they were not possessed as were the Greeks to understand the structure of the universe. The Arabs translated and commented extensively and even critically on Greek works but nothing of great moment or magnitude was added to the truths already known. By a.d. 1500 their empire was destroyed by the Christians in the West and by internal strife in the East.

当阿拉伯人建立并扩展其文明时，另一种文明正在西欧形成。这个地区在约公元500年至1500年的中世纪达到了较高的文化水平。这种文化由天主教会主导；其教义无论多么深刻、可取，都不鼓励研究物理世界。基督教的上帝统治宇宙，人的职责是侍奉并取悦他，由此赢得救赎，使灵魂得以在来世享有欢乐与荣光。地上的生活条件无关紧要，艰难与痛苦不仅应当忍受，实际上还应当经历，作为对人信仰上帝的考验。可以理解，希腊时代因研究物理世界而产生的数学与科学兴趣，此时处于最低点。中世纪欧洲的思想家虔诚地追求真理，但他们从启示与《圣经》研究中寻找真理。因此，中世纪思想家没有为自然具有数学设计提供更多证据。不过，中世纪晚期哲学确实支持自然行为具有规律性与统一性的信念，尽管认为这仍受上帝意志支配。

While the Arabs were building and expanding their civilization, another civilization was being founded in Western Europe. A high level of culture in this region was attained in the medieval period, which extended from about a.d. 500 to 1500. This culture was dominated by the Catholic Church, and its teachings, however deep and meritorious, did not favor the study of the physical world. The Christian God ruled the universe and man s role was to serve and please Him and by so doing win salvation, whereupon the soul would live in an after-life of joy and splendor. The conditions of life on this earth were immaterial and hardship and suffering were not only to be tolerated but were in fact to be undergone as a test of man’s faith in God. Understandably, interest in mathematics and science which had been motivated in Greek times by the study of the physical world was at a nadir. The intellectuals of medieval Europe were devoted seekers of truths but these they sought in revelation and in the study of the Scriptures. Hence medieval thinkers did not adduce additional evidence for the mathematical design of nature. However, late medieval philosophy did support the belief in the regularity and uniformity of nature’s behavior, though this was thought to be subject to the will of God.

*我们将在第V章进一步讨论印度人与阿拉伯人的工作。

*We shall say more about the work of the Hindus and Arabs in Chapter V.

中世纪晚期的欧洲，受到许多革命性力量的震动与改变。在使中世纪文明转变为现代文明的诸多影响中，对我们当前主题最重要的，是获得并研究希腊著作。通过阿拉伯语译本，以及在拜占庭帝国完整保存的希腊著作，欧洲人认识了这些作品。事实上，1453年土耳其人征服这一帝国时，许多希腊学者带着书籍逃往西方。欧洲思想复兴的领袖正是从希腊著作中得知：自然是按照数学设计的，这种设计和谐、审美上令人愉悦，也是关于自然的内在真理。自然不仅理性而有序，而且依照不可违抗、不可改变的规律行动。欧洲科学家以古希腊后继者的身份，开始研究自然。

Late medieval Europe was shaken and altered by a number of revolutionary influences. Among the many which converted the medieval civilization into the modern, the most important for our present concern was the acquisition and study of Greek works. These became known through the Arabic translations and through Greek works which had been kept intact in the Byzantine Empire. In fact, when the Turks conquered this empire in 1453 many Greek scholars fled westward with their books. It was from Greek works that the leaders of the intellectual revitalization of Europe learned nature is mathematically designed and this design is harmonious, aesthetically pleasing, and the inner truth about nature. Nature not only is rational and orderly but acts in accordance with inexorable and immutable laws. European scientists began their study of nature as the children of ancient Greece.

希腊理想的复兴促使一些人研究自然，这是毋庸置疑的。但数学与科学复兴的速度和强度，还应归于许多其他因素。推翻一种文化并促成另一种文化发展的力量，既多样又复杂。许多学者研究过科学的兴起，大量历史研究致力于准确找出其原因。这里我们只列举这些因素，不作更多探讨。

That the revival of Greek ideals induced some to take up the study of nature is indubitable. But the speed and intensity of the revival of mathematics and science were due to many other factors. The forces which overthrew one culture and fostered the development of a new one are numerous and complicated. The rise of science has been studied by many scholars and much history has been devoted to pinpointing the causes. We shall not attempt here to do more than name them.

自由工匠阶层的兴起，以及随之而来对材料、技艺和技术的兴趣，产生了科学问题。由寻找原料与黄金推动的地理探险，带来了对陌生地域与习俗的认识，挑战了中世纪欧洲文化。新教革命否定某些天主教教义，从而引发争论，甚至导致对两种宗教的怀疑。清教徒强调劳动与知识对人类的实用价值；火药的引入产生了抛射体运动等新的军事问题；远离陆地、航行数千英里海域又提出了种种问题——这些都推动了自然研究。印刷术的发明，使原本教会能够控制的知识得以传播。虽然学者对其中某种或某几种力量影响自然研究的程度看法不一，但对于我们的目的，只需指出这些力量数量众多，以及一个普遍认可的事实：追求科学确已成为现代欧洲文明的主导特征。

The rise of a class of free artisans, and a consequent interest in materials, skills, and technology, generated scientific problems. Geographical explorations, motivated by the search for raw materials and gold, introduced knowledge of strange lands and customs which challenged medieval European culture. The Protestant revolution rejected some Catholic doctrines, thereby fostering controversy and even skepticism concerning both religions. The Puritan emphasis on work and utility of knowledge to mankind, the introduction of gunpowder, which raised new military problems such as the motion of projectiles, and the problems raised by the navigations over thousands of miles of sea out of sight of land all motivated the study of nature. The invention of printing permitted the spread of knowledge which the Church had been able to control. Though authorities differ on the degree to which one or more of these forces may have influenced the investigation of nature, it suffices for our purposes to note their multitude and the universally accepted fact that the pursuit of science did become the dominant feature of modern European civilization.

欧洲人总体上并未立即回应这些新力量与新影响。在通常称为人文主义的时期，更突出的特征是研究、吸收希腊著作，而不是积极追求希腊人的目标。但到约公元1500年，受到希腊目标熏陶的头脑——即把理性应用于自然研究，并寻找深层数学设计的目标——开始行动。然而，他们面临一个严重问题：希腊目标与当时主流文化相冲突。希腊人相信自然的数学设计，相信自然始终不变地遵循某种理想方案；中世纪晚期思想家却把一切计划与行动归于基督教的上帝。他是设计者与创造者，自然的一切行动都遵循他制定的方案。宇宙是上帝的造物，受其意志支配。文艺复兴以及此后几个世纪的数学家与科学家，都是正统基督徒，因而接受这一教义。但天主教教导绝不包括希腊人关于自然数学设计的学说。那么，理解上帝宇宙的努力，如何与寻找自然数学规律相调和？答案是增添一条新教义：基督教的上帝以数学方式设计了宇宙。因此，天主教认为努力理解上帝的意志与造物至为重要的教义，转化为寻找上帝对自然的数学设计。事实上，十六、十七世纪以及十八世纪大部分时期数学家的工作，是一种宗教探索；这一点我们很快会看得更清楚。寻找自然的数学规律，是一种虔敬行为，将揭示其造物的荣耀与宏伟。数学知识，即关于上帝宇宙设计的真理，与《圣经》的任何一行文字同样神圣不可侵犯。人不能指望像上帝自己那样清楚地理解神的计划，但可以谦卑、审慎地至少努力接近上帝的心意，从而理解上帝的世界。

The Europeans generally did not respond immediately to the new forces and influences. During the period often labelled humanistic the study and absorption of Greek works were far more characteristic than active pursuit of the Greek objectives. But by about a.d. 1500 minds infused with Greek goals—the application of reason to the study of nature and the search for the underlying mathematical design—began to act. However, they faced a serious problem. The Greek goals were in conflict with the prevailing culture. Whereas the Greeks believed in the mathematical design of nature, nature conforming invariably and unalterably to some ideal plan, late medieval thinkers ascribed all plan and action to the Christian God. He was the designer and creator, and all the actions of nature followed the plan laid down by this agency. The universe was the handiwork of God and subject to His will. The mathematicians and scientists of the Renaissance and several succeeding centuries were orthodox Christians and so accepted this doctrine. But Catholic teachings by no means included the Greek doctrine of the mathematical design of nature. How then was the attempt to understand God’s universe to be reconciled with the search for the mathematical laws of nature? The answer was to add a new doctrine, that the Christian God had designed the universe mathematically. Thus the Catholic doctrine postulating the supreme importance of seeking to understand God’s will and His creations took the form of a search for God’s mathematical design of nature. Indeed the work of sixteenth-, seventeenth-, and most eighteenth-century mathematicians was, as we shall soon see more clearly, a religious quest. The search for the mathematical laws of nature was an act of devotion which would reveal the glory and grandeur of His handiwork. Mathematical knowledge, the truth about God’s design of the universe, was as sacrosanct as any line of Scripture. Man could not hope to perceive the divine plan as clearly as God Himself understood it, but man could with humility and modesty seek at least to approach the mind of God and so understand God’s world.

还可以进一步断言：这些数学家确信自然现象背后存在数学规律，并坚持寻找，是因为他们先验地相信，上帝已把这些规律融入宇宙的构造。每发现一条自然规律，都被欢呼为上帝才智的证据，而非研究者才智的证据。数学家与科学家的信念和态度，体现了席卷文艺复兴欧洲的更广泛文化现象。新近重新发现的希腊著作，与一个深度虔诚的基督教世界相遇；出生于后者、却受前者吸引的思想领袖，融合了双方的学说。

One can go further and assert that these mathematicians were sure of the existence of mathematical laws underlying natural phenomena and persisted in the search for them because they were convinced a priori that God had incorporated them into the construction of the universe. Each discovery of a law of nature was hailed as evidence of God’s brilliance rather than the investigator’s. The beliefs and attitudes of the mathematicians and scientists exemplify the larger cultural phenomenon that swept Renaissance Europe. The recently rediscovered Greek works confronted a deeply devout Christian world, and the intellectual leaders born in one and attracted to the other fused the doctrines of both.

希腊人关于自然数学设计的学说，与文艺复兴时代相信上帝是这一设计作者的信念相结合，并在欧洲扎根；对此，最有力的证据或许来自尼古拉·哥白尼与约翰内斯·开普勒的工作。直到十六世纪，唯一健全而有用的天文学理论，是喜帕恰斯与托勒密的地心体系。专业天文学家接受这一理论，并把它用于历法计算与航海。哥白尼（1473—1543）开始研究新的天文学理论。他于1497年进入博洛尼亚大学，学习天文学。1512年，他开始履行东普鲁士弗劳恩堡主教座堂教士的职责。这份工作使他有充裕时间作天文观察，并思考相关理论。经过多年思考与观察，哥白尼形成了新的行星运动理论，将其写入经典著作《天体运行论》。他于1507年完成第一个版本，却担心会激怒教会，不敢出版。该书于1543年，即他去世的那一年问世。

Perhaps the most impressive evidence that the Greek doctrine of the mathematical design of nature coupled with the Renaissance belief in God’s authorship of that design had taken hold in Europe is furnished by the work of Nicolaus Copernicus and Johannes Kepler. Up to the sixteenth century, the only sound and useful astronomical theory was the geocentric system of Hipparchus and Ptolemy. This was the theory accepted by professional astronomers and applied to calendar-reckoning and navigation. Work on a new astronomical theory was begun by Copernicus (1473-1543). At the University of Bologna, which he entered in 1497, he studied astronomy. In 1512 he assumed his duties as canon of the Cathedral of Frauenberg in East Prussia. This work left Copernicus with plenty of time to make astronomical observations and to think about the relevant theory. After years of reflection and observation, Copernicus evolved a new theory of planetary motions which he mcor porated in a classic work, On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres. He had written his first version in 1507 but feared to publish it because it would antagonize the Church. The book appeared in 1543, the year in which he died.

当哥白尼开始思考天文学时，托勒密理论已经变得更复杂。为使理论符合主要由阿拉伯人积累的更多观察资料，人们在托勒密原有本轮之外，又增添了更多本轮。在哥白尼时代，这一理论总共需要七十七个圆，才能描述太阳、月亮与当时已知五颗行星的运动。对许多天文学家来说，正如哥白尼在序言中所说，这一理论复杂得令人难以容忍。

When Copernicus began to think about astronomy, the Ptolemaic theory had become somewhat more complicated. More epicycles had been added to those introduced by Ptolemy in order to make the theory fit the increased amount of observational data gathered largely by the Arabs. In Copernicus’s time the theory required a total of seventy-seven circles to describe the motion of the sun, moon, and the five planets known then. To many astronomers the theory, as Copernicus says in his Preface, was scandalously complex.

哥白尼研究过希腊著作，确信宇宙是按照数学与和谐原则设计的。和谐要求一个比复杂扩展后的托勒密理论更悦人的理论。他读到某些希腊作者，尤其是阿里斯塔克（公元前三世纪），曾提出一种可能性：太阳静止，地球绕太阳运行，同时绕自身轴旋转。他决定探索这一可能性。

Copernicus had studied the Greek works and had become convinced that the universe was mathematically and harmoniously designed. Harmony demanded a more pleasing theory than the complicated extension of Ptolemaic theory. He had read that some Greek authors, notably Aristarchus (third century b.c.), had suggested the possibility that the sun was stationary and that the earth revolved about the sun and rotated on its axis at the same time. He decided to explore this possibility.

他的推理最终使他运用托勒密的均轮与本轮模式（第I章）描述天体运动，却作出一个极其重要的改变：太阳位于每个均轮的中心。地球本身成为沿本轮运动、同时自转的行星。由此，他取得了相当大的简化。他把圆（均轮与本轮）的总数，从地心理论所需的七十七个减少到三十四个。

The upshot of his reasoning was that he used the Ptolemaic scheme of deferent and epicycle (Chapter I) to describe the motions of the heavenly bodies, with, however, the all-important difference that the sun was at the center of each deferent. The earth itself became a planet moving on an epicycle while rotating on its axis. Thereby he achieved considerable simplification. He was able to reduce the total number of circles (deferents and epicycles) to thirty-four instead of the seventy-seven required in the geocentric theory.

更显著的简化由约翰内斯·开普勒（1571—1630）完成，他是科学史上最引人入胜的人物之一。在因宗教与政治事件而充满个人不幸与艰辛的一生中，开普勒有幸于1600年成为著名天文学家第谷·布拉赫的助手。布拉赫当时正在进行广泛的新观察，这是希腊时代以来首次重大的观察工作。这些观察以及开普勒自己进行的其他观察，对他无比宝贵。布拉赫于1601年去世后，开普勒继任为奥地利皇帝鲁道夫二世的宫廷数学家。

The more remarkable simplification was achieved by Johannes Kepler (1571-1630), one of the most intriguing figures in the history of science. In a life beset by many personal misfortunes and hardships occasioned by religious and political events, Kepler had the good fortune in 1600 to become an assistant to the famous astronomer Tycho Brahe. Brahe was then engaged in making extensive new observations, the first major undertaking since Greek times. These observations and others which Kepler made himself were invaluable to him. When Brahe died in 1601 Kepler succeeded him as Imperial Mathematician to Emperor Rudolph II of Austria.

开普勒的科学推理令人着迷。和哥白尼一样，他是一位神秘主义者，也相信世界由上帝按照某种简单、美丽的数学方案设计。他在《宇宙的奥秘》（1596）中说，创造者心中的数学和谐，提供了“天体的数目、大小与运动为何如此而非彼”的原因。这一信念支配了他的一切思想。但开普勒也具备我们今天认为属于科学家的品质。他能够冷静地运用理性。虽然丰富的想象力激发他构想新的理论体系，但他知道理论必须符合观察；晚年他更清楚地看到，经验资料确实可能提示科学的基本原理。因此，一旦发现数学假说与观察数据不符，即使最心爱的假说，他也会舍弃。恰恰是这种不可思议的坚持——拒绝容忍当时任何其他科学家都会忽略的差异——引导他接受了激进的科学观念。他还具有使伟人能够完成非凡劳动的谦逊、耐心与精力。

Kepler s scientific reasoning is fascinating. Like Copernicus he was a mystic, and like Copernicus he believed that the world was designed by God in accordance with some simple and beautiful mathematical plan. He said in his Mystery of the Cosmos (1596), the mathematical harmonies in the mind of the Creator furnish the cause “why the number, the size, and the motion of the orbs are as they are and not otherwise.” This belief dominated all his thinking. But Kepler also had qualities which we now associate with scientists. He could be coldly rational. Though his fertile imagination triggered the conception of new theoretical systems, he knew that theories must fit observations and, in his later years, saw even more clearly that empirical data may indeed suggest fundamental principles of science. He therefore sacrificed even his most beloved mathematical hypotheses when he saw that they did not fit observational data, and it was precisely this incredible persistence in refusing to tolerate discrepancies any other scientist of his day would have disregarded that led him to espouse radical scientific ideas. He also had the humility, patience, and energy that enable great men to perform extraordinary labor.

开普勒的信念保证了自然数学规律的存在；他对这些规律的追寻，却使他多年沿着错误的道路探索。在《宇宙的奥秘》序言中，他说：“我要证明，上帝创造宇宙、规定宇宙秩序时，心中考虑的是自毕达哥拉斯与柏拉图时代就已知的五种几何正多面体；他依照这些尺度，确定了天体的数目、比例及其运动关系。”然而，他试图以五种正多面体为基础建立理论，所得推论却不符合观察。他作出了非凡努力，试图以修正后的形式运用这一方法，之后才将其放弃。

Kepler’s search for the mathematical laws of nature, which his beliefs assured him existed, led him to spend years in following up false trails. In the Preface to his Mystery of the Cosmos, we find him saying: “I undertake to prove that God, in creating the universe and regulating the order of the cosmos, had in view the five regular bodies of geometry as known since the days of Pythagoras and Plato, and that he has fixed according to those dimensions the number of heavens, their proportions, and the relations of their movements.” However, the deductions from his attempt to build a theory based on the five regular polyhedra were not in accord with observations, and he abandoned this approach only after he had made extraordinary efforts to apply it in modified form.

但在后来寻找和谐数学关系的努力中，他取得了卓越成功。他最著名、最重要的结果，今天称为开普勒行星运动三定律。前两条发表于1609年的一部著作，其书名很长，通常用开头部分《新天文学》或末尾部分《火星运动评论》来称呼。第一定律尤其非凡，因为开普勒打破了两千年来必须用圆或球描述天体运动的传统。托勒密和哥白尼都用均轮与几个本轮描述任一行星的运动；开普勒不再诉诸这种方法，而是发现一个椭圆就足够。他的第一定律指出，每颗行星沿椭圆运行，太阳位于这些椭圆轨道各自的一个共同焦点上（图2.1）。每个椭圆的另一个焦点，只是没有任何物体存在的数学点。这个定律对于容易地理解行星轨道，具有巨大价值。当然，开普勒像哥白尼一样补充说，地球沿其椭圆轨道运行时，也绕自身轴旋转。

But he was eminently successful in later efforts to find harmonious mathematical relations. His most famous and important results are known today as Kepler’s three laws of planetary motion. The first two were published in a book of 1609 bearing a long title and often referred to by the first part, The New Astronomy, or by the last part, Commentaries on the Motion of the Planet Mars. The first of these laws is especially remarkable, for Kepler broke with the tradition of two thousand years that circles or spheres must be used to describe heavenly motions. Instead of resorting to deferent and several epicycles, which both Ptolemy and Copernicus had used to describe the motion of any one planet, Kepler found that a single ellipse would do. His first law states that each planet moves on an ellipse and that the sun is at one (common) focus of each of these elliptical paths (Fig. 2.1). The other focus of each ellipse is merely a mathematical point at which nothing exists. This law is of immense value in comprehending readily the paths of the planets. Of course Kepler, like Copernicus, added that the earth also rotates on its axis as it travels along its elliptical path.

图2.1 每颗行星沿椭圆绕太阳运行。

Figure 2.1. Each planet moves in an ellipse about the sun.

但天文学要有实用价值，就必须走得更远。它必须告诉我们如何预测行星的位置。如果观察发现某颗行星处于一个特定位置，例如图2.1中的P点，人可能想知道它何时会处于某个其他位置，比如至点或分点。所需要的，是行星沿各自轨道运行的速度。

But astronomy had to go much further if it was to be useful. It must tell us how to predict the positions of the planets. If one finds by observation that a planet is at a particular position, P, say, in Figure 2.1, he might like to know when it will be at some other position such as a solstice or an equinox, for example. What is needed is the velocity with which the planets move along their respective paths.

在这里，开普勒也迈出了激进的一步。哥白尼与希腊人一直使用恒定速率。行星沿其本轮运动，在相等时间内经过相等的弧；每个本轮的中心，也以恒定速率沿另一个本轮或均轮运动。但开普勒的观察告诉他，行星沿椭圆运动时，速率并不恒定。经过艰难、漫长的探索，他成功找到了正确的速度规律。他发现：如果行星在例如一个月内从P运动到Q（图2.2），那么只要面积PSQ等于面积P′SQ′，它从P′运动到Q′也需要一个月。由于P比P′更接近太阳，若面积PSQ与P′SQ′相等，弧PQ就必定长于弧P′Q′。因此，行星并非以恒定速率运动。事实上，它们越接近太阳，运动越快。

Here, too, Kepler made a radical step. Copernicus and the Greeks had always used constant velocities. A planet moved along its epicycle so as to cover equal arcs in equal times, and the center of each epicycle also moved at a constant velocity on another epicycle or on a deferent. But Kepler s observations told him that a planet moving on its ellipse does not move at a constant speed. A hard and long search for the correct law of velocity ended successfully. What he discovered was that if a planet moves from P to Q (Fig. 2.2) in, say, one month, then it will also move from P' to Q' in one month, provided that the area PSQ equals the area P'SQ'. Since P is nearer the sun than P' is, the arc PQ must be larger than the arc P'Q' if the areas PSQ and P'SQ' are equal. Hence the planets do not move at a constant velocity. In fact, they move faster when closer to the sun.

发现第二定律，使开普勒欣喜若狂。虽然它不像恒定速率定律那样容易应用，但仍然证实了他的根本信念：上帝运用数学原理设计宇宙。上帝选择了稍微更精巧的方式，但无论如何，显然有一条数学规律决定行星运动的快慢。

Kepler was overjoyed to discover this second law. Although it is not so simple to apply as a law of constant velocity, it nonetheless confirmed his fundamental belief that God had used mathematical principles to design the universe. God had chosen to be just a little more subtle, but, nevertheless, a mathematical law clearly determined how fast the planets moved.

还有一个重大问题没有解决：什么规律描述行星到太阳的距离？现在，行星到太阳的距离并不恒定这一事实，使问题变得复杂。因此，开普勒寻找一个能把这一事实考虑进去的新原理。他相信自然不仅按照数学设计，而且按照和谐原则设计；他对“和谐”这个词的理解十分字面化。他相信存在一种天体音乐，会产生和谐的音调效果；这不是实际的声音，而是通过把有关行星运动的事实转换为音符，可以辨识的东西。他沿这条线索探索，通过数学论证与音乐论证的惊人结合，得到一条规律：若T为任一行星的公转周期，D为它到太阳的平均距离，则T2 = kD3，其中k是对所有行星都相同的常数。这就是开普勒行星运动第三定律，也是他在《世界的和谐》（1619）中得意地宣布的定律。

Another major problem remained. What law described the distances of the planets from the sun? The problem was now complicated by the fact that a planet’s distance from the sun was not constant. Hence Kepler searched for a new principle which would take this fact into account. He believed that nature was not only mathematically but harmoniously designed and he took this word “harmony” very literally. Thus he believed that there was a music of the spheres, which produced a harmonious tonal effect, not in actual sound but discernible by some translation of the facts about planetary motions into musical notes. He followed this lead and after an amazing combination of mathematical and musical arguments arrived at the law that, if T is the period of-revolution of any planet and D is its mean distance from the sun, then T2 = kD3, where k is a constant which is the same for all the planets. This is Kepler’s third law of planetary motion and the one he triumphantly announced in his book The Harmony of the World (1619).

陈述第三定律之后，开普勒情不自禁地唱起了对上帝的颂歌：“太阳、月亮与行星，以你们不可言说的语言荣耀他吧！天上的和谐，以及一切理解他奇妙造物者，赞美他吧。我的灵魂啊，赞美你的创造者！一切都由他而存在，并在他之中存在。我们最熟知的东西，既包含于他之中，也包含于我们徒劳的科学之中。”

After stating his third law Kepler broke forth into a paean to God: “Sun, moon, and planets glorify Him in your ineffable language! Celestial harmonies, all ye who comprehend His marvelous works, praise Him. And thou, my soul, praise thy Creator! It is by Him and in Him that all exists. That which we know best is comprised in Him, as well as in our vain science.”

哥白尼与开普勒确信上帝必定以和谐、简单的方式设计世界；他们必须应对的反对意见，足以显示这一确信有多么强烈。即使托勒密理论也认为其他行星在运动；希腊学说以这些行星由特殊的轻物质组成，因而容易运动来解释这一点。但沉重的地球如何能运动起来？哥白尼和开普勒都不能回答。反对地球自转的一种论证认为，地表物体会飞入空间，正如旋转平台上的物体会飞出去。两人都无法反驳。对于旋转的地球本身会四分五裂这一进一步反对，哥白尼无力地回答，地球运动是自然的，不会毁坏地球。随后他反问：地心理论要求天空每天极其迅速地运动，为什么天空不会散架？另一个反对意见是：如果地球由西向东自转，那么抛入空中的物体会落在原位置以西，因为物体在空中时，地球已移动。此外，如果地球绕太阳公转，那么由于物体速度与其重量成正比——至少希腊与文艺复兴物理学如此主张——地球上较轻的物体应该被抛在后面。甚至空气也应当被抛在后面。对最后这个论点，哥白尼回答，空气具有土性，所以会与地球协调运动。这些反对意见的实质在于，自转并公转的地球，与亚里士多德提出、哥白尼和开普勒时代普遍接受的运动理论不相容。

The strength of Copernicus’s and Kepler’s conviction that God must have designed the world harmoniously and simply can be judged by the objections with which they had to contend. That the other planets were in motion even according to Ptolemaic theory was explained by the Greek doctrine that these were made of special, light matter and therefore easily moved, but how could the heavy earth be put into motion? Neither Copernicus nor Kepler could answer this question. An argument against the earth’s rotation maintained that objects on the surface would fly off into space just as an object on a rotating platform will fly off. Neither man could rebut this argument. To the further objection that a rotating earth would itself fly apart, Copernicus replied weakly that the earth’s motion was natural and could not destroy the planet. Then he countered by asking why the sky did not fall apart under the very rapid daily motion which the geocentric theory called for. Yet another objection was that, if the earth rotated from west to east, an object thrown up into the air would fall back to the west of its original position, because the earth moved while the object was in the air. If, moreover, the earth revolved about the sun, then, since the velocity of an object is proportional to its weight, or so at least Greek and Renaissance physics maintained, lighter objects on the earth should be left behind. Even the air should be left behind. To the last argument Copernicus replied that air is earthy and so moves in sympathy with the earth. The substance of these objections is that a rotating and revolving earth did not fit in with the theory of motion due to Aristotle and commonly accepted in Copernicus’s and Kepler’s time.

另一类反对日心理论的科学论证，来自天文学本身。最严重的一个源于日心理论把恒星视为固定的。然而，六个月中，地球在空间中的位置约改变一亿八千六百万英里。因此，如果某时记录一颗恒星的方向，六个月后再记录，就应该观察到方向的差异。但哥白尼或开普勒时代没有观察到这种差异。哥白尼认为，恒星距离太远，所以方向差异小得无法观察。他的解释没有说服批评者；他们反驳说，如果恒星如此遥远，就不应能清楚地看到。在这一点上，哥白尼的答案是正确的。最近恒星在六个月间的方向变化为0.31″；数学家弗里德里希·威廉·贝塞尔于1838年首次测出了这一变化，当时他已经拥有一架优良的望远镜。

Another class of scientific arguments against a heliocentric theory came from astronomy proper. The most serious one stemmed from the fact that the heliocentric theory regarded the stars as fixed. However, in six months the earth changes its position in space by about 186 million miles. Hence if one notes the direction of a particular star at one time and again six months later, he should observe a difference in direction. But this difference was not observed in Copernicus’s or Kepler’s time. Copernicus argued that the stars are so far away that the difference in direction was too small to be observed. His explanation did not satisfy his critics, who countered that, if the stars were that distant, then they should not be clearly observable. In this instance, Copernicus’s answer was correct. The change in direction over a six-month period for the nearest star is an angle of 0.31"; and this was first detected in 1838 by the mathematician Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel, who by that time had a good telescope at his disposal.

传统派还问：如果地球以约每秒18英里的速度绕太阳运动，又在赤道处以约每秒0.3英里的速度自转，为什么我们感觉不到任何运动？事实上，我们的感官告诉我们，太阳正在天空中移动。对开普勒时代的人来说，我们感觉不到自己以新天文学所要求的极高速度运动，这一论据无可反驳。所有这些反对地球运动的科学理由，都很有分量，不能简单斥为拒绝看见真理的顽固派的执拗。

The traditionalists asked further, why do we not feel any motion if the earth is moving around the sun at about 18 miles per second and is rotating at the equator at about 0.3 miles per second? Our senses, in fact, tell us that the sun is moving in the sky. To people of Kepler’s time, the argument that we do not feel ourselves moving at the very high speeds called for by the new astronomy was incontrovertible. All of these scientific objections to a moving earth were weighty and could not be dismissed as the stubbornness of die-hards who refused to see the truth.

哥白尼与开普勒都深信宗教，却都否定了当时基督教的一项主流教义。这项教义肯定，人位于宇宙中心，是上帝最主要的关切。相反，日心理论把太阳放在宇宙中心，破坏了教会这一令人宽慰的教条。它使人显得只是可能众多的漂泊者之一，在冰冷天空中游荡。人似乎不大可能生来就为光荣地生活，并在死后进入天堂。人是上帝照料对象的可能性，也似乎变小了。哥白尼指出，宇宙如此巨大，谈论中心毫无意义，从而抨击地球位于宇宙中心的教义。但这一反驳对同时代人几乎没有说服力。

Copernicus and Kepler were deeply religious and yet both denied one of the prevailing doctrines of Christianity. This doctrine affirmed that man was at the center of the universe; he was the chief concern of God. The heliocentric theory, in contrast, by putting the sun at the center of the universe, undermined this comforting dogma of the Church. It caused man to appear to be one of a possible host of wanderers drifting through a cold sky. It seemed less likely that he was born to live gloriously and to attain paradise upon his death. Less likely, too, was it that he was the object of God’s ministrations. Copernicus attacked the doctrine that the earth is at the center of the universe by pointing out that the size of the universe is so immense that to speak of a center is meaningless. But this counter-argument carried little weight with his contemporaries.

面对所有这些反对日心理论的意见，哥白尼与开普勒只有一个压倒性的回答：他们各自实现了数学上的简化，得到了更和谐、在审美上更优越的理论。如果能给出更好的数学描述，那么鉴于上帝设计了世界、而且显然会采用更优越理论的信念，日心理论必定正确。

Against all these objections to a heliocentric theory, Copernicus and Kepler had but one overwhelming retort. Each had achieved mathematical simplification and a more harmonious and aesthetically superior theory. If a better mathematical account could be given, then, in view of the belief that God had designed the world and would clearly have used the superior theory, the heliocentric theory must be correct.

哥白尼的《天体运行论》与开普勒的众多著作中，有许多段落明确证明，他们确信自己找到了正确理论。例如，开普勒谈到自己的椭圆运动理论时说：“我在灵魂最深处见证了它的真实，并以难以置信、令人陶醉的喜悦凝视它的美。”他1619年著作《世界的和谐》的标题本身，以及他无尽地颂扬上帝、表达对上帝宏伟数学设计的满足，都展现了这一确信。

There are many passages in Copernicus’s On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres and in Kepler’s numerous writings which bear unmistakable testimony to their conviction that they had found the right theory. Kepler, for example, remarked of his elliptical theory of motion, “I have attested it as true in my deepest soul and I contemplate its beauty with incredible and ravishing delight.” The very title of Kepler’s work of 1619, The Harmony of the World, and endless paeans to God, expressing satisfaction with the grandeur of God’s mathematical design, exhibit his conviction.

最初只有数学家支持新理论。这并不奇怪。只有确信宇宙按照数学、以简单方式设计的数学家，才具有足够的精神勇气，忽视当时主流的哲学、宗教与科学反驳，并欣赏这种革命性天文学的数学。只有对数学在宇宙设计中的重要性怀有不可动摇信念的人，才敢于面对大量强大反对，肯定新理论。

At first only mathematicians supported the new theory. This is not surprising. Only a mathematician convinced that the universe was mathematically and simply designed would have had the mental fortitude to disregard the prevailing philosophical, religious, and scientific counterarguments and to appreciate the mathematics of such a revolutionary astronomy. One possessed of unshakable convictions about the importance of mathematics in the design of the universe would have dared to affirm the new theory against the mass of powerful opposition it met.

新理论的支持，来自一项意想不到的发展。十七世纪初，望远镜被发明出来；伽利略听说后，自己制作了一架。随后，他开始观察天空，令同时代人震惊。他发现了木星的四颗卫星（如今我们能观察到十二颗），这一发现表明，运动的行星也可以拥有卫星。他看到月球表面不规则且有山脉，太阳上有黑子，土星赤道周围有凸起（我们如今称为土星环）。这进一步证明，行星与地球类似，绝非希腊和中世纪思想家所认为的、由特殊以太物质构成的完美天体。此前看来只是一条宽阔光带的银河，通过望远镜可以看出由数千颗恒星组成。因此，天空中悬浮着其他太阳，很可能还有其他行星系统。哥白尼曾预测，如果人类视力能得到增强，就能观察到金星与水星的盈亏，如同肉眼可以辨认月亮盈亏。伽利略确实用望远镜看到了金星盈亏。他的观察使他确信哥白尼体系正确，并在经典著作《关于两大世界体系的对话》（1632）中强力捍卫它。新理论获得接受，还因为天文学家、地理学家与航海者用它计算更简单。到十七世纪中叶，科学界愿意在日心体系的基础上前进，数学规律是真理的主张得到了无可估量的加强。

Support for the new theory came from an unexpected development. Early in the seventeenth century the telescope was invented and Galileo, upon hearing of this invention, built one himself. He then proceeded to make observations of the heavens which startled his contemporaries. He detected four moons of Jupiter (we can now observe twelve) and this discovery showed that a moving planet can have satellites. Galileo saw irregular surfaces and mountains on the moon, spots on the sun, and a bulge around the equator of Saturn (which we now call the rings of Saturn). Here was further evidence that the planets were like the earth and certainly not perfect bodies composed of some special ethereal substance, as Greek and medieval thinkers had believed. The Milky Way, which had hitherto appeared to be just a broad band of light, could be seen with the telescope to be composed of thousands of stars. Thus there were other suns and presumably other planetary systems suspended in the heavens. Copernicus had predicted that if human sight could be enhanced, then man would be able to observe phases of Venus and Mercury, just as the naked eye can discern phases of the moon. With his telescope Galileo did view the phases of Venus. His observations convinced him that the Copernican system was correct and in the classic Dialogue on the Great World Systems (1632) he defended it strongly. The new theory won acceptance also because it was simpler for calculations made by astronomers, geographers, and navigators. By the middle of the seventeenth century the scientific world was willing to proceed on a heliocentric basis and the claim of mathematical laws to truth was immeasurably strengthened.

在十七世纪初的思想氛围中，坚持地球绕太阳公转以及每天自转的学说，绝非随意之举。伽利略在宗教裁判所受审，是众所周知的。虔诚的天主教徒帕斯卡发现，自己的著作被列入《禁书目录》，因为他竟敢在《致外省人信札》中挑战耶稣会士，宣称：“你们取得罗马针对伽利略的裁决，谴责他关于地球运动的意见，也是徒劳的，因为这不能证明地球静止不动。……”

To maintain the doctrines of the revolution of the earth around the sun and the daily rotation of the earth in the intellectual atmosphere of the early seventeenth century was by no means a casual matter. Galileo’s trial before the Inquisition is well known. The devout Catholic Pascal found his works on the Index of Prohibited Books because he had the temerity to defy the Jesuits by declaring in his Provincial Letters: “It was also in vain that you did obtain the decree of Rome against Galileo which condemned his opinion touching the motion of the earth, for that will not prove that the earth is standing still. . . .”

哥白尼与开普勒毫不怀疑地接受了希腊关于自然按照数学设计的学说与天主教关于上帝创造并设计宇宙的教义的融合。勒内·笛卡尔（1596—1650）则着手系统、清晰而有力地建立新的科学哲学。笛卡尔首先是哲学家，其次是宇宙论者，第三是物理学家，第四是生物学家，第五才是数学家；尽管如此，他仍被视为数学王冠上的宝石之一。他的哲学十分重要，因为它主导了十七世纪思想，并影响了牛顿和莱布尼茨这样的巨人。他的首要目标，是找到在一切领域中确立真理的方法；他在基本著作《正确运用理性并在科学中寻求真理的方法论》（1637）中追求这一目标。

Copernicus and Kepler accepted unquestioningly the fusion of the Greek doctrine that nature is designed mathematically and the Catholic doctrine that God created and designed the universe. Rene Descartes (1596-1650) set about erecting the new philosophy of science systematically, clearly, and forcefully. Descartes was primarily a philosopher, second a cosmologist, third a physicist, fourth a biologist, and only fifth a mathematician, though he is regarded as one of the gems in the diadem of mathematics. His philosophy is important because it dominated seventeenth-century thought and influenced such giants as Newton and Leibniz. His primary goal, to find the method of establishing truths in all fields, he pursued in his basic work, Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting the Reason and Seeking for Truth in the Sciences (1637).

笛卡尔开始构建哲学时，只接受那些在他看来无可怀疑的事实。那么，他如何区分可接受与不可接受的证据？在《指导心智的规则》（写于1628年，死后出版）中，他说：“对于我们打算研究的对象，应当探究的不是别人想过什么，也不是我们自己猜测什么，而是我们能够清楚、明白地直观把握什么，或能确定地推导出什么，因为除此之外，没有获得知识的途径。”心智对基本、清楚且分明的真理的直接把握——一种直觉能力——以及对其结果的演绎，构成他知识哲学的核心。因此，按照笛卡尔的看法，只有两种心智活动能使我们获得知识而毫无犯错之忧：直觉与演绎。不过，在《规则》中，他更相信直觉：“直觉是纯粹而专注的心智所形成的无疑认识，仅从理性之光产生，比演绎更为确定。”

Descartes began the construction of his philosophy by accepting only those facts that were to him beyond doubt. How then did he differentiate between acceptable and unacceptable evidence? In his Rules for the Direction of the Mind (written in 1628 but published posthumously), he stated: “Concerning the objects we propose to study, we should investigate not what others have thought nor what we ourselves conjecture, but what we can intuit clearly and evidently or deduce with certainty, for there is no other way to acquire knowledge.” The mind’s immediate apprehension of basic, clear, and distinct truths—an intuitive power— and the deduction of consequences are the essence of his philosophy of knowledge. There are thus, according to Descartes, only two mental acts that enable us to arrive at knowledge without any fear of error: intuition and deduction. However, in the Rules he gave greater credence to intuition: “Intuition is the undoubting conception of a pure and attentive mind, which arises from the light of reason alone, and is more certain than deduction.”

在《方法论》中，他捍卫了心智的存在及其拥有的确定、无可怀疑的知识。依靠基本直觉，他急于证明上帝存在。随后，他用一个显然涉及循环推理的论证，重新使自己确信，我们的直觉和演绎方法必定健全，因为上帝不会欺骗我们。他说，上帝是“一种无限、永恒、不变、独立、全知、全能的实体，我自己以及其他一切……都由他创造”。

In the Discourse, he defended the existence of mind and the sure and indubitable knowledge it possesses. By relying upon fundamental intuitions Descartes in the Discourse hastened to prove that God exists. And then with an argument that surely involves circular reasoning he reassured himself that our intuitions and methods of deduction must be sound because God would not deceive us. God he stated is “a substance that is infinite, eternal, immutable, independent, all-knowing, all-powerful and by which I myself and everything else . . . have been created.”

至于数学本身的真理，他在《沉思录》（1641）中说：“我把我对于图形、数，以及其他属于算术和几何、一般属于纯粹抽象数学的事物，所清楚认识的真理，视为最确定的。”“只有数学家成功获得了确定性与明证，因为他们从最容易、最简单的东西开始。”数学的概念与真理并不来自感官。它们自出生起就内在于我们的心智，由上帝放置在那里。对物质三角形的感官知觉，绝不能使心智获得理想三角形的概念。心智同样清楚，三角形的内角和必定是180°。

As for truths in mathematics proper, he said in his Meditations (1641), “I counted as the most certain the truths which I conceived clearly as regards figures, numbers, and other matters which pertain to arithmetic and geometry, and, in general to pure and abstract mathematics.” “Only the mathematicians contrived to reach certainty and evidence since they started from what is easiest and simplest.” The concepts and truths of mathematics do not come from the senses. They are innate in our minds from birth and are placed there by God. Sense perception of material triangles could never give the mind the concept of an ideal triangle. It is equally clear to the mind that the sum of the angles of a triangle must be 180°.

笛卡尔接着转向物理世界。他说，我们可以确信，心智清楚认识的直觉以及由此作出的演绎，都适用于物理世界。对他来说，上帝用数学设计世界，是明白无疑的。他在《方法论》中肯定存在“上帝在自然中确立的某些规律，以及他印入我们灵魂的某些观念；一旦我们对它们作了充分反思，就再也不能怀疑，世界中一切存在或发生之事，都精确遵循这些规律”。

Descartes turned next to the physical world. We can be sure, he said, that the intuitions which the mind recognizes clearly and the deductions from them apply to the physical world. It was clear to him that God designed the world mathematically. In his Discourse he affirmed the existence of “certain laws which God has so established in nature and of notions which he has impressed in our souls, that once we have reflected sufficiently upon them, we can no longer doubt their being accurately observed in all that exists or happens in the world.”

笛卡尔进一步肯定，自然规律是不变的，因为它们只是预先确定的数学模式的一部分。甚至在出版《方法论》之前，他就在1630年4月15日致神学家、与数学家关系密切的马兰·梅森神父的信中写道：

Descartes affirmed further that the laws of nature are invariable since they are but part of a predetermined mathematical pattern. Even before publishing his Discourse, Descartes wrote to Father Marin Mersenne, a theologian and close associate of mathematicians, on April 15, 1630:

不要害怕到处宣告：上帝在自然中确立这些规律，正如君主在王国中制定法律。……正如国王越不为臣民熟知，便越有威严，我们认为上帝的伟大不可理解，却不认为我们没有君王。有人会告诉你，如果上帝确立了这些真理，他就能像国王修改法律一样改变它们；对此应回答，若他的意志能够改变，那便可能。但我把这些真理理解为永恒而不变，正如我对上帝的判断一样。

Do not be afraid to proclaim everywhere that God established these laws in nature just as a sovereign establishes laws in his kingdom. . . . And just as a king has more majesty when he is less familiarly known by his subjects, we judge God’s greatness as incomprehensible and do not think that we are without a king. One will tell you that if God established these truths, He would be able to change them just as a king changes his laws; to which one should reply that it is possible if His will can change. But I understand these truths as eternal and unvarying in the same way that I judge God.

在这里，笛卡尔否定了当时盛行的信念，即上帝不断干预宇宙的运行。

Here Descartes denied the prevailing belief that God continually intervenes in the functioning of the universe.

为了研究物理世界，笛卡尔希望只运用数学，因为他在《方法论》中说：“在迄今于科学中寻求真理的所有人中，只有数学家成功作出了证明，也就是说，提出了明白且确定的理由。”在研究物理世界时，他确信数学已经足够。他在《哲学原理》（1644）中说：

To study the physical world Descartes wished to employ only mathematics, for, he said in the Discourse, “Of all those who have hitherto sought for truth in the Sciences, it has been the mathematicians alone who have been able to succeed in making any demonstrations, that is to say, producing reasons which are evident and certain.” In the study of the physical world, Descartes was sure mathematics would suffice. He said in the Principles of Philosophy (1644),

我坦率承认，对于有形事物，我所知道的质料，只有……几何学家称为量、并作为其证明对象的那种东西。处理它时，我只考虑分割、形状与运动；简言之，除非某事能以数学证明所具有的同样明证，从那些共同概念（其真理性无可怀疑）中推导出来，我就不承认它是真的。既然用这种方式，我们能够解释自然的一切现象……我便不认为应当承认任何额外的物理原理，也不认为我们有权寻找其他原理。

I frankly confess that in respect to corporeal things I know of no other matter than that. . . which the geometers entitle quantity and take as being the object of their demonstrations. In treating it I consider only the divisions, the shapes and the movements, and in short admit nothing as true save what can be deduced from those common notions (the truth of which cannot be doubted) with the same evidence as is secure in mathematical demonstration. And since, in this manner we can explain all the phenomena of nature, ... I do not think that we should admit any additional physical principles, or that we have the right to look for any other.

笛卡尔在《原理》中明确指出，科学的本质是数学。他说，他“既不承认，也不希望物理学具有几何或抽象数学之外的任何原理，因为这样便能解释自然的一切现象，并能对它们给出可靠证明”。客观世界是凝固的空间，或具象化的几何。因此，其性质应能从几何的第一原理推导出来（他和同时代人几乎把几何作为数学的同义词，因为当时数学的大部分是几何）。

Descartes was explicit in his Principles that the essence of science was mathematics. He says that he “neither admits nor hopes for any principles in Physics other than those which are in Geometry or in Abstract Mathematics, because thus all phenomena of nature are explained and sure demonstrations of them can be given.” The objective world is space solidified or geometry incarnate. Its properties should therefore be deducible from the first principles of geometry (the term that he and others of his time used as practically synonymous with mathematics because the bulk of mathematics was then geometry).

笛卡尔详细阐述了世界为何必能被数学把握。他坚持，物质最根本、最可靠的性质，是形状、广延以及在空间和时间中的运动；这些全都可以用数学描述。由于形状可归结为广延，他断言：“给我广延与运动，我就能构造宇宙。”他确实补充说，一切物理现象都是受力推动的分子的机械作用结果。但力也遵循不变的数学规律。

Descartes elaborated on why the world must be accessible to mathematics. He insisted that the most fundamental and reliable properties of matter are shape, extension, and motion in space and time, all of which are mathematically describable. Since shape reduces to extension, Descartes asserted, “Give me extension and motion and I shall construct the universe.” He did add that all physical phenomena are the result of the mechanical action of molecules moved by forces. But forces too obeyed invariable mathematical laws.

笛卡尔把外部世界看作仅由运动中的物质构成，那么他如何解释味道、气味、颜色与声音的性质？在这里，他采用了较早的希腊学说，即德谟克利特关于第一性质与第二性质的学说。第一性质，即物质与运动，存在于物理世界；第二性质，即味道、气味、颜色、温暖，以及声音的悦耳或刺耳，只是外部原子撞击人的感觉器官时，第一性质在这些器官中引起的效果。真实世界是在空间与时间中可用数学表达的物体运动的总和；整个宇宙是一台宏伟、和谐、按照数学设计的机器。科学，以及事实上任何试图确立秩序与度量的学科，都受数学支配。他在《指导心智的规则》第IV条中说：

Since Descartes regarded the external world as consisting only of matter in motion, how could he account for tastes, smells, colors, and the qualities of sounds? Here Descartes adopted an older Greek doctrine, Democritus’s doctrine of primary and secondary qualities. The primary qualities, matter and motion, exist in the physical world; the secondary qualities, taste, smell, color, warmth, and the pleasantness or harshness of sounds, are only effects which the primary qualities induce in the sense organs of human beings by the impact of external atoms on these organs. The real world is the totality of mathematically expressible motions of objects in space and time and the entire universe is a great, harmonious, and mathematically designed machine. Science and in fact any discipline that sought to establish order and measurement were subject to mathematics. He said in Rule IV of his Rules for the Direction of the Mind:

一切以研究秩序和度量为目的的科学，都与数学相关；至于这种度量是在数、形状、星辰、声音还是其他对象中寻求，并不重要。因此，应当存在一门一般科学，解释关于秩序和度量所能知道的一切，并且不依赖于对特定对象的任何应用来考察；事实上，这门科学有一个经过长期使用而确立的专有名称，即数学。……它在易学性与重要性方面远远超过依赖它的各门科学，证明便是：它同时涵盖这些科学研究的全部对象，以及许多其他对象。……

All the sciences, which have for their end investigations concerning order and measure, are related to mathematics, it being of small importance whether this measure be sought in numbers, forms, stars, sounds, or any other object; that accordingly, there ought to exist a general science which should explain all that can be known about order and measure, considered independently of any application to a particular subject, and that, indeed, this science has its own proper name consecrated, by long usage, to wit, mathematics. . . . And a proof that it far surpasses in facility and importance the sciences which depend upon it is that it embraces at once all the objects to which these are devoted and a great many others besides. . . .

笛卡尔对数学本身的贡献，并非提供新的真理，而是提供一种强有力的方法，我们如今称之为解析几何（第V章）。从技术角度看，解析几何使数学方法论发生了革命。

Descartes’s contributions to mathematics proper did not offer new truths but rather a powerful methodology which we now call analytic geometry (Chapter V). From the technical standpoint, analytic geometry revolutionized mathematical methodology.

笛卡尔在科学上的贡献，虽不像哥白尼、开普勒或牛顿的工作那样规模宏大、意义广泛，却绝不可忽视。他的涡旋理论（第III章）是十七世纪占主导地位的宇宙论。他创立了机械论哲学，即认为包括人体在内的一切自然现象——灵魂除外——都可归结为遵循力学规律的粒子运动。在力学本身中，他表述了惯性定律，如今称为牛顿运动第一定律：若没有力作用于物体，而物体静止，它就保持静止；若物体正在运动，就继续以恒定速率沿直线运动。

In science, too, Descartes’s contributions, though not of the magnitude and broad significance of the work of Copernicus, Kepler, or Newton, were certainly not negligible. His theory of vortices (Chapter III) was the dominant cosmological theory of the seventeenth century. He was the founder of the philosophy of mechanism, that is, the philosophy that all natural phenomena including the human body, but excepting the soul, reduce to the motions of particles obeying the laws of mechanics. In mechanics proper, he formulated the law of inertia, now known as Newton’s first law of motion: If no force acts on a body and the body is at rest, it will remain at rest, and if it is in motion it will continue to move in a straight line at a constant speed.

光学——尤其是透镜设计——是他的另一项主要兴趣。事实上，他附在《方法论》之后的《几何学》的一部分，以及《屈光学》的全部，都用于讨论光学。他与威勒布罗德·斯涅尔共同享有发现正确光折射定律的功绩；这一定律描述光通过介质的突变界面，例如从空气进入玻璃或水时，如何运动。希腊人开始了光学的数学化，而笛卡尔的工作确立了它作为数学科学的地位。他还对地理学、气象学、植物学、解剖学（动物解剖）、动物学、心理学，甚至医学，作出了重要贡献。

Optics—the design of lenses in particular—was another major interest. Indeed part of his Geometry and all of the Dioptrics, which he appended to his Discourse, are devoted to optics. He shares with Willebrord Snell the discovery of the correct law of refraction of light, that is, how light behaves when it passes through an abrupt change in medium, as from air to glass or water. The Greeks began the mathematization of optics but Descartes’s work established the subject as a mathematical science. He made important contributions also to geography, meteorology, botany, anatomy (in the dissection of animals), zoology, psychology, and even medicine.

虽然笛卡尔的哲学与科学学说颠覆了亚里士多德主义和中世纪经院哲学，但在一个根本方面，他仍是一位经院哲学家：他从自己的心智中抽取关于存在与实在本性的命题。他相信先验真理，相信智力凭自身力量就能达到对万物的完美认识。因此，他依据先验推理表述运动规律。（实际上，在生物学工作与某些其他领域中，他确实进行实验，并从实验中得出重要结论。）然而，他把自然现象归结为纯粹物理事件，在使科学摆脱神秘主义和隐秘力量方面贡献很大。

Though Descartes’s philosophical and scientific doctrines subverted Aristotelianism and medieval scholasticism, in one fundamental respect he was a scholastic: he drew from his own mind propositions about the nature of being and reality. He believed in a priori truths and that the intellect by its own power may arrive at a perfect knowledge of all things. Thus he stated laws of motion on the basis of a priori reasoning. (Actually in his biological work and in some other fields he did experiment and drew significant conclusions from his experiments.) However, by reducing natural phenomena to purely physical happenings, he did much to rid science of mysticism and occult forces.

十七世纪伟大数学家之一布莱兹·帕斯卡（1623—1662），虽然在哲学上没有同样巨大的影响，却欣然支持数学及科学的数学规律是真理这一信念。笛卡尔谈的是心智清楚接受的直觉，而帕斯卡谈的是内心的接受。真理必须清楚、分明地向内心呈现，或者是这类真理的逻辑结果。他在《思想录》中告诉我们：

Though not as influential in his philosophy, one of the great mathematicians of the seventeenth century, Blaise Pascal (1623-1662), readily added his support to the belief that mathematics and the mathematical laws of science are truths. Unlike Descartes, who spoke of intuitions clearly acceptable to the mind, Pascal spoke of acceptability to the heart. Truths must either appeal clearly and distinctly to the heart or be logical consequences of such truths. In his Pensees he tells us:

我们关于空间、时间、运动、数等第一原理的知识，与通过推理获得的任何知识一样确定。事实上，由内心与本能提供的这种知识，必然是推理建立结论的基础。理性若要求内心先证明第一原理，才同意接受它们，便毫无意义而荒谬；这就像内心要求先直觉把握理性证明的所有命题，才同意接受它们一样。

Our knowledge of the first principles, such as space, time, motion, number, is as certain as any knowledge we obtain by reasoning. As a matter of fact, this knowledge provided by our hearts and instinct is necessarily the basis on which our reasoning has to build its conclusions. It is just as pointless and absurd for reason to demand proof of first principles from the heart before agreeing to accept them as it would be for the heart to demand an intuition of all the propositions demonstrated by reason before agreeing to accept them.

对帕斯卡来说，科学是研究上帝的世界。仅仅为了享乐而追求科学，是错误的。把享乐作为科学的主要目的，就是败坏研究，因为这样会使人产生“求学的贪欲或情欲，对知识放纵的胃口”。“这种科学研究，源于预先把自我当作事物中心的关切，而不是关切于在周围一切自然现象中寻找上帝的存在与荣耀。”

For Pascal, science is the study of God’s world. The pursuit of science for mere enjoyment is wrong. To make enjoyment the chief end of science is to corrupt research, for then one acquires “a greed or lust for learning, a profligate appetite for knowledge.” “Such a study of science springs from a priori concern for self as the center of things rather than a concern for seeking out, amid all surrounding natural phenomena, the presence of God and His glory.”

在塑造现代数学与科学的开创性思想家中，伽利略·伽利莱（1564—1642）与笛卡尔齐名。当然，他也确信自然按照数学设计，而且是上帝设计的。他在1610年《试金者》中的话非常著名：

Of the seminal thinkers who forged modern mathematics and science, Galileo Galilei (1564-1642) ranks with Descartes. Of course, he, too, was certain that nature is mathematically designed, and designed by God. His statement in The Assayer of 1610 is famous:

哲学［自然］写在那部永远摆在我们眼前的巨著之中——我指的是宇宙——但若不先学会它的语言、掌握它所用的符号，我们就不能理解它。这部书用数学语言写成，符号是三角形、圆以及其他几何图形；没有它们的帮助，就不可能理解其中的一个字；没有它们，人只能徒劳地在黑暗迷宫中徘徊。

Philosophy [nature] is written in that great book which ever lies before our eyes—I mean the universe—but we cannot understand it if we do not first learn the language and grasp the symbols in which it is written. The book is written in the mathematical language, and the symbols are triangles, circles and other geometrical figures, without whose help it is impossible to comprehend a single word of it; without which one wanders in vain through a dark labyrinth.

自然简单而有序，其行为具有规律性与必然性。它依照完美、不变的数学规律运行。神的理性是自然中理性秩序的源泉。上帝把严格的数学必然性赋予世界；人虽然其理性与上帝的理性相关，却只能艰难地把握这种必然性。因此，数学知识不仅是绝对真理，也与《圣经》的任何一行文字同样神圣不可侵犯。而且，研究自然与研究《圣经》同样虔敬。“上帝在自然的行动中向我们显示自己的奇妙，丝毫不亚于在《圣经》的神圣言辞中。”

Nature is simple and orderly and its behavior is regular and necessary. It acts in accordance with perfect and immutable mathematical laws. Divine reason is the source of the rational in nature. God put into the world that rigorous mathematical necessity which men reach only laboriously, even though their reason is related to God’s. Mathematical knowledge is therefore not only absolute truth but as sacrosanct as any line of the Scriptures. Moreover, the study of nature is as devout as the study of the Bible. “Nor does God less admirably reveal himself to us in Nature’s actions than in the Scriptures’ sacred dictions.”

伽利略在《关于两大世界体系的对话》（1632）中断言，在数学中，人达到一切可能知识的顶峰，所得知识并不低于神的智力所拥有的。当然，神的智力所知道、所理解的数学真理数量，比人多得无限；但就客观确定性而言，人类心智所知的少数真理，人知道得与上帝一样完美。

Galileo asserted in his Dialogue on the Great World Systems (1632) that in mathematics man reaches the pinnacle of all possible knowledge—a knowledge not inferior to that possessed by the divine intellect. Of course the divine intellect knows and conceives an infinitely greater number of mathematical truths than man does but with regard to objective certainty the few verities known by the human mind are known as perfectly by man as by God.

虽然伽利略曾是数学教授与宫廷数学家，但他的主要贡献，是对科学方法的诸多创新。其中最著名的，是要求放弃亚里士多德视为科学真正目标的物理解释，转而追求数学描述。这两个目标的差别很容易说明。一个被释放的物体落向地面，而且速度不断增加。亚里士多德和遵循其方法的中世纪科学家，试图说明下落的原因，推想这一原因是机械性的。伽利略则仅用数学规律描述下落，以现代符号表示，即d = 16t2，其中d是物体在t秒内下落的英尺数。这个公式并不说明物体为什么下落，看起来远少于人们想了解的现象内容。但伽利略确信，我们应当追求的是对自然的描述性知识。他在《关于两门新科学》中写道：“落体运动加速的原因，并非研究的必要部分。”更一般地，他指出，自己将研究并证明运动的某些性质，而不考虑其原因可能是什么。实证科学研究应当与终极原因问题分离，并放弃对物理原因的思辨。伽利略大可以这样告诫科学家：职责不在于追问为何，职责只在于量化。

Though Galileo was a professor of mathematics and a court mathematician, his major contribution was his many innovations in scientific method. Of these the most notable was his injunction to abandon physical explanation, which Aristotle had regarded as the true goal of science, and to seek instead mathematical description. The difference in these two goals is readily illustrated. A body which is dropped falls to earth, and in fact falls with increasing velocity. Aristotle and the medieval scientists who followed his methodology sought to account for the cause of the fall, which presumably was mechanical. Instead, Galileo merely described the fall with the mathematical law which, stated in modern notation, is d = 16t2, where d is the number of feet the body falls in t seconds. This formula says nothing about why the body falls and would seem to offer far less than what one would want to know about the phenomenon. But Galileo was sure that the knowledge of nature we should seek was descriptive. He wrote in his Two New Sciences, “The cause of the acceleration of the motion of falling bodies is not a necessary part of the investigation.” More generally, he pointed out that he was going to investigate and demonstrate some of the properties of motion without regard to what the causes might be. Positive scientific inquiries were to be separated from questions of ultimate causation, and speculation about physical causes was to be abandoned. Galileo may well have put it to scientists: theirs not to reason why, theirs but to quantify.

即使今天，人们对伽利略纲领这一条款的第一反应，也可能是否定的。用公式描述现象，似乎至多只是第一步。真正把握科学职能的，似乎是亚里士多德学派：解释现象为何发生。就连笛卡尔也反对伽利略寻求描述性公式的决定。他说：“伽利略关于物体在空无空间中下落所说的一切，都毫无基础；他首先应当确定重量的本性。”笛卡尔还说，伽利略应思考终极理由。但根据后来的发展，如今我们知道，伽利略以描述为目标的决定，是任何人在科学方法论上作出的最深刻、最富成果的创新。它的意义——后面将更充分地显现——在于使科学更加明确地置于数学的统摄之下。

First reactions to this plank of Galileo’s program are likely even today to be negative. Descriptions of phenomena in terms of formulas hardly seem to be more than a first step. It would seem that the true function of science had really been grasped by the Aristotelians, namely, to explain why phenomena happened. Even Descartes protested Galileo’s decision to seek descriptive formulas. He said, “Everything that Galileo says about bodies falling in empty space is built without foundation: he ought first to have determined the nature of weight.” Further, said Descartes, Galileo should reflect about ultimate reasons. But we now know, in the light of subsequent developments, that Galileo’s decision to aim for description was the deepest and the most fruitful innovation that anyone has made about scientific methodology. Its significance, which will be more fully apparent later, is that it placed science far more squarely under the aegis of mathematics.

伽利略的下一条原则，是科学的任何分支都应以数学为模型。这隐含两个基本步骤。数学从公理，即清楚、自明的真理出发，然后通过演绎推理确立新的真理。因此，科学的任何分支都应从公理或原理出发，再进行演绎。而且，应当从公理推出尽可能多的结果。当然，这个方案曾由亚里士多德提出；他心中也以数学为模型，力求科学具有演绎结构。

Galileo’s next principle was that any branch of science should be patterned on the model of mathematics. Two essential steps are implied here. Mathematics starts with axioms, that is, clear, self-evident truths. From these it proceeds by deductive reasoning to establish new truths. So any branch of science should start with axioms or principles and then proceed deductively. Moreover, one should pull out from the axioms as many consequences as possible. Of course, this plan was advanced by Aristotle, who also aimed at deductive structure in science with the mathematical model in mind.

然而，在获得第一原理的方法上，伽利略与希腊人、中世纪学者及笛卡尔根本不同。伽利略之前的人和笛卡尔相信，心智提供基本原理。心智只需思考某类现象，就会立即认识到根本真理。这种心智能力在数学中表现得很清楚。思考数或几何图形时，等量加等量所得仍相等、两点确定一条直线等公理，会立即浮现，而且是毋庸置疑的真理。同样，希腊人发现某些物理原理也同样令人信服。宇宙中一切物体都应有一个自然位置，似乎再合适不过。静止状态显然似乎比运动状态更自然。要使物体开始并保持运动，就必须施加力，似乎也无可怀疑。相信心智提供根本原理，并不否认观察可能帮助我们获得它们。但观察只是唤起正确的原理，正如看到熟悉的面孔，可能唤起有关那个人的事实。

However, Galileo departed radically from the Greeks, the medievalists, and Descartes in the method of obtaining first principles. The pre-Galileans and Descartes had believed that the mind supplies the basic principles. The mind had but to think about any class of phenomena and it would immediately recognize fundamental truths. This power of the mind was clearly evidenced in mathematics. Axioms such as equals added to equals give equals and two points determine a line suggested themselves immediately in thinking about number or geometrical figures and were indubitable truths. So too did the Greeks find some physical principles equally appealing. That all objects in the universe should have a natural place was no more than fitting. The state of rest seemed clearly more natural than the state of motion. It seemed indubitable, too, that to put and keep bodies in motion force must be applied. To believe that the mind supplies fundamental principles does not deny that observation might help us to reach these principles. But observation merely evokes the correct principles just as the sight of a familiar face may call to mind facts about that person.

正如伽利略所说，这些学者首先按照自己预设的原理，决定世界应当如何运行。伽利略决定，物理学不同于数学，第一原理必须来自经验与实验。获得正确基本原理的方法，是注意自然说什么，而不是心智喜欢什么。他公开批评那些接受符合自己预想的自然行为规律的科学家与哲学家。他说，自然并非先造出人的大脑，再把世界安排得能为人类智力接受。对于不断重复亚里士多德、争论其意涵的中世纪学者，伽利略批评说，知识来自观察，而非书本。争论亚里士多德是徒劳的。他称这些人为纸上科学家，他们幻想研究科学就像研究《埃涅阿斯纪》或《奥德赛》，或靠校勘文本。“当我们已经得到自然的裁决时，权威便一文不值。”

These savants, as Galileo put it, first decided how the world should function in accordance with their preconceived principles. Galileo decided that in physics as opposed to mathematics first principles must come from experience and experimentation. The way to obtain correct and basic principles is to pay attention to what nature says rather than what the mind prefers. He openly criticized scientists and philosophers who accepted laws which conformed to their preconceived ideas as to how nature must behave. Nature did not first make men’s brains, he said, and then arrange the world so that it would be acceptable to human intellects. To the medievalists who kept repeating Aristotle and debating what he meant, Galileo addressed the criticism that knowledge comes from observation and not from books. It was useless to debate about Aristotle. Those who did he called paper scientists who fancied that science was to be studied like the Aeneid or the Odyssey or by collation of texts. “When we have the decree of nature, authority goes for nothing.”

当然，某些文艺复兴思想家以及伽利略的同时代人弗朗西斯·培根，也已得出实验必不可少的结论。在新方法的这一具体条款上，伽利略并非领先于所有人。然而，现代派的笛卡尔仍不认可伽利略依靠实验的明智。他说，感官事实只会导致错觉。理性能洞穿这些错觉。根据心智提供的天赋一般原理，我们可以推导并理解自然的具体现象。实际上，如前所述，笛卡尔在许多科学工作中确实进行了实验，并要求理论符合事实，但在哲学上，他仍受制于心智的真理。

Of course, some Renaissance thinkers and Galileo’s contemporary Francis Bacon had also arrived at the conclusion that experimentation was necessary. In this particular plank of his new method Galileo was not ahead of all others. Yet the modernist Descartes did not grant the wisdom of Galileo’s reliance upon experimentation. The facts of the senses, Descartes said, can only lead to delusion. Reason penetrates such delusions. From the innate general principles supplied by the mind we can deduce particular phenomena of nature and understand them. Actually, as we noted earlier, in much of his scientific work Descartes did experiment and require that theory fit facts, but in his philosophy he was still tied to truths of the mind.

少数数学物理学家同意伽利略的看法：单凭理性不能保证物理原理正确。克里斯蒂安·惠更斯实际批评过笛卡尔。英国物理学家也抨击纯粹理性主义。罗伯特·胡克（1635—1703）说，伦敦皇家学会的成员“眼前有如此多严重的实例：大多数人因为只依赖人类理性的力量，而迷失于错误与虚假之中；因此，他们如今开始用感官来修正一切假说”。

A few mathematical physicists agreed with Galileo that reason alone could not ensure correct physical principles. Christian Huygens actually criticized Descartes. The English physicists also attacked pure rationalism. Robert Hooke (1635-1703) said that the members of the Royal Society of London “having before their eyes so many fatal instances of the errors and falsehoods in which the greater part of mankind had wandered because they relied upon the strength of human reason alone, have now begun to correct all hypotheses by sense”

当然，伽利略认识到，实验可能使人获得错误原理，从而由此作出的演绎也可能错误。因此，他提出，而且看来确实运用了实验，既检验推理结论，也获取基本原理。然而，伽利略究竟在多大程度上进行了实验，确实值得怀疑。他某些被认为做过的实验，有时称为Gedanken（德语，意为“思想”）实验，即他想象如果进行实验，必定会发生什么。尽管如此，他认为物理原理必须建立在经验与实验之上的学说，仍具有革命性，至关重要。他本人毫不怀疑，上帝用来塑造宇宙的某些真实原理，仍可通过心智获得；但他为经验的作用打开大门，也让怀疑的魔鬼溜了进来。如果科学的基本原理必须来自经验，数学的公理为什么不能呢？直到1800年，这个问题都没有困扰伽利略及其后继者。数学仍享有特殊地位。

Of course, Galileo realized that one may glean an incorrect principle from experimentation and that as a consequence the deductions from it could be incorrect. Hence he proposed and presumably did use experiments to check the conclusions of his reasonings as well as to acquire basic principles. However, the extent to which Galileo experimented is certainly open to question. Some of his presumed experiments are sometimes called Gedanken (German for “thoughts”) experiments, that is, he imagined what must happen were one to experiment. Nevertheless, his doctrine that physical principles must rest on experience and experiments is revolutionary and crucial. Galileo himself had no doubt that some true principles among those used by God to fashion the universe could still be reached by the mind, but by opening the door to the role of experience he allowed the devil of doubt to slip in. If the basic principles of science must come from experience, why not the axioms of mathematics? This question did not trouble Galileo or his successors until 1800. Mathematics still enjoyed a privileged position.

在科学工作中，伽利略专注于物质与运动。他独立于笛卡尔，清楚认识了如今称为牛顿运动第一定律的惯性原理。他还成功获得了竖直上升与下落的物体、沿斜面滑动的物体，以及抛射体的运动规律。他证明最后一类物体的轨迹是抛物线。总之，他获得了地上物体的运动规律。虽然如同一切重大创新一样，都能找到先驱，但没有谁像伽利略那样清楚地理解指导科学研究的概念与原理，也没有谁以如此简单、有效的方式展示其应用。

In his scientific work Galileo concentrated on matter and motion. He recognized clearly and independently of Descartes the principle of inertia, now called Newton’s first law of motion. He was successful also in obtaining the laws of motion of bodies that rise straight up and fall, bodies sliding along inclined planes, and projectiles. The motion of this last class he showed was parabolic. In sum, he obtained the laws of motion of terrestrial objects. Though, as in every major innovation, predecessors can be found, no one was so clear as Galileo about the concepts and principles that were to guide scientific inquiry, and no one demonstrated their application in so simple and effective a manner.

伽利略的科学哲学与方法论，在当时具有根本创新性，为艾萨克·牛顿的成就作了铺垫；牛顿恰好出生于伽利略去世的那一年。

Radically innovative for his time, Galileo’s philosophy and methodology of science were prefatory to the accomplishments of Isaac Newton, who was born in the year that Galileo died.

III 科学的数学化

III. The Mathematization of Science

任何特定理论中的真正科学，都只与其中的数学一样多。

In any particular theory there is only as much real science as there is mathematics.

伊曼努尔·康德

Immanuel Kant

如果科学的数学规律是上帝融入宇宙设计中的真理这一确信还需要加强，那么艾萨克·牛顿爵士（1642—1727）极其出色地提供了这种加强。虽然牛顿是剑桥大学数学教授，位列伟大数学家之中，但他作为物理学家的地位更高。他的工作开创了科学的新纪元与新方法，扩大并深化了数学的作用。

If the conviction that the mathematical laws of science were truths incorporated by God in His design of the universe needed any reinforcement, it was superbly provided by Sir Isaac Newton (1642- 1727). Though Newton was a professor of mathematics at Cambridge University and is ranked as one of the great mathematicians, he has a still higher rank as a physicist. His work inaugurated a new era and a new methodology in science which increased and deepened the role of mathematics.

哥白尼、开普勒、笛卡尔、伽利略与帕斯卡的工作，确实表明某些自然现象依照数学规律运行；这些人不仅确信上帝如此设计宇宙，还确信人类的数学思维与上帝的设计相符。然而，十七世纪占主导地位的科学哲学或方法论，是由笛卡尔表述并推进的。笛卡尔确实说，全部物理学都归结为几何；他和其他人常用几何作为数学的同义词。但大多数牛顿之前的学者，尤其是惠更斯，所采用的笛卡尔方法，还为科学提出了一个额外职能：对自然现象的作用提供物理解释。

The work of Copernicus, Kepler, Descartes, Galileo, and Pascal did indeed demonstrate that some phenomena of nature operated in accordance with mathematical laws, and all of these men were convinced not only that God had so designed the universe but that the mathematical thinking of humans was in accord with God’s design. However, the philosophy or methodology of science predominant in the seventeenth century was formulated and advanced by Descartes. Descartes did indeed say that all of physics reduces to geometry, the word he and others often used as a synonym for mathematics. But Descartes’s methodology, adopted by most pre-Newtonians, especially Huygens, proposed an additional function of science, namely, to provide a physical explanation of the action of natural phenomena.

希腊人，尤其是亚里士多德，也曾试图用物理方式解释自然现象的行为。他们的主要理论认为，一切物质由土、气、火、水四种元素组成，具有重、轻、干、湿中的一种或多种性质。这些性质解释物质为何表现得如我们所见：火因轻而上升，土性物质因重而下落。中世纪学者又增添了许多性质，如相感，用以解释一个物体对另一个物体的吸引，如磁铁吸铁；以及相斥，用以解释一个物体被另一个物体排斥。

The Greeks, notably Aristotle, had also sought to explain in physical terms the behavior of natural phenomena, and their chief theory was that all matter was composed of four elements, earth, air, fire, and water, and these possessed one or more qualities, heaviness, lightness, dryness, and moisture. These qualities explained why matter behaved as it seemingly does: fire rises because it is light whereas earthy matter falls because it possesses the quality of heaviness. To these qualities the medieval scholars added many others, such as sympathy, which accounted for the attraction of one body to another as iron to a magnet, and antipathy, to account for the repulsion of one body by another.
