笛卡尔则摒弃所有这些性质，坚持一切物理现象都能用物质与运动解释。物质的本质属性是广延，它可以测量，因而可归结为数学。此外，没有物质，就不可能有广延。因此，真空不可能存在，空间充满物质。而且，物质只通过直接接触作用于物质。不过，物质由微小、不可见的粒子组成，它们的大小、形状及其他性质各不相同。由于粒子太小而不可见，为了解释人能观察到的较大现象，就必须对其行为作出假说。在这种观点中，整个空间充满粒子，它们带动较大的聚合体——行星——绕太阳运动。这就是笛卡尔涡旋理论的核心。

Descartes, on the other hand, discarded all these qualities and insisted that all physical phenomena could be explained in terms of matter and motion. The essential attribute of matter was extension and this was measurable and so reducible to mathematics. Further, there could be no extension without matter. Hence a vacuum was impossible. Space was filled with matter. Moreover, matter acted on matter only by direct contact. However, matter was composed of small, invisible particles that differed in size, shape, and other properties. Because these particles were too small to be visible it was necessary to make hypotheses about how they behaved in order to account for the larger phenomena that man can observe. In this view all of space was filled with particles which swept the larger accumulations, the planets, around the sun. This is the essence of Descartes’s vortex theory.

笛卡尔是机械论的创始人，法国哲学家兼教士皮埃尔·伽桑狄（1592—1655）、英国哲学家托马斯·霍布斯（1588—1679），以及荷兰数学家兼物理学家克里斯蒂安·惠更斯（1629—1695），都追随了他。因此，惠更斯在《光论》（1690）中，假定空间充满以太粒子，光的运动由一个粒子传到下一个粒子，以此解释各种光学现象。事实上，该书副标题是“解释反射与折射中发生之事的原因”。惠更斯在导言中说，在真正的哲学中，“人以机械运动来理解一切自然效果的原因。在我看来，我们必须这样做，否则就放弃在物理学中理解任何东西的一切希望。”伽桑狄在一点上不同：他相信原子在虚空中运动。

Descartes was the founder of the mechanistic theory, and he was followed in this by the French philosopher and priest Pierre Gassendi (1592-1655), the English philosopher Thomas Hobbes (1588-1679), and the Dutch mathematician and physicist Christian Huygens (1629— 1695). Thus Huygens in his Treatise on Light (1690) accounted for various phenomena of light by the assumption that space was filled with ether particles which transmitted the motion of light from one to the next. In fact the subtitle of his book reads, “In which are explained the causes of that which occurs in Reflexion and in Refraction.” In his Introduction, Huygens said that in the true philosophy, “One conceives the causes of all natural effects in terms of mechanical motion. This, in my opinion, we must necessarily do, or else renounce all hopes of ever comprehending anything in Physics.” In one respect Gassendi differed: he believed that atoms moved in a void.

关于微小粒子如何作用的物理假说，至少在大体上，确实解释了自然的宏观行为。但它们是心智的创造。而且，笛卡尔及其追随者的物理假说是定性的。它们能够解释，但由于是定性的，不能精确预测观察与实验将揭示什么。莱布尼茨把这批物理假说称为一部美丽的传奇。

Physical hypotheses about how the minute particles acted did account, at least in the large, for the gross behavior of nature. But they were creations of the mind. Moreover, the physical hypotheses of Descartes and his followers were qualitative. They could explain but because they were qualitative they could not predict precisely what observation and experimentation would reveal. Leibniz called this collection of physical hypotheses a beautiful romance.

伽利略开创了一种相反的科学哲学：科学必须寻求数学描述，而非物理解释。而且，基本原理必须由实验，以及从实验作出的归纳获得。遵循这一哲学，也受到老师艾萨克·巴罗的影响，牛顿用数学前提取代物理假说，改变了科学的进程，因而能够以培根所要求的确定性进行预测。此外，这些前提是从实验与观察推得的。

A counter-philosophy of science was inaugurated by Galileo. Science must seek mathematical description rather than physical explanation. Moreover, the basic principles must be derived from experiments and induction from experiments. In accordance with this philosophy, Newton, influenced also by his teacher Isaac Barrow, changed the course of science by adopting mathematical premises in place of physical hypotheses and could consequently predict with the certainty that Bacon had called for. Moreover, the premises were inferred from experiments and observations.

伽利略研究物体下落与抛射体飞行，预示了牛顿的工作。牛顿处理的是更广泛的问题，也是约1650年科学家最关心的问题：能否在伽利略的地上运动规律与开普勒的天体运动规律之间建立联系？认为所有运动现象都应从同一组原理推出，可能显得宏大而过分，但十七世纪信奉宗教的数学家却十分自然地产生了这一想法。上帝设计了宇宙，因此理应期待自然的一切现象遵循同一总体方案。由一个心智设计宇宙，几乎肯定会采用同一组基本原理来支配相关现象。对十七世纪致力于探寻上帝自然设计的数学家与科学家来说，寻找各种地上与天上运动背后的统一性，十分合理。

Galileo anticipated Newton in that he treated the fall of a body and the flight of a projectile. Newton tackled a far broader problem, one which was uppermost in the minds of the scientists about 1650. Could one establish a connection between Galileo’s laws of terrestrial motions and Kepler’s laws of celestial motions? The thought that all the phenomena of motion should follow from one set of principles might seem grandiose and inordinate, but it occurred very naturally to the religious mathematicians of the seventeenth century. God had designed the universe, and it was to be expected that all phenomena of nature would follow one master plan. One mind designing a universe would almost surely have employed one set of basic principles to govern related phenomena. To the mathematicians and scientists of the seventeenth century engaged in the quest for God’s design of nature, it seemed very reasonable that they should seek the unity underlying the diverse earthly and heavenly motions.

在执行建立普遍运动规律的计划时，牛顿对代数、几何，尤其是微积分（第VI章），作出了许多贡献。但这些只是实现科学目标的辅助手段。实际上，他认为数学本身干枯而贫瘠，只是表达自然规律的工具。他专注于寻找能够建立地上与天体运动统一理论的科学原理。幸运的是，正如德尼·狄德罗所说，自然向牛顿敞开了秘密。

In the course of executing his program of producing universal laws of motion, Newton made many contributions to algebra, geometry, and above all the calculus (Chapter VI). But these were merely aids to his scientific goals. In fact he considered mathematics proper to be dry and barren, and only a tool for the expression of natural laws. He concentrated on finding the scientific principles that would lead to a unifying theory of earthly and celestial motions. Fortunately, as Denis Diderot put it, nature admitted Newton into her confidence.

牛顿当然熟悉伽利略确立的原理。但这些原理涵盖得还不够广。由运动第一定律可以清楚看出，行星必定受到某种把它们拉向太阳的力，因为如果没有力作用，每颗行星都会沿直线运动。甚至在牛顿开始工作之前，许多人就想到有一种力不断把每颗行星拉向太阳，包括哥白尼、开普勒、著名实验物理学家罗伯特·胡克、物理学家兼著名建筑师克里斯托弗·雷恩、埃德蒙·哈雷及其他人。人们还猜测，这种力对远处行星的作用必定弱于对近处行星的作用，并且随着太阳与行星间距离的平方增大而减小。但在牛顿工作之前，所有这些关于引力的想法，都未超出猜测。

Newton was, of course, familiar with the principles established by Galileo. But these were not sufficiently encompassing. It was clear from the first law of motion that the planets must be acted on by a force which pulls them toward the sun, for, if no force were acting, each planet would move in a straight line. The idea of a force which constantly pulls each planet toward the sun had occurred to many men, Copernicus, Kepler, the famous experimental physicist Robert Hooke, the physicist and renowned architect Christopher Wren, Edmund Halley, and others, even before Newton set to work. It had also been conjectured that this force exerted on a distant planet must be weaker than that exerted on a nearer one and that this force must decrease as the square of the distance between sun and planet increased. But, before Newton’s work, none of these thoughts about a gravitational force advanced beyond speculation.

牛顿采用了同时代人已经提出的猜想，即任意两个质量分别为m与M、相距r的物体之间，吸引力F由下式给出：

Newton adopted the conjecture already made by his contemporaries, namely, that the force of attraction, F, between any two bodies of masses m and M, respectively, separated by a distance r is given by the formula

这个公式中，G是一个常数，即无论m、M和r为何值，它都是同一个数。该常数的值取决于质量、力和距离所用的单位。他还推广了伽利略的地上运动规律；这些推广如今称为牛顿运动三定律。第一条就是笛卡尔与伽利略已经肯定的规律：如果没有力作用于物体，那么物体若静止，就保持静止；若运动，就以恒定速率沿直线运动。第二条指出，若有力作用于质量为m的物体，就会使它产生加速度；而且，力等于质量乘以加速度。用符号表示，就是F = ma。第三条肯定，如果物体A对物体B施加力F，那么B也对A施加一个大小相等、方向相反的力。从这三条定律和万有引力定律，牛顿很容易推导出地上物体的行为。

In this formula, G is a constant, that is, it is the same number no matter what m, M, and r may be. The value of this constant depends upon the units used for mass, force, and distance. He also generalized Galileo’s laws of terrestrial motion; these generalizations are now known as Newton’s three laws of motion. The first is the law Descartes and Galileo had already affirmed: that if no force acts on a body, then if the body is at rest it will remain at rest and if in motion it will move along a straight line at a constant speed. The second states that, if a force acts on a body of mass ra, then it will give that body an acceleration; moreover, the force equals the mass times the acceleration. In symbols, F = ma. The third law affirms that if a body A exerts a force F on body B then B exerts a force on A that is equal in magnitude but opposite in direction to the force F. From these three laws and the law of gravitation Newton deduced readily the behavior of earthly bodies.

至于天体运动，牛顿真正伟大的胜利，是证明开普勒经过多年观察与试错才获得的三条定律，也是万有引力定律与运动三定律的数学结果。因此，在牛顿工作之前似乎与地上运动无关的行星运动规律，被证明与地上运动规律来自同样的基本原理。在这个意义上，牛顿“解释”了行星运动规律。此外，由于开普勒定律符合观察，从万有引力定律推导出它们，构成了后者正确性的极强证据。

As for heavenly motions, Newton’s truly great triumph was his demonstration that the three Keplerian laws, which Kepler had obtained only after years of observation and trial and error, were also mathematical consequences of the law of gravitation and the three laws of motion. Flence the laws of planetary motion, which before Newton’s work seemed to have no relation to earthly motions, were shown to follow from the same basic principles as did the laws of earthly motions. In this sense, Newton “explained” the laws of planetary motion. Further, since the Keplerian laws agree with observations, their derivation from the law of gravitation constituted superb evidence for the correctness of that law.

刚才所述从运动定律与万有引力定律作出的少数推导，不过是牛顿成就的样本。他运用万有引力定律，解释了此前不为人理解的现象，即海洋潮汐。潮汐源于月亮，以及作用较小的太阳，对大范围水体施加的引力。牛顿根据收集的月潮——即月亮造成的潮汐——高度数据，计算了月球质量。他与克里斯蒂安·惠更斯计算了地球赤道周围的隆起。他和其他人还证明，彗星轨道符合万有引力定律。因此，彗星也被承认为太阳系中遵循规律的成员，不再被看作偶然出现的东西，或上帝派来实施毁灭的来客。随后，牛顿证明，月亮和太阳对地球赤道隆起的吸引，使地球自转轴在二万六千年的周期中描绘出圆锥，而不是始终指向同一颗恒星。这种地轴方向的周期变化，使春分与秋分的时间每年略有改变；喜帕恰斯早在一千八百年前就观察到这一事实。这样，牛顿解释了岁差。

The few deductions from the laws of motion and the law of gravitation just described are but a sample of what Newton was able to accomplish. He applied the law of gravitation to explain a phenomenon which theretofore had not been understood, namely, the oceans’ tides. These were due to the gravitational forces exerted by the moon, and to a lesser extent the sun, on large bodies of water. From the data collected on the height of lunar tides, that is, tides due to the moon, Newton calculated the moon’s mass. Newton and Christian Huygens calculated the bulge of the earth around the equator. Newton and others also showed the paths of comets to be in conformity with the law of gravitation. Hence the comets, too, were recognized as lawful members of our solar system and ceased to be viewed as accidental occurrences or visitations from God intended to wreak destruction. Newton then showed that the attraction of the moon and the sun on the earth’s equatorial bulge causes the axis of the earth’s rotation to describe a cone over a period of 26,000 years instead of always pointing to the same star in the sky. This periodic change in the direction of the earth’s axis causes a slight change each year in the time of the spring and fall equinoxes, a fact which had been observed by Hipparchus 1800 years earlier. Thus Newton explained the precession of the equinoxes.

最后，牛顿运用近似方法，解决了若干涉及月球运动的问题。例如，月球运动平面与地球运动平面略有倾斜。他证明，这一现象来自太阳、地球与月球在万有引力定律下的相互作用。牛顿及其直接后继者，对于行星、彗星、月球与海洋的运动，推导出了如此众多而重要的结果，以至于随后两百年间，人们把他们的成就视为“对世界体系的阐释”。

Finally, Newton, using approximate methods, solved a number of problems involving the motion of the moon. For example, the plane in which the moon moves is inclined somewhat to the plane in which the earth moves. He was able to show that this phenomenon follows from the interaction of the sun, earth, and moon under the law of gravitation. Newton and his immediate successors deduced so many and such weighty consequences about the motions of the planets, the comets, the moon, and the seas that their accomplishments were viewed for the next two hundred years as the “explication of the System of the World.”

在所有这些工作中，牛顿采用了伽利略寻求数学描述而非物理解释的主张。他不仅统一了开普勒、伽利略与惠更斯大量的实验和理论成果，还把数学描述与演绎置于一切科学说明与预测的首位。在其标题恰如其分的主要著作《自然哲学的数学原理》（1687）的序言中，他说：

In all of this work, Newton adopted Galileo’s proposal to seek mathematical description rather than physical explanation. Newton not only unified a vast number of experimental and theoretical results of Kepler, Galileo, and Huygens but he placed mathematical description and deduction at the forefront of all scientific accounts and prediction. In the Preface to his aptly titled major work, Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy (1687), he said,

既然古人（如帕普斯所告诉我们的）认为，力学是研究自然事物最重要的科学，而近代人拒绝实体形式与隐秘性质，努力使自然现象服从数学规律，我便在本书中研究与哲学［科学］有关的数学……因此，把这部著作作为哲学的数学原理奉献出来，因为哲学的全部任务似乎在于：从运动现象研究自然的力，然后由这些力证明其他现象；第一卷与第二卷中的一般命题，正是为此而设。……然后，我用其他同样是数学性的命题，从这些力推导出行星、彗星、月亮和海洋的运动。

Since the ancients (as we are told by Pappus) esteemed the science of mechanics of greatest importance in the investigation of natural things, and the moderns, rejecting substantial forms and occult qualities, have endeavored to subject the phenomena of nature to the laws of mathematics, I have in this treatise cultivated mathematics as far as it relates to philosophy [science] . . . and therefore I offer this work as the mathematical principles of philosophy, for the whole burden in philosophy seems to consist in this—from the phenomena of motions to investigate the forces of nature, and then from these forces to demonstrate the other phenomena; and to this end the general propositions in the first and second Books are directed. . . . Then from these forces, by other propositions which are also mathematical, I deduce the motions of the planets, the comets, the moon, and the sea.

显然，数学将发挥主要作用。

Clearly, mathematics was to play the major role.

牛顿有充分理由强调定量的数学规律，而非物理解释，因为其天体力学的核心物理概念是引力，而引力的作用根本无法用物理方式解释。即使两个物体隔着数亿英里的空无空间，引力仍使它们相互吸引；这一概念似乎与亚里士多德学派和中世纪学者为解释科学现象所虚构的诸多性质同样不可思议。牛顿同时代人坚持机械解释，把力理解为物体接触的效果，即一个物体“推”另一个物体；他们尤其反感这一概念。放弃物理机制而采用数学描述，甚至震惊了最伟大的科学家。惠更斯认为引力观念“荒谬”，因为它通过空无空间作用，排除了任何机制。他惊讶于牛顿竟然仅以数学性的引力原理为基础，费尽心力作出如此大量繁重计算。许多其他人，包括莱布尼茨，都反对对引力的纯数学描述。莱布尼茨于1690年读过牛顿《原理》后开始批评，直到去世才停止。伏尔泰于1727年参加牛顿葬礼后返回，感叹自己在伦敦留下了真空，却在笛卡尔哲学仍占主导地位的法国发现了充实空间（充满物质的空间）。解释“超距作用”的努力，一直持续到1900年。

Newton had good reason to emphasize quantitative mathematical laws as opposed to physical explanation because the central physical concept in his celestial mechanics was the force of gravitation and the action of this force could not be explained at all in physical terms. The concept of a gravitational force that attracted any two masses to each other even when separated by hundreds of millions of miles of empty space seemed as incredible as many of the qualities that the Aristotelians and medieval scholars had invented to account for scientific phenomena. The concept was especially repugnant to Newton’s contemporaries who insisted on mechanical explanations and had come to see force as the effect of contact between bodies wherein one body “pushes” another. The abandonment of physical mechanism in favor of mathematical description shocked even the greatest scientists. Huygens regarded the idea of gravitation as “absurd” because its action through empty space precluded any mechanism. He expressed surprise that Newton should have taken the trouble to make such a number of laborious calculations with no foundation but the mathematical principle of gravitation. Many others, including Leibniz, objected to the purely mathematical account of gravitation. Leibniz began his critique in 1690 after reading Newton’s Principia and he kept it up until he died. Voltaire returning from Newton’s funeral in 1727 remarked that he had left a vacuum in London and found a plenum (space filled with matter) in France, where Descartes’s philosophy still held sway. The attempts to explain “action at a distance” persisted until 1900.

但牛顿令人惊叹的贡献之所以可能，正因为他即使完全缺乏物理理解，也依靠数学描述。代替物理解释，他确实拥有描述引力如何作用的定量表述，既有意义，也可应用。因此，他在《原理》开头说：“因为在这里，我只打算给出这些力的数学概念，而不考虑其物理原因和所在。”在该书接近结尾处，他再次强调：

But Newton’s amazing contributions were made possible by his reliance on mathematical description even where physical understanding was completely lacking. In lieu of physical explanation, Newton did have a quantitative formulation of how gravity acted, which was significant and usable. And this is why he says at the beginning of his Principia, “For I here design only to give a mathematical notion of these forces, without considering their physical causes and seats.” And toward the end of the book he repeats this thought:

但我们的目的，只是从现象追究这种力的大小与性质，并把在某些简单情形中发现的东西用作原理，由此以数学方式估计它在更复杂情形中的效果。……我们说以数学方式［斜体为牛顿所加］，是为了避免一切关于这种力的本性或性质的问题；我们不希望被理解为用任何假说确定这些问题。……

But our purpose is only to trace out the quantity and properties of this force from the phenomena, and to apply what we discover in some simple cases as principles, by which, in a mathematical way, we may estimate the effects thereof in more involved cases. ... We said in a mathematical way [the italics are Newton’s], to avoid all questions about the nature or quality of this force, which we would not be understood to determine by any hypothesis. . . .

牛顿在1692年2月25日致理查德·本特利牧师博士的信中，确实写道：

In his letter of February 25, 1692 to the Reverend Dr. Richard Bentley, Newton did write:

认为引力是物质天赋、内在、本质的性质，使一个物体可以隔着真空，在没有任何其他媒介传递作用与力的情况下，远距离作用于另一个物体，在我看来如此荒谬，以至于我相信，凡在哲学问题上具有足够思考能力的人，都不可能陷入这种看法。引力必定由某种始终依照一定规律行动的作用者造成；但这一作用者是物质的还是非物质的，我留给读者考虑。

That gravity should be innate, inherent, essential to matter, so that one body may act upon another at a distance through a vacuum, without the mediation of anything else, by and through which the action and force may be conveyed from one to another, is to me so great an absurdity that I believe no man who has in philosophical matters a competent faculty of thinking can ever fall into it. Gravity must be caused by an agent acting constantly according to certain laws, but whether this agent be material or immaterial I have left to the consideration of my readers.

尽管牛顿在数学上取得成功，缺乏物理机制仍不断困扰科学家，而他们试图补足机制的努力并未成功。乔治·贝克莱主教在对话《阿尔西弗隆》（1732）中指出：

Despite Newton’s mathematical successes the absence of a physical mechanism continued to bother scientists but their efforts to supply one were not successful. Bishop George Berkeley in his dialogue Alcipbron (1732) made this point:

欧弗拉诺：……请容我恳求你，阿尔西弗隆，不要被

Euphranor: . . . Let me entreat you, Alciphron, be not amused by

术语迷惑；撇开“力”这个词，排除

terms: lay aside the word force, and exclude every other thing

思想中的一切其他东西，然后看看你对于

from your thoughts, and then see what precise idea you have of

力有何精确观念。 阿尔西弗隆：力是物体中产生运动与

force. Alciphron: Force is that in bodies which produceth motion and

其他可感效果的东西。 欧弗拉诺：那么，它是不同于这些效果的东西？ 阿尔西弗隆：是的。 欧弗拉诺：现在请排除对其作用主

other sensible effects. Euphranor: It is then something distinct from those effects? Alciphron: It is. Euphranor: Be pleased now to exclude the consideration of its sub¬

体和效果的考虑，依它自身的精确观念思考力

ject and effects, and contemplate force itself in its own precise

本身。 阿尔西弗隆：我承认，这并不是件容易的事。 欧弗拉诺回答：看来你我都不能形成观念的东西，按照你自己的话，人的心智与能力大体相同，那么我们可以认为，其他人也并不比我们更有关于它的观念。

idea. Alciphron: I profess I find it no such easy matter. And that, replied Euphranor, which it seems that neither you nor I can frame an idea of, by your own remark of men’s minds and faculties being made much alike, we may suppose others have no more an idea of than we.

牛顿确实希望引力的本性得到研究和认识。但与他的希望及普遍信念相反，从来没有人解释引力如何作用；这种力的物理实在性从未得到证明。它是一种由人能够施力而启发的科学虚构。不过，从定量规律作出的数学演绎如此有效，以至于这种方法被接受为物理科学不可分割的一部分。因此，科学所做的，是牺牲物理上的可理解性，换取数学描述与数学预测。

Newton did hope that the nature of the force of gravity would be investigated an d learned. Contrary to Newton’s hope and popular belief, no one has ever explained how gravity acts; the physical reality of this force has never been demonstrated. It is a scientific fiction suggested by the human ability to exert force. However, the mathematical deductions from the quantitative law proved so effective that this approach has been accepted as an integral part of physical science. What science has done, then, is to sacrifice physical intelligibility for mathematical description and mathematical prediction.

十七世纪的工作常被概括为：数学物理学家建立了机械世界图景，一个像机器一样运行的世界。当然，如果“机械”是指用重、轻、相感及前述其他力作用于粒子和有广延物体来描述运动，那么亚里士多德与中世纪科学家的物理学也是机械的。然而，十七世纪的人，尤其是笛卡尔学派，摒弃了前人为解释运动而假定的多种性质，把力限制为物质性而明显的东西：重量，或抛掷物体所需的力。可以把这种牛顿之前的物理学称为物质物理学。数学能作描述，却不是根本。

The work of the seventeenth century is often summarized by the statement that the mathematical physicists built up a mechanical world picture, a world operating like a machine. Of course the physics of Aristotle and of medieval scientists was also mechanical if one means by that word an account that describes motion by forces such as heaviness, lightness, sympathy, and others noted earlier, acting on particles and extended bodies. However, the men of the seventeenth century, the Cartesians especially, discarded the multiplicity of qualities that their predecessors had hypothesized to account for motion and restricted force to the material and obvious: weight or the force required to throw an object. One could call this pre-Newtonian physics a material physics. Mathematics could describe but was not fundamental.

因此，牛顿力学与旧力学的根本差别，并不在于引入数学描述物体行为。数学不只是以方便、简短、清楚且更一般的语言帮助物理学；它提供了基本概念。引力仅仅是一个数学符号的名称。同样，在牛顿运动第二定律（F = ma，即力等于质量乘以加速度）中，力是任何使质量产生加速度的东西。力本身的本性，在物理上可能无法认识。因此，牛顿谈到并使用向心力与离心力，尽管这些力的机制并不为人所知。

The essential difference between Newtonian mechanics and the older mechanics, then, was not the introduction of mathematics to describe the behavior of bodies. Mathematics was not just an aid to physics in the sense of a convenient, briefer, clearer, and more general language; rather it provided the fundamental concepts. Gravitational force is merely a name for a mathematical symbol. Likewise in Newton’s second law of motion (F = ma, force equals mass times acceleration) force is anything that gives acceleration to a mass. The nature of the force itself may be physically unknowable. Thus Newton spoke of and used centripetal and centrifugal forces though the mechanism of these forces is not known.

甚至质量概念，在牛顿力学中也是一种虚构。当然，质量就是物质，而物质是真实的，正如塞缪尔·约翰逊踢一块石头所“证明”的。但对牛顿来说，质量的首要性质是惯性，其意义由运动第一定律表达：若无力作用于某个质量，它若静止，就保持静止；若运动，就以恒定速度沿直线运动。为什么是直线？为什么不是圆？实际上，伽利略确实相信惯性运动是圆周运动。而为什么应该以恒定速度运动？没有力作用时，为什么这个质量不总是静止，或以恒定加速度运动？惯性性质是虚构的概念，而不是实验事实。没有任何质量完全不受力。牛顿运动定律中唯一的物理实在要素是加速度。我们能观察并测量物体的加速度。

Even the notion of mass is a fiction in Newtonian mechanics. To be sure, mass is matter and matter is real as Samuel Johnson “demonstrated” by kicking a stone. But for Newton the primary property of mass is inertia whose meaning is expressed in Newton’s first law of motion, namely, that if no force acts on a mass and if it is at rest it will remain at rest, and if it is in motion it will move in a straight line at a constant velocity. Why a straight line? Why not a circle? Indeed Galileo did believe that inertial motion is circular. And why should it move at a constant velocity? Why if no force acts does not the mass always remain at rest or move with a constant acceleration? The property of inertia is a fictitious concept and not an experimental fact. No mass is free of all forces. The only element of physical reality in Newton’s laws of motion is acceleration. We can observe and measure the acceleration of objects.

无论多么不情愿放弃物理解释，牛顿通过运用数学概念、定量表述，以及从所得公式作出的数学演绎，重塑了十七世纪的整个物理学*。他的巅峰著作向人类呈现了新的世界秩序：整个宇宙受一组共同的、只能用数学表达的物理原理控制。这个宏伟方案涵盖石块下落、海洋潮汐、行星及其卫星的运动、彗星桀骜不驯的飞掠，以及星空球体辉煌而庄严的运动。牛顿方案对使世界相信自然按照数学设计、自然真正的规律是数学规律，起了决定性作用。牛顿的《原理》是物理解释的墓志铭。拉普拉斯曾说，牛顿是一个极其幸运的人，因为宇宙只有一个，而他成功找到了它的规律。

However reluctantly he abandoned physical explanation, Newton recast the entire body of seventeenth-century physics by employing mathematical concepts, their quantitative formulation, and mathematical deductions from the resulting formulas.* Newton’s crowning work presented mankind with a new world order, a universe controlled throughout by a common set of only mathematically expressible physical principles. Here was a majestic scheme which embraced the fall of a stone, the tides of the oceans, the motions of the planets and their moons, the defiant sweep of the comets, and the brilliant, stately motion of the sphere of stars. The Newtonian scheme was decisive in convincing the world that nature is mathematically designed and that the true laws of nature are mathematical. Newton’s Principles is an epitaph to physical explanation. Laplace once remarked that Newton was a most fortunate man because there was just one universe and he had succeeded in finding its laws.

整个十八世纪，数学家——他们同时也是主要的科学家——都沿着牛顿的计划前进。拉格朗日1788年的《分析力学》，可视为牛顿数学方法的最佳范例。该书完全用数学处理力学，几乎不提物理过程。事实上，拉格朗日自豪地说，他不需要这些过程，甚至不需要几何图形。研究流体动力学、弹性力学、电学和磁学等更新的物理分支时，人们采用的，仍是牛顿处理力学与天文学的方法。定量的数学方法成为科学的本质，而真理最可靠地存在于数学之中。

Throughout the eighteenth century, the mathematicians, who were also the major scientists, pursued Newton’s plan. Lagrange’s Analytical Mechanics of 1788 may be regarded as the prime example of Newton’s mathematical approach. In this book, mechanics was treated entirely mathematically. There was little reference to physical processes. In fact, Lagrange boasted that he had no need of these or even of geometrical diagrams. As newer branches of physics—hydrodynamics, elasticity, electricity, and magnetism—were tackled, it was Newton’s approach to mechanics and astronomy that was adopted. The quantitative, mathematical method became the essence of science, and truth resided most securely in mathematics.

充满革新精神的十七世纪，面对的是一个定性的世界，对它的研究由数学描述来辅助。它留给后世的，却是一个数学的、定量的世界，以数学公式取代物理世界的具体性。这是自然数学化的开端，而这一进程至今仍蓬勃发展。詹姆斯·金斯爵士在《神秘的宇宙》（1930）中说：“宇宙的伟大建筑师，如今开始显得像一位纯数学家。”他至少落后于时代两个世纪。

The insurgent seventeenth century found a qualitative world whose study was aided by mathematical description. It bequeathed to posterity a mathematical, quantitative world which substituted mathematical formulas for the concreteness of the physical world. It was the beginning of the mathematization of nature which flourishes to this very day. When Sir James Jeans remarked in The Mysterious Universe (1930), “The Great Architect of the Universe now begins to appear as a pure mathematician,” he was at least two centuries behind the times.

*在《光学》中，牛顿确实给出了物理解释。然而，这些解释不足以说明光的全部行为。

*In his Opticks Newton did give physical explanations. However, they were not adequate to explain all of the behavior of light.

虽然如前所述，牛顿本人对单纯依赖没有物理解释支持的数学公式感到不安，但他不仅倡导自然哲学（物理科学）的数学原理，而且确实相信，它真实地描述了那些现象。这一确信从何而来？答案是，牛顿像同时代所有数学家与科学家一样，相信上帝按照数学原理设计了世界。他在《光学》（1704）中，对上帝作为宇宙创造者而存在的经典论证，表述得极为雄辩：

Though, as we have noted, Newton himself was not at ease about relying solely upon mathematical formulas unsupported by physical explanations, he nevertheless not only advocated his mathematical principles of natural philosophy (physical science) but certainly believed it to be a true account of the phenomena he described. Whence came the conviction? The answer is that Newton like all the mathematicians and scientists of his day believed that God designed the world in accordance with mathematical principles. Most eloquent is Newton’s statement in his Opticks (1704) of the classic argument for the existence of God as the framer of the universe:

自然哲学的主要任务，是从现象进行论证，不虚构假说，并从结果推导原因，直到抵达最初的原因，而那肯定不是机械性的。……几乎没有物质的地方存在着什么？太阳与行星之间没有稠密物质，为什么仍相互吸引？自然为什么从不徒劳行事？我们在世界中看到的一切秩序与美，又从何而来？彗星有何目的？行星为什么都沿同心轨道向同一方向运动？是什么阻止恒星彼此坠落到一起？动物身体怎么会构造得如此巧妙，其各部分又各有何目的？眼睛是没有光学技艺就被造出来的吗？耳朵是没有声音知识就被造出来的吗？身体运动如何遵循意志？动物的本能从何而来？……正确考察这些问题之后，现象岂不表明：存在一个无形、活着、有智力、无所不在的存在者，他在无限空间中，如同在自己的感觉器官中，亲密地看见事物本身，彻底感知它们，并因它们直接呈现在他面前而完全理解它们？

The main business of natural philosophy is to argue from phenomena without feigning hypotheses, and to deduce causes from effects, till we come to the very first, which certainly is not mechanical. . . . What is there in places almost empty of matter, and whence is it that the sun and planets gravitate towards one another, without dense matter between them? Whence is it that nature doth nothing in vain; and whence arises all the order and beauty we see in the world? To what end are comets, and whence is it that planets move all one and the same way in orbs concentric, and what hinders the fixed stars from falling upon one another? How came the bodies of animals to be contrived with so much art, and for what ends were their several parts?” Was the eye contrived without skill in optics, or the ear without knowledge of sounds? How do the motions of the body follow from the will, and whence is the instinct in animals? . . . And these things being rightly dispatched, does it not appear from phenomena that there is a being incorporeal, living, intelligent, omnipresent, who, in infinite space, as it were in his sensory, sees the things themselves intimately, and thoroughly perceives them; and comprehends them wholly by their immediate presence to himself?

牛顿在《自然哲学的数学原理》第三版中，回答了自己的问题：

In the third edition of his Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy, Newton answers his own questions:

这个由太阳、行星与彗星组成的至美体系，只能来自某个有智力、强大存在者的谋划与统治。……这个存在者治理一切，并非作为世界的灵魂，而是作为万物之主。……

This most beautiful system of sun, planets, and comets could only proceed from the counsel and dominion of an intelligent and powerful Being. . . . This Being governs all things, not as the Soul of the world, but as Lord over all. . . .

牛顿也确信，上帝是一位技艺高超的数学家与物理学家。他在1692年12月10日致理查德·本特利牧师的信中说：

Newton was convinced, too, that God was a skilled mathematician and physicist. He said in a letter to the Reverend Richard Bentley of December 10, 1692,

因此，要创造这个［太阳］体系及其全部运动，需要一个原因，能够理解并相互比较太阳与行星各自的物质量，以及由此产生的引力；各大行星到太阳的距离，以及次级行星［即卫星］到土星、木星和地球的距离；还有这些行星能够绕中心天体中相应物质量旋转的速度。能在如此多样的天体中，一并比较并调节所有这些因素，说明这一原因并非盲目或偶然，而是极其精通力学与几何。

To make this [solar] system, therefore, with all its motions, required a cause which understood, and compared together the quantities of matter in the several bodies of the sun and planets, and the gravitating powers resulting from thence; the several distances of the primary planets from the sun, and of the secondary ones [i.e., moons] from Saturn, Jupiter, and the earth; and the velocities with which these planets could revolve about those quantities of matter in the central bodies; and to compare and adjust all these things together in so great a variety of bodies, argues that cause to be not blind or fortuitous, but very skilled in mechanics and geometry.

科学应当揭示上帝荣耀的设计。牛顿给本特利的同一封信，以这个想法开篇：“我撰写关于我们体系的论著［《自然哲学的数学原理》］时，注意的是那些可能使深思之人信仰神的原理；发现它有助于这个目的，没有什么比这更令我高兴。”牛顿的通信中还有许多类似信件。

Science should uncover God’s glorious designs. Newton began the same letter to Bentley with this thought: “When I wrote my treatise about our system [The Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy], I had an eye on such principles as might work with considering men for the belief in a Deity; and nothing can rejoice me more than to find it useful for that purpose.” There are many other such letters in Newton’s correspondence.

牛顿的宗教兴趣，是其数学与科学工作的真正动力。他首先相信，基督教教义是上帝的启示。上帝是一切自然力、一切存在与发生之事的原因。神的意图、引导与控制，存在于所有现象中。从年轻时起，牛顿就批判性地研究并解释宗教著作，晚年则完全投身神学。他的《论〈但以理书〉的预言与〈圣约翰启示录〉》（1733年出版）和《古代王国编年史订正》（未出版）仍然存在，还有数百篇他试图确定《圣经》事件年代的手稿。科学是一种崇拜形式，尽管科学工作本身应当排除神秘或超自然力量。牛顿本人欣喜于自己的工作揭示了全能上帝的手。他认为，加强宗教基础远比科学与数学成就重要，因为后者仅限于展示上帝对自然世界的设计。他常为艰难、有时枯燥的科学工作辩护，因为他觉得它通过提供上帝在宇宙中安排秩序的证据，支持了宗教。这与研究《圣经》同样虔诚。揭示宇宙结构，可以彰显上帝的智慧。上帝也是一切发生之事的原因。因此，奇迹不过是上帝偶尔干预宇宙的通常运行。上帝有时也可能必须介入，纠正某种运行故障，如同钟表匠修理钟表。

Newton’s religious interests were the true motivation of his mathematical and scientific work. He believed first of all that the doctrines of Christianity were a revelation from God. God was the cause of all natural forces, of everything that exists and happens. Divine intent, guidance, and control were present in all phenomena. From his youth on, Newton made critical studies and interpretations of religious writings and late in life devoted himself entirely to theology. His books Observations on the Prophecies of Daniel and the Apocalypse of St. John (published in 1733) and The Chronology of Ancient Kingdoms Amended (not published) are extant, as are hundreds of manuscript papers in which he attempted to fix the chronology of Biblical events. Science was a form of worship though the scientific work proper was to be kept free of mystical or supernatural forces. Newton himself rejoiced that his work revealed the hand of an omnipotent God. He considered strengthening the foundations of religion far more important than scientific and mathematical achievements, for the latter were restricted to displaying God’s design of the natural world only. He often justified the hard and at times dreary scientific work because he felt it supported religion by providing evidence of God’s order in the universe. It was as pious a pursuit as the study of the Scriptures. The wisdom of God could be manifested by disclosing the structure of the universe. God was also the cause of whatever happened. Thus miracles were only God’s occasional intervention in the usual functioning of the universe. God might also occasionally have to intervene to correct some malfunctioning, much as a watchmaker might repair clocks.

如果上帝设计了宇宙、数学与科学的作用是揭示这一设计的信念还需要加强，那么戈特弗里德·威廉·莱布尼茨（1646—1716）提供了这种加强。和笛卡尔一样，他首先是一位哲学家，而且更加多才多艺；他对数学、科学、历史、逻辑、法律、外交与神学的贡献，都是第一流的。和牛顿一样，他认为科学是科学家有义务承担的宗教使命。在一封1699或1700年未注明日期的信中，他写道：“在我看来，全人类的主要目标，必须是认识并展开上帝的奇迹；这也是上帝把地球的统治权赋予人的原因。”

If the belief that God has designed the universe and that the role of mathematics and science was to uncover that design needed any reinforcement, it was provided by Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1646-1716). Like Descartes, Leibniz was primarily a philosopher and even more versatile; his contributions to mathematics, science, history, logic, law, diplomacy, and theology were first-rate. Like Newton, Leibniz regarded science as a religious mission which scientists were duty bound to undertake. In an undated letter of 1699 or 1700 he wrote, “It seems to me that the principal goal of the whole of mankind must be the knowledge and development of the wonders of God, and that this is the reason that God gave him the empire of the globe.”

在《神义论》（1710）中，他肯定了当时已很熟悉的思想：上帝是创造这个精心设计世界的智者。他以世界与上帝的统一，解释真实世界与数学世界的协调，并最终捍卫数学对真实世界的适用性。Cum Deus calculat, fit mundus（上帝计算之时，世界便被创造）。数学与自然之间存在预定和谐。宇宙是可设想的最完美者，是一切可能世界中最好的世界，而理性思考揭示它的规律。

In his Essais de Tbeodicee (1710), he affirmed the by that time familiar thought that God is the intelligence who created this carefully designed world. His explanation of the concord between the real and the mathematical worlds, and his ultimate defense of the applicability of mathematics to the real world, was the unity of the world and God. Cum Deus calculat, fit mundus (as God calculates, so the world is made). There is a pre-established harmony between mathematics and nature. The universe is the most perfect conceivable, the best of all possible worlds, and rational thinking discloses its laws.

真正的知识天赋于我们的心智，不过与柏拉图不同，并不是由于某种先前的存在。感官决不能教给我们必然真理，如上帝存在，或所有直角都相等。因此，数学公理是天赋真理，力学、光学等演绎科学的基本原理也是如此；在这些科学中，“为了形成关于感性事物的确定观念，感官当然十分必要；为了确立某些事实，实验也是必要的。……但证明的力量，取决于可理解的观念与真理，唯有它们能使我们辨认必然之物。……”

True knowledge is innate in our minds though not, contrary to Plato, because of some prior existence. The senses could never teach us necessary truths such as that God exists or that all right angles are equal. Thus the axioms of mathematics are innate truths as are the fundamental principles of the deductive sciences such as mechanics and optics, “in which to be sure the senses are very necessary, in order to have certain ideas of sensible things, and experiments are necessary to establish certain facts. . . . But the force of the demonstrations depends upon intelligible notions and truths, which alone are capable of making us discern what is necessary. . . .”

莱布尼茨的数学与科学工作广泛而有价值，我们后面还有机会进一步讨论。不过，与笛卡尔有些相似，他的贡献在于技术。他对微积分与微分方程开端的研究，以及对某些正在形成的概念——如我们如今所谓动能——的重要性的认识，都是最高水平的。但他没有贡献新的基本自然规律。相反，最能推动人类追求真理的，是他的科学哲学，其中数学的作用是根本性的。

Leibniz’s mathematical and scientific work was extensive and valuable and we shall have occasion to say more about it later. However, somewhat like Descartes’s, his contributions were to technique. His work in the calculus and in the beginnings of differential equations and his recognition of the importance of some emerging concepts such as what we now call kinetic energy were of the highest order. But Leibniz did not contribute any new fundamental laws of nature. Rather it was his philosophy of science, in which the role of mathematics was fundamental, that was most important in spurring on man’s search for truths.

虽然十八世纪的人极大扩展了数学与数学科学，但就使思想界相信数学及科学的数学规律是真理而言，他们的工作主要是一场续演。伯努利家族的几位成员——尤其是詹姆斯（1665—1705）与约翰（1667—1748）兄弟，以及约翰之子丹尼尔（1700—1782）——莱昂哈德·欧拉（1707—1783）、让·勒朗·达朗贝尔（1717—1783）、约瑟夫—路易·拉格朗日（1736—1813）、皮埃尔—西蒙·拉普拉斯（1749—1827）及许多其他人，继续对自然作数学研究。在数学本身中，他们都继续发展微积分技术，并创立了全新的分支，尤其是常微分方程、偏微分方程、微分几何、变分法、无穷级数与复变函数。这些本身被接受为真理，也为自然研究提供了更强大的工具。欧拉于1741年说：“通常人们承认数学的初等部分有用；这种用处不仅没有在高等数学中终止，事实上，随着这门科学越发展，其用处越大。”

Though the men of the 18th century extended vastly both mathematics and the mathematical sciences, insofar as convincing the intellectuals that mathematics and the mathematical laws of science are truths is concerned, their work was largely an encore. The several Bernoullis— especially the brothers James (1665-1705) and John (1667-1748) and John’s son Daniel (1700-1782)—Leonhard Euler (1707-1783), Jean Le Rond d’Alembert (1717-1783), Joseph-Louis Lagrange (1736-1813), Pierre-Simon Laplace (1749-1827), and many others continued the mathematical investigation of nature. In mathematics proper all of these men continued the development of the techniques of the calculus and created totally new branches, notably ordinary and partial differential equations, differential geometry, the calculus of variations, infinite series, and functions of a complex variable. These were in themselves accepted as truths but also furnished more powerful tools for the investigation of nature. As Euler put it in 1741: “The usefulness of mathematics, commonly allowed to its elementary parts, not only does not stop in higher mathematics but is in fact so much greater, the further that science is developed.”

这些数学工作的目标，是获得更多自然规律，更深入理解自然设计。成功既众多又深刻。最大的努力在于天文学，即推进牛顿描述并预测天体运动的工作。牛顿的主要理论推导，是行星轨道为椭圆；他很清楚，只有天上存在太阳与一颗行星时，这才正确。但牛顿时代以及十八世纪大部分时期，已知有六颗行星；它们相互吸引，又全都被太阳吸引。而且，地球、木星与土星还有卫星。因此，椭圆轨道受到摄动。精确轨道是什么？十八世纪所有伟大数学家都研究过这个问题。

The goal of this mathematical work was the attainment of more laws of nature, a deeper penetration of nature’s design. And the successes were numerous and profound. The greatest effort was in astronomy, to carry further the work of Newton in describing and predicting the motions of the heavenly bodies. Newton’s chief theoretical derivation, that the path of a planet is an ellipse, is, as he well knew, correct only were the sun and just one planet in the heavens. But in Newton’s days and during most of the eighteenth century, six planets were known; each attracts the others and all are attracted by the sun. Moreover, some—the earth, Jupiter, and Saturn—have moons. Hence the elliptical path is perturbed. What are the precise paths? All the great mathematicians of the eighteenth century worked on this problem.

问题的核心，是三个天体彼此之间的引力作用。如果能设计一种程序确定第三个天体的摄动影响，就可以用它确定第四个天体的摄动影响，如此继续。然而，即使一般的三体运动问题，其精确解至今也没有获得。取而代之的，是人们设计出越来越好的近似程序。

The core of this problem is the question of the mutual gravitational effects of three bodies on each other. If one could devise a procedure to determine the perturbing effect of a third body, this procedure could be used to determine the perturbing effect of a fourth body, and so on. However, exact solution of the general problem of the motion of even three bodies has not been obtained even today. Instead, better and better approximate procedures were devised.

即使用近似方法，十八世纪的成功仍非凡。天文学数学工作精确性最具戏剧性的证明之一，是阿列克西—克洛德·克莱罗（1713—1765）对哈雷彗星回归的预测。几个人都曾观察到这颗彗星，哈雷于1682年试图确定其轨道。他预测它将于1758年回归。1758年11月14日，克莱罗在巴黎科学院会议上宣布，哈雷彗星将于1759年4月中旬重新到达离太阳最近的位置，可能误差为三十天。彗星提前一个月出现。一个月的误差可能显得很大，但彗星至多只能被观察几天，而这颗彗星已经七十七年没有被看到了。

Even with approximate methods the successes of the eighteenth century were remarkable. One of the most dramatic proofs of the accuracy of the mathematical work in astronomy is the prediction by Alexis-Claude Clairaut (1713-1765) of the return of what had been known as Halley’s comet. This comet had been observed by several men, and Halley in 1682 attempted to determine its orbit. He predicted that it would return in 1758. On November 14, 1758, Clairaut announced at a session of the Paris Academy of Sciences that Halley’s comet would return to its position nearest the sun in the middle of April 1759, with a possible error of thirty days. The comet appeared one month ahead of schedule. The error of one month may seem enormous but comets can be observed for only a few days at most and this one had not been seen for seventy-seven years.

天文学的另一重大成功，来自拉格朗日与拉普拉斯的工作。人们在月球与行星运动中观察到若干不规则性。这可能意味着某颗行星会离太阳越来越远，或落入太阳。拉格朗日与拉普拉斯证明，已观察到的木星与土星速度中的不规则性是周期性的，因此其运动基本稳定。这个世纪的工作，汇集于科学杰作之一，拉普拉斯的《天体力学》，它从1799年至1825年以五卷形式出版。

Another of the great successes in astronomy was due to the work of Lagrange and Laplace. A number of irregularities had been observed in the motions of the earth’s moon and the planets. These irregularities could mean that a planet might move farther and farther from the sun or move into the sun. Lagrange and Laplace proved that the irregularities that had been observed in the velocities of Jupiter and Saturn were periodic so that basically their motions were stable. The work of the century is embodied in one of the masterpieces of science, Laplace’s Celestial Mechanics, which appeared in five volumes from 1799 to 1825.

事实上，拉普拉斯把一生都奉献给天文学；他研究的每个数学分支，都打算应用于天文学。众所周知，他写作时常省略困难的数学步骤，只说“很容易看出……”。这件事真正说明的是，他对数学细节缺乏耐心，想赶快进行应用。他对数学的诸多基本贡献，是其伟大自然哲学工作的副产品，并由其他人进一步发展。

In fact Laplace devoted his entire life to astronomy, and every branch of mathematics he investigated he intended for application to astronomy. The story is well known that in his writings he often omitted difficult mathematical steps and said, “It is easy to see. . . .” The real point of this story is that he was impatient with mathematical details and wanted to get on with the application. His many, basic contributions to mathematics were by-products of his great work in natural philosophy and were developed by others.

同样戏剧性的是，人们常讲的海王星发现故事。虽然发现发生于1846年，却以十八世纪的数学工作为基础。1781年，威廉·赫歇尔用一架强大的新望远镜发现天王星。但天王星轨道不符合预测。阿列克西·布瓦尔提出假说：还有一颗未知行星正在摄动天王星运动。人们多次尝试通过观察，或计算其可能大小与轨道，寻找这颗行星。1841年，剑桥大学二十二岁的学生约翰·柯西·亚当斯（1811—1892），能够相当准确地估计这颗推测行星的质量、位置与轨道。格林尼治皇家天文台台长、著名的乔治·艾里爵士得知后，却拒绝关注。但另一位年轻天文学家，法国人于尔班·J.J.勒威耶（1811—1877），独立完成了与亚当斯大致相同的工作，并把寻找行星的一套指示寄给德国天文学家约翰·伽勒。伽勒于1846年9月23日收到信息，当晚就在距勒威耶预测方向仅52角秒的地方发现海王星。使如此惊人、精确到百分之一万分之一以内的预测成为可能的天文学理论，其真理性怎能受到怀疑？

Equally dramatic is the oft-told account of the discovery of the planet Neptune. Though it took place in 1846, the discovery was based on eighteenth-century mathematical work. In 1781 William Herschel, using a powerful new telescope, discovered the planet Uranus. But the path of Uranus did not adhere to predictions. The hypothesis was advanced by Alexis Bouvard that still another unknown planet was perturbing the motion of Uranus. Many attempts were made to locate such a planet by observation or by calculations of its possible size and path. In 1841 John Couch Adams (1811-1892), a twenty-two-year-old student at Cambridge University, was able to make a close estimate of the mass, position, and path of the conjectured planet. When informed of this work, the eminent Sir George Airy, director of the Royal Astronomical Observatory at Greenwich, refused to pay attention to it. But another young astronomer, the Frenchman Urbain J. J. Leverrier (1811-1877), having independently done about the same thing as Adams, sent a set of directions for locating the planet to the German astronomer Johann Galle. Galle received the information on September 23, 1846, and that very evening discovered Neptune only 52 seconds of arc away from the direction predicted by Leverrier. How could one doubt the truth of an astronomical theory which made possible such remarkable predictions, indeed predictions accurate to within one ten-thousandth of a percent?

除天文学之外，早在希腊时代就已在一定程度上接受数学处理的科学，是光学。十七世纪初显微镜与望远镜的发明，激起了人们对光学的巨大兴趣；如同希腊时代，十七与十八世纪每位数学家都在这个领域工作过。我们已指出，十七世纪的斯涅尔与笛卡尔找到了托勒密徒劳寻求的光折射定律：光通过介质突变界面，例如从空气进入水时，如何运动。奥勒·罗默（1644—1710）注意到光速有限；牛顿发现白光是从红到紫各种颜色的混合，又激起了对光学的大量兴趣。牛顿的《光学》（1704）极大推进了这一学科，并帮助改进显微镜与望远镜。在这里，数学也仍是主要工具。十八世纪，人们深入研究光学，欧拉三卷本的光学著作是另一座里程碑。

Beyond astronomy, the science which had already yielded somewhat to mathematical treatment even in Greek times was optics. The early seventeenth-century inventions of the microscope and the telescope stimulated enormous interest in optics and, as in Greek times, every mathematician of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries worked in this area. We have already noted that in the seventeenth century Snell and Descartes had found what Ptolemy had sought in vain, the law of refraction of light: how light behaves when it moves through an abrupt change in media, as from air to water. The fact that light has a finite velocity was noted by Olaus Roemer (1644-1710), and Newton’s discovery that white light is a composite of all colors from red to violet stimulated enormous additional interest in optics. Newton’s Opticks (1704) advanced this subject immensely and contributed to the improvement of microscopes and telescopes. Here, too, mathematics was the major instrument. In the eighteenth century the subject was pursued intensively, and Euler’s three-volume work on optics is another landmark.

光的物理本性远非清楚。牛顿认为光是粒子的运动，惠更斯谈波动，却又几乎不是通常意义的波；欧拉首次用数学处理光的振动，并推导运动方程。他倡导光的波动本性，是唯一反对牛顿的人；十九世纪初奥古斯丁—让·菲涅耳与托马斯·杨的工作，证明了他这一主张。但即使那时，光的本性也并未变得更清楚，数学规律仍是支柱。如今接受的光理论，即电磁理论，还要五十年才会出现。

The physical nature of light was by no means clear. Whereas Newton thought that light was a motion of particles and Huygens spoke of wave motion though hardly in the sense of waves—Euler was the first to treat the vibrations of light mathematically and to derive the equations of motion. In his advocacy of the wave nature of light he was the only one to oppose Newton and was vindicated by the early nineteenth-century work of Augustin-Jean Fresnel and Thomas Young. But the nature of light did not become any clearer even then and mathematical laws remained the mainstay. The currently accepted theory of light, the electromagnetic theory, was still fifty years in the future.

十八世纪开辟了几个新的研究领域，并至少取得部分成功。其中第一个，是乐音的数学描述与分析。这里的故事较长，始于研究振动琴弦——小提琴弦——发出的声音。丹尼尔·伯努利、达朗贝尔、欧拉与拉格朗日各有贡献，但也对某些数学分析激烈争论。虽然直到十九世纪初约瑟夫·傅里叶（1768—1830）开展工作后，争论才获解决，十八世纪仍取得巨大进展。我们如今知道，每个乐音都由基音或第一谐波，以及更高次谐波构成；所有高次谐波的频率（音乐术语中的音高）都是基频的整数倍。这一认识在十八世纪大师们的工作中得到确证。它是今天设计电话、留声机、无线电与电视等一切录制和传输设备的基础。

During the eighteenth century several new fields of investigation were opened and at least partial successes achieved. The first of these was the mathematical description and analysis of musical sounds. The story here is somewhat lengthy. It began with the study of sounds given off by a vibrating string, a violin string. Daniel Bernoulli, d’Alembert, Euler, and Lagrange each made contributions but also had sharp disagreements on some of the mathematical analysis. Although the controversies were not settled until Joseph Fourier (1768-1830) did his work in the early nineteenth century, enormous progress was made in the eighteenth century nevertheless. Our present understanding that every musical sound consists of a fundamental or first harmonic and higher harmonics whose frequencies (pitches, in musical terminology) are all integral multiples of the frequency of the fundamental was established conclusively in the work of the eighteenth-century masters. This understanding is basic in the design today of all recording and transmitting instruments such as the telephone, phonograph, radio, and television.

十八世纪至少还开创了另一数学物理分支：研究流体（液体与气体）的流动，以及物体在流体中的运动。牛顿已经考虑并处理过一个问题：物体应具有何种形状，才能以最小阻力在流体中前进。奠基性经典是丹尼尔·伯努利的《流体动力学》（1738）；他顺便指出，这一理论可能用于描述血液在人类动脉与静脉中的流动。随后，欧拉在一篇基本论文（1755）中推导了可压缩流体的运动方程。他在文中说：

Still another branch of mathematical physics was at least initiated in the eighteenth century, the study of the flow of fluids (liquids and gases) and the motion of bodies in fluids. Newton had already considered and treated the problem of what shape a body should have in order to move forward in a fluid with least resistance. The founding classic was Daniel Bernoulli’s Hydrodynamica (1738) in which, incidentally, he noted that the theory might be used to describe the flow of blood in human arteries and veins. It was followed by a basic paper of Euler’s (1755) in which he derived the equations for the motion of compressible fluids. In this paper Euler said:

如果我们不能达到对流体运动的完整认识，原因不应归于力学，也不应归于已知运动原理不足。在这里，抛弃我们的是［数学］分析本身，因为整个流体运动理论，刚刚已被归结为求解分析公式。

If it is not permitted to us to penetrate to a complete knowledge concerning the motion of fluids, it is not to mechanics, or to the insufficiency of the known principles of motion, that we must attribute the cause. It is [mathematical] analysis itself which abandons us here, since all the theory of the motion of fluids has just been reduced to the solution of analytic formulas.

实际上，流体理论远比欧拉所设想的丰富，大约七十年后又增添了许多内容。欧拉忽略了黏性。（水流动自如，是无黏性的；而例如油流动缓慢，具有一定黏性。）尽管如此，仍可说欧拉创立了流体动力学，这门科学适用于船舶与飞机的运动。

Actually, there is much more to the theory of fluids than Euler envisaged, which was added some seventy years later. Euler neglected viscosity. (Water flows freely and is non-viscous, whereas oil, for example, flows sluggishly and is somewhat viscous.) Nevertheless, Euler can be said to have founded the science of hydrodynamics which applies to the motion of ships and airplanes.

如果十八世纪的人还需要更多证据，证明世界按照数学、而且以最高效的方式设计，上帝确实是自然一切运行的建筑师，那么他们在另一项数学发现中找到了证据。希罗已证明（第I章），光从点P经镜面反射到点Q，采取最短路径。由于在这种情形中光以恒定速率传播，最短路径也意味着最短时间。

If men of the eighteenth century needed any additional evidence that the world was mathematically and indeed most efficiently designed and that God was surely the architect of all the workings of nature, they found it in another mathematical discovery. Heron had proved (Chapter I) that light in going from a point P to a point Q via reflection from a mirror takes the shortest path. Since the light travels in such a situation at a constant velocity, the shortest path also means least time.

十七世纪，数学巨人之一皮埃尔·德·费马（1601—1665），依据相当有限的证据，提出最短时间原理，肯定光从一点到另一点时，总走所需时间最短的路径。显然，上帝安排光不仅遵循数学规律，而且以最高效的方式传播。当费马成功从这一原理推导出先前斯涅尔与笛卡尔发现的光折射定律时，他更加确信这一原理正确。

In the seventeenth century Pierre de Format (1601-1665), one of the giants of mathematics, had asserted on the basis of rather limited evidence his Principle of Least Time, which affirms that light in traveling from one point to another always takes the path requiring least time. Apparently God had arranged that light not only obey mathematical laws but travel most efficiently. Fermat became all the more convinced of the correctness of his principle when he succeeded in deriving from it the law of refraction of light previously discovered by Willebrord Snell and Descartes.

到十八世纪初，数学家已有几个令人印象深刻的实例，表明自然确实试图使某些重要量最大或最小。最初反对费马原理的克里斯蒂安·惠更斯，证明该原理确实适用于性质连续变化的介质中的光传播。甚至牛顿运动第一定律——不受任何力干扰的运动物体沿直线，即最短路径前进——也体现了自然的节约性。

By the early eighteenth century mathematicians had several impressive examples of the fact that nature does attempt to maximize or minimize some important quantities. Christian Huygens, who had at first objected to Fermat’s principle, showed that it does hold for the propagation of light in media with continuously changing character. Even Newton’s first law of motion, which states that an object in motion and undisturbed by any force follows a straight line—the shortest path—is an example of nature’s economy.

十八世纪的人确信，完美宇宙不会容忍浪费，因此自然的作用应当是达到目的所需的最小作用，于是开始寻找一般原理。首先表述这种原理的是皮埃尔—路易·莫罗·德·莫佩尔蒂（1698—1759）。他主要是一位数学家，曾率队赴拉普兰，测量子午线上一度的长度。他的测量显示，地球确实在两极扁平，正如牛顿与惠更斯根据理论论证所得的结论。这一发现驳倒了让—多米尼克·卡西尼及其子雅克的相反论点。莫佩尔蒂因此被称为“压扁地球的人”；或者如伏尔泰所说，他压扁了地球，也压扁了卡西尼父子。

The men of the eighteenth century were convinced that, since a perfect universe would not tolerate waste, the action of nature should be the least required to achieve its purposes and a search for a general principle was undertaken. The first formulation of such a principle was offered by Pierre-Louis Moreau de Maupertuis (1698-1759), who was primarily a mathematician and had led an expedition to Lapland to measure the length of one degree along a meridian. His measurement showed that the earth is indeed flattened at the poles as Newton and Huygens had concluded from theoretical arguments. Maupertuis’s findings disposed of the contrary arguments of Jean-Dominique Cassini and his son Jacques. Maupertuis was dubbed the “earth-flattener,” or, as Voltaire put it, Maupertuis flattened the earth and the Cassinis.

1744年，研究光理论时，他在题为《此前看来不相容的不同自然规律的协调》的论文中，提出了著名的最小作用原理。他从费马原理出发，但当时人们争论，光在例如水中是否比空气中更快（笛卡尔与牛顿如此认为），还是更慢（费马如此认为）；因此，他放弃最短时间，代之以作用量概念。他说，作用量是质量、速度与所经过距离之乘积的积分（微积分意义上的积分），自然发生的任何事情，都使作用量最小。他未说明应在哪个时间区间内取这一乘积，而且在光学及某些力学问题的每项应用中，都赋予作用量不同含义，因此表述有些含糊。

In 1744, while working with the theory of light, he propounded his famous principle of least action in a paper entitled “Accord of different laws of nature which hitherto had appeared incompatible.” He worked from Fermat’s principle but, in view of disagreements at that time as to whether the velocity of light was greater in water, say, than in air (as Descartes and Newton believed) or smaller (as Fermat believed), Maupertuis abandoned least time and substituted the concept of action. Action, Maupertuis said, is the integral (in the calculus sense) of the product of mass, velocity, and distance traversed, and any happenings in nature are such as to make the action least. Maupertuis was somewhat vague in failing to specify the time interval over which the product was to be taken and in assigning a different meaning to action in each of the applications he made to optics and some problems of mechanics.

虽然有某些物理实例支持其原理，莫佩尔蒂也因神学理由倡导它。物质行为的规律，必须具备与上帝创造相称的完美性；最小作用原理似乎符合标准，因为它表明自然是节约的。他宣称，这一原理是普遍自然规律，也是关于上帝存在与智慧的第一个科学证明。

Though he had some physical examples to support his principle, Maupertuis advocated it also for theological reasons. The laws of the behavior of matter had to possess the perfection worthy of God’s creation and the least action principle seemed to satisfy the criterion because it showed that nature was economical. Maupertuis proclaimed his principle to be a universal law of nature and the first scientific proof of the existence and wisdom of God.

十八世纪最伟大的数学家莱昂哈德·欧拉，在1740年至1744年间曾就这一主题与莫佩尔蒂通信。他同意，上帝必定按照某种这样的基本原理构造宇宙，而原理的存在证明了上帝之手。他这样表达确信：“既然宇宙的结构最为完美，是至为睿智的创造者的作品，那么宇宙中发生的任何事情，都必定体现某种最大或最小的规则。”

Leonhard Euler, the greatest of eighteenth-century mathematicians, who had corresponded with Maupertuis on this subject between 1740 and 1744, agreed with Maupertuis that God must have constructed the universe in accordance with some such basic principle and that the existence of the principle evidenced the hand of God. He expressed this conviction in these words: “Since the fabric of the universe is most perfect and the work of a most wise Creator, nothing at all takes place in the universe in which some rule of maximum or minimum does not appear.”

欧拉比莫佩尔蒂更进一步，相信一切自然现象的行为都使某个函数最大或最小，因此基本物理原理应包含一个取最大或最小值的函数。上帝作为数学家的智慧，无疑超过十六与十七世纪人们的认识。欧拉的宗教信念也使他确信，上帝把运用人的能力理解其规律的任务托付给人。自然之书敞开在我们眼前，却用一种我们不能立即理解的语言写成；但凭坚持、热爱与苦功，可以学会这种语言。这种语言就是数学。既然世界是最好的，规律也必定美丽。

Euler went further than Maupertuis in his belief that all natural phenomena behave so as to maximize or minimize some function and so the basic physical principles should contain a function that is maximized or minimized. God was surely a wiser mathematician than sixteenth- and seventeenth-century men had appreciated. Euler’s religious convictions also assured him that God has entrusted man with the task of using his faculties to understand His laws. The book of nature was open before us but written in a language that we do not understand at once but can, with persistence, love, and suffering, learn. The language is mathematics. Since the world is the best possible, the laws must also be beautiful.

拉格朗日澄清并推广了最小作用原理。作用量本质上成为能量，由这一推广后的原理，可以推导更多力学问题的解。（这一原理处于变分法的核心；拉格朗日利用欧拉的初步工作，创立了这一新数学分支。）英国的“第二位牛顿”威廉·R.哈密顿（1805—1865）又进一步推广了它。今天，它是力学基础中最全面的原理，并成为物理学其他分支中称为变分原理的类似原理的范型。然而，正如我们将看到的，到哈密顿时代，莫佩尔蒂与欧拉关于上帝把这一原理融入宇宙设计的推论，已被放弃。对其意义的解释将发生变化的某些迹象，可见于伏尔泰的《阿卡基亚博士的故事》，其中嘲弄了这种关于上帝存在的论证。不过，十八世纪的人仍坚定相信，如此包罗万象的原理，只能意味着世界被设计为遵循它，设计者当然就是上帝。

The Principle of Least Action was clarified and generalized by Lagrange. Action became essentially energy and from this generalized principle it became possible to deduce solutions for many more mechanical problems. (This principle is at the heart of the subject of the calculus of variations, a new branch of mathematics which Lagrange, using preliminary work by Euler, founded.) The principle was further generalized by William R. Hamilton (1805-1865), Britain’s “second Newton.” It is today the most comprehensive principle underlying mechanics and has served as the paradigm for similar principles, called variational principles, in other branches of physics. However, as we shall see, by Hamilton’s time the inferences that Maupertuis and Euler drew as to God’s incorporation of this principle in the design of the universe were abandoned. Some indication that a change in the interpretation of its significance would occur can be obtained from Voltaire’s History of Doctor Akakia, in which he mocked this argument for the existence of God. However, the eighteenth-century men were still firmly convinced that such an all-embracing principle could mean only that the world had been designed, by God of course, to conform to it.

十八世纪最伟大的思想家，明确肯定了数学的统治地位。著名数学家让·勒朗·达朗贝尔，是德尼·狄德罗（1718—1784）编写法国著名《百科全书》的主要合作者；他说：“世界的真正体系，已经得到认识、发展与完善。”自然规律显然就是数学规律。

The reign of mathematics was affirmed in no uncertain terms by the greatest intellects of the eighteenth century. As the renowned mathematician Jean Le Rond d’Alembert, chief collaborator of Denis Diderot (1718-1784) in the writing of the famous French Encyclopedia, put it, “The true system of the world has been recognized, developed and perfected.” Natural law clearly was mathematical law.

更著名的是拉普拉斯的陈述：

More famous is the statement of Laplace:

我们可以把宇宙的现状，视为过去的结果与未来的原因。如果某个智力在任一时刻，知道驱动自然的全部力，以及构成自然的各个存在者的相互位置，而且足够强大，能够把这些资料纳入分析，就能把宇宙中最大天体与最轻原子的运动，汇聚到同一个公式中。对这样的智力，没有什么是不确定的；未来如同过去，都会呈现在它眼前。

We may regard the present state of the universe as the effect of its past and the cause of its future. An intellect which at any given moment knew all the forces that animate nature and the mutual positions of the beings that compose it, if this intellect were vast enough to submit the data to analysis, could condense into a single formula the movement of the greatest bodies of the universe and that of the lightest atom: for such an intellect nothing could be uncertain; and the future just like the past would be present before its eyes.

威廉·詹姆斯在《实用主义》中，这样描述该时期数学家的态度：

William James in his Pragmatism described the attitude of the mathematicians of this period thus:

当最初的数学、逻辑与自然的统一性，最初的规律被发现时，人们如此沉醉于由此产生的清晰、美与简化，以至于相信自己确实破译了全能者永恒的思想。他的心智也以三段论发出雷鸣与回响。他也用圆锥曲线、平方、根与比例思考，像欧几里得那样进行几何活动。他制定开普勒定律，让行星遵循；他使落体速度与时间成正比增长；他制定正弦定律，让光在折射时遵从。……他思考万物的原型，设计其变化；当我们重新发现这些奇妙安排中的任何一项时，便把握了他的心智最切实的意图。

When the first mathematical, logical and natural uniformities, the first laws, were discovered, men were so carried away by the clearness, beauty and simplification that resulted that they believed themselves to have deciphered authentically the eternal thoughts of the Almighty. His mind also thundered and reverberated in syllogisms. He also thought in conic sections, squares and roots and ratios, and geometrized like Euclid. He made Kepler’s laws for the planets to follow; he made velocity increase proportionally to the time in falling bodies, he made the law of sines for light to obey when refracted. ... He thought the archetypes of all things and devised their variations; and when we rediscover any one of these wondrous institutions, we seize his mind in its very literal intention.

自然按照数学设计、设计者是上帝这一确信，甚至由诗人表达出来，例如约瑟夫·艾迪生在《赞美诗》中写道：

The conviction that nature was mathematically designed, designed by God, was expressed even by poets, Joseph Addison, for instance, in his Hymn:

高高在上的辽阔苍穹， 连同蔚蓝的缥缈天空， 繁星闪耀的天宇，光辉的框架， 宣告它们伟大创造者的名。 不倦的太阳日复一日， 展示其创造者的威力； 向每一片土地昭示， 全能之手的造物。

The spacious firmament on high, With all the blue ethereal sky, And spangled heavens, a shining frame, Their great Original proclaim. Th’ unwearied Sun from day to day Does his Creator’s power display; And publishes to every land The work of an Almighty hand.

* * *

* * *

所有行星也依次， 在运转中证实这消息， 把真理从一极传向另一极。

And all the planets in their turn, Confirm the tidings as they roll, And spread the truth from pole to pole.

到十八世纪末，数学如同一棵牢牢扎根于实在的大树，根系已有两千年历史，枝干宏伟，高耸于其他一切知识体系之上。这样一棵树，无疑将永远存活。

By the end of the eighteenth century, mathematics was like a tree firmly grounded in reality, with roots already two thousand years old, with majestic branches, and towering over all other bodies of knowledge. Surely such a tree would live forever.

IV 第一次崩溃：真理的凋零

IV. The First Debacle: The Withering of Truth

每个时代都有自己的神话，并称之为更高的真理。

Every age has its myths and calls them higher truths.

佚名

Anonymous

十九世纪以吉祥的景象开篇。拉格朗日仍在活跃；拉普拉斯正处于能力巅峰；傅里叶（1768—1830）努力撰写1807年的手稿，后来将其纳入经典《热的理论》（1822）；卡尔·弗里德里希·高斯（1777—1855）刚出版数论的里程碑《算术研究》（Disquisitiones arithmeticae，1801），即将以大量贡献赢得“数学王子”称号；而法国的高斯——奥古斯丁—路易·柯西（1789—1857）——也开始在1814年的一篇论文中展示非凡实力。

The nineteenth century opened auspiciously. Lagrange was still active; Laplace was at the height of his power; Fourier (1768— 1830) was working hard on his manuscript of 1807, which was later incorporated in his classic Theory of Heat (1822); Karl Friedrich Gauss (1777-1855) had just published a landmark in the theory of numbers, his Disquisitiones arithmeticae (Arithmetical Dissertations, 1801), and was soon to burst forth with a mass of contributions that earned for him the title Prince of Mathematics; and Augustin-Louis Cauchy (1789— 1857), the French counterpart of Gauss, had begun to show his extraordinary strength in a paper of 1814.

简述这些人的工作，可以显示十九世纪上半叶在揭示更多自然设计方面的巨大进展。虽然高斯对数学本身作出辉煌贡献——其中一项我们很快就会讨论——但他把一生的大部分用于物理研究。事实上，他不是数学教授，而是在近五十年间担任哥廷根的天文学教授与天文台台长。他最投入于天文学，对它的兴趣可追溯至1795—1798年在哥廷根求学时。1801年，他取得首次显著成功。当年1月1日，朱塞佩·皮亚齐（1746—1826）发现小行星谷神星。虽然只能观察几周，当时仅二十四岁的高斯仍将新数学理论应用于观察数据，预测了它的轨道。年底再度观察时，其位置与预测几乎一致。1802年，威廉·奥尔伯斯发现另一颗小行星智神星，高斯再次成功确定轨道。他早期的全部天文学工作，汇集于主要著作之一《天体运动论》（1809）。

A few words about the work of these men may give some indication of the immense progress made in the first half of the nineteenth century toward uncovering more of nature’s design. Though Gauss made magnificent contributions to mathematics proper—we shall be discussing one of these shortly—he devoted most of his life to physical studies. In fact he was not a professor of mathematics but for almost fifty years a professor of astronomy and director of the observatory at Gottingen. Astronomy occupied him most and his interest in it dates back to his student days of 1795-1798 at Gottingen. He achieved his first notable success in 1801. On January 1 of that year Giuseppi Piazzi (1746-1826) discovered the minor planet Ceres. Although it was possible to observe it for only a few weeks, Gauss, then only twenty-four years old, applied new mathematical theory to the observations and predicted the planet’s path. It was observed at the end of the year very nearly in accord with Gauss’s predictions. When Wilhelm Olbers discovered another minor planet, Pallas, in 1802, Gauss again successfully determined its path. All of this early work on astronomy was summarized in one of Gauss’s major works, the Theory of Motion of Heavenly Bodies (1809).

后来，应汉诺威公爵请求，高斯主持汉诺威测量，创立大地测量学，并由此获得微分几何的开创性思想。1830至1840年间，他在理论与实验磁学的物理研究中，也取得卓越声望。他建立了测量地磁场的方法。电磁理论创始人詹姆斯·克拉克·麦克斯韦在《电磁通论》中说，高斯的磁学研究重建了整个学科，包括仪器、观察方法和结果计算。他关于地磁的论文，是物理研究的典范。为纪念这些工作，磁学中的单位被称为高斯。

Later, at the request of the Duke of Hannover, Gauss led a survey of Hannover, founded the science of geodesy, and derived therefrom seminal ideas in differential geometry. During the years from 1830 to 1840 Gauss also earned great distinction in his physical research on theoretical and experimental magnetism. He established a method of measuring the earth’s magnetic field. James Clerk Maxwell, the founder of electromagnetic theory, says in his Electricity and Magnetism that Gauss’s studies of magnetism reconstituted the whole science, the instruments used, the methods of observation, and the calculation of results. Gauss’s papers on terrestrial magnetism are models of physical research. In honor of this work the unit of magnetism is called the gauss.

高斯与威廉·韦伯（1804—1891）虽非电报观念的首创者（此前已有许多尝试），但1833年，他们设计了一种实用装置，使指针依电线所传电流的方向向左或向右转。这只是高斯诸多发明之一。他还研究了自欧拉时代以来受到忽略的光学；1838—1841年的研究，为处理光学问题提供了全新基础。

Though Gauss and Wilhelm Weber (1804-1891) did not originate the idea of telegraphy (there were many earlier attempts), in 1833 they designed a practical device which made a needle rotate right or left depending upon the direction of electric current sent over a wire. This was but one of Gauss’s several inventions. He also worked in optics, which had been neglected since Euler’s days, and his investigations of 1838-1841 gave a totally new basis for the handling of optical problems.

在十九世纪数学界，与高斯同等的领袖地位，应当归于柯西。他的兴趣遍及各领域。数学方面，他写了七百多篇论文，数量仅次于欧拉。其著作的现代版本共二十六卷，涵盖数学所有分支。他创立了复变函数理论（第VII与VIII章）。但他至少把同样多的精力用于物理问题。1815年，他凭水波论文获法国科学院奖。他对杆和金属薄片等弹性膜的平衡，以及弹性介质中的波，写了基本著作，是这一数学物理分支的创始人之一。他接续菲涅耳创立的光波理论，将其扩展到光的色散与偏振。柯西是一位杰出的数学物理学家。

Leadership on a level with Gauss in the nineteenth-century mathematical world must be accorded to Cauchy. He had universal interests. In mathematics he wrote over seven hundred papers, second only to Euler in number. His works in a modern edition fill twenty-six volumes and embrace all branches of mathematics. He was the founder of the theory of functions of a complex variable (Chapers VII and VIII). But Cauchy devoted at least as much of his energy to physical problems. In 1815 he won a prize awarded by the French Academy of Sciences for a paper on water waves. He wrote fundamental works on the equilibrium of rods and elastic membranes such as metal sheets and on waves in elastic media and was one of the founders of that branch of mathematical physics. He took up the theory of light waves, which Augustin-Jean Fresnel had initiated, and extended the theory to the dispersion and polarization of light. Cauchy was a superb mathematical physicist.

傅里叶虽不完全与高斯、柯西同级，但他的工作尤其值得注意，因为他使又一个自然现象——热传导——受数学支配。他认为这是最重要的宇宙论研究之一，因为研究地球内部的热传导，可能表明地球从熔融状态冷却而来，由此或能估计地球年龄。在这项工作中，他极大推进了无穷三角级数，即如今的傅里叶级数理论，使其适用于应用数学的许多其他领域。对傅里叶的工作若只作克制的赞扬，是不公正的。

Though Fourier was not quite in the same class as Gauss and Cauchy, his work is especially noteworthy because he brought one more natural phenomenon under the dominion of mathematics, the conduction of heat. Fourier regarded this subject as one of the most important cosmological studies because study of the conduction of heat within the earth might show that the earth had cooled down from a molten state. Thereby some estimate of the age of the earth might be made. In the course of this work he so advanced the theory of infinite trigonometric series, now called Fourier series, that it became applicable to many other areas of applied mathematics. It would be unjust to praise Fourier’s work in measured terms.

高斯、柯西、傅里叶以及数百位其他人的成就，进一步提供了看似不可争辩的证据：越来越多的真实自然规律正在被揭示。确实，在整个世纪，数学巨人们继续沿前人路线前进，创造更强大的数学工具，并成功用于进一步研究自然。他们在寻找自然数学规律的道路上奋进，仿佛受到一种信念催眠：他们这些数学家，是发现上帝设计的受膏者。

These achievements of Gauss, Cauchy, Fourier, and hundreds of others were additional, seemingly incontestable evidence that more and more true laws of nature were being uncovered. And indeed throughout the century the giants of mathematics continued to pursue the course set by their predecessors and to create more powerful mathematical machinery and employ it successfully in the further investigation of nature. They forged ahead in the search for the mathematical laws of nature as though hypnotized by the belief that they, the mathematicians, were the anointed ones to discover God’s design.

如果他们留意自己同道与志趣相投者中的某些人的话，或许能为即将面对的灾难作好准备。近代早期，弗朗西斯·培根就在《新工具》（Novum organum，即推理的新工具，1620）中指出：

Had they paid attention to the words of some of their own brethren and kindred spirits, they might have been prepared for the disaster they soon would face. Early in the modern period Francis Bacon in his Novum organum (New Instrument [of reasoning], 1620) had noted:

种族偶像根植于人性，根植于人类这一种族本身。因为认为人的感官是事物的尺度，是错误的。相反，感官与心智的一切知觉都以人为参照，而不是以宇宙为参照；人的心智像不平整的镜子，把自己的性质赋予发出光线的各种对象，使它们扭曲、变形。

The idols of the tribe are inherent in human nature, and the very tribe or race of man. For man’s sense is falsely asserted to be tke standard of things. On the contrary, all the perceptions, both of the senses and the mind, bear reference to man, and not to the universe, and the human mind resembles those uneven mirrors, which impart their own properties to different objects, from which rays are emitted, and distort and disfigure them.

在同一著作中，培根要求以经验与实验为一切知识的基础，还说：

In this same work Bacon, calling for experience and experimentation as the basis for all knowledge, also said:

通过论辩确立的公理，不可能足以发现新的成果，因为自然的精微，远远超过论辩的精微。

It cannot be that axioms established by argumentation can suffice for the discovery of new works, since the subtlety of nature is greater many times over than the subtlety of argument.

无意之中，即使最虔诚者也开始作出一些区分，逐渐排除了上帝在宇宙设计中的作用。

Unintentionally, even the most faithful began to make distinctions that led gradually to the elimination of God’s role in the design of the universe.

哥白尼与开普勒的日心理论工作，虽被两人赞为上帝数学智慧的证据，却与《圣经》关于人类重要性的陈述相矛盾。伽利略、罗伯特·波义耳与牛顿肯定，其科学工作的目标是证明上帝的设计与存在，但科学工作本身并不涉及上帝。事实上，伽利略在一封信中说：“在我看来，任何关于《圣经》的讨论，本来可以永远搁置；从未有任何恪守适当界限的天文学家或科学家涉足这种事情。”当然，正如我们所见，他相信上帝的数学设计；这句话只意味着，解释自然运行时，不应诉诸神秘或超自然力量。在伽利略时代，全能上帝能够改变设计的信念仍占主导。然而，无论多么虔诚，笛卡尔还是断言自然规律不变，暗中限制了上帝的能力。牛顿也相信固定秩序，却指望上帝使世界按照计划持续运行。他比喻为钟表匠不断维修钟表。他有充分理由求助于上帝干预。虽然知道每颗行星的轨道并非完美椭圆，因为其他行星在摄动它，但他不能用数学证明不规则性或偏离椭圆的情况，源于其他行星的吸引。因此，他担心，除非上帝不断干预，使太阳系按照计划运转，其稳定性就会遭到破坏。

The work of Copernicus and Kepler on the heliocentric theory, hailed by both as evidence of God’s mathematical wisdom, nevertheless contradicted statements in the Scriptures as to the importance of man. Galileo, Robert Boyle, and Newton affirmed that the objective of their scientific work was to evidence God’s design and presence, but their scientific work proper did not involve God. In fact Galileo says in one of his letters, “For my part any discussion of the Sacred Scriptures might have lain dormant forever; no astronomer or scientist who remained within proper bounds has ever gotten into such things. Of course, Galileo, as we have seen, believed in God’s mathematical design; all he meant by this statement was that no mystic or supernatural forces should be invoked to explain the workings of nature. In Galileo’s time the belief that the omnipotent God could change the design still held sway. It was Descartes, however devout, who asserted the invariability of the laws of nature and implicitly limited God’s power. Newton too believed in a fixed order but banked on God to keep the world functioning according to plan. He used the analogy of a watchmaker keeping a watch in repair. Newton had good reason to call upon God’s intervention. Though he was well aware that the path of any one planet was not a perfect ellipse because other planets were perturbing its path, he could not demonstrate mathematically that the irregularities or the departures from the elliptical path were due to the attractions exerted by the other planets. Hence he feared that the stability of the solar system would be disrupted unless God continually intervened to keep it moving according to plan.

莱布尼茨反对。1715年11月，他致信哲学家、牛顿拥护者塞缪尔·克拉克，对牛顿认为上帝需要偶尔修理并上紧钟表的看法说：“看来，他［上帝］没有足够的预见，把它造为永动的。……依我之见，世界中的同一力量与活力始终恒定，只依照自然规律，从一部分物质传到另一部分。”因此，莱布尼茨指责牛顿贬低上帝能力。他实际上指控牛顿促成英国宗教的衰落。

Leibniz objected. In a November 1715 letter to the philosopher and champion of Newton, Samuel Clarke, he said of Newton’s view that God needs to repair and wind up the watch occasionally, “He [God] had not, it seems, sufficient foresight to make it a perpetual motion. . . . According to my opinion, the same force and vigour remain constant in the world, and only pass from one part of matter to another, in conformity with the laws of nature.” Thus Leibniz charged Newton with deprecating God’s power. Leibniz actually accused Newton of contributing to the decline of religion in England.

莱布尼茨并非毫无道理。牛顿的工作，无意间开启了自然哲学与神学的分离或解放。如前所述，伽利略坚持物理科学必须与神学分开。牛顿在《原理》中遵守这一教义，并在对自然现象作纯数学描述方面取得更大进展。因此，上帝越来越被排除出科学理论的数学表述。确实，牛顿无法解释的异常，后来研究者基本都作了解释。

Leibniz was not off the mark. Newton’s work unintentionally initiated a divorce or emancipation of natural philosophy from theology. Galileo, as we have noted, had insisted that physical science must be kept separate from theology. Newton adhered to this doctrine in his Principles and made much greater progress toward a purely mathematical account of natural phenomena. Thus God was excluded more and more from mathematical accounts of scientific theories. Indeed, the aberrations that Newton could not explain were essentially accounted for by later investigators.

涵盖天上与地上运动的普遍规律，开始主导思想界；预测与观察持续吻合，说明这些规律完美无缺。牛顿之后，人们虽仍相信这种完美证明上帝的设计，但上帝退居背景，宇宙数学规律成为焦点。莱布尼茨看到《原理》的某些意涵：有无上帝，世界都按照方案运行，因此斥其反基督教。对于获得纯数学结果的关切，逐渐代替对于上帝设计的关切。欧拉之后，许多数学家仍相信上帝存在、他设计了世界，并认为数学是主要为破译上帝设计提供工具的科学；但十八世纪数学越发展、成功越多，数学工作的宗教动力就越减弱，上帝的存在也越黯淡。

Universal laws embracing heavenly and earthly motions began to dominate the intellectual scene, and the continued agreement between predictions and observations bespoke the perfection of the laws. Though belief that this perfection was evidence of God’s design continued after Newton’s time, God sank into the background and the mathematical laws of the universe became the focus. Leibniz saw some of the implications of Newton’s Principles, a world functioning according to plan with or without God, and attacked the book as anti-Christian. The concern for the attainment of purely mathematical results gradually replaced the concern for God s design. Though many a mathematician after Euler continued to believe in God’s presence, His design of the world, and mathematics as the science whose mam function was to provide the tools to decipher God s design, the further the development of mathematics proceeded in the eighteenth century and the more numerous its sue-cesses, the more the religious inspiration for mathematical work receded and God’s presence became dim.

拉格朗日与拉普拉斯虽出身天主教家庭，却是不可知论者。拉普拉斯完全否定上帝是宇宙数学设计者的信念。有个著名故事：他送拿破仑一部《天体力学》，拿破仑说：“拉普拉斯先生，听说你写了这部关于宇宙体系的大书，却从未提到其创造者。”据说他回答：“我不需要这个假说。”自然取代了上帝。如高斯所说：“自然啊，你是我的女神，我的服务服从你的规律。”高斯实际上相信一位永恒存在、全知全能的上帝，但关于上帝的思想，与数学或寻找自然数学规律无关。

Lagrange and Laplace though of Catholic parentage were agnostics. Laplace completely rejected any belief in God as the mathematical designer of the universe. There is a well-known story that when Laplace gave Napoleon a copy of his Celestial Mechanics Napoleon remarked, “Monsieur Laplace, they tell me you have written this large book on the system of the universe and have never even mentioned its Creator. Laplace is said to have replied, “I have no need of this hypothesis.” Nature replaced God. As Gauss put it, “Thou, nature, are my goddess, to thy laws my services are bound.” Gauss did in fact believe in an eternally existing, omniscient, and omnipotent God but thoughts about God had nothing to do with mathematics or the search for mathematical laws of nature.

哈密顿关于最小作用原理（第III章）的评论，也揭示思想视野的变化。他在一篇

Hamilton’s remark about the Principle of Least Action (Chapter III) also reveals the change in intellectual outlook. He said in an article

1833年的文章中说：

of 1833:

虽然最小作用定律已由此跻身物理学最高定理之列，但它以宇宙的节约性为由，宣称具有宇宙论必然性，如今普遍被拒绝。这种拒绝看来合理，理由之一是，声称被节约的量，事实上常被大量耗费。……因此，我们不能假定，在神的宇宙理念中设计了对这种量的节约，尽管可以相信，这一理念包含某种高层次的简单性。

Although the law of least action has thus attained a rank among the highest theorems of physics, yet its pretensions to a cosmological necessity, on the ground of economy in the universe, are now generally rejected. And the rejection appears just, for this, among other reasons, that the quantity pretended to be economized is in fact often lavishly expended. ... We cannot, therefore, suppose the economy of this quantity to have been designed in the divine idea of the universe, though a simplicity of some high kind may be believed to be included in that idea.

回顾起来，可以看到，上帝以数学设计自然的学说，恰恰受到数学家自身工作的削弱。思想界越来越确信，人类理性是一种极强大的能力，其最佳证据就是数学家的成功。那么，即使仅仅为加强宗教与伦理的主流教义，难道不也能用理性为它们辩护吗？幸运或不幸的是，把理性应用于宗教信念的基础，破坏了许多人的正统信仰。宗教信念从正统，漂移到理性主义超自然论、自然神论、不可知论等中间阶段，乃至彻底无神论。这些运动影响了十八世纪那些文化广博的数学家。该时代理性主义、反教权的思想领袖德尼·狄德罗说：“若要我相信上帝，就必须让我摸到他。”并非所有十九世纪数学家都否认上帝的作用。虔诚天主教徒柯西说，人“毫不犹豫地拒绝任何与启示真理相矛盾的假说”。尽管如此，上帝是宇宙数学设计者的信念，还是开始消退。

In retrospect one can see that the doctrine of God s mathematical design of nature was being undermined by the very work of the mathematicians themselves. The intellectuals became more and more convinced that human reason was a most powerful faculty and the best evidence for it was the successes of the mathematicians. Could not then reason be applied to justify prevailing doctrines of religion and ethics if for no less salutary a reason than to reinforce them? Fortunately, or unfortunately, the application of reason to the foundation of religious beliefs undermined the orthodoxy of many. Religious beliefs drifted from orthodoxy to various intermediate stages such as rationalistic supernaturalism, deism, agnosticism, and outright atheism. These movements had their effect on mathematicians, who, in the eighteenth century, were men of broad culture. As Denis Diderot, the rationalistic, anticlerical, leading intellectual of the age put it, “If you want me to believe in God, you must make me touch him.” Not all nineteenth-century mathematicians denied God’s role. Cauchy, a devout Catholic, said that man “rejects without hesitation any hypothesis which is in contradiction with revealed truth.” Nevertheless the belief in God as the mathematical designer of the universe began to fade.

这一信念的削弱，很快带来问题：自然的数学规律为什么必然是真理？最早否定真理者之一，是狄德罗，他在《关于解释自然的思想》（1753）中说，数学家如同赌徒，双方都用自己创造的抽象规则玩游戏。他们研究的主题只是约定，在实在中没有基础。同样批判的是贝尔纳·勒·博维耶·德·丰特奈尔（1657—1757）的《世界的多样性》。他以一个比喻抨击天体运动规律不变的信念：在玫瑰的记忆所及范围内，从来没有园丁死去。

The weakening of this belief soon entailed the question of why the mathematical laws of nature were necessarily truths. Among the first to deny truths was Diderot in his Thoughts on the Interpretation of Nature (1753). He said the mathematician was like a gambler: both played games with abstract rules that they themselves had created. Their subjects of study were only matters of convention that had no foundation in reality. Equally critical was the intellectual Bernard Le Bovier de Fontenelle (1657-1757) in his Plurality of Worlds. He attacked the belief in the immutability of the laws of the heavenly motions with the observation that as long as roses could remember no gardener ever died.

数学家喜欢相信，自己创造哲学家赖以生存的养料。但十八世纪，在否认关于物理世界的真理方面，哲学家走在前列。我们略过托马斯·霍布斯（1588—1679）、约翰·洛克（1632—1704）与乔治·贝克莱主教（1685—1753）的学说，不是因为它们容易驳倒，而是因为不如激进的戴维·休谟（1711—1776）影响深远；后者实际上不仅赞同贝克莱，还更进一步。在《人性论》（1739—1740）中，休谟主张，我们既不认识心智，也不认识物质；二者都是虚构。我们感知感觉；意象、记忆与思想等简单观念，不过是感觉的微弱效果。任何复杂观念，只是简单观念的集合。心智就是我们的感觉与观念集合。除能以直接经验检验者外，我们不应假定任何实体存在；但经验只提供感觉。

Mathematicians prefer to believe that they create the nourishment on which philosophers feed. But in the eighteenth century the philosophers were in the van in denying truths about the physical world. We shall pass over the doctrines of Thomas Hobbes (1588-1679), John Locke (1632-1704), and of Bishop George Berkeley (1685-1753) not because they are easily refutable but because they were not as influential as those of the radical David Hume (1711-1776) who, in effect, not only endorsed Berkeley but went even further. In his Treatise of Human Nature (1739-40), Hume maintained that we know neither mind nor matter; both are fictions. We perceive sensations; simple ideas such as images, memories, and thoughts are but faint effects of sensations. Any complex idea is but a collection of simple ideas. The mind is identical with our collection of sensations and ideas. We should not assume the existence of any substances other than those which can be tested by immediate experience; but experience yields only sensations.

休谟对物质同样怀疑。谁能保证存在一个永久的、坚实物体的世界？我们所知的，只是自己对这样一个世界的感觉。反复感觉到椅子，不能证明椅子确实存在。空间与时间，不过是观念向我们出现的方式与次序。同样，因果性不过是观念之间的习惯联系。空间、时间与因果性都不是客观实在。我们被感觉的力量与牢固性误导，相信了这类实在。一个具有固定性质的外部世界的存在，实际上是无根据的推论；感觉的来源无法解释。它们来自外部对象、心智本身，还是上帝，我们不能断言。
