Thus from the principles of the secular sciences to the foundations of religious revelation, from metaphysics to matters of taste, from music to morals, from the scholastic disputes of theologians to matters of trade, from the laws of princes to those of people, from natural law to the arbitrary law of nations . . . everything has been discussed and analyzed, or at least mentioned.

各领域都会发现真理的信心，被数学中没有真理的认识击碎。人类心中仍可能保持希望，甚至信念：政治、伦理、宗教、经济以及许多其他领域能够获得真理；但这一希望最有力的支持已失去。数学向世界提供人能获得真理的证明，又摧毁了证明。恰恰是理性的两项胜利，非欧几里得几何与四元数，为这场思想灾难铺平道路。

This confidence that truths would be discovered in all fields was shattered by the recognition that there is no truth in mathematics. The hope and perhaps even the belief that truths can be obtained in politics, ethics, religion, economics, and many other fields may still persist in human minds, but the best support for the hope has been lost. Mathematics offered to the world proof that man can acquire truths and then destroyed the proof. It was non-Euclidean geometry and quaternions, both triumphs of reason, that paved the way for this intellectual disaster.

威廉·詹姆斯说：“人的思想生活，几乎完全在于以概念秩序，取代经验最初呈现的知觉秩序。”但概念秩序并非对知觉秩序的真实描述。

As William James put it, “The intellectual life of man consists almost wholly in his substitution of a conceptual order for the perceptual order in which his experience originally comes.” But the conceptual order is not a veridical account of the perceptual.

随着真理丧失，人失去了思想中心、参照框架，以及一切思想确立的权威。“人类理性的骄傲”跌落，带倒了真理的殿堂。历史教训是，我们最坚定的信念不应教条地断言；事实上，最应怀疑它们。它们标志的不是我们的征服，而是局限与边界。

With the loss of truth, man lost his intellectual center, his frame of reference, the established authority for all thought. The “pride of human reason” suffered a fall which brought down with it the house of truth. The lesson of history is that our firmest convictions are not to be asserted dogmatically; in fact they should be most suspect; they mark not our conquests but our limitations and our bounds.

对数学真理性的信念史，可以用华兹华斯《不朽的启示》的诗句概括。1750年，数学家可以这样谈自己的创造：

The history of the belief in the truth of mathematics can be summarized in the words of Wordsworth’s “Intimations of Immortality.” In 1750 mathematicians could say of their creations,

我们拖曳着荣耀的云彩而来， 来自上帝，我们的家园。

But trailing clouds of glory do we come From God, who is our home.

到1850年，他们不得不悲伤地承认：

By 1850 they were obliged to admit ruefully,

然而我知道，无论走到哪里， 一种荣耀已从大地消逝。

But yet I know where’er I go. That there hath passed away a glory from the earth.

但这段历史不应太令人沮丧。埃瓦里斯特·伽罗瓦谈数学说：“［这门］科学是人类心智的作品；心智注定更多是研究而非知道，更多是寻求真理而非发现真理。”或许真理的本性就是愿意难以捉摸。或者如罗马哲学家卢修斯·塞涅卡所说：“自然不会一下子揭示她所有的奥秘。”

But the history should not be too discouraging. Evariste Galois said of mathematics, “[This] science is the work of the human mind, which is destined rather to study than to know, to seek the truth rather than to find it.” Perhaps it is in the nature of truth that it wishes to be elusive. Or as the Roman philosopher Lucius Seneca put it, “Nature does not at once disclose all Her mysteries.”

V 一门逻辑学科的非逻辑发展

V. The Illogical Development of a Logical Subject

我们不悲伤，反从留下的东西中寻找力量。

We will grieve not, rather find strength in what remains behind.

华兹华斯

Wordsworth

两千多年来，数学家相信自己在揭示自然数学设计方面极为成功。但如今，他们不得不认识到数学规律不是真理。这两千年间，他们也相信自己遵守希腊人的真理方案，即把演绎推理应用于数学公理，保证结论与公理同样可靠。科学的数学规律异常精确，因此对某些数学论证正确性的少数分歧，被置之不理。甚至最敏锐的数学家也确信，推理中的瑕疵很容易消除。但十九世纪，他们对于自身推理的泰然自若遭到击碎。

For over two thousand years mathematicians believed that they were highly successful in uncovering the mathematical design of nature. But now they were obliged to recognize that mathematical laws were not truths. During these two millennia mathematicians also believed that they were adhering to the Greek plan for arriving at truths, namely, to apply deductive reasoning to mathematical axioms, thus ensuring conclusions as reliable as the axioms. Because the mathematical laws of science were remarkably accurate the few disagreements that did take place about the correctness of some mathematical arguments were brushed aside. Even the most acute mathematicians were sure that any blemishes in the reasoning could readily be removed. However, in the nineteenth century the equanimity of mathematicians with respect to their reasoning was shattered.

什么使数学家睁开眼睛？他们如何认识到推理不健全？十九世纪最初几十年，对微积分健全性的攻击得不到令人满意的反驳，已有少数人因此不安。但主要仍是迫使数学家放弃真理主张的同样创造——非欧几里得几何与四元数——使大多数人深刻认识到逻辑的悲惨状况。

What happened to open the eyes of the mathematicians? How did they come to recognize that they were not reasoning soundly? A few men had already become disturbed in the early decades of the nineteenth century by the attacks on the soundness of the calculus which were not being satisfactorily countered. But it was primarily the very same creations that forced mathematicians to abandon their claim to truth— non-Euclidean geometry and quaternions—that drove home to most mathematicians the sad state of the logic.

研究非欧几里得几何时，自然不断参照欧几里得几何的类似定理与证明，于是惊人地发现：两千年来被专家赞为严格证明典范的欧几里得几何，从逻辑角度看，缺陷严重。自四元数开始的新代数创造（第IV章），使数学家足够不安，想重新检查普通实数、复数的算术与代数的逻辑基础；即使别无理由，也要重新确信这些数的性质牢固确立。在这领域，他们发现的也令人震惊。原以为高度逻辑化的学科，实际上以完全非逻辑的方式发展。

The work on non-Euclidean geometry, wherein constant reference to analogous theorems and proofs of Euclidean geometry was natural, resulted in the surprising revelation that Euclidean geometry, which had been hailed for two thousand years by the experts as the model of rigorous proof, was from a logical standpoint seriously defective. The creation of new algebras, commencing with quaternions (Chapter IV), disturbed mathematicians enough to make them want to re-examine the logical underpinnings of the arithmetic and algebra of the ordinary real and complex numbers, if for no other reason than to reassure themselves that the properties of these numbers were securely established. And what they found in this area too was startling. What they had thought to be highly logical subjects had actually been developed totally illogically.

洞见最丰富的源泉是回顾。正凭新创造提供并磨砺的后见之明，数学家终于看到了前代数代人没有看到，或虽看到却在急于获取真理中忽略的东西。数学家当然不会放弃学科。除在科学中持续有效之外，数学本身也是为自身而存在的知识体系，许多追随柏拉图的数学家把它视为超感性实在。因此，他们决定，至少可以重新检查数学逻辑结构，补足或重建有缺陷的部分。

The most fertile source of insight is hindsight, and it is with the hindsight afforded and sharpened by the new creations that mathematicians finally saw what generations of their predecessors had failed to see or had seen and glossed over in their impetuously eager drive to obtain truths. The mathematicians were certainly not going to abandon their subject. Beyond its continuing remarkable effectiveness in science, mathematics proper was a body of knowledge in and for itself which many mathematicians, following Plato, regarded as an extra-sensible reality. Hence the mathematicians decided that the least they could do was to re-examine the logical structure of mathematics and to supply or reconstruct the defective portions.

我们知道，演绎数学始于希腊人，第一个看似健全的结构是欧几里得《几何原本》。他从定义、公理出发，推导定理。看看他的某些定义：

We know that deductive mathematics began with the Greeks and that the first seemingly sound structure was Euclid s Elements. Euclid started with definitions and axioms and deduced theorems. Let us look at some of Euclid’s definitions.

定义1：点是没有部分的东西。 定义2：线［现代术语中的曲线］是没有宽度的长度。 定义4：直线是一条与其自身上的点均匀平齐的线。

Definition 1. A point is that which has no parts. Definition 2. A line [curve in modern terminology] is breadthless length. Definition 4. A straight line is a line that lies evenly with the points on itself.

亚里士多德曾指出，定义必须用其他已知概念描述所定义的概念。既然必须有起点，他断言，就必须从不定义的概念开始。虽然许多迹象表明，约公元前300年在亚历山大里亚生活、工作的欧几里得，了解古典希腊人的著作，尤其亚里士多德的著作，但他仍定义了所有概念。

Now Aristotle had pointed out that a definition must describe the concept being defined in terms of other concepts already known. Since one must start somewhere, there must be,'he asserted, undefined concepts to begin with. Though there are many indications that Euclid, who lived and worked in Alexandria about 300 b.c., knew the works of the classical Greeks and of Aristotle in particular, he nevertheless defined all his concepts.

对这一缺陷有两种解释：欧几里得不同意必须有不定义的术语；或如某些辩护者所说，他认识到这一必要性，却只想以开头的定义，直观提示术语意义，使人知道随后公理是否确实正确。若是后者，就不应把定义纳入正文。无论其意图如何，两千年来几乎所有后继数学家，都没注意需要不定义的术语。帕斯卡在《论几何精神》（1658）中提醒这一需要，但提醒被忽略。

There have been two explanations of this flaw. Either Euclid did not agree that there must be undefined terms or, as some defenders of Euclid state, he realized that there must be undefined terms but intended his initial definitions to give only some intuitive ideas of what the defined terms meant, so that one could know whether the axioms which were to follow were indeed correct assertions. In the latter case he should not have included the definitions in his text proper. Whatever Euclid’s intentions were, practically all the mathematicians who followed him for two thousand years failed to note the need for undefined terms. Pascal in his Treatise on the Geometrical Spirit (1658) called attention to this need but his reminder was ignored.

欧几里得公理如何？他大概追随亚里士多德，陈述适用于一切推理的五条共同概念，以及只适用于几何的五条公设。一条共同概念说，同等于一物的事物彼此相等。他把“事物”用于长度、面积、体积与整数，这个词无疑太模糊。然而，更不妥的是：重合的事物相等。他用这一公理证明两三角形全等：把一个放在另一个之上，根据给定事实，说明它们必定重合。但要叠放，就必须移动三角形，并假定它在移动中性质不变。这条公理实际上说，我们的空间是齐性的，即图形无论放在哪里，性质都相同。这或许合理，却仍是额外假定。此外，定义中未处理运动概念。

What about Euclid’s axioms? Presumably following Aristotle, he stated five common notions that apply in all reasoning and five postulates that apply only to geometry. One common notion states that things equal to the same thing are equal to each other. Euclid applied the word things to lengths, areas, volumes, and whole numbers. Certainly the word things was too vague. More misguided, however, was his common notion: Things which coincide are equal. He used this axiom to prove that two triangles are congruent by placing one triangle on top of another and showing, by using some given facts, that the triangles must coincide. However, to place one triangle on another he had to move it and in so doing he assumed that it did not change properties during the motion. The axiom really says that our space is homogeneous; that is, the properties of figures are the same wherever they may be placed. This may be a reasonable assumption but it is an additional assumption nevertheless. Also, the concept of motion was not treated in the definitions.

而且，欧几里得使用许多从未陈述的公理。如高斯指出，他谈点位于其他点之间、线位于其他线之间，却从未处理介于其间的概念及性质。显然，他心中有几何图形，把实际图形具有、却未纳入公理的性质带入推理。图形可以辅助思考与记忆，却不能成为推理基础。莱布尼茨指出，另一条未经明确说明便使用的公理，涉及技术上所谓连续性。他使用这一事实：连接直线ℓ一侧的A与另一侧B的线（图5.1），与ℓ有一个公共点。从图看，这当然明显；但没有关于线的公理保证公共点存在。甚至能否谈直线ℓ的两侧？这也需要公理。

Moreover, Euclid used many axioms he never stated. As Gauss noted, Euclid spoke of points lying between other points and lines lying between other lines but never treated the notion of betweenness and its properties. Evidently he had geometrical figures in mind and took over into his reasoning properties the actual figures possessed but which were not incorporated in the axioms. Figures may be an aid to thinking and to memory but they cannot be the basis of reasoning. Another axiom used without explicit mention—this was noted by Leibniz—involves what is technically called continuity. Euclid used the fact that a line joining A (Fig. 5.1) on one side of a line ℓ to B on the other side has a point in common with ℓ. This is certainly evident from a figure. But no axiom about lines assures us of the existence of this common point. Can one even speak of two sides of the line ℓ? This, too, requires an axiom.

图5.1

Figure 5.1

除定义、公理的缺陷外，《几何原本》还有许多不充分的证明。有些定理证明错误；有些只证明所断言定理的特殊情形或特殊构形。不过，后一类缺陷相对次要，更容易补救。人们以为欧几里得对粗略图形作了精确证明，但整体判断其工作，实际上是对精确绘制的图形作了粗略证明。简言之，他的表述缺陷严重。

Beyond failings in its definitions and axioms, the Elements also contains many inadequate proofs. Some theorems are incorrectly proved. Others prove only a special case or a special configuration of the theorem asserted. These latter failings are, however, relatively minor in that they can be more readily remedied. Euclid had supposedly given accurate proofs of loosely drawn figures. However, if one judges Euclid’s work as a whole one must say that in fact he gave loose proofs of accurately drawn figures. In short, Euclid’s presentation was woefully defective.

尽管《几何原本》有这些缺陷，约1800年以前，最优秀的数学家、科学家与哲学家仍视其为严格证明的理想。帕斯卡在《思想录》中说：“几何精神在一切能够完美分析的学科中表现卓越。它从公理出发，作出其真理性可由普遍逻辑规则证明的推论。”牛顿的老师、剑桥大学前任教授艾萨克·巴罗，列举几何确定性的八个理由：概念清楚；定义无歧义；直觉保证共同概念普遍为真；公设明显可能、容易想象；公理数量少；量的生成方式清楚可想；证明次序容易；避免未知之物。还可引用许多类似证词。直到1873年，著名数论学家亨利·约翰·斯蒂芬·史密斯仍说：“几何若不严格，就什么也不是。……几乎普遍同意，欧几里得的方法在严格性上无可挑剔。”

Despite all these defects in the Elements, the best mathematicians, scientists, and philosophers before about 1800 regarded it as the ideal of rigorous proof. Pascal said in his Pensees, The geometrical spirit excels in all those subjects that are capable of a perfect analysis. It starts with axioms and draws inferences whose truth can be demonstrated by universal logical rules.” Isaac Barrow, Newton’s teacher and predecessor at Cambridge University, listed eight reasons for the certainty of geometry: the clarity of its concepts; its unambiguous definitions; our intuitive assurance of the universal truth of its common notions; the clear possibility and easy imaginability of its postulktes; the small number of its axioms; the clear conceivability of the mode by which magnitudes are generated; the easy order of the demonstrations; and the avoidance of things not known. Many more such testimonials could be adduced. As late as 1873 Henry John Stephen Smith, a noted number theorist, said: “Geometry is nothing if it be not rigorous. . . . The methods of Euclid are, by almost universal consent, unexceptionable in point of rigour.”

但非欧几里得几何的研究揭示如此多缺陷，人们不能再赞赏欧几里得几何的逻辑完美性。非欧几里得几何是欧几里得几何逻辑触礁沉没的暗礁。原被确信为坚实的地面，证明却是沼泽。

However, the work on non-Euclidean geometry revealed so many defects that the logical perfection of Euclidean geometry could no longer be admired. Non-Euclidean geometry was the reef on which the logic of Euclidean geometry foundered. A piece of ground that had confidently been thought to be solid proved to be marshland.

欧几里得几何当然只是数学一部分。自1700年起，远为庞大的部分是数的数学。看看数的逻辑发展如何。埃及人和巴比伦人使用整数、分数，甚至2、3等无理数，在实际应用中求其近似。但这些民族，乃至公元前四世纪以前的希腊人的数学，基于直觉或经验，因此谈不上褒贬逻辑结构。

Euclidean geometry is, of course, only a part of mathematics. Since 1700 by far the larger part has been the mathematics of number. Let us see how the logical development of numbers fared. The Egyptians and Babylonians worked with whole numbers, fractions, and even irrational numbers such as 2 and 3. Irrationals they approximated in practical applications. However, since the mathematics of these peoples and even of the Greeks before the fourth century b.c. was intuitively or empirically based, there could be no praise or criticism of logical structure.

我们所知最早对整数的逻辑处理，见于欧几里得《几何原本》第VII、VIII、IX卷。他提供定义，例如，单位是使每个存在事物被称为一的东西，数是由单位组成的多。它们显然不充分，更不用说他也未认识到需要不定义的概念。他推导整数性质时使用上述共同概念，不幸某些证明错误。尽管如此，希腊人与后继者确实相信，整数理论有了令人满意的逻辑基础。他们也允许自己直接谈整数的比，后人称其为分数，尽管比的概念未定义。

The first logical treatment of the whole numbers known to us is in Books VII, VIII, and IX of Euclid’s Elements. Here Euclid offered definitions such as, a unit is that by virtue of which each of the things that exist is called one, and a number is a multitude composed of units. Clearly these are inadequate, to say nothing about the fact that here too he did not recognize the need for undefined concepts. In deducing the properties of whole numbers Euclid used the common notions mentioned above. Unfortunately some of his proofs are faulty. Nevertheless, the Greeks and their successors did believe that the theory of whole numbers had secured a satisfactory logical foundation. They also permitted themselves to speak without more ado about ratios of whole numbers, which later generations called fractions, though the concept of ratio was not defined.

希腊人在数的逻辑发展中，确实遇到一个对他们无法克服的困难。我们知道，公元前五世纪的毕达哥拉斯学派最先强调整数及整数之比在自然研究中的重要性，并坚持整数是万物的“尺度”。他们惊愕、不安地发现，某些比，如等腰直角三角形斜边与直角边之比，不能用整数表达。他们称能用整数表达者为可公度比，不能者为不可公度比。因此，我们表示为无理数2的东西，是不可公度比。这一发现归于梅塔蓬图姆的希帕索斯（公元前五世纪）。古老故事说，当时毕达哥拉斯学派正在海上，希帕索斯因在宇宙中发现一个否定万象可归结为整数或其比的学说的要素，被扔进海里。

The Greeks did encounter one to them insuperable difficulty in the logical development of numbers. As we know, the Pythagoreans of the fifth century b.c. were the first to stress the importance of the whole numbers and ratios of whole numbers in the study of nature and in fact they insisted that the whole numbers were the “measure” of all things. They were startled and disturbed to discover that some ratios, for example, the ratio of the hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle to an arm, cannot be expressed by whole numbers. They called ratios which are expressed by whole numbers commensurable ratios and those that are not so expressible, incommensurable ratios. Thus what we express as the irrational number 2 was an incommensurable ratio. The discovery of incommensurable ratios is attributed to Hippasus of Metapontum (fifth century b.c.). An old story relates that the Pythagoreans were at sea at the time and Hippasus was thrown overboard for having produced an element in the universe which denied the Pythagorean doctrine that all phenomena in the universe can be reduced to whole numbers or their ratios.

毕达哥拉斯学派证明了2与1不可公度，即2是无理数；按亚里士多德说法，方法是归谬法，也就是间接证明。它说明，若等腰直角三角形斜边与直角边可公度，同一个数就必须既奇又偶，当然不可能。证明如下：假设斜边与直角边之比可表示为a/b，a、b为整数；若有公因子，假定已约去。若a/b = 2，则a2 = 2b2。a2为偶数，故a必为偶数，因为奇数平方为奇数*。a/b已是最简分数，因此a为偶数时，b必为奇数。令a = 2c，则a2 = 4c2；又a2 = 2b2，故4c2 = 2b2，即2c2 = b2，因此b2为偶数。于是b为偶数，因为若为奇数，平方也为奇数。但b又是奇数，因此矛盾。

The proof that 2 is incommensurable with 1, or irrational, was given by the Pythagoreans and according to Aristotle the method was a reductio ad absurdum, that is, the indirect method. It shows that if the hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle is commensurable with an arm then the same number must be both odd and even, which of course is untenable. The proof runs as follows: Suppose the ratio of hypotenuse to arm is expressible as ab, where a and b are whole numbers, and if a and b have a common factor suppose that this is cancelled. If ab = 2, then a2 = 2b2. Since a2 is even, a must be even, for the square of any odd number is odd.* Now the ratio ab is in its lowest terms and therefore since a is even b must be odd. Since a is even, let a = 2c. Then a2 = 4c2 and since a2 = 2b2, 4c2 = 2b2, or 2c2 = b2, and so b2 is even. Then b is even, for if it were odd its square would be odd. But b is also odd, and so there is a contradiction.

*任何奇整数均可表示为某个n对应的2n + 1。于是(2n + 1)²= 4n2 + 4n + 1，必为奇数。

*Any odd whole number can be expressed as 2n + 1 for some n. Then (2n + 1)² = 4n2 + 4n + 1, and this is necessarily odd.

毕达哥拉斯学派与一般古典希腊人，不接受无理数，因为无法理解概念。证明告诉我们2不是整数之比，却不告诉我们无理数是什么。如前所述，巴比伦人确实使用这类数，但无疑不知道，他们的小数（六十进制）近似永不能精确。我们可以赞扬其无忧无虑的精神，却不能称其为数学家。古典希腊人属于另一种思想类型，不能满足于近似。

The Pythagoreans and the classical Greeks generally would not accept irrational numbers because an understanding of the concept eluded them. The Pythagorean proof tells us that 2 is not a ratio of whole numbers but it does not tell us what an irrational is. The Babylonians, as we have noted, did work with such numbers. But they undoubtedly did not know that their decimal (sexagesimal) 'approximations could never be made exact. We may hail their blithe spirits but mathematicians they never were. The classical Greeks were of a different intellectual breed and could not be content with approximation.

无理数的发现提出了希腊数学的核心问题。柏拉图在《法律篇》中要求认识不可公度量。曾一度为柏拉图学生的欧多克索斯解决了问题：以几何方式理解一切量。因此，长度、角度、面积和体积，其中某些若以数表达将为无理数，都用几何处理。例如，欧几里得把毕达哥拉斯定理表述为，直角三角形斜边上的正方形，等于两直角边上的正方形之和。他说正方形之和，是指两个面积在几何上合并，等于斜边上正方形的面积。求助几何可以理解。把1与2作为长度，即线段处理时，二者的区别就被消除了。

The discovery of irrationals posed a problem which is central to Greek mathematics. Plato in the Laws called for a knowledge of incom-mensurables. The resolution of the problem, which was due to Eudoxus, for a time a pupil of Plato, was to think of all magnitudes geometrically. Thus lengths, angles, areas, and volumes, some of which would be irrational if expressed numerically, were treated geometrically. For example, Euclid states the Pythagorean theorem in the form, the square on the hypotenuse of a right triangle is the sum of the squares on the arms. And by the sum of the squares he meant that the two areas geometrically combined equalled the area of the square on the hypotenuse. The resort to geometry is understandable. When 1 and 2 are treated as lengths, that is, line segments, the distinction between 1 and 2 is obliterated.

无理数问题不仅是用数表示长度、面积、体积。二次方程，如x2 − 2 = 0的根很可能为无理数，因此古典希腊人以几何求解，使根表现为线段，又避免使用无理数。这称为几何代数。因此，《几何原本》既是几何著作，也是代数著作。

The problem presented by irrational numbers was greater than just that of representing lengths, areas, and volumes numerically. Since the roots of quadratic equations, e.g., x2 - 2 = 0, can very well be irrational numbers, the classical Greeks solved these equations geometrically so that the roots appeared as line segments and again the need to use irrational numbers was avoided. This development is referred to as geometrical algebra. Euclid’s Elements is consequently a treatise on algebra as well as geometry.

把除整数理论外的一切数学转为几何，有几个重大后果。首先，迫使数与几何严格分离，因为只有几何能处理不可公度比。自欧几里得起，这两分支必须严格区分。此外，几何涵盖数学的大部分，成为几乎所有“严格”数学的基础，至少直到1600年。我们仍称x2为x平方、x3为x立方，而不是x的二次方、三次方，因为对于一般量，x2与x3曾只有几何意义。

The conversion of all of mathematics except the theory of whole numbers into geometry had several major consequences. For one thing, it forced a sharp separation between number and geometry, for only geometry could handle incommensurable ratios. From Euclid’s time onward these two branches of mathematics had to be sharply distinguished. Also, because geometry embraced the bulk of mathematics it became the basis for almost all “rigorous” mathematics until at least 1600. We still speak of x2 as x square and x3 as x cube instead of x second or x third because for general magnitudes x2 and x3 once had only geometrical meaning.

用几何表示数及数的运算，当然不实用。把2·3理解为矩形面积，在逻辑上或可满足；若需知道乘积数值，却不够。对科学与工程，几何图形远不如能计算到所需小数位的数值答案有用。应用科学与工程必须定量。海上船舶要知道位置，必须以经纬度数值知道。有效建造建筑、桥梁、船舶与水坝，必须知道所用长度、面积与体积的数量尺度，使各部分恰好配合；事实上，必须在施工前获得这些定量知识。但古典希腊人视精确推理为至高重要，贬低商业、航海、建筑与历法应用，满足于用几何解决无理数困难。

The geometric representation of numbers and of operations with numbers was, of course, not practical. One might be satisfied logically to think of 2 • 3 as the area of a rectangle but if one needed to know the product numerically this would not suffice. For science and engineering, geometrical figures are not nearly so useful as a numerical answer which can be calculated to as many decimal places as needed. Applied science and engineering must be quantitative. When a ship at sea needs to know its location, it must know it numerically, in terms of degrees of latitude and longitude. To construct efficiently buildings, bridges, ships, and dams, one must know the quantitative measures of lengths, areas, and volumes to be employed, so that the parts will fit nicely; in fact this quantitative knowledge must be obtained in advance of the construction. But the classical Greeks, who regarded exact reasoning as paramount in importance and deprecated applications to commerce, navigation, construction, and calendar-reckoning, were content with their geometrical solution of the difficulty with irrational numbers.

约公元前300年，亚历山大里亚希腊文明继古典希腊文明而起（第I章），融合了古典希腊、埃及与巴比伦文明。从逻辑发展看，它产生演绎数学与经验数学的奇特混合。主要数学家阿基米德与阿波罗尼奥斯，大体追求《几何原本》的公理演绎几何。甚至在力学著作中，阿基米德也从公理出发证明定理。但亚历山大里亚人受更务实的埃及人、巴比伦人影响，把数学用于实际。因此，他们推导可定量测量长度、面积、体积的公式。埃及亚历山大里亚的工程师希罗（公元一世纪），在《度量论》中给出三角形面积公式：s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c),其中a、b、c为边长，s为半周长。这类公式的值常为无理数。这个公式尤其非凡。古典希腊人认为三个以上数的乘积无意义，因为没有几何意义；希罗却没有这种顾虑。亚历山大里亚希腊人发展的许多纯科学与应用科学中，包括历法、计时、航海数学、光学、地理学、气体力学与流体静力学（第I章），都自由使用无理数。

Classical Greek civilization was succeeded about 300 b.c. by Alexandrian Greek civilization (Chapter I). This was a fusion of classical Greek civilization and the Egyptian and Babylonian civilizations. From the standpoint of the logical development it produced a curious blend of deductive and empirical mathematics. The chief mathematicians, Archimedes and Apollonius, pursued in the main the axiomatic, deductive geometry of Euclid’s Elements. Even in his treatises on mechanics, Archimedes started with axioms and proved theorems. However, the Alexandrians, influenced by the more practically minded Egyptians and Babylonians, put mathematics to use. And so we find in Alexandria that formulas which would permit quantitative measures of lengths, areas, and volumes were derived. Thus the Alexandrian-Egyptian engineer Heron (first century a.d.) in his Metrica gives as the formula for the area of a triangle:s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c),s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c), wherein a, b, and c are the lengths of the sides and s is half the perimeter. The values given by such formulas are often irrational numbers. This particular formula is remarkable. Whereas the classical Greeks regarded the product of more than three numbers as meaningless because the product had no geometrical significance, Heron had no such qualms. In the many pure and applied sciences that the Alexandrian Greeks developed, calendar-reckoning, the measurement of time, the mathematics of navigation, optics, geography, pneumatics, and hydrostatics (Chapter I), irrational numbers were used freely.

亚历山大里亚人的最高成就，是喜帕恰斯与托勒密创立定量天文学，即能预测行星、太阳与月球运动的地心天文学（第I章）。为此，他们创立三角学，使人可根据三角形部分要素的信息，计算其他要素。托勒密方法不同于现代，必须计算圆的弦长。他以演绎几何建立某些弦长与其他弦长关系的基本结果，再使用算术与少量代数，计算最终关心的弦长。大多弦长为无理数。他满足于有理近似，但工作中毫不犹豫地使用无理数。

The supreme achievement of the Alexandrians was the creation of a quantitative astronomy by Hipparchus and Ptolemy, a geocentric astronomy which enabled man to predict the motions of the planets, the sun, and the earth’s moon (Chapter I). To develop this quantitative astronomy Hipparchus and Ptolemy created trigonometry, the branch of mathematics that enables one to calculate some parts of a triangle on the basis of information about other parts. Because Ptolemy approached trigonometry differently from the modern method, he was obliged to calculate the lengths of chords of a circle. Though he used deductive geometry to establish his basic results as to how some chords relate to others in size, he then proceeded to use arithmetic and bits of algebra to calculate the lengths of the chords with which he was finally concerned. Most of these lengths are irrational. Ptolemy was content to obtain rational approximations but in the course of his work he did not hesitate to use irrationals.

然而，亚历山大里亚希腊人如此自由使用、继承自埃及人与巴比伦人的算术与代数，没有逻辑基础。托勒密及其他人大体采用埃及、巴比伦态度，未经批判地使用π、2、3等无理数，必要时求近似。最著名的无理数应用，是阿基米德计算π介于3又1/10与3又10/71之间。无论他是否知道π无理，为获得近似，他计算了许多必定知道是无理数的平方根。

However, the arithmetic and algebra used so freely by the Alexandrian Greeks and taken over from the Egyptians and the Babylonians, had no logical foundation. Ptolemy and the other Alexandrian Greeks generally adopted the Egyptian and Babylonian attitude. Irrational numbers such as π, 2, 3, and the like were used uncritically and approximated where necessary. For example, the most famous use of irrationals was Archimedes’ calculation that π lies between 3 110 and 3 1071. Whether or not he knew that π was irrational, he calculated any number of square roots that he surely knew to be irrational in order to obtain the approximations.

对本书目的，同样值得注意的是，他们独立于几何，恢复埃及与巴比伦代数。复兴中的突出人物是希罗与另一位亚历山大里亚希腊人丢番图（公元三世纪）。两人都为算术、代数问题本身研究它们，不依赖几何提供动机或支撑逻辑。希罗用纯算术程序提出并解决代数问题。例如：给定正方形，面积与周长之和为896英尺，求边长。为解相应二次方程，他在两边加4配方，再取平方根。他不证明，只描述进行何种运算。著作中有许多类似问题。

As noteworthy for present purposes as the free use of irrationals was the resumption, independent of geometry, of Egyptian and Babylonian algebra. Outstanding in the revival were Heron and Diophantus (third century, a.d.), another Greek of Alexandria. Both treated arithmetical and algebraic problems in and for themselves and did not depend upon geometry either for motivation or to bolster the logic. Heron formulated and solved algebraic problems by purely arithmetical procedures. For example, he treated this problem: Given a square such that the sum of its area and perimeter is 896 feet, find the side. To solve the pertinent quadratic equation Heron completed the square by adding 4 to both sides and took the square root. He did not prove but merely described what operations to perform. There are many such problems in Heron’s work.

希罗在《几何论》中谈相加面积、周长与直径；当然，他指相加数值。同样，说把正方形乘以正方形，是指求数值乘积。他还把大量希腊几何代数转为算术、代数过程。他与后继者的某些问题，与公元前2000年巴比伦、埃及文本中的完全相同。这些希腊代数工作以文字写出，不使用符号，也不给程序证明。自希罗起，导向方程的问题也成为常见谜题。

In his Geometrica Heron spoke of adding an area, a circumference, and a diameter. In using such words he meant, of course, that he wanted to add the numerical values. Likewise when he said he multiplied a square by a square he meant that he was finding the product of the numerical values. Heron also translated much of the Greek geometrical algebra into arithmetical and algebraic processes. Some of his and his successors’ problems are exactly those which appeared in Babylonian and Egyptian texts of 2000 b.c. This Greek algebraic work was written in verbal form. No symbolism was used. Nor were any proofs of the procedures given. From the time of Heron onward, problems leading to equations were also a common form of puzzle.

亚历山大里亚希腊代数在丢番图处达到顶峰。我们几乎不知道其出身、生平。他的工作远超同时代人，却不幸来得太晚，未能在当时产生大影响，因为毁灭浪潮（第II章）已淹没文明。他写过几部完全失传的书，但最伟大著作《算术》仍有六部分；他称全书十三部分。如埃及莱因德纸草书，它是独立问题的集合。献辞说，写成为系列练习，是帮助一位学生学习。

The highest point of Alexandrian Greek algebra was reached with Diophantus. We know almost nothing about his origins or life. His work, which towers above his contemporaries’, unfortunately came too late to be highly influential in his times because a destructive tide (Chapter II) was already engulfing the civilization. Diophantus wrote several books which are entirely lost, but we do have six parts of his greatest work, the Arithmetical which, Diophantus said, comprised thirteen parts. The Arithmetica, like the Egyptian Rhind papyrus, is a collection of separate problems. The dedication says that it was written as a series of exercises to help one of his students learn the subject.

丢番图的一大进步，是在代数中引入某些符号。没有其亲笔手稿，只有十三世纪以后较晚的抄本，因此不知准确形式；但他确实用过对应于我们的x、直至x6的幂，以及1/x的符号。符号出现当然非凡，而使用高于三次的幂更加非凡，因为如前所述，古典希腊人认为三个以上因子的乘积没有几何意义。但纯算术上，这些乘积有意义，正是他采用的基础。

One of Diophantus’s big steps was to introduce some symbolism in algebra. Since we do not have manuscripts written by him but only much later ones, dating from the thirteenth century on, we do not know his precise forms, but he did use symbols corresponding to our x, powers of x up to x6, and our 1/x. The appearance of such symbolism is of course remarkable, but the use of powers higher than three is all the more extraordinary because, as we have noted, for the classical Greeks a product of more than three factors had no geometrical significance. On a purely arithmetical basis, however, such products do have a meaning, and this is precisely the basis Diophantus adopted.

丢番图把解法写成连贯文字，如我们写散文。运算完全是算术性的，不诉诸几何说明或支持断言。因此，(x − 1)(x − 2)如我们一样用代数计算。他也使用a2 − b2 = (a − b)(a + b)等恒等式及更复杂的恒等式。严格说，是步骤用到恒等式，恒等式本身却未出现。

Diophantus wrote out his solutions in a continuous text, as we write prose. His execution of the operations is entirely arithmetical; that is, there is no appeal to geometry to illustrate or substantiate his assertions. Thus, (x - \){x - 2) is carried out algebraically as we do it. He also used algebraic identities such as a2 - b2 = (a - b)(a + b) and more complicated ones. Strictly, he made steps which used identities, but these identities themselves do not appear.

其代数另一非凡特点，是求解不定方程，例如一个方程含两个未知数。以前也考虑过，在毕达哥拉斯学派关于x2 + y2 = z2的整数解研究及其他著作中出现。但丢番图广泛研究，创立了如今确实称为丢番图分析的代数分支。

Another unusual feature of Diophantus’s algebra is his solution of indeterminate equations, for example, one equation in two unknowns. Such equations had been considered before, in the Pythagorean work on integral solutions of x2 + y2 = z2 and in other writings. Diophantus, however, pursued the subject extensively and was the founder of the branch of algebra now called, in fact, Diophantine analysis.

丢番图虽以代数运用著名，却只接受正有理根，忽略其他根。即使一元二次方程有两个正有理根，也只给较大者。方程明显导向两个负根、无理根或虚根时，他拒绝方程，说不可解。对于无理根，他回溯步骤，说明修改方程后可得有理根。这里，他不同于希罗与阿基米德。希罗是工程师，所求量可能无理，因此接受，但当然求近似获得有用值。阿基米德也求精确答案，无理时以不等式界定其范围。

Though Diophantus is notable for his use of algebra, he accepted only positive rational roots and ignored all others. Even when a quadratic equation in one unknown had two positive rational roots, he gave only one, the larger one. When an equation clearly led to two negative roots, or irrational or imaginary roots, he rejected the equation and said it was not solvable. In the case of irrational roots, he retraced his steps and showed how by altering the equation he could get a new one which had rational roots. Here Diophantus differed from Heron and Archimedes. Heron was an engineer and the quantities he sought could be irrational. Hence, he accepted them, though, of course, he approximated to obtain a useful value. Archimedes also sought exact answers, and when they were irrational he obtained inequalities to bound the irrational.

不知道丢番图如何获得方法。他不诉诸几何，不大可能是转换欧几里得解二次方程的方法。而且，欧几里得没有不定问题；作为一类，它们在丢番图处是新的。缺乏亚历山大里亚晚期思想连续性资料，我们难在希腊前人中找到工作痕迹。他的方法实际上更接近巴比伦，有模糊迹象显示巴比伦影响。但不同于巴比伦人，他用符号，并求解不定方程。整体工作是代数的丰碑。

We do not know how Diophantus arrived at his methods. Since he made no appeal to geometry, it is not likely that he translated Euclid’s methods for solving quadratics. Indeterminate problems, moreover, do not occur in Euclid and as a class are new with Diophantus. Because we lack information on the continuity of thought in the late Alexandrian period, we cannot find many traces of Diophantus’s work in his Greek predecessors. His methods are, in fact, closer to Babylonian, and there are vague indications of Babylonian influences. However, unlike the Babylonians, he used symbolism and undertook the solution of indeterminate equations. His work as a whole is a monument in algebra.

就算术、代数而言，希罗、丢番图，以及阿基米德、托勒密的著作，像埃及、巴比伦程序性文本，告诉人怎样做。欧几里得、阿波罗尼奥斯与阿基米德几何中的演绎、有序证明消失了。问题以归纳处理：展示具体问题解法，推想适用于未指明范围的一般类别。整数、分数、无理数等各种数类，当然没有定义（欧几里得对整数不完善的工作除外），也没有能建立演绎结构的公理基础。

The works of Heron and Diophantus, and of Archimedes and Ptolemy as far as arithmetic and algebra are concerned, read like the procedural texts of the Egyptians and Babylonians which tell us how to do things. The deductive orderly proof of the geometry of Euclid, Apollonius, and Archimedes was gone. The problems were treated inductively in that they showed methods for solving concrete problems presumably applicable to general classes whose extent was not specified. The various types of numbers, whole numbers, fractions, and irrationals (except for Euclid’s imperfect work with the whole numbers) were certainly not defined. Nor was there any axiomatic basis on which a deductive structure could be erected.

因此，希腊人遗留了截然不同、发展方式不相似的两数学分支：一边是演绎、系统、虽有些缺陷的几何；另一边是经验算术及其代数扩展。古典希腊人要求数学结果从明确公理基础演绎得到，然而独立算术与代数出现，却无自身逻辑结构，这成为数学史的重大反常现象之一。

Thus, the Greeks bequeathed two sharply different and dissimilarly developed branches of mathematics. On the one hand, there was the deductive, systematic, albeit somewhat faulty geometry, and on the other, the empirical arithmetic and its extension to algebra. In view of the fact that the classical Greeks required mathematical results to be derived deductively from an explicit axiomatic basis, the emergence of an independent arithmetic and algebra with no logical structure of its own proffered what became one of the great anomalies of the history of mathematics.

阿拉伯人最终摧毁亚历山大里亚希腊文明后，印度人与阿拉伯人接过数学的接力棒，更进一步违背古典希腊数学观。他们当然使用整数与分数，也毫不犹豫使用无理数，甚至引入无理数加、减、乘、除的新正确规则。这些规则无逻辑基础，如何提出、为何正确？答案是类比推理。例如，显然36 = 49正确，便认为规则ab = ab对所有a、b成立。印度人甚至说，根式可像整数处理。

The Hindus and Arabs, who carried the ball for mathematics after the final destruction of the Alexandrian Greek civilization by the Arabs, violated still further the classical Greek concept of mathematics. They of course used whole numbers and fractions, but they also used irrational numbers unhesitatingly. In fact, they introduced new and correct rules for adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing irrational numbers. Since these rules did not have a logical foundation, how could they have been devised and why were they correct? The answer is that the Hindus and Arabs reasoned by analogy. Thus the rule ab = ab was justi-fled for all numbers a and b because evidently 36 = 49 was correct. In fact, the Hindus said that radicals could be handled like integers.

印度人远比希腊人天真，未看到无理数概念的逻辑困难。对计算的兴趣使他们忽略希腊思想中的根本区别。但随意把类似有理数的程序用于无理数，确实推动数学进步。而且，其全部算术完全独立于几何。

The Hindus were far more naive than the Greeks in that they failed to see the logical difficulties involved in the concept of irrational numbers. Their interest in calculation caused them to overlook distinctions that were fundamental in Greek thought. However, in casually applying to irrationals procedures like those used for rationals, they helped mathematics to make progress. Moreover, their entire arithmetic was completely independent of geometry.

印度人引入负数表示债务，增加数学家的逻辑苦恼。在这种应用中，正数表示资产。最早已知运用者是约公元628年的婆罗摩笈多；他仅陈述负数四则运算规则，无定义、公理或定理。十二世纪主要印度数学家婆什迦罗指出，正数的平方根有正、负两个。他提出负数平方根问题，却说没有平方根，因为其平方将为负数，而负数不能是平方。

The Hindus added to the logical woes of mathematicians by introducing negative numbers to represent debts. In such uses positive numbers represented assets. The first known use was by Brahmagupta about a.d. 628, who merely stated rules for the four operations with negative numbers. No definitions, axioms, or theorems appeared. Bhaskara, the leading Hindu mathematician of the twelfth century, pointed out that the square root of a positive number is twofold, positive and negative. He brought up the matter of square root of a negative number but said that there is no square root because the square of it would be a negative number and a negative number can not be a square.

并非所有印度人接受负数。甚至婆什迦罗给问题两解50与−5时，也说：“这里不取第二个值，因为不合适；人们不认可负解。”尽管如此，引入后负数使用日益增加。

Negative numbers were not accepted by all the Hindus. Even Bhaskara said, while giving 50 and -5 as two solutions of a problem, “The second value is in this case not to be taken, for it is inadequate; people do not approve of negative solutions.” Nevertheless, negative numbers were used increasingly after they were introduced.

印度人在代数也有进展，用词语缩写与少量符号描述运算和未知数。符号虽不广泛，却足以认为这方面优于丢番图。解法只给步骤，无理由或证明。一般承认二次方程的负根与无理根。

The Hindus also made some progress in algebra. They used abbreviations of words and a few symbols to describe operations and unknowns. The symbolism, though not extensive, was enough for us to regard Hindu algebra as superior in this respect to Diophantus’s. Of solutions only the steps were given. No reasons or proofs accompanied them. Generally, negative and irrational roots of quadratic equations were recognized.

印度人运用代数，比迄今所述更自由。例如，三角学告诉我们，任意角A满足sin2A + cos2A = 1。对三角学创始人及系统阐述者之一托勒密，这个方程表述为涉及圆弦关系的几何命题。如前所述，他虽自由用算术从已知长度计算未知长度，基本数学与论证却是几何性的。印度人则把三角关系表达得近似上述形式。而且，从sin A计算cos A时，能够且确实使用该方程与简单代数。即他们远比依赖几何更依赖代数，表达并推导角的正弦、余弦关系。

The Hindus used algebra even more freely than we have thus far indicated. For example, we learn in trigonometry that if A is any angle then sin2 A + cos2 A = 1. For Ptolemy, one of the creators and the systematic expositor of trigonometry, this equation was phrased as a geometrical statement involving a relation between the chords of a circle. Though, as we noted, Ptolemy did use arithmetic freely to calculate unknown lengths in terms of known ones, his basic mathematics and arguments were geometrical. The Hindus expressed the trigonometric relationships much as stated above. Moreover, to calculate cos A from sin A, they could and did use the above equation and simple algebra. That is, Hindu trigonometry relied far more on algebra than on geometry to express and derive relations among the sines and cosines of angles.

概述表明，印度人兴趣与贡献在数学的算术、计算活动，而非演绎模式。他们称数学为ganita，即计算科学。有许多好程序与娴熟技术，却无证据表明考虑证明。他们有规则，却显然无逻辑顾虑。而且，任何数学领域都没有获得一般方法或新视角。

As our survey indicates the Hindus were interested in and contributed to the arithmetical and computational activities of mathematics rather than to the deductive pattern. Their name for mathematics is ganita, which means the science of calculation. There is much good procedure and technical facility but no evidence that they considered proof at all. They had rules but apparently no logical scruples. Moreover, no general methods or new viewpoints were arrived at in any area of mathematics.

相当确定，印度人不理解自身贡献的意义。少数好思想，如1至9的独立符号、把六十进位值记数转换为十进制、负数，以及承认0为数，都随意引入，似乎不知是有价值的创新。他们对数学价值不敏感，把自己提出的好思想，与埃及、巴比伦最粗糙思想混合。阿拉伯历史学家比鲁尼（973—1048）说：“我只能把其数学与天文学文献……比作珍珠贝与酸枣的混合，珍珠与粪便的混合，或昂贵水晶与普通石子的混合。两类在他们眼中相等，因为他们不能提升到严格科学演绎的方法。”他们特长在算术，又扩展算术、代数，因此工作扩大了以经验、直觉为基础的数学部分。

It is fairly certain that the Hindus did not appreciate the significance of their own contributions. The few good ideas they had, such as separate symbols for the numbers from 1 to 9, the conversion from positional notation in base 60 to base 10, negative numbers, and the recognition of 0 as a number, were introduced casually with no apparent realization that they were valuable innovations. They were not sensitive to mathematical values. The fine ideas which they themselves advanced, they commingled with the crudest ideas of the Egyptians and Babylonians. The Arab historian al-Biruni (973-1048) said of Hindus, “I can only compare their mathematical and astronomical literature ... to a mixture of pearl shells and sour dates, or of pearl and dung, or of costly crystals and common pebbles. Both kinds of things are equal in their eyes, since they cannot raise themselves to the methods of a strictly scientific deduction.” Since their special gift was arithmetical and they had added to arithmetic and algebra, the effect of the Hindu work was to enlarge the portion of mathematics which rested on empirical and intuitive foundations.

印度人几乎忽略演绎几何，阿拉伯人却批判性研究希腊几何，充分理解演绎证明在确立这一分支的作用。但在阿拉伯数学中作用更大的算术、代数领域，他们像印度人一样，满足于经验、具体、直觉基础。某些人确以几何论证支持二次方程解法，但主要方法不同于古典希腊人，是代数性的。对于x3 + 3x2 + 7x + 5 = 0等三次方程，只给几何构造，因为代数程序尚待发现。但构造不能以直尺、圆规完成，论证不严格演绎。在数学活跃的所有世纪，阿拉伯人在自己的贡献中，顽强抵抗了精确推理的诱惑。

Whereas the Hindus practically ignored deductive geometry, the Arabs made critical studies of the Greek geometrical works and appreciated fully the role of deductive proof in establishing this branch of mathematics. However, in the field of arithmetic and algebra, which played a larger role in Arabic mathematics, the Arabs proceeded much like the Hindus. They were content to treat these subjects on the same empirical, concrete, and intuitive basis as their Hindu predecessors. Some Arabs did give geometrical arguments to support their solutions of quadratic equations but the primary approach and methodology of solution, unlike that of the classical Greeks, was algebraic. In the case of the solution of cubic equations, such as x3 + 3x2 + 7x + 5 = 0, they gave only geometric constructions because the algebraic process was yet to be discovered. But these constructions could not be carried out with straightedge and compass and the arguments were not strictly deductive. During all the centuries in which they were active in mathematics, the Arabs in their own contributions manfully resisted the lures of exact reasoning.

印度与阿拉伯数学最有趣的特点，是自相矛盾的数学观。埃及与巴比伦人满足于以经验接受少数算术、几何规则，不奇怪，这是几乎所有人类知识的自然基础。但印度与阿拉伯人知道希腊人提出的全新数学证明概念，却在算术、代数中完全不关注演绎证明。印度态度尚可解释：虽知希腊著作，却少关注，主要追随亚历山大里亚希腊人对算术、代数的处理。但阿拉伯人充分了解希腊几何，甚至批判研究。而且，两文明都有几百年利于纯科学研究的条件，因此实用成果的压力，不必使人牺牲证明换即时效用。两民族怎会与古典及许多亚历山大里亚希腊人如此不同地处理这两领域？

The most interesting feature of the mathematics of the Hindus and Arabs is their self-contradictory concept of the subject. That the Egyptians and Babylonians were content to accept their few arithmetic and geometric rules on an empirical basis is not surprising. This is a natural basis for almost all human knowledge. But the Hindus and Arabs were aware of the totally new concept of mathematical proof promulgated by the Greeks. Yet in arithmetic and algebra they did not concern themselves at all with the notion of deductive proof. The Hindu attitude is somewhat rationalizable. Though they did indeed possess some knowledge of the Greek works, they paid little attention to them and followed primarily the Alexandrian Greek treatment of arithmetic and algebra. But the Arabs were fully aware of Greek geometry and, as we have observed, even made critical studies of it. Moreover, in both civilizations, conditions for the pursuit of pure science were favorable for a number of centuries so that the pressure to produce practically useful results need not have caused mathematicians to sacrifice proof for immediate utility. How could both peoples treat the two areas of mathematics so differently from the classical and many of the Alexandrian Greeks?

有许多可能答案。尽管阿拉伯人评论演绎几何，两文明总体缺乏批判性，因此可能满足于原样接受数学：几何应演绎，算术、代数却可经验性或启发性。第二种可能是，双方，尤其阿拉伯人，理解几何与算术、代数的标准差异，却不知如何为算术提供逻辑基础。似乎支持这一解释的事实，是阿拉伯人至少给出几何依据，支撑二次、三次方程解法。

There are numerous possible answers. Both civilizations were on the whole uncritical, despite the Arabic commentaries on deductive geometry. Hence they may have been content to take mathematics as they found it: geometry was to be deductive but arithmetic and algebra could be empirical or heuristic. A second possibility is that both of these peo-pies, the Arabs especially, appreciated the widely different standards for geometry as opposed to arithmetic and algebra but did not see how to supply a logical foundation for arithmetic. One fact which seems to vouch for such an explanation is that the Arabs did at least support their solution of quadratic and cubic equations by giving the geometric basis.

还有其他可能的解释。印度人与阿拉伯人都偏好算术、代数，以及三角关系的代数表达。这种倾向可能表明不同的思维方式，也可能反映他们对各自文明需求的回应。两种文明都注重实际，而如我们谈亚历山大里亚希腊人时所指出，实际需求确实需要算术、代数所提供的定量结果。支持思维特征可能不同这一论点的一个证据，来自欧洲人对印度人与阿拉伯人传下的数学遗产的反应。我们将看到，欧洲人远更为算术与几何的不同状况而困扰。无论如何，印度人与阿拉伯人的大胆尝试，再次使算术、代数走到前台；就实用性而言，使其几乎与几何并驾齐驱。

There are other possible explanations. Both the Hindus and Arabs favored arithmetic, algebra, and the algebraic formulation of trigonometric relationships. This predisposition may bespeak a different mentality or may reflect the response to the needs of the civilizations. Both of these civilizations were practically oriented and, as we have had occasion to note in connection with the Alexandrian Greeks, practical needs do call for quantitative results that are supplied by arithmetic and algebra. One bit of evidence which favors the thesis that there may be different mental traits comes from the reaction of the Europeans to the mathematical heritage handed down by the Hindus and Arabs. As we shall see, the Europeans were far more troubled by the disparate states of arithmetic and geometry. In any case, Hindu and Arab venturesomeness brought arithmetic and algebra to the fore once again and, insofar as utility is concerned, placed it almost on a par with geometry.

中世纪晚期与文艺复兴时期的欧洲人，部分通过阿拉伯人，部分通过直接获得希腊手稿，取得既有数学知识时，试图面对两种数学提出的困境。真正的数学，看来无疑应是希腊人的演绎几何。另一方面，他们无法否认自古代发展起来、却无逻辑基础的算术与代数的实用性和效力。

When the Europeans of the late medieval period and the Renaissance acquired the existing knowledge of mathematics partly through the Arabs and partly through the direct acquisition of Greek manuscripts, they attempted to face the dilemma presented by the two kinds of mathematics. Real mathematics seemed definitely to be the deductive geometry of the Greeks. On the other hand, the Europeans could not deny the utility and efficacy of the arithmetic and algebra that had been developed since ancient times but had no logical foundation.

他们首先面对的问题，是如何处理无理数。意大利数学家卢卡·帕乔利（约1445—约1514）、著名德国修士及耶拿数学教授米夏埃尔·施蒂费尔（1486？—1567）、医生、学者兼无赖杰罗姆·卡尔丹（1501—1576），以及军事工程师西蒙·斯蒂文（1548—1620），沿用印度、阿拉伯传统使用无理数，并引入越来越多的类型。例如，施蒂费尔使用形如a+bnm的无理数。卡尔丹使用含立方根的无理数。弗朗索瓦·韦达（1540—1603）关于π的表达式，体现了无理数使用的程度。他考察单位半径圆内接的4、8、16、……边正多边形，发现

The first problem they faced was what to do about irrational numbers. The Italian mathematician Luca Pacioli (c. 1445-c. 1514), the prominent German monk and professor of mathematics at Jena, Michael Stifel (I486?—1567), the physician, scholar, and rogue Jerome Cardan (1501-1576), and the military engineer Simon Stevin (1548-1620) used irrational numbers in the tradition of the Hindus and Arabs and intro duced more and more types. Thus Stifel worked with irrationals of the form a+bnm. Jerome Cardan worked with irrationals involving cube roots. The extent to which irrationals were used is exemplified by Francois Vieta’s (1540-1603) expression for π. By considering regular polygons of 4, 8, 16, ••• sides inscribed in a circle of unit radius, Vieta found that

2π=12·12+1212·12+1212+1212⋯

2π=12·12+1212·12+1212+1212⋯

文艺复兴的一项新创造——对数——自由使用了无理数。约翰·纳皮尔（1550—1617）在十六世纪晚期发明正数的对数，目的正是此后对数一直服务的用途：加速算术运算。虽然多数正数的对数是无理数，而且纳皮尔的计算方法自由使用无理数，所有数学家仍欢迎它们带来的劳动节省。

Irrational numbers were used freely in one of the new creations of the Renaissance—logarithms. Logarithms for positive numbers were invented in the late sixteenth century by John Napier (1550-1617) for the very purpose to which they have since been put, namely, to speed up arithmetic processes. Though the logarithms of most positive numbers are irrational—and Napier’s method of calculating them used irrationals freely—all mathematicians welcomed the saving of labor that they afforded.

无理数计算自由进行，但某些使用者自己却为它们是否真正是数而苦恼。施蒂费尔在主要算术、代数著作《完整算术》（Arithmetica Integra，1544）中，呼应欧几里得关于量不同于数的观点，即欧多克索斯的几何理论；但顺应新发展，又考虑以十进记数表示无理数。他烦恼的是，无理数以小数表达，需要无限多个数字。一方面，他论证说：

Calculations with irrationals were carried on freely, but the problem of whether irrationals were really numbers troubled some of the very same people who worked with them. Thus Stifel in his major work, the Aritbmetica Integra (1544), which dealt with arithmetic and algebra, echoed Euclid’s view of magnitudes (the geometrical theory of Eudoxus) as different from numbers, but then, in line with the new developments, considered expressing irrationals in the decimal notation. What troubled him was that an irrational expressed as a decimal requires an infinite number of digits. On the one hand he argued,

在证明几何图形时，有理数无能为力之处，无理数接替它们，恰能证明有理数无法证明的东西，……因此，我们受到促动，被迫断言它们确实是数；迫使我们如此的，是使用它们产生的结果，我们感到这些结果真实、确定、恒定。另一方面，其他考虑迫使我们否认无理数根本是数。也就是说，试图将其化为记数形式［小数形式］……时，发现它们永远逃逸，没有一个能被精确地把握其自身。……本性如此缺乏精确性的东西，不能称为真正的数。……因此，正如无限数不是数，无理数也不是真正的数，而隐藏在某种无限之云中。

Since, in proving geometrical figures, when rational numbers fail us irrational numbers take their place and prove exactly those things which rational numbers could not prove, ... we are moved and compelled to assert that they truly are numbers, compelled that is, by the results which follow from their use—results which we perceive to be real, certain, and constant. On the other hand, other considerations compel us to deny that irrational numbers are numbers at all. To wit, when we seek to subject them to numeration [decimal form] ... we find that they flee away perpetually so that not one of them can be apprehended precisely in itself. . . . Now that cannot be called a true number which is of such a nature that it lacks precision. . . . Therefore, just as an infinite number is not a number, so an irrational number is not a true number, but lies hidden in a kind of cloud of infinity.

施蒂费尔接着说，真正的数不是整数就是分数，显然无理数两者都不是，因此不是真正的数。一个世纪后，帕斯卡与巴罗说，无理数只是符号，不能独立于连续几何量存在；无理数运算的逻辑必须由欧几里得量论提供依据，但该理论不足以承担这一任务。

Then Stifel added that real numbers are either whole numbers or fractions, and, obviously, irrationals are neither and so are not real numbers. A century later, Pascal and Barrow said that irrational numbers are mere symbols which have no existence independent of continuous geometrical magnitude, and the logic of operations with irrationals must be justified by the Euclidean theory of magnitudes, but this theory was inadequate for the purpose.

另一方面，也有人明确断言无理数是正当实体。斯蒂文承认无理数是数，以有理数越来越精确地逼近它们；约翰·沃利斯（1616—1703）在《代数》（1685）中也接受无理数为完全意义上的数。但两人均未提供逻辑基础。

There were, on the other hand, positive assertions that the irrational numbers are legitimate entities. Stevin recognized irrationals as numbers and approximated them more and more closely by rationals and John Wallis (1616-1703) in his Algebra (1685) also accepted irrationals as numbers in the full sense. However, neither Stevin nor Wallis supplied any logical foundations.

而且，笛卡尔在《几何学》（1637）、费马在1629年手稿中创立解析几何时，两人都没有关于无理数的清楚概念。然而，双方预设所有正实数与直线上的点一一对应，或直线上任一点到某原点的距离都可用数表达。其中许多数是无理数，两人就隐含地接受了它们，尽管没有逻辑基础。

Moreover, when Descartes in his Geometry (1637) and Fermat in his manuscript of 1629 created analytic geometry, neither had any clear notion about irrational numbers. Nevertheless, both presupposed a one-to-one correspondence between all the positive real numbers and the points on a line, or that the distance of any point on a line from some origin can be expressed as a number. Since many of these numbers were irrational, both men implicitly accepted irrationals, even though these had no logical foundation.

欧洲人也须面对负数。它们通过阿拉伯文本传入欧洲，但十六、十七世纪多数数学家不承认它们是数；即便承认，也不接受为方程的根。十五世纪的尼古拉·许凯（1445？—1500？）与十六世纪的施蒂费尔，均称负数为荒谬的数。卡尔丹给出负数根，却认为是不可能的解，只是符号。他称其为虚构的，而称正根为真实的。韦达完全排斥负数。笛卡尔有限度地接受，称负根为假根，因为它们声称代表比无还小的数。然而，他已证明，给定方程，可得另一方程，其根比原方程根大任意指定数量。因此，负根方程可变为正根方程。他说，故可把假根变为真根，从而勉强接受负数。但他从未真正与它们和解。帕斯卡认为从0减去4全然胡说。他在《思想录》中说：“我认识一些人，他们竟不理解，从零取去四，剩下的还是零。”

The Europeans also had to face negative numbers. These numbers became known in Europe through Arab texts, but most mathematicians of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries did not accept them as numbers or, if they did, would not accept them as roots of equations. In the fifteenth century Nicolas Chuquet (1445P-1500?) and in the sixteenth Stifel both spoke of negative numbers as absurd numbers. Cardan gave negative numbers as roots of equations but considered them impossible solutions, mere symbols. He called them fictitious, whereas he called positive roots real. Vieta discarded negative numbers entirely. Descartes accepted them to an extent. He called negative roots of equations false on the ground that they claim to represent numbers less than nothing. However, he had shown that given an equation one can obtain another whose roots are larger than the original one by any given quantity. Thus an equation with negative roots could be transformed into one with positive roots. Hence, he said, we can turn false roots into real roots and so reluctantly accepted negative numbers. However, he never did make his peace with them. Pascal regarded the subtraction of 4 from 0 as pure nonsense. He said in his Pensees, “I have known those who could not understand that to take four from zero there remains zero.”

神学家、数学家及帕斯卡密友安托万·阿尔诺（1612—1694），提出一个反对负数的有趣论证。他质疑−1 : 1 = 1 : −1，说−1小于+1，怎能小者比大者，等同大者比小者？莱布尼茨承认有异议，却认为可以用这种比例计算，因为形式正确，正如人们用虚量计算一样（我们很快会看到，虚量已被引入）。然而，他又含糊地说，凡无对数的量，都应称为虚的（不存在的）。据此，−1不存在，因为正对数对应大于1的数，负对数［！］对应0与1之间的数。因此，负数没有可用的对数。事实上，若log(−1)有一个数值，按对数法则，log−1应为其一半。但−1肯定没有对数。

An interesting argument against negative numbers was given by Antoine Arnauld (1612-1694), theologian, mathematician, and close friend of Pascal. Arnauld questioned that -1 : 1 = 1 : -1 because, he said, -1 is less than +1; hence, how could a smaller be to a greater as a greater is to a smaller? Leibniz agreed that there is an objection here but argued that one can calculate with such proportions because their form is correct just as one calculates with imaginary quantities (which as we shall shortly see had already been introduced). Nevertheless, he equivocated, one should call imaginary (non-existent) all those quantities which have no logarithm. On this basis -1 does not exist because positive logarithms belong to numbers greater than 1 and negative logarithms [!] belong to numbers between 0 and 1. There is then no logarithm available for negative numbers. In fact, if there were a number for log (-1), then, according to the laws of logarithms, log −1 would have to be half of that number. But certainly −1 has no logarithm.

托马斯·哈里奥特（1560—1621）是最早偶尔把负数单独放在方程一边的代数学家之一。但他不接受负根，甚至在死后出版的《解析艺术的应用》（Artis analyticae praxis，1631）中“证明”这种根不可能。拉斐尔·邦贝利（十六世纪）给负数相当清楚的定义，但无法证明运算法则，因为连正数必需的基础也不存在*。斯蒂文在方程中使用正、负系数，并接受负根。阿尔贝·吉拉尔（1595—1632）在《代数新发明》（Invention nouvelle en algèbre，1629）中，把负数与正数同等对待；即使二次方程两根都为负，也都给出。吉拉尔与哈里奥特均用减号表示减法运算与负数，但应使用不同符号，因为负数是独立概念，而减法是运算。

One of the first algebraists who occasionally placed a negative number by itself on one side of an equation was Thomas Harriot (1560-1621). But he did not accept negative roots and even “proved” in his posthumously published Artis analyticae praxis (Analytical Arts Applied, 1631) that such roots are impossible. Raphael Bombelh (16th century) gave rather clear definitions for negative numbers, though he could not justify the rules of operation because the necessary foundation even for the positive numbers was not available." Stevin used positive and negative coefficients in equations and accepted negative roots. In his Invention nouvelle en algebre (New Invention in Algebra, 1629) Albert Girard (1595-1632) placed negative numbers on a par with positive numbers and gave both roots of a quadratic equation even when both were negative. Both Girard and Harriot used the minus sign for the operation of subtraction and for negative numbers, though separate symbols should be used because a negative number is an independent concept whereas subtraction is an operation.

*正如W. H. 奥登所说：负乘负得正， 缘由不必论。

!,'As W. H. Auden put it: Minus times minus is plus, The reason for this we need not discuss.

总体而言，十六、十七世纪很少数学家能坦然对待负数，或根本接受它们；当然，也不承认它们为真正的方程根。还有奇怪信念。沃利斯虽思想超前，接受负数，却认为它们既大于∞又小于0。他在《无穷小算术》（Arithmetica infinitorum，1655）中论证：a为正时，a/0为无穷；分母改为负数，如b为负的a/b，由于分母更小，比值应大于a/0。因此，比值必大于∞。

On the whole, not many of the sixteenth- and seventeenth-century mathematicians felt at ease with or accepted negative numbers at all, and of course they did not recognize them as true roots of equations. There were also curious beliefs about them. Though Wallis was advanced for his times and accepted negative numbers, he thought they were larger than ∞ as well as less than 0. In his Aritbmetica infinitorum (Arithmetic of Infinitesimals, 1655) he argued that, since the ratio a/0, when a is positive, is infinite, then when the denominator is changed to a negative number, as in ab with b negative, the ratio should be greater than a/0 because the denominator is smaller. Thus the ratio must be greater than

邦贝利与斯蒂文等较先进思想家，提出一种表示方式，无疑有助于最终接受整个实数系。邦贝利假定，实数与直线上的长度（选定单位后）一一对应，并为长度定义四则运算。他认为，实数及其运算由这些长度与对应几何运算定义。因此，实数系在几何基础上获得合理解释。斯蒂文也视实数为长度，相信如此解释也解决无理数困难。当然，在这种观点下，实数仍与几何相联。

Some of the more advanced thinkers, Bombelli and Stevin, proposed a representation which certainly aided in the ultimate acceptance of the whole real number system. Bombelli supposed that there is a one-to-one correspondence between real numbers and lengths on a line (with a chosen unit), and he defined for the lengths the four basic operations. He regarded the real numbers and their operations as defined by these lengths and the corresponding geometric operations. Thus, the real number system was rationalized on a geometric basis. Stevin, too, regarded real numbers as lengths and believed that with this interpretation the difficulties with irrationals also are resolved. Of course, in this view the real numbers were still tied to geometry.

欧洲人尚未克服无理数与负数困难，又误打误撞闯入我们如今称为复数的领域，增添负担。他们把算术的开平方运算推广到出现的任何数，例如解二次方程时，便得到这些新数。卡尔丹在《大术》（Ars magna，1545）第37章提出并求解：把10分为两部分，乘积为40。这个似乎荒谬的问题有解，正如达朗贝尔所说：“代数慷慨，常给予比索求更多的东西。”若一部分为x，方程为x(10 − x) = 40。卡尔丹得到根5 + −15与5 − −15，随后说它们是“诡辩的量，虽巧妙却无用”。“暂且抛开涉及的精神折磨”，将两者相乘，乘积为25 − (−15)，即40。随后他说：“算术的精妙就这样前进，其终点，正如人所说，既精致又无用。”

Without having overcome their difficulties with irrational and negative numbers, the Europeans added to their burdens by blundering into what we now call complex numbers. By extending the use of the arithmetical operation of square root to whatever numbers appeared, for example, in solving quadratic equations, they obtained these new numbers. Thus Cardan in Chapter 37 of his Ars magna (The Great Art, 1545) set up and solved the problem of dividing 10 into two parts whose product is 40. This seemingly absurd problem has a solution for, as d’Alembert remarked, “Algebra is generous; it often gives more than one demands of it.” If x is one part, the equation for x is x(10 - x) = 40. Cardan obtained the roots 5 + −15 and 5 - −15 and then says there are “sophistic quantities which though ingenious are useless.” “Putting aside the mental tortures involved,” multiply 5 + −15 and 5 - −15; the product is 25 - (-15) or 40. He then stated, “So progresses arithmetic subtlety, the end of which, as is said, is as refined as it is useless.”

卡尔丹书中提出的三次方程代数解法，使他进一步涉及复数。虽只寻找、获得实根，他的公式也给出存在的复根。奇怪的是，所有根均为实时，公式却给出复数，本应由其导出实根。因此，他本应极重视复数；但不知如何求复数立方根、从而导出实根，便留下困难未解决。他以另一方法求实根。

Cardan became further involved with complex numbers in the algebraic method of solving cubic equations which he presented in his book. Though he sought and obtained only the real roots, his formula also gives the complex roots when these are present. Peculiarly, when all the roots are real, his formula yields complex numbers from which the real roots should be derivable. Hence, he should have attached great importance to complex numbers but, since he did not know how to find the cube root of complex numbers and thereby derive the real roots, he left this difficulty unresolved. He found the real roots in another way.

邦贝利也考察复数作为三次方程的解，以几乎现代形式提出复数四则运算，却仍认为无用、是“诡辩的”。吉拉尔确实承认复数至少是方程的形式解。他在《代数新发明》中说：“有人可能问：这些不可能的解［复根］有何用？我回答：有三个用处，使一般规则确定，保证没有其他解，以及它们的实用性。”但其先进观点没有影响。

Bombelli, too, considered complex numbers as the solutions of cubic equations and he formulated in practically modern form the four operations with complex numbers, but he still regarded them as useless and “sophistic.” Albert Girard did recognize complex numbers as at least formal solutions of equations. In his New Invention in Algebra he stated, “One could say: What are these impossible solutions [complex roots]? I answer: For three things, for the certitude of the general rules, that there are no other solutions, and for their utility.” However, Girard’s advanced views were not influential.

笛卡尔也排斥复根，创造了“虚的”一词。他在《几何学》中说：“真根与假根［负根］都不总是真实的；有时是虚的。”他认为，负根至少能通过将原方程变为正根方程而成为“真实的”；复根却不能如此。因此，它们不真实，而是虚的；它们不是数。

Descartes also rejected complex roots and coined the term imaginary. He said in his Geometry, “Neither the true nor the false [negative] roots are always real; sometimes they are imaginary.” He argued that whereas negative roots can at least be made “real” by transforming the equation in which they occur into another equation whose roots are positive, this cannot be done for complex roots. These, therefore, are not real but imaginary; they are not numbers.

连牛顿也不认为复根重要，很可能因为当时它们无物理意义。他在《普遍算术》（第2版，1728）中说：“方程的根经常为不可能的［复数］，是正当的，否则就会把不可能的问题情形表现得仿佛可能。”即没有物理或几何意义的解的问题，应有复根。

Not even Newton regarded complex roots as significant, most likely because in his day they lacked physical meaning. In fact, he said in his Universal Arithmetic (2nd ed., 1728), “But it is just that the Roots of Equations should be often impossible [complex], lest they should exhibit the cases of Problems that are impossible as if they were possible.” That is, problems which do not have a physically or geometrically meaningful solution should have complex roots.

莱布尼茨常被引用的话，体现对复数认识不清：“神的精神在分析的这一奇迹、理想世界的这一异象、存在与不存在之间的这一两栖者中，找到崇高出口；我们称它为负一的虚根。”莱布尼茨虽形式化使用复数，却不理解本质。为说明他与约翰·伯努利在微积分中使用它们的正当性，他说这未带来坏处。

The lack of clarity about complex numbers is illustrated by Leibniz’s oft-quoted statement, “The Divine Spirit found a sublime outlet in that wonder of analysis, that portent of the ideal world, that amphibian between being and not-being, which we call the imaginary root of negative unity.” Though Leibniz worked with complex numbers formally, he possessed no understanding of their nature. To justify the use he and John Bernoulli made of them in the calculus, Leibniz said no harm came of it.

十六、十七世纪虽无清楚理解，实数、复数的运算程序仍被改进、扩展。沃利斯在《代数》（1685）中，展示如何以几何表示实系数二次方程的复根。他实质上说，复数不比负数更荒谬；负数可在有向直线上表示，复数就应可在平面中表示。他确实给出不完整的复数表示，也给ax2 + bx + c = 0的实根或复根以几何构造。工作虽正确，却遭忽略，因为数学家不愿接受复数应用。

Despite the lack of any clear understanding during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, the operational procedures with real and complex numbers were improved and extended. In his Algebra (1685) Wallis showed how to represent geometrically the complex roots of a quadratic equation with real coefficients. Wallis said, in effect, that complex numbers are no more absurd than negative numbers and, since the latter can be represented on a directed line, it should be possible to represent complex numbers in a plane. He did give an incomplete representation of complex numbers and also a geometrical construction for the roots of ax2 + bx + c = 0 when the roots are real or complex. Though Wallis’s work was correct, it was ignored because mathematicians were not receptive to the use of complex numbers.

十七世纪数学逻辑还产生了其他问题，我们将在下一章处理；这里继续考察十八世纪数学家试图理解、证明自己使用无理数、负数、复数及代数的正当性时遇到的困难。对于（正）无理数，虽然没人定义它们、建立性质，直觉上却更易接受，因为其性质与整数、分数相同。因此，数学家自由使用，不再质疑意义或性质。包括欧拉在内的一些人相信，逻辑基础已在欧多克索斯量论中，该理论见于《几何原本》第V卷。欧多克索斯确有量的比例理论，与几何相联，却绝不是无理数理论。但十八世纪这些人对无理数，即便逻辑不清，良心也已安然。

Though other problems in the logic of mathematics arose in the seventeenth century, which we shall deal with in the next chapter, here we shall pursue the difficulties mathematicians encountered in the eighteenth century in seeking to understand and justify their work with irrational, negative, and complex numbers and with algebra. As for (positive) irrational numbers, though nothing had been done to define them and establish their properties, they were intuitively more acceptable because their properties were those of whole numbers and fractions; hence, mathematicians used them freely and raised no new challenges about their meaning or properties. Some, Euler among them, believed that the logical basis was at hand in the Eudoxian theory of magnitudes, which is expounded in Book V of Euclid’s Elements. Eudoxus did give a theory of proportion for magnitudes, a theory tied to geometry, but by no means a theory of irrational numbers. However, the consciences of these eighteenth-century men, if not their logic, were clear about irrationals.

负数远比无理数更困扰数学家，可能因为没有现成几何意义，运算法则也更奇怪。约1650年起虽较自由使用，但概念与逻辑基础不清，人们仍含糊应付其依据，或抗议使用。理性时代一位大思想家让·勒龙·达朗贝尔（1717—1783），在著名《百科全书》的“负”条目中说：“问题导向负解，意味着假设某部分为假，却被认作真。”他在负量论文中又说：“得到负解，意味着该数的相反数［对应正数］才是所求解。”

Negative numbers troubled mathematicians far more than irrational numbers did, perhaps because negatives had no readily available geometrical meaning and the rules of operation were stranger. Though negative numbers were used rather freely from about 1650 onward, since the concept and its logical foundation were not clear mathematicians continued to fudge the justification or protest their use. In his article “Negative” in the famous Encyclopedie, one of the great intellectuals of the Age of Reason, Jean Le Rond d’Alembert (1717-1783) stated that “a problem leading to a negative solution means that some part of the hypothesis was false but assumed to be true.” In his paper on negative quantities, he added, “arriving at a negative solution means that the opposition of the number [the corresponding positive] is the desired solution.

十八世纪最伟大数学家莱昂哈德·欧拉，写出有史以来最杰出的代数教科书之一。在《代数完全导论》（1770）中，他解释减去−b等于加b，因为“取消债务与馈赠礼物意义相同”。他还论证(−1)(−1) = +1，因为乘积必为+1或−1，既已证明1(−1) = −1，故(−1)(−1)必为+1。十八世纪最好的教科书，仍混淆表示减法的减号，与−2中表示负数的同一符号。

Leonhard Euler, the greatest of eighteenth-century mathematicians, wrote one of the outstanding algebra texts of all times. In his Complete Introduction to Algebra (1770), he justified the operation of subtracting -b as equivalent to adding b because “to cancel a debt signifies the same as giving a gift. He also argued that (—1)(—1) = +1 because the product must be +1 or -1 and, since he had already shown that 1(-1) = -1, then (—1)(—1) must be +1. The best texts of the eighteenth century continued to confuse the minus sign used to denote subtraction and the same sign as used in, say, -2 to denote a negative number.

整个十八世纪，人们提出许多对负数的反对意见。英国数学家弗朗西斯·马塞雷斯男爵（1731—1824），剑桥克莱尔学院院士、皇家学会会员，写过体面数学论文及厚重人寿保险理论专著。1759年出版《论代数中负号的使用》。他把二次方程类型仔细分开，说明如何避免负数，尤其负根（但允许仅表示、不实际执行从小量减去大量）。有负根的方程另行考虑，当然拒绝负根。三次方程也如此。随后他谈负根说：

Many objections to negative numbers were voiced throughout the eighteenth century. The English mathematician, Baron Francis Maseres (1731-1824), a Fellow of Clare College in Cambridge and a member of the Royal Society, wrote respectable papers in mathematics and put out a substantial treatise on the theory of life insurance. In 1759 he published his Dissertation on the Use of the Negative Sign in Algebra. He showed how to avoid negative numbers (except to indicate, without actually performing, the subtraction of a larger quantity from a smaller one), and especially negative roots, by carefully segregating the types of quadratic equations. Those with negative roots are considered separately and of course the negative roots are rejected. He does the same with cubics. Then he says of negative roots:

……据我所能判断，它们只会搅乱整个方程理论，把本性极清楚简单的东西弄得晦涩神秘。……因此，真希望负根从未进入代数，或被再次排除。若如此，有充分理由认为，许多博学聪明之人目前对代数计算的异议——认为它晦涩、充满几乎无法理解的概念——将被消除；因为确定的是，代数，或普遍算术，其本性并不比几何更不简单、更不清楚，或更不能证明。

. . . they serve only, as far as I am able to judge, to puzzle the whole doctrine of equations, and to render obscure and mysterious things that are in their own nature exceeding plain and simple. ... It were to be wished therefore that negative roots had never been admitted into algebra or were again discarded from it: for if this were done, there is good reason to imagine, the objections which many learned and ingenious men now make to algebraic computations, as being obscure and perplexed with almost unintelligible notions, would be thereby removed; it being certain that Algebra, or universal arithmetic, is, in its own nature, a science no less simple, clear, and capable of demonstration, then geometry.

关于复数意义与使用的争论更加激烈。某些数学家引入负数的对数（以及复数的对数），而这些对数是复数，使困境加剧。

The debates about the meanings and use of complex numbers were even more strident. The quandaries were compounded by the fact that some mathematicians introduced logarithms of negative numbers (as well as logarithms of complex numbers) which were complex numbers.

自1712年起，莱布尼茨、欧拉与约翰·伯努利通过书信、论文，激烈争论复数意义，尤其负数、复数的对数。莱布尼茨与伯努利沿用笛卡尔“虚的”一词指复数，并以此表示这些数（以及负数）不存在，尽管两人都奇迹般地在微积分中有效使用这些不存在的数。

Beginning in 1712, Leibniz, Euler, and John Bernoulli debated hotly through letters and papers the meaning of complex numbers and especially logarithms of negative and complex numbers. Leibniz and Bernoulli used Descartes’s term “imaginary” for complex numbers and by imaginary meant that such numbers (and negative numbers) did not exist, though both miraculously managed to make good use of these non-existent numbers in the calculus.

如前所述，莱布尼茨给出各种论证，认为负数无对数。约翰·伯努利认为log a = log(−a)，给出数种支持论证。其中一种利用正数对数定理，认为log(−a) = (12)log(−a)² = (12)log a2 = log a；另一种用微积分得同样结论。多年间，两人交换许多信件，所写大多是胡说。

Leibniz, as we have noted, gave various arguments to the effect that there are no logarithms for negative numbers. John Bernoulli’s position was that log a = log (-a) and supported this with several arguments. One, using the theorem on logarithms for positive numbers, was that log (-a) = 12 log(−a)² = 12 log a2 = log a. Another, using the calculus, drew the same conclusion. Many letters were exchanged over the years by Leibniz and John Bernoulli. Most of what was written was nonsense.

欧拉有真正答案。在1751年发表的《方程的虚根研究》中，他公布结果。最终结果正确，但由错误论证得到，适用于所有复数，包括实数，因为x + iy中y为0时就是实数。其结果为：log(x + iy) = log(ρeiφ) = log ρ + i(φ ± 2nπ)*。但同代人不理解他的论文。

Euler had the real answer. He published his result in a paper which appeared in 1751, “Investigations on the Imaginary Roots of Equations.” His final result, correct but obtained by an incorrect argument, applies to all complex numbers, which include the real, for if y is 0 in x + iy, the number is real. His result is: log (x + iy) = log(ρeiφ) = log ρ + i(φ ± 2nπ).* However, Euler’s paper was not understood by his contemporaries.

欧拉已在1747年4月15日信中把结果告知达朗贝尔。他甚至指出，正实数有无限多个对数，但只有一个为实数，即我们通常在实数计算中使用的那个。达朗贝尔未被通信或论文说服，在《论负量的对数》中，提出各种形而上学、分析与几何论证，否认这些对数存在。他成功给主题披上更神秘的面纱。他还称与高明欧拉的分歧只是用词问题，试图掩饰。

Euler had communicated his results to d’Alembert in a letter of April 15, 1747. He even pointed out that there were infinitely many logarithms of a positive real number but that only one was a real number; this is the one we usually use in computing with real numbers. D’Alembert was not convinced by the correspondence or the paper, and in his essay “On Logarithms of Negative Quantities,” he advanced all sorts of metaphysical, analytical, and geometrical arguments to deny the existence of such logarithms. He succeeded in shrouding the subject in more mystery. He also tried to cover up his differences with the masterful Euler by saying that they were just a matter of words.

参与争论的所有人，自己的思想都不一致。十八世纪上半叶，人们相信某些复数运算，例如复数的复数次幂，可能需要全新种类的数。但达朗贝尔自己在《对风的一般原因的思考》（1747）中，证明所有复数运算只产生复数。证明确需欧拉与拉格朗日修补，但此事中他迈出了重要一步。他或许认识到自己关于复数的思想处于混乱状态，因为他为《百科全书》撰写数学条目，却只字不提复数。

All of the men involved in this controversy were inconsistent in their own thinking. During the first half of the eighteenth century it was believed that some operations on complex numbers, for example, a complex power of a complex number, might call for a totally new kind of number. But it was d’Alembert himself, in Reflections on the General Cause of Winds (1747), who proved that all operations on complex numbers would lead only to complex numbers. His proof did have to be mended by Euler and Lagrange; yet in this matter d’Alembert had made a significant step. Perhaps d Alembert recognized the confused state of his own ideas on complex numbers, because in the Encyclopedie, for which he wrote the mathematical articles, he said nothing about them.

*欧拉这里使用所谓复数的极形式。ρ = x2+y2，φ是从原点到x + iy的线段与x轴的夹角。若y为0，则φ为0。

*Euler uses here what is called the polar form of a complex number. ρ = x2+y2 and φ is the angle that the line segment from the origin to x + iy makes with the x-axis. If y is 0, then φ is 0.

显然，欧拉仍未弄清复数。在1770年出版、十八世纪最好的代数教科书《代数》中，他说：

Apparently Euler, too, was still not clear about complex numbers. In his Algebra of 1770, the best algebra text of the eighteenth century, he said,

负数的平方根既非零，也不小于零或大于零。因此显然不能归入可能的数［实数］。所以必须说，它们是不可能的数。这引导我们得到这种数的概念：本性上不可能，通常称为虚数或想象的数，因为只存在于想象中。

The square roots of negative numbers are neither zero, nor less than zero, nor greater than zero. Then it is clear that the square roots of negative numbers cannot be included among the possible numbers [real numbers]. Consequently we must say that these are impossible numbers. And this circumstance leads us to the concept of such numbers, which by their nature are impossible, and ordinarily are called imaginary or fancied numbers, because they exist only in the imagination.

他也犯复数运算错误。在《代数》中写道：−1 · −4 = 4 = 2，因为ab = ab。

He also made mistakes with complex numbers. In his Algebra he writes −1 · −4 = 4 = 2 because ab = ab.

欧拉虽称复数为不可能的数，却说它们有用。他认为用处在于告诉我们，哪些问题有答案、哪些没有。例如，若要求把12分成乘积为40的两部分（令人想起卡尔丹），便得6 + −4与6 − −4。他说，由此知道问题无法解决。

Though he calls complex numbers impossible numbers, Euler says they are useful. And his idea of their use is that they tell us which problems do or do not have an answer. Thus, if we are asked to separate 12 into two parts whose product is 40 (shades of Cardan) we would find that the parts are 6 + −4 and 6 - −4. Thereby, he says, we recognize that the problem cannot be solved.

尽管对复数有许多异议，整个十八世纪，人们仍把实数规则用于复数，有效地使用它们，因此数学家获得一些信心。复数用于数学论证中间步骤时，最终结果证明正确，这一事实产生显著作用。然而，对论证有效性、常常甚至对结果的怀疑，仍不断困扰数学家。

Despite the many objections to complex numbers, throughout the eighteenth century complex numbers were used effectively by applying rules that applied to real numbers, and so mathematicians acquired some confidence in them. Where used in intermediate stages of mathematical arguments, the final results proved to be correct and this fact had telling effect. Yet doubts as to the validity of the arguments and often even of the results continued to plague mathematicians.

达朗贝尔在《百科全书》中谈负数时，表达了接受无理数、负数、复数这几类麻烦数的一般态度。该条目全不清楚。他最后说，“负数的代数运算法则，普遍为全世界接受，并被承认为精确，不管我们对这些量有什么观念。”

The general attitude toward acceptance of the several troublesome types of numbers, irrational, negative, and complex, was expressed by d’Alembert apropos of negative numbers in the Encyclopedie. The article is not at all clear. D’Alembert concluded that the “algebraic rules of operation with negative numbers are generally admitted by the whole world and acknowledged as exact, whatever idea we may have about these quantities.”

欧洲人几世纪来努力理解各种数时，另一重大逻辑问题被推到前台：提供代数的逻辑。第一部系统整理重要新结果的著作，是卡尔丹《大术》，说明如何解x3 + 3x2 + 6x = 10等三次方程，以及x4 + 3x3 + 6x2 + 7x + 5 = 0等四次方程。约一百年内，大量其他结果，包括数学归纳法、二项式定理，以及求低次、高次方程根的近似方法，被加入代数体系；主要贡献者为韦达、哈里奥特、吉拉尔、费马、笛卡尔与牛顿。但这些结果没有证明。卡尔丹及后来的邦贝利、韦达确给三次、四次方程解法以几何论证，但忽略负根、复根，当然不能算证明。而且，引入四次、五次等高次方程，意味着限于三维的几何不能成为证明基础。其他作者所给结果，通常只是具体例子启发的断言。

During the centuries that the Europeans struggled to understand the various types of numbers, another major logical problem was thrust to the fore, that of supplying the logic of algebra. The first work that organized significantly new results was Cardan’s The Great Art which showed how to solve cubic equations such as x3 + 3x2 + 6x = 10 and quartic equations such as x4 + 3x3 + 6x2 + 7x + 5 = 0. Within about one hundred years, a large number of other results, mathematical induction, the binomial theorem, and approximate methods of finding roots of low and high degree equations, were added to the body of algebra, the chief contributors being Vieta, Harriot, Girard, Fermat, Descartes, and Newton. But there were no proofs of these results. It is true that Cardan and the later algebraists Bombelli and Vieta gave geometrical arguments to support their methods for solving cubic and quartic equations but, since they ignored negative and complex roots, these arguments were certainly not proofs. Moreover, the introduction of higher degree equations such as the quartic and quintic meant that geometry which was limited to three dimensions could not be the basis of proof. Results given by the other authors were most often merely assertions suggested by concrete examples.

韦达朝正确方向迈了一步。从埃及、巴比伦时代直到韦达，数学家只求解数值系数的一次、二次、三次、四次方程。因此，3x2 + 5x + 6 = 0与4x2 + 7x + 8 = 0等方程，被认为彼此不同，虽然显然同一解法适用于双方。而且，为避免负数，x2 − 7x + 8 = 0等方程长期以x2 + 8 = 7x形式处理。因此，同次数有许多方程类型，各自单独处理。韦达的一项重大贡献，是引入字母系数。

A step in the right direction was made by Vieta. From the time of the Egyptians and the Babylonians right up to Vieta’s work, mathematicians solved linear, quadratic, cubic, and quartic equations with numerical coefficients only. Thus, equations such as 3x2 + 5x + 6 = 0 and 4x2 + 7x + 8 = 0 were regarded as different from each other though it was clear that the same method of solution applied to both. Moreover, to avoid negative numbers, an equation such as x2 - 7x + 8 = 0 was for a long time, treated in the form x2 + 8 = 7x. Hence, there were many types of equations of the same degree and each was treated separately. Vieta’s contribution, a major one, was to introduce literal coefficients.

韦达受过律师训练，通常以数学为爱好，自费印刷、传播著作。虽已有一些人零星、偶然地使用字母，他却首个有目的、系统地如此。主要新用途，不仅表示未知数或其幂，而是表示一般系数。因此，用我们的记法写成ax2 + bx + c = 0，就能一举处理所有二次方程；其中字母系数a、b、c可代表任何数，而x代表须求其值的未知量。

Vieta was trained as a lawyer. Generally, he pursued mathematics as a hobby and printed and circulated his work at his own expense. Though a number of men had used letters for sporadic and incidental purposes, Vieta is the first man to do so purposefully and systematically. The chief new use was not just to represent an unknown or powers of an unknown but as general coefficients. Thus all second-degree equations could be treated in one swoop by writing (in our notation) ax2 + bx + c = 0, wherein a, b, and c, the literal coefficients, could stand for any numbers, whereas x stands for an unknown quantity or quantities whose values are to be found.

韦达称新代数为logistica speciosa（类型计算），区别于logistica numerosa（数值计算）。他充分意识到，研究一般二次方程ax2 + bx + c = 0，就是研究整类表达式。在《分析艺术导论》（In artem analyticam isagoge，1591）中区分这两者时，他划出了算术与代数的界线。他说，代数是对事物的种类或形式进行运算的方法，即logistica speciosa；算术与数值系数方程处理数，即numerosa。因此，凭这一举措，代数成为一般类型的形式与方程的研究，因为一般情形中的处理，涵盖无限多个特殊情形。

Vieta called his new algebra logistica speciosa (calculation with types) as opposed to logistica numerosa (calculation with numbers). He was fully aware of the fact that when he studied the general second-degree equation ax2 + bx + c = 0, he was studying an entire class of expressions.
