Then Leibniz’s dy/dx which for Leibniz was a ratio of infinitesimals in his sense, was for Euler actually 00. However, 00, he maintained, could have many values. Euler’s argument was that n • 0 = 0 for any number n. Hence, if we divide by 0, we have n = 00. The usual process of finding the derivative determines the value of 00 for the particular function involved. He illustrated this for the function y = x2. He gave x the increment h (he used ω). At this stage presumably h is not zero. (Compare this with (1) through (4) above.) Consequently

kh=2x+h.

kh=2x+h.

莱布尼茨让 h 成为无穷小而非零，欧拉则说 h 为零；所以在此例中，kh 这个0/0之比，被发现等于2x。

Where Leibniz allowed h to become infinitesimal but not zero, Euler said h was zero, and so in this case the ratio kh, which is 00, is found to equal 2x.

欧拉强调，这些微分，即 h 和 k 的最终值，是绝对的零；除了它们彼此的比以外，不能从中推断任何东西，而这个比最终被求得为有限量。《微分学原理》第三章中还有更多这种说法。他在那里鼓励读者说，这一概念并不像通常所想的那样隐藏着巨大的奥秘，虽然它使许多人对微积分产生怀疑。当然，欧拉对求导过程的论证并不比牛顿和莱布尼茨的更可靠。

Euler emphasized that these differentials, the ultimate values of b and k, were absolute zeros and that nothing could be inferred from them other than their mutual ratio, which was in the end evaluated as a finite quantity. There is more of this nature in the third chapter of the Institutiones. There he encouraged the reader by remarking that this notion does not hide so great a mystery as is commonly thought although in the mind of many it rendered the calculus suspect. Of course, Euler’s justification of the process of finding the derivative was no sounder than that of Newton and Leibniz.

欧拉用这种形式化而错误的方法处理微积分，确实作出的贡献是：使微积分摆脱几何，以算术和代数为基础。这一步至少为最终在数的基础上论证微积分铺平了道路。

What Euler did contribute in his formalistic, incorrect approach to the calculus was to free it from geometry and base it on arithmetic and algebra. This step at least prepared the way for the ultimate justification of the calculus on the basis of number.

十八世纪随后建立微积分基础的尝试中，最雄心勃勃的是拉格朗日的尝试。像贝克莱及其他人一样，他相信微积分得到正确结果，是因为错误相互抵消。他在《解析函数论》（1797；第二版1813）中进行这种重建。书的副标题很能说明问题：“包含微分学的主要定理，不使用无穷小量、渐逝量、极限和流数，并归结为有限量的代数分析之术”（斜体为引者所加）。

The most ambitious of the subsequent eighteenth-century attempts to build the foundations of the calculus was made by Lagrange. Like Berkeley and others, he believed that the correct results obtained by the calculus were due to the fact that errors were offsetting each other. He worked out his reconstruction in his Tbeorie des fonctions analy-tiques (1797; 2nd edition, 1813). The subtitle of his book is revealing: “Containing the principal theorems of the differential calculus without the use of the infinitely small, of vanishing quantities, of limits and fluxions, and reduced to the art of algebraic analysts of finite quantities” (italics added).

拉格朗日批评牛顿的方法，指出牛顿在考虑弧与弦的极限比时，并非认为弦与弧在消失之前或之后相等，而是在它们消失之际相等。拉格朗日正确地指出：

Lagrange criticized Newton’s approach by pointing out that when Newton considered the limiting ratio of arc to chord, he considered chord and arc equal not before vanishing or after vanishing but when they vanished. Lagrange correctly pointed out:

这种方法有一个重大不便：它在各量可以说不再是量的状态下考虑它们。因为只要两个量仍然是有限的，我们总能很好地理解它们的比；但一旦比的两项同时成为零，这个比就无法给头脑提供清晰而精确的观念。

That method has the great inconvenience of considering quantities in the state in which they cease, so to speak, to be quantities; for though we can always well conceive the ratios of two quantities, as long as they remain finite, that ratio offers to the mind no clear and precise idea, as soon as its terms both become nothing at the same time.

他对莱布尼茨的无穷小量和欧拉的绝对零同样不满意；两者“虽然实际上正确，却不够清楚，不能作为一门科学的基础，因为这门科学的确定性应当建立在自身的明证之上”。

He was equally dissatisfied with the infinitely small quantities of Leibniz and with the absolute zeros of Euler, both of “which although correct in reality are not sufficiently clear to serve as foundation of a science whose certitude should rest on its own evidence.”

拉格朗日希望赋予微积分以古人证明的全部严谨性，打算通过把微积分归结为代数来达到这一点。具体说，他提议用无穷级数来严谨地奠定微积分的逻辑基础；而无穷级数虽然被看作代数的一部分，其逻辑却比微积分更加混乱。他“谦虚”地说，牛顿竟没有想到他［拉格朗日］的方法，实在令人惊讶。

Lagrange wished to give the calculus all the rigor of the demonstrations of the ancients and he proposed to do this by reducing the calculus to algebra. Specifically, Lagrange proposed to use infinite series—which were regarded as part of algebra but whose logic was still more confused than that of the calculus—to found the logic of the calculus rigorously. With “modesty” he remarked that it was surprising that his [Lagrange’s] method had not occurred to Newton.

我们不必追究拉格朗日建立微积分基础的细节。除了完全没有根据地使用级数，他还进行大量代数步骤，这只会使读者更难看出其中缺少导数的恰当定义。事实上，他求出导数的方式，与任何前人的方式一样粗糙。拉格朗日相信，他已摒弃极限概念，把微积分建立在代数之上。尽管错误重重，他的基础理论仍被若干杰出的后继者接受。

We need not pursue the details of Lagrange’s foundation of the calculus. Beyond using series in a manner totally unjustified, he performed a mass of algebraic steps which only made it more difficult for the reader to see that the proper definition of the derivative was lacking. Indeed, what he did was to obtain it in as crude a manner as any of his predecessors had. Lagrange believed that he had dispensed with the limit concept and had founded the calculus on algebra. Despite all his errors, Lagrange’s foundation was accepted by a number of his outstanding successors.

西尔韦斯特-弗朗索瓦·拉克鲁瓦（1765—1843）在1797—1800年出版的一部有影响的三卷本著作中，追随拉格朗日，坚持微积分只是代数扩展的信念。在较简短的一卷本《微积分初等论》（1802）中，拉克鲁瓦使用了极限理论（就当时对这理论的理解程度而言），但他说，这仅仅是为了节省篇幅。

The belief that the calculus was merely an extension of algebra was maintained by Sylvestre-Fran^ois Lacroix (1765-1843) in an influential three-volume work of 1797-1800, wherein Lacroix followed Lagrange. In a briefer one-volume work, An Elementary Treatise on the Differential and Integral Calculus (1802), Lacroix used the theory of limits (insofar as that theory was understood at the time) but, Lacroix said, only to save space.

十九世纪初，一些英国数学家决定引进欧洲大陆更出色的分析研究。查尔斯·巴贝奇（1792—1871）、约翰·赫歇尔（1792—1871）和乔治·皮科克（1791—1858），在剑桥大学读本科时创立了分析学会，并翻译了拉克鲁瓦较简短的微积分著作。但译者在序言中说：

Some British mathematicians of the early nineteenth century decided to take over the superior Continental work on analysis. Charles Babbage (1792-1871), John Herschel (1792-1871), and George Peacock (1791- 1858), who as undergraduates at Cambridge University founded the Analytical Society, translated Lacroix’s briefer calculus. But the translators stated in their Preface:

现在向公众提供译本的拉克鲁瓦这部著作……可以看作他那部微积分巨著的节本，虽然在最初原理的证明中，他以达朗贝尔的极限方法，代替了前一部著作所采用的拉格朗日那种最正确、最自然的方法……。

The work of Lacroix, of which a translation is now presented to the Public . . . may be considered as an abridgement of his great work in the Differential and Integral Calculus, although in the demonstration of the first principles, he has substituted the method of limits of d’Alembert, in the place of the most correct and natural method of Lagrange, which was adopted in the former. . . .

皮科克说，极限理论不可接受，因为它把微分学的原理与代数分开了。赫歇尔和巴贝奇也赞同。

Peacock said the theory of limits was not acceptable because it separated the principles of the differential calculus from algebra. Herschel and Babbage agreed.

十八世纪末的数学界已清楚认识到，迫切需要为微积分建立适当基础。在拉格朗日的建议下，柏林科学院数学部于1784年提出，在1786年向数学中无穷问题的最佳解答颁奖。拉格朗日于1766至1787年担任该部主任。竞赛公告如下：

It was clear to the mathematical world of the late eighteenth century that proper foundations for the calculus were urgently needed, and at the suggestion of Lagrange the Mathematics section of the Berlin Academy of Sciences, of which he was director from 1766 to 1787, proposed in 1784 that a prize be awarded in 1786 for the best solution to the problem of the infinite in mathematics. The announcement of the competition read as follows:

数学所产生的效用、人们对它的敬重，以及它正当地享有的最卓越的“精确科学”荣誉称号，都归功于它的原理之清晰、证明之严谨和定理之精确。

The utility derived from mathematics, the esteem it is held in, and the honorable name of “exact science” par excellence justly given it, are all the due of the clarity of its principles, the rigor of its proofs, and the precision of its theorems.

为了确保知识中这一优美部分永远保持这些宝贵优点，需要对数学中所谓的无穷建立清晰而精确的理论。

In order to ensure the perpetuation of these valuable advantages in this elegant part of knowledge, there is needed a clear and precise theory of what is called Infinite in Mathematics.

众所周知，高等几何［数学］经常使用无穷大和无穷小。然而，古代几何学家，甚至古代分析学家，都尽力避免任何接近无穷的东西，而某些杰出的现代分析学家也承认，“无穷大的量”这个说法本身就是矛盾。

It is widely known that advanced Geometry [mathematics] regularly employs the infinitely great and the infinitely small. The geometers of antiquity, however, and even the ancient analysts, took pains to avoid anything approaching the infinite, whereas certain eminent modern analysts admit that the phrase infinite magnitude is a contradiction in terms.

因此，科学院希望得到一种解释：为什么从一个矛盾的假定出发，竟能推导出如此多的正确定理；同时，希望提出一个可靠、清晰、总之真正属于数学的原理，可以恰当地代替无穷原理，而又不使借助它进行的研究过于困难或过于冗长。要求以尽可能的普遍性，以及尽可能的严谨、清楚和简明，来处理这一题目。

The Academy, therefore, desires an explanation of how it is that so many correct theorems have been deduced from a contradictory supposition, together with enunciation of a sure, a clear, in short a truly mathematical principle that may properly be substituted for that of the infinite without, however, rendering investigations carried out by its means overly difficult or overly lengthy. It is required that the subject be treated in all possible generality and with all possible rigor, clarity, and simplicity.

除科学院正式院士以外，竞赛向所有人开放。共收到二十三篇论文。竞赛结果的官方评语如下：

The competition was open to all comers with the exception of regular members of the Academy. Twenty-three papers in all were submitted. The official finding on the outcome of the contest reads as follows:

科学院收到了许多关于这一题目的论文。所有作者都忽略了解释：如此多的正确定理，如何能从无穷量之类矛盾的假定中推导出来。他们都或多或少地忽视了所要求的清楚、简明，尤其是严谨。多数人甚至没有看出，所寻求的原理不应限于无穷小分析，还应扩展到代数，以及按古人方式处理的几何。

The Academy has received many essays on this subject. Their authors have all overlooked explaining how so many correct theorems have been deduced from a contradictory supposition, such as that of an infinite quantity. They have all, more or less, disregarded the qualities of clarity, simplicity, and above all rigor that were required. Most of them have not even perceived that the principle sought should not be restricted to the infinitesimal calculus, but should be extended to algebra and to geometry treated in the manner of the ancients.

因此，科学院认为，所提出的问题没有得到完整回答。

The feeling of the Academy, therefore, is that its query has not met with a full response.

不过，科学院发现，最接近其意图的参赛者，是一篇法文论文的作者，其题辞为：“无穷是吞没我们思想的深渊。”因此，科学院投票决定将奖授予他。

However, it has found that the entrant who comes closest to its intentions is the author of the French essay that has for its motto: “The Infinite is the abyss in which our thoughts are engulfed.” The Academy has, therefore, voted him the prize.

获奖者是瑞士数学家西蒙·吕利耶。科学院于同年，即1786年，出版了他的《高等微积分初等论述》。无疑，科学院数学部的判断基本正确。其余论文中，除卡诺的一篇（第七章）外，没有一篇哪怕试图解释：无穷小分析如何从错误的假定出发，确立正确的定理。吕利耶的论文在质量上无疑很突出，虽然其基本思想丝毫不是原创。据吕利耶说，他的论文是“发展了……达朗贝尔先生在《百科全书》的‘微分’条目和他的《杂集》中仅作勾勒、可以说只是提出的那些思想”。在《论述》的第一章中，吕利耶对极限理论本身作了些改进。他首次在印刷文本中引入了 lim 形式的极限符号。因此，他把导数 dP/dx 记为 lim ΔP/Δx（我们的 kh）；但是，吕利耶对极限理论的贡献微乎其微。

The winner was the Swiss mathematician, Simon L’Huillier. The Academy published his “Elementary Exposition of the Higher Calculus” in that same year, 1786. There is no doubt that the judgment made by the Mathematics section of the Academy was essentially right. None of the other papers (except one by Carnot (Chapter VII)) made even so much as an attempt to explain how it was that infinitesimal analysis established theorems that are correct after starting from suppositions that are false. L Huillier s undoubtedly stood out in its quality, although its fundamental idea was not in the slightest degree original. According to L’Huillier, his essay represented “the development of ideas . . . that M. d’Alembert had only sketched and, as it were, proposed in the article ‘Differentiel’ in the Encyclopedic and in his Melanges.” In the opening chapter of the Exposition, L’Huillier improved somewhat the theory of limits itself. He introduced for the first time in a printed text the symbol for a limit in the form lim. Thus he denoted the derivative dP/dx as lim AP/Ax (our kh), but L’Huillier’s contribution to the theory of limits was minuscule.

尽管十八世纪几乎每位数学家都对微积分的逻辑作过某种努力，或至少发表过看法，也有一两位走上了正确道路，但所有努力都没有成效。任何精微的问题，不是被忽视，就是被遗漏。极大的数与无穷大之间几乎没有区分。对于任何有限 n 都成立的定理，对于无穷大的 n 必然也成立，这似乎很清楚。同样，差商 kh（见式(3)）被导数取代，而像式(7)那样有限多项的和与积分，也几乎不作区分。他们自由地从一个过渡到另一个。伏尔泰把微积分描述为“对一个无法设想其存在的东西，进行精确计数和测量的技艺”，这句话可以概括他们的工作。这个世纪使微积分严谨化的努力，尤其是欧拉和拉格朗日这样的巨人的努力，其总体效果却是使同时代人和后继者困惑并受误导。总的说来，他们错得如此明显，以致人们可能对数学家终有一天能澄清其中逻辑感到绝望。

Though almost every mathematician of the eighteenth century made some effort or at least a pronouncement on the logic of the calculus and though one or two were on the right track, all of their efforts were unavailing. Any delicate questions were either ignored or overlooked. The distinction between a very large number and an infinite number was hardly made. It seemed clear that a theorem which held for any finite n must hold for n infinite. Likewise the difference quotient kh (see (3)) was replaced by a derivative, and the sum of a finite number of terms, such as occur in (7), and an integral were hardly distinguished. They passed from one to the other freely. Their work could be summed up in Voltaire’s description of the calculus as “the art of numbering and measuring exactly a Thing whose Existence cannot be conceived.” The net effect of the century s efforts to rigorize the calculus, particularly those of giants such as Euler and Lagrange, was to confound and mislead their contemporaries and successors. They were, on the whole, so blatantly wrong that one could despair of mathematicians’ ever clarifying the logic involved.

数学家对符号的信赖远胜于对逻辑的信赖。由于无穷级数对所有 x 值都具有同样的符号形式，使级数收敛的 x 值与使它发散的 x 值之间的区别，似乎不值得注意。即使人们认识到1 + 2 + 3……之类的级数有无穷大的和，数学家也宁愿尝试给这个和赋予意义，而不愿质疑求和是否适用。当然，他们完全明白需要某些证明。我们已经看到，欧拉确实试图为使用发散级数提供依据，而他和拉格朗日等人也确实试图建立微积分的基础。不过，这些少数追求严谨的努力——其意义在于表明严谨的标准随时代而变化——未能证明这个世纪的工作的有效性；人们几乎是执意采取这样一种立场：无法医治的，只好忍受。

Mathematicians trusted the symbols far more than logic. Because infinite series had the same symbolic form for all values of x, the distinction between values of x for which series converged and values for which they diverged did not seem to demand attention. And even though it was recognized that some series, such as 1 + 2 + 3 ••• , had an infinite sum, mathematicians preferred to try to give meaning to the sum, rather than to question the applicability of a summation. Of course, they were fully aware of the need for some proofs. V7e have seen that Euler did try to justify his use of divergent series, and both he and Lagrange, among others, did attempt a foundation for the calculus. But the few efforts to achieve rigor—significant because they show that standards of rigor vary with the times—did not succeed in validating the work of the century and men almost willfully took the position that what cannot be cured must be endured.

十八世纪思想家的论证有一个奇特之处，就是诉诸“形而上学”这个词。使用它，是为了暗示在数学本身的领域之外存在一批真理，必要时可以调用它们，为自己的工作提供依据，虽然这些真理究竟是什么并不清楚。诉诸形而上学，旨在使理性无法支持的论证获得可信性。因此，莱布尼茨断言，形而上学在数学中的用途比我们认识到的更多。他把1/2作为级数1 − 1 + 1 − ……的和的论证，以及他的连续性原理，除了莱布尼茨自己的断言之外，都没有更多可取之处，却都被冠以形而上学的依据，仿佛这种“依据”能使它们不容争议。欧拉也诉诸形而上学，认为我们在分析中必须顺从它。十七、十八世纪的数学家，当无法为一个论断提供更好的论证时，便习惯说，其理由是形而上学的。

One curious feature of the arguments used by eighteenth-century thinkers was their recourse to the term metaphysics. It was used to imply that there was a body of truths lying outside the domain of mathematics proper which could, if necessary, be called upon to justify their work, though just what these truths were was not clear. The appeal to metaphysics was meant to give credence to arguments that reason failed to support. Thus, Leibniz asserted that metaphysics is of more use in mathematics than we realize. His argument for taking 12 to be the sum of the series 1 − 1 + 1 − ⋯ and his principle of continuity, neither of which had more to recommend it than Leibniz’s own assertion, were justified as metaphysical as though this “justification” placed them beyond dispute. Euler, too, appealed to metaphysics and argued that we must acquiesce to it in analysis. When they could provide no better argument for an assertion, seventeenth- and eighteenth-century mathematicians were wont to say the reason was metaphysical.

就这样，十八世纪结束时，微积分以及建立在微积分之上的分析各分支，其逻辑完全陷于混乱。事实上，可以说基础的状况在1800年比1700年更糟。巨人们，尤其是欧拉和拉格朗日，提出了错误的逻辑基础。由于他们是权威，许多同行不加批判地接受并重复他们的主张，甚至在他们的基础之上建立更多分析。另一些较次要的数学家，对大师们提出的东西并不十分满意，却确信只须澄清或作些小修改，就能得到完全清晰的基础。当然，他们被引上了错误的道路。

And so the eighteenth century ended with the logic of the calculus and of the branches of analysis built on the'calculus in a totally confused state. In fact, one could say that the state of the foundations was worse in 1800 than in 1700. Giants, notably Euler and Lagrange, had given incorrect logical foundations. Because these men were authorities, many of their colleagues accepted and repeated uncritically what they proposed and even built more analysis on their foundations. Other lesser lights were not quite satisfied with what the masters had advanced, but they were confident that a totally clear foundation could be secured merely by clarification or minor emendation. Of course they were being led down false trails.

七、非逻辑的发展：约1800年的困境

VII. The Illogical Development: The Predicament circa 1800

啊，诸神啊，为什么二加二应当等于四？

Ah, Why, ye Gods, should two and two make four?

亚历山大·蒲柏

Alexander Pope

到1800年，数学处于一种极其矛盾的境地。它在表述和预测物理现象方面的成功，卓越得超乎一切预期。另一方面，正如许多十八世纪学者已经指出的，这个庞大结构没有逻辑基础，因此不能保证数学是正确的。这种矛盾状态在十九世纪上半叶继续存在。许多数学家奋力推进到物理科学的新领域，取得更加巨大的成功，却没有着手解决逻辑基础问题。相反，对负数和复数、代数，以及微积分及其扩展——所谓的分析——的批评仍在继续。

By 1800, MATHEMATICS WAS IN A HIGHLY PARADOXICAL SITUATION. Its successes in representing and predicting physical phenomena were beyond all expectation superlative. On the other hand, as many eighteenth-century men had already pointed out, the massive structure had no logi cal foundation, and there was therefore no assurance that the mathematics was correct. This paradoxical state continued in the first half of the nineteenth century. While many mathematicians plowed ahead into new areas of physical science and achieved still greater successes, the logical foundation was not tackled. Rather, criticisms of negative and complex numbers, algebra, and the calculus and its extensions to what is called analysis continued.

我们来考察十九世纪初的困境。对于当时仍存在的少数反对使用无理数的意见，可以很快略过。如前所述，无理数可以看作直线上的点；在直观上，它们并不比整数和分数难接受多少，而且服从与整数、分数相同的法则。至于它们的用途，毫无疑问。因此，尽管无理数没有逻辑根据，仍被接受了。令人苦恼且在直观上难以接受的元素，是负数和复数。十九世纪，人们对它们的攻击和拒绝，仍像以前几个世纪一样猛烈。

Let us examine the predicament in the early nineteenth century. We can pass quickly over the few objections that were still made to the use of irrational numbers. These, as mentioned earlier, could be thought of as points on a line; intuitively they were not much more difficult to accept than whole numbers and fractions, and they obeyed the same laws as whole numbers and fractions. As to their utility, there could be no question. Hence, though there was no logical basis for irrational numbers, they were accepted. The troublesome and intuitively unacceptable elements were the negative numbers and the complex numbers. They were attacked and rejected in the nineteenth century with the same virulence as in previous centuries.

奥古斯都·德·摩根的岳父、剑桥大学耶稣学院研究员威廉·弗伦德（1757—1841），在《代数原理》（1796）的序言中直截了当地宣称：

William Frend (1757-1841), father-in-law of Augustus De Morgan and a fellow of Jesus College, Cambridge, declared outright in the Preface to his Principles of Algebra (1796):

［一个数］可以从一个比它大的数中减去，但企图从一个比它小的数中减去它，是荒谬的。然而，代数学家却这样做；他们谈论小于零的数，谈论负数乘负数从而产生正数，谈论一个数是虚的。于是他们说，每个二次方程都有两个根，让学习者去试哪一个适用于给定方程；他们谈论解一个方程，而这个方程必须有两个不可能的根才可解；他们能找出某些不可能的数，相乘却产生1。这全是使常识退缩的行话；但是，一旦被采用，它就像许多其他虚构物一样，在那些喜欢轻信而讨厌认真思考的任何迹象的人中，找到最卖力的支持者。

[A number] submits to be taken away from a number greater than itself but to attempt to take it away from a number less than itself is ridiculous. Yet this is attempted by algebraists who talk of a number less than nothing; of multiplying a negative number into a negative number and thus producing a positive number; of a number being imaginary. Hence they talk of two roots to every equation of the second order [degree], and the learner is to try which will succeed in a given equation; they talk of solving an equation, which requires two impossible roots to make it soluble; they can find out some impossible numbers, which, being multiplied together, produce unity. This is all jargon, at which common sense recoils; but, from its having been once adopted, like many other figments, it finds the most strenuous supporters among those who love to take things upon trust and hate the color of a serious thought.

在马塞雷斯男爵（第五章）1800年出版的一部书所收的一篇文章中，弗伦德批评了方程根的个数等于其次数这条一般规则。他说，它只对少数方程成立，当然，他所举的都是必然只有正根的方程。接着，他谈到接受一般规则的数学家：“为了掩饰他们一般命题的错误，并至少在言辞上给它一个真理的外观，他们发现自己不得不给一批量冠以似是而非的名称，竭力让这些量冒充这些方程的根，尽管它们实际上不是……”

In an essay included in a book by Baron Maseres (Chapter V) published in 1800, Frend criticized the general rule that an equation has as many roots as its degree. He said this is true of only a few equations, and of course he cited those which necessarily have all positive roots. He then said of the mathematicians who accept the general rule, “they find themselves under a necessity of giving specious names to a parcel of quantities which they endeavor to make pass for roots of these equations, though in truth they are not so, in order to cover the falsehood of their general proposition, and give it, in words at least, an appearance of truth . . .”

著名的法国几何学家拉扎尔·N. M. 卡诺（1753—1823），除了自身的原创贡献外，还凭《论无穷小分析的形而上学》（1797；修订第二版1813）产生了广泛影响，该书被译成多种语言。他直言，某物小于零这一概念是荒谬的。负数可以作为有助于计算的虚构实体引入代数。然而，它们肯定不是量，而且可能导致错误结论。

Lazare N. M. Carnot (1753-1823), a well-known French geometer, was influential beyond his own original contributions by virtue of his Reflections on the Metaphysics of Infinitesimal Calculus (1797; 2nd edition revised, 1813), which was translated into many languages. He asserted flatly that the notion of something less than nothing was absurd. Negative numbers could be introduced into algebra as fictitious entities useful for calculation. However, they were certainly not quantities and could lead to erroneous conclusions.

十八世纪关于负数和复数的对数的争论，使数学家如此困惑，以致他们到了十九世纪仍不得不质疑负数和复数。1801年，剑桥大学的罗伯特·伍德豪斯发表了《论借助虚量所得某些结论的必然真理性》。他说：“在关于对数应用于负量和不可能量的争论中，参与的数学家相互指摘的悖论与矛盾，可以用作反对在研究中使用这些量的论据。”

The eighteenth-century controversies on the logarithms of negative and complex numbers had bewildered mathematicians so much that even in the nineteenth century they were impelled to question both negative and complex numbers. In 1801, Robert Woodhouse of Cambridge University published a paper “On the Necessary Truth of Certain Conclusions Obtained by Means of Imaginary Quantities.” He said, “The paradoxes and contradictions mutually alleged against each other, by mathematicians engaged in the controversy concerning the application of logarithms to negative and impossible quantities, may be employed as arguments against the use of those quantities in investigation.”

柯西无疑是最伟大的数学家之一，也是十九世纪最初几十年中建立复变函数论的人，却拒绝把 a + b−1 之类的表达式当作数。在著名的《分析教程》（Cours d’analyse，1821）中，他说，这类表达式作为整体没有意义。不过，它们确实表达了关于实数 a 和 b 的某些内容。例如，方程

Cauchy, certainly one of the greatest mathematicians and the man who founded the theory of functions of a complex variable during the first few decades of the nineteenth century, refused to treat expressions such as a + b −1 as numbers. In his famous Corns d’analyse (Course on Analysis, 1821), he said such expressions regarded as a totality have no meaning. However, they do say something about the real numbers a and b. For example, the equation

a+b−1=c+d−1

a+b−1=c+d−1

告诉我们 a = c 且 b = d。“每个虚方程，都只是两个实量方程的符号表示。”迟至1847年，他还提出一个相当繁复的理论，以证明复数运算的合理性，却避免使用 −1。他说，这个量“我们可以完全摒弃，可以毫无遗憾地放弃，因为人们不知道这个假想的符号表示什么，也不知道应赋予它何种意义”。

tells us that a = c and b = d. “Every imaginary equation is only the symbolic representation of two equations between real quantities.” As late as 1847 he gave a rather involved theory which would justify operations with complex numbers but avoid the use of −1, a quantity which, he said, “we can repudiate completely and which we can abandon without regret because one does not know what this pretended sign signifies nor what sense one ought to attribute to it.”

1831年，著名数理逻辑学家、对代数作有贡献的奥古斯都·德·摩根（1806—1871），在《论数学的学习及其困难》中表达了对负数和复数的异议。顺便说来，他声称书中没有任何内容，是当时牛津和剑桥所使用的最佳著作中找不到的。

In 1831, Augustus De Morgan (1806-1871), a famous mathematical logician and a contributor to algebra, expressed his objections to both negative and complex numbers in his book On the Study and Difficulties of Mathematics. He said, incidentally, that his book contained nothing that could not be found in the best works then in use at Oxford and Cambridge.

虚表达式 −a 和负表达式 −b 有这样一个相似之处：任何一个作为问题的解出现，都表明某种不一致或荒谬。就实际意义而言，两者同样是虚的，因为0 − a与 −a 一样不可理解。

The imaginary expression −a and the negative expression -b have this resemblance, that either of them occurring as the solution of a problem indicates some inconsistency or absurdity. As far as real meaning is concerned, both are equally imaginary, since 0 - a is as inconceivable as −a.

然后，德·摩根用一个问题来说明。父亲56岁，儿子29岁。什么时候父亲的年龄是儿子的两倍？他解56 + x = 2(29 + x)，得到 x = −2。他说，这个结果荒谬。但是，他继续说，如果把 x 改为 −x，解56 − x = 2(29 − x)，就得到 x = 2。他得出结论：我们把原来的问题表述错了。负答案表明，我们第一次列方程时犯了错误。

Then De Morgan illustrates by means of a problem. A father is 56; his son is 29. When will the father be twice as old as the son? He solves 56 + x = 2(29 + x) and obtains x = -2. This result, he says, is absurd. But, he continues, if we change x to —x and solve 56 − x = 2(29 − x), we get x = 2. He concludes that we phrased the original problem wrongly. The negative answer shows that we made a mistake in the first formulation of the equation.

随后转而谈到复数，他说：

Then turning to complex numbers, he stated:

我们已经表明，符号 −a 毫无意义，或者说，它是自相矛盾而荒谬的。然而，借助这类符号，却建立了代数中一个很有用的部分。它依赖一个必须由经验验证的事实：普通的代数法则可以应用于这些表达式［复数］，而不导致任何错误结果。诉诸这种性质的经验，似乎违反了本书开头确立的最初原理。我们不能否认，实际上的确如此；但必须记住，这只是一个庞大学科中孤立而小小的一部分，对于该学科的所有其他分支，这些原理都完全适用。［他所说的原理是：数学真理必然通过演绎推理从公理得出。］

We have shown the symbol −a to be void of meaning, or rather self-contradictory and absurd. Nevertheless, by means of such symbols, a part of algebra is established which is of great utility. It depends upon the fact, which must be verified by experience that the common rules of algebra may be applied to these expressions [complex numbers] without leading to any false results. An appeal to experience of this nature appears to be contrary to the first principles laid down at the beginning of this work. We cannot deny that it is so in reality, but it must be recollected that this is but a small and isolated part of an immense subject, to all other branches of which these principles apply in their fullest extent. [The principles he referred to are that mathematical truths follow necessarily by deductive reasoning from axioms.]

然后，他比较负根和复根：

He then compared negative roots and complex roots:

因此，负结果与虚结果之间有这样一个明显区别：当问题的答案为负时，改变产生该结果的方程中 x 的符号，我们或者能发现列方程方法中的错误，或者能说明问题的提法过于狭窄，可以扩展，使之容许一个满意的答案。当问题的答案为虚时，情况就不是这样。

There is, then, this distinct difference between the negative and the imaginary result. When the answer to a problem is negative, by changing the sign of x in the equation which produced that result, we may either discover an error in the method of forming that equation or show that the question of the problem is too limited and may be extended so as to admit of a satisfactory answer. When the answer to a problem is imaginary this is not the case.

在书中稍后的地方，他说：

Somewhat later in the book he said:

我们不主张全面讨论负量的使用等问题中一切赞成和反对的论证，以此阻碍学生的进步，因为他无法理解这些论证，而且双方的论证都不能定论。不过，可以让他知道，确实存在困难，并向他指出困难的性质；然后，他通过考虑足够多、分别处理的例子，便可以对这些规则所导出的结果建立信心。

We are not advocates for stopping the progress of the student by entering fully into all the arguments for and against such questions, as the use of negative quantities, etc., which he could not understand, and which are inconclusive on both sides; but he might be made aware that a difficulty does exist, the nature of which might be pointed out to him, and he might then, by the consideration of a sufficient number of examples, treated separately, acquire confidence in the results to which the rules lead.

伟大的数学家之一威廉·R. 哈密顿，对接受负数和复数也没有更积极的态度。我们以前已有机会谈到他在其他领域的工作。他在1837年的一篇论文中表达了异议：

One of the great mathematicians, whose work in other areas we have had occasion to treat, William R. Hamilton, was no more inclined to accept negative and complex numbers. In a paper of 1837 he expressed his objections:

当负数和虚数的学说像通常那样以这类原理表述时，怀疑它，甚至不相信它，并不需要特别的怀疑主义：较大的量可以从较小的量中减去，余数小于零；两个负数，即各自表示小于零的量的数，可以相乘，而积是正数，即表示大于零的量的数；因此，虽然一个数的平方，即它与自身相乘的积，无论这个数为正或负，总是正的，却又可以发现、设想或确定一些称为虚数的数，并按正数和负数的一切法则对它们进行运算，好像它们服从这些法则一样，尽管它们的平方是负的，因而必须假定它们本身既不是正数，也不是负数，也不是零数，于是，它们据说表示的量，既不能大于零，也不能小于零，甚至不能等于零。在这种根据之上建立一门科学，一定很困难；尽管逻辑的形式可以从中构建一个对称的表达式体系，也可以学到一种实用技艺，正确应用那些似乎依赖于这些根据的有用规则。*

But it requires no peculiar scepticism to doubt, or even to disbelieve, the doctrine of Negatives and Imaginaries, when set forth (as it has commonly been) with principles like these: that a greater magnitude may be subtracted from a less, and that the remainder is less than nothing-, that two negative numbers, or numbers denoting magnitudes each less than nothing, may be multiplied the one by the other, and that the product will be a positive number, or a number denoting a magnitude greater than nothing; and that although the square of a number, or the product obtained by multiplying that number by itself, is therefore always positive, whether the number be positive or negative, yet that numbers, called imaginary, can be found or conceived or determined, and operated on by all the rules of positive and negative numbers, as if they were subject to those rules, although they have negative squares, and must therefore be supposed to be themselves neither positive nor negative, nor yet null numbers, so that the magnitudes which they are supposed to denote can neither be greater than nothing, nor less than nothing, nor even equal to nothing. It must be hard to found a science on such grounds as these, though the forms of logic may build up from them a symmetrical system of expressions, and a practical art may be learned of rightly applying useful rules which seem to depend upon them.*

作为逻辑学家与德·摩根共享荣誉的乔治·布尔（1815—1864），在《思维规律的研究》（1854）中说，−1 是一个无法解释的符号。然而，在三角学中使用它，我们便从可解释的表达式，经过不可解释的表达式，进入可解释的表达式。

George Boole (1815-1864), who shares honors with De Morgan as a logician, in An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854), said of −1 that it is an uninterpretable symbol. However, by using it in trigonometry, we pass from interpretable expressions through uninterpretable ones into interpretable ones.

使数学家在一定程度上接受复数的，不是逻辑，而是韦塞尔、阿尔冈和高斯的几何表示（第四章）。然而，在高斯的工作中，我们仍能发现他不愿接受复数的证据。高斯对代数基本定理给出了四个证明；该定理说，每个 n 次多项式方程恰有 n 个根。在前三个证明（1799、1815和1816）中，他处理的是系数为实数的多项式，而且预先假定笛卡尔平面的点与复数一一对应，虽然他没有明确地定义这种对应。实际作图时，并非绘出 x + iy，而是把 x 和 y 作为实平面上一个点的坐标。此外，这些证明没有真正使用复函数论，因为他把所涉函数的实部和虚部分开了。在1811年给贝塞尔的信中，他更明确地写道，a + ib 由点(a, b)表示，而且可以沿许多路径从复平面的一点到另一点。根据这三个证明及其他未发表工作所体现的思考判断，无疑高斯仍然关心复数和复函数的地位。在1825年12月11日的一封信中，他说自己无法摆脱“负量和虚量的真正形而上学。−1 的真正意义，总是迫切地浮现在我的脑海中，但很难用言辞把握它”。

What reconciled mathematicians somewhat to complex numbers was not logic but the geometrical representation of Wessel, Argand, and Gauss (Chapter IV). Nevertheless, in Gauss’s work we can still find evidence of his reluctance to accept complex numbers. Gauss gave four proofs of the fundamental theorem of algebra, which states that every polynomial equation of the nth. degree has exactly n roots. In the first three proofs (1799, 1815, and 1816), he dealt with polynomials whose coefficients are real numbers, and, in addition, he presupposed a one-to-one correspondence of points of the Cartesian plane and complex numbers, though he did not define the correspondence explicitly. There was no actual plotting of x + iy but rather of x and y as coordinates of a point in the real plane. Moreover, the proofs did not really use complex function theory because he separated the real and imaginary parts of the functions involved. He was more explicit in a letter to Bessel of 1811, wherein he wrote that a + ib was represented by the point (a,b) and that one could go from one point to another of the complex plane by many paths. There is no doubt, if one judges from the thinking exhibited in these three proofs and in other unpublished works, that Gauss was still concerned about the status of complex numbers and functions. In a letter of December 11, 1825, he said he could not tear himself away from “the true metaphysics of negative and imaginary quantities. The true sense of Vm is always pressingly present in my mind but it would be difficult to grasp it in words.”

不过，到1831年，高斯对于自己或其他数学家接受复数，即使仍有任何顾虑，也已经克服了这些顾虑，并公开描述了复数的几何表示。在那一年的论文中，高斯非常明确。他不仅把 a + bi 表示为复平面上的点，还描述了复数的几何加法和乘法（第四章）。随后他指出，分数、负数和实数已被充分理解，而复数尽管价值巨大，却一直只是被容忍。对许多人来说，它们似乎不过是符号游戏。但是，“在这里［这种几何表示中］，−1 的直观意义得到了完全有根据的展示，要把这些量纳入算术对象的领域，不需要更多东西。”因此，高斯自己也满足于直观理解。他还说，如果单位1、−1和 −1 当初不是被称为正、负、虚单位，而是被称为正向、反向和侧向单位，人们就不会觉得这些数中有某种阴暗的奥秘。他说，几何表示使虚数的真正形而上学获得了新的阐明。他引入了“复数”这个词，以区别于笛卡尔的“虚数”，并用 i 表示 −1。高斯没有评论另一个同样重要的事实：他和同时代人自由使用实数，尽管实数没有逻辑基础。

However, by 1831, if Gauss still possessed any scruples about his own or other mathematicians’ acceptance of complex numbers, he had overcome them, and he publicly described the geometric representation of complex numbers. In papers of that year Gauss was very explicit. He not only gave the representation of a + bi as a point in the complex plane but described the geometrical addition and multiplication of complex numbers (Chapter IV). He then pointed out that the fractions, negative numbers, and real numbers were then well understood, whereas complex numbers had just been tolerated despite their great value. To many they appeared to be just a play with symbols. But “Here [in this geometrical representation] the demonstration of an intuitive meaning of Vh is completely grounded and more is not needed in order to admit these quantities into the domain of the objects of arithmetic.” Thus, Gauss himself was content with an intuitive understanding. He also said that if the units 1, -1, and −1 had not been given the names positive, negative, and imaginary units but direct, inverse, and lateral, people would not have gotten the impression that there is some dark mystery in these numbers. The geometrical representation, he said, puts the true metaphysics of imaginary numbers in a new light. He introduced the term “complex numbers”—as opposed to Descartes’s term imaginary numbers”—and used i for −1. Gauss did not comment on what was equally significant, namely, that he and his contemporaries used real numbers freely despite the fact that these had no logical foundation.

*我们将在下一章看到哈密顿如何解决复数带来的问题。

We shall see in the next chapter Hamilton’s resolution of the problem presented by complex numbers.

在1849年的一篇论文中——我们稍后还会多说一点——高斯更加自由地使用复数，因为他说，现在人人都熟悉它们。但事实并非如此。主要由柯西在十九世纪前三分之一时期建立的复变复值函数理论，被用于流体动力学很久以后，剑桥大学的教授们对令人反感的 −1，仍保持着不可克服的厌恶，并采用笨重的办法，尽可能避免它的出现或使用。

In a paper of 1849, about which we shall say a little more later, Gauss used complex numbers much more freely because, he said, by now everyone is familiar with them. But this was not so. Long after the theory of complex functions of a complex variable was developed principally by Cauchy in the first third of the nineteenth century and employed in hydrodynamics, Cambridge University professors preserved an invincible repulsion to the objectionable −1, and cumbrous devices were adopted to avoid its occurrence or use wherever possible.

十九世纪上半叶，代数的逻辑基础也显著缺失。这一领域的问题是：人们用字母代表各种数，并把字母当作具有正整数的一切熟悉而直观可接受的性质来运算。当用任何数——负数、无理数或复数——代入字母时，这些运算结果都是正确的。但是，由于这些数并没有被真正理解，其性质也未在逻辑上确立，这种字母的使用当然没有根据。似乎字母表达式的代数有自己的一套逻辑，能够解释其效力和正确性。因此，在十九世纪三十年代，数学家开始处理如何为字母或符号表达式的运算提供依据的问题。

In the first half of the nineteenth century, the logical foundation of algebra was also noticeable by its absence. The problem in this area was that letters were used to represent all types of numbers and were manipulated as though they possessed all the familiar and intuitively acceptable properties of the positive integers. The results of these manipulations were correct when any numbers—negative, irrational, or complex were substituted for the letters. But because these types of numbers were not really understood nor were their properties logically established, this use of letters was certainly unjustified. It seemed as though the algebra of literal expressions possessed a logic of its own, which accounted for its effectiveness and correctness. Hence in the 1830s, mathematicians tackled the problem of justifying operations with literal or symbolic expressions.

剑桥大学数学教授乔治·皮科克（1791—1858）首先考虑了这一问题。他区分了算术代数和符号代数。前者处理代表正整数的符号，因此有牢固根据。在这里，只允许结果为正整数的运算。皮科克认为，符号代数采用算术代数的规则，却取消仅限于正整数的限制。算术代数中推导出的一切结果，其表达式形式一般而数值特殊；在符号代数中，表达式的数值和形式都一般化了，而这些结果仍然正确。因此，当 a、m 和 n 为正整数时，ma + na = (m + n)a 在算术代数中成立，于是它在符号代数中对于所有 a、m 和 n 都成立。同样，当 n 为正整数时，(a + b)ⁿ 的二项式展开，如果以不指明末项的一般形式表示，就对所有 n 成立。皮科克的论证称为等价形式的永久性原理，发表于1833年向英国科学促进会提交的《关于分析某些分支近期进展和现状的报告》中。他武断地断言：

This problem was first considered by George Peacock (1791-1858), professor of mathematics at Cambridge University. He made the distinction between arithmetical algebra and symbolic algebra. The former dealt with symbols representing the positive integers and so was on solid ground. Here, only operations leading to positive integers were permissible. Symbolic algebra, Peacock argued, adopts the rules of arithmetical algebra but removes the limitation to positive integers. All the results deduced in arithmetical algebra, whose expressions are general in form but particular in value, are correct results likewise in symbolic algebra where they are general in value as well as in form. Thus ma + na = (m + n)a holds in arithmetical algebra when a, m, and n are positive integers, and it therefore holds in symbolic algebra for all a, m, and n. Likewise the binomial expansion of (a + b)ⁿ when n is a positive integer, if it is exhibited in a general form without reference to a final term, holds for all n. Peacock s argument, known as the principle of the permanence of equivalent forms, was set forth in 1833 in his “Report on the Recent Progress and Present State of Certain Branches of Analysis to the British Association for the Advancement of Science. He dogmatically affirmed:

凡是在符号形式一般而数值特定［正整数］时等价的代数形式，在符号的数值与形式都一般化时，也同样等价。

Whatever algebraical forms are equivalent when the symbols are general in form but specific in value [positive integers], will be equivalent likewise when the symbols are general in value as well as in form.

皮科克特别用这一原理为复数运算提供依据。他确实试图用“当符号在形式上是一般的”这句话来限制其含义。因此，不能陈述仅属于0和1的性质，因为这些数有特殊性质。

Peacock used this principle to justify in particular operations with complex numbers. He did try to protect his meaning by the phrase “when the symbols are general in form.” Thus, one could not state properties which belong only to 0 and 1, because these numbers have special properties.

在《代数论》第二版（1842—45；第一版1830）中，皮科克从公理推导了自己的原理。他明确指出，代数像几何一样，是演绎科学。因此，代数的过程，必须建立在对支配其中运算的全部法则或公理的完整陈述之上。运算符号，至少对于代数这一演绎科学来说，除了法则所赋予的意义外，没有其他意义。因此，加法不过是任何服从加法法则的过程。他的法则例如包括加法和乘法的结合律与交换律，以及若 ac = bc 且 c ≠ 0，则 a = b 的法则。于是，形式永久性原理在这里便通过采用公理而获得依据。

In the second edition of his Treatise on Algebra (1842-45, 1st edition 1830), Peacock derived his principle from axioms. He stated explicitly that algebra like geometry is a deductive science. Hence the processes of algebra have to be based on a complete statement of the body of laws or axioms which dictate the operations used in the processes. The symbols for the operations have, at least for the deductive science of algebra, no sense other than those given to them by the laws. Thus, addition means no more than any process which obeys the laws of addition. His laws were, for example, the associative and commutative laws of addition and multiplication, and the law that if ac = bc and c ≠ 0 then a = b. And so the principle of permanence of form was justified here by the adoption of axioms.

在十九世纪的大部分时期，皮科克宣扬的代数观点都被接受。邓肯·F. 格雷戈里（1813—1844）、奥古斯都·德·摩根和赫尔曼·汉克尔（1839—1873），只作少许修改便赞同它。

Throughout most of the nineteenth century the view of algebra affirmed by Peacock was accepted. It was endorsed with minor modifications by Duncan F. Gregory (1813-1844), Augustus De Morgan, and Hermann Hankel (1839-1873).

这一原理本质上是任意的，它回避了各种数为什么具有与整数相同性质的问题。它实际上以命令方式认可了经验上正确、却未在逻辑上确立的东西。显然，皮科克、格雷戈里和德·摩根认为，他们能把代数建成一门独立于实数和复数性质的科学。当然，把某条经验规则称为原理，并不能提高其逻辑地位。但是，正如贝克莱主教所说：“古老而根深蒂固的偏见，常常变成原理；那些一旦取得原理的权威和信誉的命题，不仅自身，而且凡从中可推导出的东西，都被认为享有免受一切审查的特权。”

The principle was essentially arbitrary and begged the question of why the various types of numbers possess the same properties as the whole numbers. It actually sanctioned by fiat what was empirically correct but not logically established. Evidently, Peacock, Gregory, and De Morgan thought that they could make a science out of algebra independent of the properties of real and complex numbers. Of course, labeling some rule of thumb a principle does not improve its logical stature. But, as Bishop Berkeley remarked, “Ancient and rooted prejudices do often pass into principles; and those propositions which once obtain the force and credit of a principle, are not only themselves, but likewise whatever is deducible from them, thought privileged from all examination.”

形式永久性原理把代数看作符号及其组合规律的科学。这种基础既模糊，又缺乏弹性。其倡导者坚持算术代数与一般代数之间的平行关系，而且僵硬到这样的程度：若坚持到底，就会毁掉代数的普遍性。他们似乎从未意识到，一个公式在符号的一种解释下为真，在另一种解释下却未必为真。恰好，四元数的创造使这条原理失效，因为这些数——今天所谓超数中最早的一类——没有乘法交换律（第四章）。因此，代表某类超数的字母，并不具有实数和复数的一切性质。所以，这条原理是错误的。皮科克及其追随者没有认识到、而四元数引入后很快变得明显的是：代数不是只有一种，而是有许多种；建立在实数和复数上的代数，只有证明字母所代表的数具有赋予字母的全部性质，才能获得依据。

The principle of permanence of form treats algebra as a science of symbols and their laws of combination. This foundation was both vague and inelastic. Its advocates insisted on a parallelism between arithmetical and general algebra so rigid that, if maintained, it would destroy the generality of algebra, and they never seem to have realized that a formula true with one interpretation of the symbols might not be true for another. It so happens that the principle was vitiated by the creation of quaternions because these numbers—the first of what are now called hypernumbers— do not possess the commutative property of multiplication (Chapter IV). Hence, letters standing for a class of hypernumbers do not possess all the properties of real and complex numbers. Thus the principle was false. What Peacock and his followers failed to appreciate but what soon became evident after the introduction of quaternions is that there is not one algebra but many, and the algebra built on the real and complex numbers could be justified only by proving that the numbers for which the letters stood possessed all the prqperties attributed to the letters.

除了代数，十九世纪初的分析也仍陷于逻辑迷雾。拉格朗日的微积分基础（第六章）未使所有数学家满意，有些人重新采取贝克莱等人的立场，认为错误相互抵消。法国大革命时期伟大的军事领袖拉扎尔·N. M. 卡诺，在《论无穷小分析的形而上学》中采取了这种立场。他的形而上学“解释”说，错误确实相互抵消。在大量讨论已经提出的各种微积分方法之后，卡诺得出结论：虽然所有方法，以及达朗贝尔极限概念的使用，实际上都等同于希腊人的穷竭法，但无穷小量更加便捷。卡诺对澄清微积分概念确实作出了贡献，但并不重大。此外，他把牛顿、莱布尼茨和达朗贝尔的思想与希腊人的穷竭法联系起来，掺入了一个错误因素。在希腊几何或代数中，没有任何东西与导数有关。

Beyond algebra, analysis in the early 1800s was still in a logical fog. Lagrange’s foundation for the calculus (Chapter VI) did not satisfy all mathematicians, and some returned to the position taken by Berkeley and others that errors were offsetting each other. This position was taken by Lazare N. M. Carnot, who was also a great military leader of the French Revolution, in his Reflections on the Metaphysics of Infinitesimal Calculus. His metaphysics “explains” that errors do compensate for each other. After much discussion of the various approaches to the calculus that had been presented, Carnot concluded that, though all methods as well as the use of d’Alembert’s limit concept were really equivalent to the Greek method of exhaustion, infinitesimals were more expeditious. Carnot did make a contribution to the clarification of the concepts of the calculus but it was not major. Moreover, in relating the ideas of Newton, Leibniz, and d Alembert to the Greek method of exhaustion he introduced a false note. There was nothing in Greek geometry or algebra related to the derivative.

分析中的错误，一直延续到十九世纪很晚。例子很多，举一两个也许就够了。整个分析的基础是连续函数概念和函数导数概念。直观上，连续函数就是能由笔尖不间断运动所画出的曲线来表示的函数（图7.1）。这类函数的导数的几何意义，是曲线上任意一点 P 处切线的斜率。从直观出发，连续函数必然在每一点都有导数，这似乎很清楚。不过，十九世纪初有些数学家不屑于使用这种直观证据，着手尽可能用逻辑论证来证明一切。A B C

The blunders in analysis continued well into the nineteenth century. Examples are numerous but perhaps one or two may suffice. Fundamental to all of analysis are the concepts of a continuous function and the derivative of a function. Intuitively a continuous function is one which can be represented by a curve drawn with an uninterrupted motion of a pencil (Fig. 7.1). The geometrical meaning of the derivative of such a function is the slope of the tangent at any point P of the curve. On an intuitive basis, it seemed clear that a continuous function must have a derivative at each point. However, some of the early nineteenth-century mathematicians were above using such intuitive evidence, and they set out to prove by logical arguments whatever they could. ABC

图7.1

Figure 7.1

不幸的是，如图7.2所示，连续函数在 A、B、C 那样今天称为角点的地方，并没有导数。然而，1806年，安德烈-马里·安培（1775—1836）“证明”了每个函数在其连续的所有点都有导数。拉克鲁瓦在著名的三卷本《微积分论》（第二版，1810—19）中，以及十九世纪几乎所有主要教科书，都给出了其他或类似的“证明”。迟至1875年，约瑟夫·L. F. 贝特朗（1822—1900）还在论文中“证明”可微性。所有这些“证明”都是错误的。有些数学家可以原谅，因为函数概念长期没有被良好定义；但是，到1830年左右，这个缺陷已得到弥补。

Unfortunately, as Figure 7.2 shows, a continuous function that has what are now called corners, as at A, B, and C, does not possess derivatives at such points. Nevertheless, in 1806 Andre-Marie Ampere (1775- 1836) “proved” that every function has a derivative at all points where it is continuous. Other or similar “proofs” were given by Lacroix in his famous three-volume work Treatise on Differential and Integral Calculus (2nd edition, 1810-19), and by almost all the leading texts of the nineteenth century. Joseph L. F. Bertrand (1822-1900) “proved the differentiability in papers as late as 1875. All of these “proofs” were wrong. Some of these mathematicians can be excused on the ground that the concept of a function was for a long time not well defined, but by 1830 or so this failing was remedied.

当人们想到连续性和可微性是全部分析的基本概念，而分析从约1650年至今一直是主要研究领域时，得知数学家对这些概念曾如此模糊、如此不确定，不免震惊。这些错误严重到今天的数学本科生若犯下，也不可原谅；然而，它们却出自最著名的人物——傅里叶、柯西、伽罗瓦、勒让德、高斯——以及许多较次要却仍是当时主要数学家的学者。

When one considers that continuity and differentiability are the basic concepts in all of analysis and that analysis has been the major field of activity from about 1650 to the present, one can only be shocked to learn how vague and uncertain mathematicians were about these concepts. The mistakes were so gross that they would be inexcusable in an undergraduate mathematics student today; yet they were made by the most famous men—Fourier, Cauchy, Galois, Legendre, Gauss and also by a multitude of lesser lights who were, nevertheless, leading mathematicians of their times.

十九世纪的教科书仍自由使用“微分”和“无穷小量”等术语，其含义不清，或自相矛盾地既被定义为非零，又被定义为零。学习微积分的学生仍然困惑，所能做的最好事情，就是遵从达朗贝尔的忠告：“坚持下去，信心就会来到。”1890至1894年就读于剑桥大学三一学院的伯特兰·罗素，在《我的哲学发展》中写道：“教我无穷小分析的人，不知道其基本定理的有效证明，却试图劝我凭信仰接受官方的诡辩。”

Texts of the nineteenth century continued to use freely terms such as differential and infinitesimal whose meanings were unclear or inconsis-tently defined to be both non-zero and zero. Students of the calculus remained perplexed, and the best they could do was to follow the advice of d’Alembert: “Persist and faith will come to you.” Bertrand Russell, who attended Trinity College, Cambridge University from 1890 to 1894, wrote in My Philosophical Development, “Those who taught me the infinitesimal calculus did not know the valid proofs of its fundamental theorems and tried to persuade me to accept the official sophistries as an act of faith.”

十七、十八和十九世纪困扰数学家的逻辑困难，在分析领域最为严重，也就是在微积分，以及建立在微积分之上的无穷级数、微分方程等领域。然而，十九世纪初，几何又成为热门研究领域。欧几里得几何得到扩展，而几何的新分支射影几何，最先由让-维克托·蓬斯莱（1788—1867）恰当地构想出来。它主要研究图形从一个位置投影到另一个位置时所保持的性质，例如一个真实的二维场景通过照相机的“眼睛”投影到胶片上。根据以前的历史，人们可以预料：尽管蓬斯莱等人悟出许多定理，在证明它们时却遇到无休止的困难。这时，证明几何结果的代数方法已可利用，主要应归功于笛卡尔和费马在十七世纪的工作；但十九世纪前期的几何学家蔑视代数方法，认为它们是异物，无法传达几何本身所提供的洞见和价值。

The logical difficulties which plagued the mathematicians during the seventeenth, eighteenth, and nineteenth centuries were most severe in the area of analysis, that is, in the calculus and in the domains such as infinite series and differential equations which were built on the calculus. However, in the early nineteenth century, geometry once again became a favorite field of study. Euclidean geometry was extended, and a new branch of geometry, projective geometry (concerned mainly with properties of figures which are retained when the figure is projected from one place to another as, for example, when a real two-dimensional scene is projected through the “eye” of a camera onto a film), was first properly envisioned by Jean-Victor Poncelet (1788-1867). As one might expect on the basis of earlier history, though Poncelet and others divined many theorems, they had endless troubles in proving them. By this time, algebraic methods of proving geometric results had become available thanks largely to the seventeenth-century work of Descartes and Fermat, but the geometers of the first part of the nineteenth century scorned algebraic methods as alien and impenetrable to the insights and values which geometry proper afforded.

为了用纯几何方法“确立”自己的结果，蓬斯莱诉诸连续性原理。在《图形的射影性质论》（1822）中，他把它表述为：“如果一个图形由另一个图形经过连续变化而产生，且后者与前者同样一般，那么第一个图形的任何性质，都可以立即断言也属于第二个图形。”如何确定两个图形何时都是一般的，他没有解释。

To “establish” his results by purely geometric methods, Poncelet appealed to the principle of continuity. In his Treatise on the Protective Properties of Figures (1822), he phrased it thus: “If one figure is derived from another by a continuous change and the latter is as general as the former, then any property of the first figure can be asserted at once for the second figure.” The determination of when both figures are general was not explained.

为了“证明”这条原理可靠，蓬斯莱使用了欧几里得几何的一条定理：圆内相交两弦的线段乘积相等（图7.3中 ab = cd）。他指出，当交点移到圆外时，就得到两条割线分别与其外部线段的乘积相等（图7.4）。不需要证明，因为连续性原理保证了该定理。进一步，当一条割线成为切线时，割线与其外部线段相等，它们的乘积仍等于另一条割线与其外部线段的乘积（图7.5中 ab = c2）。蓬斯莱用来说明连续性原理的结果，恰好是三条各自已得到充分证明的定理，确实满足或体现这条原理。但是，创造了“连续性原理”这个词的蓬斯莱，把原理作为绝对真理提出，并在《图形的射影性质论》中大胆应用它，“证明”许多新的射影几何定理。

To “demonstrate” the soundness of the principle, Poncelet used a theorem of Euclidean geometry which states the equality of the products of the segments of intersecting chords of a circle (ab = cd in Fig. 7.3). He noted that when the point of intersection moves outside the circle, one obtains the equality of the products of the secants and their external segments (Fig. 7.4). No proof was needed because the principle of continuity guaranteed the theorem. Further, when one secant becomes a tangent, the secant and its external segment become equal and their product continues to equal the product of the other secant and its external segment (ab = c2 in Fig. 7.5). The results Poncelet used to illustrate the principle of continuity happen to be three separate, well-established theorems and do satisfy or exemplify the principle. But Poncelet, who coined the term “principle of continuity,” advanced the principle as an absolute truth and applied it boldly in his Treatise to “prove” many new theorems of projective geometry.

这条原理并非蓬斯莱的新创。从广义哲学意义说，它可追溯到莱布尼茨。作为数学原理，莱布尼茨曾按前述方式（第六章）将其用于微积分。在加斯帕尔·蒙日（1746—1818）重新用它确立某类定理以前，这条原理只是偶尔被使用。他先在图形的特殊位置证明一条一般定理然后主张这条定理一般地成立，即使图形中的某些元素变为虚的也是如此。因此，要证明关于直线和曲线的定理，他会在直线截曲线时证明它，然后主张，即使直线不再截曲线、交点成为虚点，结果仍成立。

The principle was not new with Poncelet. In a broad philosophical sense the principle goes back to Leibniz. As a mathematical principle Leibniz used it in the manner indicated earlier (Chapter VI) in connection with the calculus. The principle was used only occasionally until Gaspard Monge (1746-1818) revived it to establish certain types of theorems. He proved a general theorem first for a special position of a figure and then maintained that the theorem was true generally, even when some elements in the figure became imaginary. Thus to prove a theorem about a line and a curve, he would prove it when the line cuts the curve and then maintain that the result holds even when the line no longer cuts the curve and the points of intersection are imaginary.

图7.5

Figure 7.5

巴黎科学院的一些成员批评连续性原理，认为它只有启发价值。柯西尤其批评它，说：

Some members of the Paris Academy of Science criticized the principle of continuity and regarded it as having only heuristic value. Cauchy in particular criticized the principle and said:

严格地说，这条原理只是归纳性的，借助它，可以把在某些限制下确立的定理，扩展到这些限制不再成立的情形。应用于二次曲线，它引导作者得到了精确结果。然而，我们认为，不能一般地承认它，并把它自由应用于几何甚至分析中的各种问题。过分强调它，有时可能陷入明显的错误。

This principle is properly speaking only inductive, with the aid of which one extends theorems established under certain restrictions to cases where these restrictions no longer hold. Applied to curves of the second degree it leads the author to exact results. Nevertheless we think that it cannot be admitted generally and applied freely to all sorts of questions in geometry or even in analysis. By according too much emphasis to it one could fall some times into obvious errors.

不幸的是，柯西用来攻击这条原理可靠性的例子，却正是这条原理给出的结果已由其他方法正确证明的例子。

Unfortunately the examples Cauchy used to attack the soundness of this principle were ones wherein the principle did produce results that had been correctly proved by other means.

批评者还指责，蓬斯莱等人对这条原理的信心，实际上建立在它可以由代数提供依据这一事实之上。事实上，蓬斯莱在俄国被俘时所作的一些笔记表明，他确实用代数检验过这条原理的可靠性（他曾是拿破仑军队的士兵）。蓬斯莱同意可以用代数证明它，却坚持这条原理不依赖这种证明。然而，几乎可以肯定，他依靠代数方法看出应该是什么情形，然后用这条原理作为依据，肯定几何结果。

The critics also charged that the confidence which Poncelet and others had in the principle really rested on the fact that the principle could be justified on an algebraic basis. As a matter of fact some notes Poncelet made while he was a prisoner in Russia (he was a soldier in Napoleon’s army) show that he did use algebra to test the soundness of the principle. Poncelet agreed that a proof could be based on algebra but he insisted that the principle did not depend on such a proof. However, it is quite certain that Poncelet relied on the algebraic method to see what should be the case and then affirmed the geometric results using the principle as a justification.

尽管受到一些批评，连续性原理在十九世纪仍被看作直观上清楚，因而可以作为证明方法来使用。几何学家自由地使用它。然而，从数学逻辑发展的观点看，连续性原理不过是一条为特定目的而作的武断断言，旨在给当时的人无法用纯演绎证明确立的东西提供依据。人们编造并调用这条原理，以认可形象化和直觉所提出的东西。

Despite some criticism, the principle of continuity was accepted during the nineteenth century as intuitively clear and therefore applicable as a method of proof. The geometers used it freely. However, from the standpoint of the logical development of mathematics, the principle of continuity was no more than a dogmatic ad hoc assertion intended to justify what the men of the time could not establish by purely deductive proofs. The principle was contrived and invoked to justify what visualization and intuition had adduced.

蓬斯莱对连续性原理的倡导和应用，只是数学家为了给无法有效证明的东西提供依据而走得极远的一个例子。但几何几乎各领域的逻辑状况都令人悲哀。我们知道（第五章），主要是十八世纪后期和十九世纪前期关于非欧几里得几何的工作，揭露了欧几里得几何演绎结构中的严重缺陷。然而，数学家并未赶紧修补这些缺陷，反而坚持那些定理具有绝对确定性。我们可以有把握地推断，定理的直观基础，以及实际应用所提供的佐证，如此令人信服，以致没有人深切关心这些缺陷。

Poncelet’s advocacy and application of the principle of continuity is but one example of the extraordinary lengths to which mathematicians went to justify what they could not establish by valid proof. But the logical state of geometry was sad in almost every area. As we know (Chapter V), it was chiefly the work on non-Euclidean geometry during the last part of the eighteenth and first part of the nineteenth century that revealed serious defects in the deductive structure of Euclidean geometry. Nevertheless, mathematicians did not hasten to repair these defects but in fact maintained the absolute certainty of the theorems. One may safely infer that the intuitive basis for the theorems and the corroboration which practical applications provided were so convincing that no one was deeply concerned about the defects.

非欧几里得几何的情形略有不同。十九世纪初，除了它的创始者——兰伯特、高斯、罗巴切夫斯基和鲍耶——以外，还有少数人把他们创造的几何接受为一个正当分支，虽然它的逻辑基础肯定不如欧几里得几何的基础完善。然而，特别是在高斯和黎曼关于这一学科的工作为人所知以后，不仅这四个人，几乎他们所有后继者，都相信非欧几里得几何是一致的，即其定理不会彼此矛盾，尽管他们没有证明。他们也认识到，萨凯里认为自己已得到矛盾，是错误的。

The situation was somewhat different in the case of non-Euclidean geometry. In the early 1800s, a few men in addition to its creators Lambert, Gauss, Lobatchevsky, and Bolyai—accepted the geometry they created as a proper branch even though its logical foundation was certainly not in as good a state as that of Euclidean geometry. However, especially after Gauss’s and Riemann’s work in this subject became known, not only these four men, but almost all their successors believed, though they had no proof, that the non-Euclidean geometry was consistent, that is, that its theorems would not contradict each other. They also recognized that Saccheri was wrong in believing that he had arrived at a contradiction.

但是，仍有可能发现这种几何内部的矛盾。如果发生这种情况，那么双曲几何的平行公理假设就是无效的，而欧几里得的平行公理，就将像萨凯里相信的那样，成为其其他公理的推论。因此，既没有一致性的任何证明，也没有新几何适用性的证据——后者至少可能成为令人信服的论据——许多数学家仍接受了前人视为荒谬的东西。他们的接受是一种信仰行为。非欧几里得几何的一致性问题，又悬而未决了五十年（第八章）。

However, the possibility remained open that contradictions within this geometry might still be discovered. Were this to happen, then the assumption of the parallel axiom of hyperbolic geometry would be invalid and, as Saccheri had believed, Euclid’s parallel axiom would be a consequence of his other axioms. Thus, without any proof of consistency or evidence of the applicability of the new geometry, which might at least have served as a convincing argument, many mathematicians accepted what their predecessors had regarded as absurd. Their acceptance was an act of faith. The question of the consistency of non-Euclidean geometry remained open for another fifty years (Chapter VIII).

显然，十九世纪初，没有一个数学分支在逻辑上可靠。实数系、代数、欧几里得几何，以及较新的非欧几里得几何和射影几何，要么基础不充分，要么根本没有基础。分析，即微积分及其扩展，不仅缺少自由使用的实数和代数的逻辑基础，而且微积分本身的概念——导数、积分和无穷级数——也不清楚。我们完全有理由说，数学中没有什么得到可靠的确立。

Evidently in the early nineteenth century no branch of mathematics was logically secure. The real number system, algebra, and Euclidean and the newer non-Euclidean and projective geometries had either inadequate or no foundations at all. Analysis, that is, the calculus and its extensions, lacked not only the logical foundations of the real numbers and algebra, which were used freely, but also the clarity of the concepts of calculus proper—the derivative, the integral, and infinite series. One could justifiably say that nothing in mathematics had been soundly established.

考虑到数学原来意味着什么，许多数学家对证明的态度似乎难以置信。十八世纪，分析中的含糊不清已经显而易见，有些数学家便放弃了这一领域的严谨。例如，米歇尔·罗尔（1652—1719）宣称，微积分是巧妙谬误的汇集。另一些人更进一步，像吃不到葡萄的狐狸那样，公开嘲笑希腊人的严谨。阿列克西-克洛德·克莱罗（1713—1765）在《几何原理》（1741）中说：

The attitude toward proof adopted by many mathematicians seems incredible in view of what mathematics had meant. In the eighteenth century, the obscurities in analysis were apparent and some mathematicians gave up on rigor in this area. Thus, Michel Rolle (1652-1719) taught that the calculus was a collection of ingenious fallacies. Others went further and, acting like the fox with the grapes, explicitly derided the rigor of the Greeks. Alexis-Claude Clairaut (1713-1765) said in his Elements of Geometry (1741):

欧几里得不辞辛劳地证明两个相交的圆没有同一圆心，或者一个三角形包含于另一个三角形之内时，内三角形的边长之和小于外三角形的边长之和，这不足为奇。这位几何学家必须说服那些以拒绝最明显真理为荣的顽固诡辩者；所以几何必须像逻辑一样，依靠形式推理来反驳吹毛求疵之徒。

It is not surprising that Euclid goes to the trouble of demonstrating that two circles which cut one another do not have the same center, that the sum of the sides of a triangle which is enclosed within another is smaller than the sum of the sides of the enclosing triangle. This geometer had to convince obstinate sophists who glory in rejecting the most evident truths; so that geometry must, like logic, rely on formal reasoning in order to rebut the quibblers.

克莱罗接着补充说：“但如今情势已经改变。一切涉及常识预先已知之事的推理，今天都被置之不理，只会遮蔽真理，使读者疲倦。”

Clairaut then added, But the tables have turned. All reasoning concerned with what common sense knows in advance, is today disregarded, and serves only to conceal the truth and to weary the reader.”

十八世纪及十九世纪初的态度，由 J. 厄内-弗龙斯基（1775—1853）表达出来。他是卓越的算法家，却不关心严谨。巴黎科学院的一个委员会批评他的一篇论文缺乏严谨，弗龙斯基回答说，这是“重手段而轻目的的学究气”。

The attitude of the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries was expressed by J. Hoene-Wronski (1775—1853), who was a great algorith-mist but not concerned with rigor. A paper of his was criticized by a commission of the Paris Academy of Sciences as lacking in rigor, and Wronski replied that this was “pedantry which prefers means to the end.”

拉克鲁瓦在三卷本《微积分论》第二版（1810—19）第一卷序言中说：“希腊人操心的那些精细问题，我们不再需要。”当时的典型态度是问：为什么要费力用深奥推理证明本来从不怀疑的事，或者用较不明显的东西证明较明显的东西？

Lacroix, in the second edition (1810—19) of his three-volume Treatise on Differential and Integral Calculus, said in the Preface to the first volume, “Such subtleties as the Greeks worried about we no longer need.” The typical attitude of the times was to ask why one should go to the trouble of proving by abstruse reasoning things one never doubts in the first place or of demonstrating what is more evident by means of what is less evident.

即使到十九世纪稍晚时期，卡尔·古斯塔夫·雅各布·雅可比（1804—1851），在椭圆函数工作中留下许多未完成之处，还说：“我们没有时间讲究高斯式的严谨。”许多人的行为仿佛说明，难以证明的东西就不需要证明。对大多数人来说，严谨不是关切。有些工作，他们声称能用阿基米德的方法严谨化，可即使一位现代阿基米德也做不到。尤其是微分方面的工作，在希腊数学中根本没有对应。达朗贝尔1743年的话：“直到现在……人们更关心扩大建筑，而不是照亮入口；更关心增高建筑，而不是给予基础适当的强度”，适用于整个十八世纪和十九世纪初的工作。

Even later in the nineteenth century, Karl Gustav Jacob Jacobi (1804-1851), who left many points in his work on elliptic functions incomplete, said, “For Gaussian rigor we have no time.” Many acted as though what defied proof needed no proof. For most men rigor was not a concern. Often what they said could be rigorized by the method of Archimedes, could not have been rigorized by a modern Archimedes. This is particularly true of the work on differentiation which had no parallel in Greek mathematics. What d’Alembert said in 1743, “Up to the present. . . more concern has been given to enlarging the building than to illuminating the entrance, to raising it higher than to giving proper strength to the foundations,” applies to the work of the entire eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.

到十九世纪中叶，对证明的重视已低落到这样的程度：有些数学家即使可能作出完整证明，也懒得去做。杰出的代数几何学家之一、所谓矩阵代数（第四章）的创立者阿瑟·凯莱（1821—1895），提出了一条关于矩阵的定理，称为凯莱—哈密顿定理。矩阵是数的矩形排列；对于方阵，每行和每列都有 n 个数。凯莱验证了自己的定理对2 × 2矩阵为真，并在1858年的论文中说：“我认为没有必要费力对任意阶［n × n］矩阵的一般情况，作出这一条定理的形式证明。”

By the middle of the nineteenth century, the regard for proof had fallen so low that some mathematicians did not even bother to execute full proofs where they might have been able to achieve them. Arthur Cayley (1821-1895), one of the superb algebraic geometers and the inventor of what is called matrix algebra (Chapter IV), stated a theorem on matrices known as the Cayley-Flamilton theorem. A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers and in the case of square matrices there are n numbers in each row and in each column. Cayley verified that his theorem was true for 2 by 2 matrices and in a paper of 1858 said, “I have not thought it necessary to undertake the labor of a formal proof of the theorem in the general case of a matrix of any degree [n by «].”

优秀的英国代数学家詹姆斯·约瑟夫·西尔维斯特（1814—1897），于1876至1884年在约翰斯·霍普金斯大学任教授。他在讲课时会说：“我还没有证明这个，但我确信它必然如此，就像我对任何事情能够确信的程度一样。”然后他用这个结果证明新的定理。往往到下一次课结束时，他会承认自己原来那样确信的东西是错的。1889年，他证明了一条关于3 × 3矩阵的定理，而对于证明该定理适用于 n × n 矩阵，只提示了还必须考虑的几个要点。

James Joseph Sylvester (1814-1897), an excellent British algebraist, spent the years from 1876 to 1884 as a professor at Johns Hopkins University. In his lectures he would say, “I haven’t proved this, but I am as sure as I can be of anything that it must be so.” He would then use the result to prove new theorems. Often at the end of the next lecture he would admit that what he had been so sure of was false. In 1889 he proved a theorem about 3 by 3 matrices and merely indicated a few additional points which have to be considered to prove the theorem for n by n matrices.

欧几里得在处理几何和整数时曾有良好开端，鉴于此，这部非逻辑发展史促使人们发问：为什么数学家为了使后来的发展——无理数、负数、复数、代数、微积分及其扩展——逻辑化，必须如此艰苦而又如此无效地奋斗？如我们所述（第五章），欧几里得几何和整数在直观上很容易得到良好理解，因此比较容易找出基本原理或公理，以推导其他性质，尽管欧几里得的处理本身仍有些缺陷。另一方面，无理数、负数、复数、字母运算及微积分的概念，难把握得多。

This history of illogical development, in view of the fine start made by Euclid in his treatment of geometry and the whole numbers, prompts the question, why did mathematicians have to struggle so much and so ineffectively to logicize the subsequent developments—irrational, negative, and complex numbers, algebra, the calculus and its extensions? As we have noted (Chapter V), insofar as Euclidean geometry and the whole numbers are concerned, these are so readily and well understood intuitively that it was relatively easy to find fundamental principles or axioms from which to derive other properties, though at that Euclid’s development was somewhat deficient. On the other hand, irrational, negative, and complex numbers, operations with letters, and the concepts of the calculus are far more difficult to grasp.

不过，还有更深的原因。大师们在不知不觉中，使数学的性质发生了一种微妙变化。直到约1500年，数学概念都是经验的直接理想化或抽象。诚然，那时负数和无理数已经出现，并被印度人和阿拉伯人接受。然而，虽然不应贬低他们的贡献，就依据而言，他们满足于直观和经验。当复数、广泛采用字母系数的代数，以及导数和积分的概念也进入数学以后，这门学科便由人类心灵深处产生的概念所支配。尤其是导数或瞬时变化率的概念，虽然当然在速度这一物理现象中有某种直观根据，却更多是一种智力构造。它在性质上与数学三角形完全不同。同样，理解希腊人刻意避免的无穷大量、巧妙绕开的无穷小量，以及负数和复数的努力，也陷入困境，因为数学家未能认识到，这些概念并非直接以经验为根据，而是心灵的创造。

But there is a deeper reason. A subtle change in the nature of mathematics had been unconsciously made by the masters. Up to about 1500, the concepts of mathematics were immediate idealizations of or abstractions from experience. It is true that by that time negative and irrational numbers had made their appearance and had been accepted by the Hindus and the Arabs. However, though their contributions are not to be deprecated, they were content to be intuitive and empirical insofar as justification is concerned. When, in addition, complex numbers, an extensive algebra employing literal coefficients, and the notions of derivative and integral entered mathematics, the subject became dominated by concepts derived from the recesses of human minds. In particular, the notion of the derivative or an instantaneous rate of change, though of course it has some intuitive base in the physical phenomenon of velocity, is nevertheless far more an intellectual construct. It is entirely different in quality from the mathematical triangle. Likewise, efforts to understand infinitely large quantities, which the Greeks had studiously avoided, infinitely small ones, which the Greeks had skillfully circumvented, negative numbers, and complex numbers floundered because mathematicians failed to appreciate that these concepts were not grounded in immediate experience, but creations of the mind.

换句话说，数学家是在提供概念，而不是从现实世界抽象观念。在产生思想时，他们正从感官转向智力。随着这些概念在应用中越来越有用，人们起先勉强、后来贪婪地抓住它们。在这里，熟悉所滋生的不是轻蔑，而是不加批判，甚至觉得自然。从1700年起，越来越多远离自然、从人类头脑中完整涌出的观念，将进入数学，并以更少的顾虑被接受。数学家被自己造出的力量抬高，被迫从远高于坚实大地的层次来审视自己的学科。

In other words, mathematicians were contributing concepts rather than abstracting ideas from the real world. For the genesis of their ideas they were turning from the sensory to the intellectual faculties. As these concepts proved to be more and more useful in application, they were at first grudgingly and later greedily seized upon. Familiarity in these cases did not breed contempt but uncriticalness and even naturalness. From 1700 on, more and more notions farther removed from nature and sprung full blown from human minds were to enter mathematics and be accepted with fewer qualms. Mathematicians, hoist by their own petard, were being compelled to view their subject from a level well above solid earth.

由于未能认识到新概念性质上的这种变化，他们也未意识到，公理化发展需要自明真理以外的根据。当然，新概念远比旧概念微妙，而我们现在知道，适当的公理基础并不能轻易建立。

Because they failed to recognize this change in the character of the new concepts, they also failed to realize that a basis for axiomatic development other than self-evident truth was needed. Of course, the new concepts were far more subtle than the old ones and the proper axiomatic basis, as we now know, could not have been readily erected.

那么，数学家怎样知道前进方向？鉴于他们的证明传统，他们怎么敢仅仅应用规则，并断言结论可靠？毫无疑问，解决物理问题提供了目标。一旦这些问题被数学地表述出来，高超的技术便发挥作用，新的方法和结论随之出现。数学的物理意义也指导数学步骤，并常常提供部分论证，以补足非数学的步骤。这一过程在原则上，与证明几何定理没有区别：在几何证明中，人们使用图形里完全明显的某些事实，即使没有公理或定理支持它们。

Flow then did mathematicians know where to head and, in view of their tradition of proof, how could they have dared merely to apply rules and assert the reliability of their conclusions? There is no question that solving physical problems supplied the goal. Once these were formulated mathematically, technical virtuosity took over and new methodologies and conclusions emerged. The physical meaning of the mathematics also guided the mathematical steps and often supplied partial arguments to fill in non-mathematical steps. The process was in principle no different from the proof of a theorem of geometry wherein some facts entirely obvious in a figure are used, even though no axiom or theorem supports them.

除了物理思考，在一切新的数学工作中，可靠直觉也发挥作用。基本思想或方法，总是在为结论设计出任何理性论证很久以前，就已凭直觉被把握。伟大的数学家，无论容许自己多大自由，总有可靠的本能，使自己避免毁灭性的灾难。伟人的直觉，比平庸者的演绎证明更可靠。

Beyond physical thinking, there is in all new mathematical work the role of sound intuition. The essential idea or method is always grasped intuitively long before any rational argument for the conclusion is devised. Great mathematicians, whatever license they may allow themselves, have a sure instinct for saving themselves from crushing disaster. The intuitions of great men are sounder than the deductive demonstrations of mediocrities.

用某种数学表述把握了物理问题的本质以后，尤其是十八世纪的数学家，便受到公式的诱惑。显然，公式对他们如此有吸引力，以致仅仅通过求导或积分之类形式运算，从一个公式推导出另一个公式，就足以成为它的依据。符号的魅力压倒并吞噬了他们的理性。十八世纪被称为数学的英雄时代，因为数学家以如此薄弱的逻辑武装，竟敢于并实现如此壮丽的科学征服。

Having grasped the essence of a physical problem in some mathematical formulation, the eighteenth-century mathematicians in particular were seduced by formulas. Apparently, formulas were so attractive to them that the mere derivation of one formula from another by a formal operation such as differentiation or integration was enough to justify it. The fascination of symbols overpowered and consumed their reason. The eighteenth century has been called the heroic age in mathematics because the mathematicians dared and achieved such magnificent scientific conquests with so little logical armament.

还有一个问题：为什么数学家确信自己的结果正确，虽然他们知道，特别是在十八世纪，微积分概念的表述模糊，证明也不充分？部分答案是，许多结果由经验和观察得到确认，天文学预测尤其突出（第二章）。但另一个相关因素，也使十七、十八世纪的人相信自己的工作。他们确信，上帝按照数学设计世界，而数学家正在发现并揭示这一设计（第二章）。虽然他们所揭示的只是局部，他们却认为那是潜在真理的一部分。他们相信自己正在发现上帝的某些造物，并将最终到达完整永恒真理的应许之地；这种信念支撑了他们的精神和勇气，而丰硕的科学成果则是滋养心灵、使他们得以坚持的天赐吗哪。

There is still the question of why the mathematicians were confident that their results were correct even though they knew, especially in the eighteenth century, that the concepts of tire calculus were vaguely formulated and their proofs inadequate. Part of the answer is that many of the results were confirmed by experience and observation. Outstanding were the astronomical predictions (Chapter II). But another related factor induced the seventeenth- and eighteenth-century men to believe in their work. These men were convinced that God had designed the world mathematically and that mathematicians were discovering and revealing that design (Chapter II). Though what the men of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries uncovered was partial, they thought it was part of underlying truth. The belief that they were discovering some of God’s handiwork and that they would eventually arrive at the promised land of complete eternal truths sustained their spirit and courage while the fruitful scientific results were the manna which fed their minds and enabled them to persist.

数学家只找到了所寻宝藏的一部分，但有充分迹象表明，还有更多可发现。那么，运用得如此准确的数学规律，纵然缺少数学证明的精确性，又何必计较呢？由科学证据加强的宗教信念，代替了薄弱或不存在的逻辑力量。他们如此渴望获得上帝的真理，以致没有可靠基础也继续建造。他们用成功安抚良心。成功确实如此令人陶醉，以致大多数时候，理论和严谨都被遗忘。偶尔诉诸哲学或神秘学说，又遮掩了某些困难，使它们不再显眼。在逻辑上，十七、十八世纪及十九世纪初的工作当然粗糙，但也有非凡的创造性。十九世纪末和二十世纪的人，为了贬低其成就，多少不公正地强调了这些工作的错误和不精确。

The mathematicians had found only a portion of the sought-for treasures, but there were ample indications of more to be found. Need one quibble then if the mathematical laws that applied so accurately lacked the precision of mathematical proof? Religious conviction bolstered by scientific evidence substituted for weak or non-existent logical strength. They were so eager to secure God’s truth that they continued to build without a secure foundation. They salved their consciences with success. Indeed, success was so intoxicating that most of the time theory and rigor were forgotten. An occasional recourse to philosophical or mystical doctrines cloaked some difficulties so that they were no longer visible. Logically the work of the seventeenth, eighteenth, and early nineteenth centuries was surely crude. But it was also masterfully creative. The errors and imprecision of this work have been stressed somewhat unfairly by late-nineteenth-and twentieth-century men in order to belittle its triumphs.

十七、十八世纪的数学，就像一家成交无数、交货辉煌的大公司，却由于管理不善，从根本上资不抵债。当然，顾客——购买和使用数学商品的科学家——以及债权人——毫不犹豫地投资数学股票的公众——都不知道其真实财务状况。

The mathematics of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries was like that of a large business corporation which makes numerous deals and spectacular deliveries but because of mismanagement is fundamentally insolvent. Of course, the customers—the scientists who bought and used the mathematical merchandise—and the creditors—the public which invested unhesitatingly in the stock of mathematics—were unaware of the true financial state.

于是，我们看到一种极其矛盾的局面。如今已大大扩展的数学，其逻辑从未如此糟糕。但是，数学在表述和预测自然运行方面的成功如此令人印象深刻，以致十八世纪所有知识分子比希腊人更甚，宣告自然是按数学设计的，颂扬数学是人类理性的卓越乃至崇高产物。正如约瑟夫·艾迪生在《赞美诗》中谈到天体时所说，在理性的耳中，它们全都欢欣歌唱。

And so we find a highly paradoxical state of affairs. The logic of the now vastly expanded mathematics was never in a sorrier state. But the success of mathematics in representing and predicting the ways of nature was so impressive that, still more so than the Greeks, all the intellectuals of the eighteenth century proclaimed the mathematical design of nature and extolled mathematics as the superb and even sublime product of human reason. As Joseph Addison in his Hymn said of the heavenly bodies, in reason’s ear they all rejoiced.

回顾起来，这种对数学推理的颂扬，似乎难以置信。固然，零碎的推理确实被使用过。但特别在十八世纪，文献中充斥着关于复数的意义与性质、负数和复数的对数、微积分基础、级数求和，以及我们尚未描述的其他问题的激烈争论，“混乱时代”似乎是更恰当的称呼。到1800年，数学家对结果比对其逻辑依据更有把握。从证明的角度看，这些结果只是信念。我们很快将看到，十九世纪后期的工作，才更配得上“理性时代”之名（第八章）。

In retrospect, this glorification of mathematical reasoning seems incredible. To be sure, tatters of reasoning were employed. But especially in the eighteenth century when heated debates about the meaning and properties of complex numbers, logarithms of negative and complex numbers, the foundations of the calculus, the summation of series, and other issues we have not described filled the literature, the designation Age of Confusion seems more appropriate. By 1800, mathematicians were more certain of results than of their logical justification. From the standpoint of proof the results were beliefs. As we shall soon see, it was the work of the latter part of the nineteenth century that would justify far more the name Age of Reason (Chapter VIII).

大多数数学家满足于追求创新，不太关心证明；但少数主要数学家开始为数学的非逻辑状态感到震惊。才华横溢、早熟的挪威人尼尔斯·亨里克·阿贝尔（1802—1829），在1826年给克里斯托弗·汉斯廷教授的信中，着重指出了分析局面的绝望。他抱怨：

While most mathematicians were content to pursue innovations without much concern for proof, a few of the leading mathematicians became alarmed by the illogical state of mathematics. The desperateness of the situation in analysis was underscored by the brilliant, precocious Norwegian Niels Henrick Abel (1802—1829) in a letter of 1826 to Professor Christoffer Hansteen. Fie complained about:

分析中无疑存在巨大的晦暗。它如此彻底地缺乏任何规划和体系，以致有那么多人研究它，实在奇怪。最糟糕的是，它从未得到严格处理。高等分析中，以逻辑上站得住脚的方式证明的定理非常少。到处都能看到这种从特殊推到一般的可悲做法，而这种做法竟只导致这么少的所谓悖论，尤其奇怪。

the tremendous obscurity which one unquestionably finds in analysis. It lacks so completely all plan and system that it is peculiar that so many men have studied it. The worst of it is, it has never been treated stringently. There are very few theorems in advanced analysis which have been demonstrated in a logically tenable manner. Everywhere one finds this miserable way of concluding from the special to the general and it is extremely peculiar that such a procedure has led to so few of the so-called paradoxes.

特别关于发散级数，阿贝尔于1826年1月写信给以前的老师贝恩特·霍尔姆博：

Apropos of divergent series in particular, Abel wrote in January 1826 to his former teacher Berndt Holmboe:

发散级数是魔鬼的发明，任何证明以它们为基础，都是可耻的。使用它们，可以得出任何想要的结论；正因为如此，这些级数才产生了那么多谬误和悖论……。我已极其注意所有这些，因为除了等比级数，全部数学中没有一个无穷级数，其和被严谨地确定。换句话说，数学中最重要的东西，也正是基础最薄弱的东西。尽管如此，其中多数竟是正确的，这令人异常惊讶。我正在设法找出原因；这是一个极其有趣的问题。

The divergent series are the invention of the devil, and it is a shame to base on them any demonstration whatsoever. By using them one may draw any conclusion he pleases and that is why these series have produced so many fallacies and so many paradoxes. ... I have become prodigiously attentive to all this, for with the exception of the geometrical series, there does not exist in all of mathematics a single infinite series the sum of which has been determined rigorously. In other words, the things which are most important in mathematics are also those which have the least foundation. That most of these things are correct in spite of that is extraordinarily surprising. I am trying to find the reason for this; it is an exceedingly interesting question.

在人群中，有些人不满足于用酒精淹没忧愁。同样，在数学家中，有些人不满足于陶醉于物理上的成功，以淹没对数学非逻辑状态的担忧。这些更勇敢的人，相信自己正在揭示上帝设计的一部分，或许曾从中得到安慰，但这种信念在十八世纪末被放弃后（第四章），安慰也归于无有。失去这种支持，他们觉得必须重新审查自己的工作，正视概念模糊、缺乏证明、现有证明的不足、矛盾，以及对已创造的东西究竟哪些正确的彻底混乱。他们认识到，数学并非人们传说的那种理性典范。给已被接受的东西提供依据的，不是理性，而是直觉、几何图形、物理论证、形式永久性原理之类特设原则，以及对形而上学的求助。

Among people at large, some are not content to drown their sorrows in alcohol. So among mathematicians, some were not content to drown their concern about the illogical state of mathematics in the inebriation of physical successes. Whatever solace these more courageous men may have derived from the belief that they were uncovering pieces of God’s design was nullified by the late-eighteenth-century abandonment of that belief (Chapter IV). Having lost that support they felt obliged to reexamine their work, and they faced the vagueness, the lack of proofs, the inadequacies in the existing proofs, the contradictions, and the sheer confusion about what was correct in what had been created. These men realized that mathematics had not been the paradigm of reason it was reputed to be. In place of reason, it was intuition, geometrical diagrams, physical arguments, ad hoc principles such as the principle of permanence of form, and the recourse to metaphysics that justified what had been accepted.

逻辑结构的理想，无疑早已由希腊人阐明并宣扬。因此，少数着手在算术、代数和分析中实现这一理想的数学家，相信数学家至少在欧几里得几何这个极重要的例子中，已实际做到这一点；这种信念鼓舞了他们的努力。他们想，既然有人曾登上奥林匹斯山，别人也可以再次攀登。他们未曾预见，为一切现存数学提供严谨基础的任务，将比1850年的任何数学家所能设想的更加困难、更加精微。他们也未预见随之而来的额外麻烦。

The ideal of a logical structure had certainly been made clear and proclaimed by the Greeks. And so the few mathematicians who undertook to achieve it in arithmetic, algebra, and analysis were buoyed up in their efforts by the belief that mathematicians had practically done so in at least one highly significant case, Euclidean geometry. They thought that if some had scaled Olympus once, others might scale it again. What these men did not foresee was that the task of supplying rigorous foundations for all of the existing mathematics would prove to be far more difficult and subtle than any mathematician of 1850 could possibly have envisioned. Nor did they foresee the additional troubles that were to ensue.

八、非逻辑的发展：在天堂门口

VIII. The Illogical Development: At the Gates of Paradise

今天可以说，绝对的严谨已经达到了。

One may say today that absolute rigor has been attained.

亨利·庞加莱

Henri Poincare

所谓数学批判运动的创始者认识到，两千多年来，数学家一直徘徊在直觉、似乎合理的论证、归纳推理及符号表达式形式运算的荒野中。他们提议，在数学没有适当逻辑基础的地方建立基础，消除模糊概念和矛盾，并改进欧几里得几何等分支的现有基础。这一计划始于十九世纪第二个十年。非欧几里得几何的研究更广为人知以后，运动得到扩展并加速，因为这些研究揭示了欧几里得几何结构中的缺陷。显然，即使这个被认为是严谨证明堡垒和典范的结构，也需要大修。稍后（1843），四元数的创造又挑战了人们运算实数和复数时的自信。当然，有些数学家对自己的工作过分自信，继续搞乱推理；得到正确结果时，便自欺地相信自己的证明和教科书叙述可靠。

The founders of what has been called the critical movement in mathematics realized that for over two thousand years mathematicians had wandered in a wilderness of intuitions, plausible arguments, inductive reasoning, and formal manipulation of symbolic expressions.
