They proposed to build the proper logical foundations of mathematics where none existed, to eliminate vague concepts and contradictions, and to improve the existing foundations in branches such as Euclidean geometry. This program was begun in the second decade of the nineteenth century. The movement was expanded and accelerated when the work on non-Euclidean geometry became more widely known, because this work revealed faults in the structure of Euclidean geometry. It became apparent that even that structure, the presumed stronghold and paradigm of rigorous proof, needed overhauling- Just a little later (1843), the creation of quaternions challenged the assurance with which real and complex numbers were manipulated. Of course, some mathematicians, cocksure of their own work, continued to bungle their reasoning and, when they obtained correct results, deceived themselves into believing that their proofs and textbook presentations were sound.

虽然批判思想家承认，数学关于物理世界真理的主张必须放弃，他们仍充分认识到，数学在天体和地面力学、声学、流体动力学、弹性、光学、电学、磁学及工程各分支中的巨大成就，以及在这些领域预测的惊人准确性。数学虽然在不可战胜的真理旗帜保护下作战，它的胜利必定来自某种根本的、也许神秘的力量。数学对自然的非凡适用性尚待解释（第十五章），但没人能否认这一事实本身，也没人敢扔掉如此强大的工具。当然，不应因容忍盘根错节的逻辑困难和矛盾而危及这种力量。此外，数学家虽然忽视逻辑可靠性而违反了自己的原则，却不打算让学科永远停留在实用基础上。他们的声望岌岌可危。否则，他们怎能把自己的高尚活动与埋头俗务的工程师和工匠的活动区分开呢？

Though the critical thinkers acknowledged that the claim of mathematics to truth about the physical world had to be abandoned, they did appreciate the enormous achievements in celestial and terrestrial mechanics, acoustics, fluid dynamics, elasticity, optics, electricity, magnetism, and the many branches of engineering, and the incredible accuracy of predictions in these areas. Though mathematics had fought under the protection of the invincible banner of truth, it must have achieved its victories through some essential, perhaps mysterious strength. The extraordinary applicability of mathematics to nature was yet to be explained (Chapter XV), but no one could deny the fact itself or dared to throw away such an all-powerful tool. Certainly this power should not be imperiled by countenancing mazes of logical difficulties and contradictions. Moreover, although mathematicians had violated their own principles in disregarding logical soundness, they were not going to let their subject rest forever on a pragmatic basis. Their prestige was at stake. How could they otherwise distinguish their noble-minded activity from that of earth-grubbing engineers and artisans?

于是，一些数学家着手重新走过那些沿模糊小径匆忙推进的路线，为已经达到的目标开辟可靠、清晰的道路。他们决定把很大一部分精力，投入数学基础的建设，以及某些领域基础的重建。

And so some mathematicians undertook to retravel the hasty progress through barely distinct trails and to hew sound, clear-cut paths to the objectives they had already attained. They decided to devote much of their energies to construction and in some areas reconstruction of the foundations of mathematics.

整顿数学大厦，需要强有力的措施。显然，没有坚实大地可以作为数学的根据，因为看似坚固的真理之地已被证明靠不住。但或许可以通过建立另一种坚实基础，使结构稳定。这个基础包括完整、措辞明确的公理和定义，以及对所有结果的明确证明，不论它们在直觉上显得多么明显。此外，取代对真理依赖的，将是逻辑相容性或一致性。公理和定理将彼此紧密依存，使整个结构牢固。无论它与大地的关系怎样，它都会保持为一体，正如摩天大楼随风摆动，却从底到顶保持坚固。

To put the house of mathematics in order called for strong measures. It was clear that there was no solid earth on which to base mathematics, for the seemingly firm ground of truth had proved to be deceptive. But perhaps the structure could be made stable by constructing a solid foundation of another kind. This would consist of complete, sharply worded axioms and definitions, and explicit proof of all results no matter how obvious they might seem to the intuition. Moreover, in place of reliance upon truth there was to be logical com patibility or consistency. The axioms and theorems were to be so completely dependent upon each other that the entire structure would be solid. No matter how it rested in relation to the earth it would hold together much as a skyscraper sways with the wind but remains firm from base to tip.

数学家首先建立微积分的逻辑。微积分预先依赖实数系和代数，而两者都没有逻辑基础；因此，从纯逻辑观点看，这一步的不合理，可以用一个比喻说明。一座五十层办公楼挤满租户、家具和其他设备，业主突然意识到整个结构摇摇欲坠，必须重建。他决定从第二十层开始重建。

The mathematicians began by building the logic of the calculus. Since the calculus presupposes the real number system and algebra, neither of which had a logical foundation, the irrationality from a purely logical standpoint of this step may be seen by an analogy. A fifty-story office building becomes crowded with tenants, furniture, and other equipment and the owner suddenly realizes that the entire structure is shaky and must be rebuilt. He decides to do so by starting at the twentieth floor.

这个起点的选择有其原因。我们已指出，到1800年，各种数已如此熟悉，以致尽管没有逻辑基础，人们也不太担心其性质的可靠性。欧几里得几何的神圣性也受到质疑，但在应用上同样未遇困难。事实上，两千年的可靠使用，为逻辑未能证明的东西提供了信心。另一方面，微积分是分析的源泉，在这一庞大领域，已出现不严密的证明、悖论乃至矛盾，而且并非所有结果都得到实用上的认可。

There is an explanation for the choice of starting point. We have already noted that by 1800 the various types of numbers had become so familiar that even though they had no logical basis there was not too much concern about the soundness of their properties. The sanctity of Euclidean geometry had also been questioned, but here, too, no difficulties in application had been encountered. In fact, two thousand years of reliable usage lent assurance to what logic had failed to demonstrate. The calculus, on the other hand, was the fount of analysis and in this huge area, loose proofs, paradoxes, and even contradictions had appeared and not all results had pragmatic sanction.

十九世纪初，三个人——神父、哲学家兼数学家伯恩哈德·波尔查诺（1781—1848）、尼尔斯·亨里克·阿贝尔和奥古斯丁-路易·柯西（1789—1857）——决定必须解决微积分严谨化的问题。不幸的是，波尔查诺在布拉格工作，他的著作几十年都不为人知。阿贝尔二十七岁便去世，因此未能把这项事业推进很远。柯西在当时数学世界的中心工作，到1820年已被公认为伟大数学家之一。因此，柯西在发起数学严谨化运动中所起的作用，获得最多承认，产生最大影响。

Early in the nineteenth century three men, the priest, philosopher, and mathematician Bernhard Bolzano (1781-1848), Niels Henrick Abel, and Augustin-Louis Cauchy (1789—1857), decided that the problem of rigorizing the calculus must be tackled. Unfortunately, Bolzano worked in Prague and his writings did not become known for many decades. Abel died at the age of twenty-seven and so did not get far into the enterprise. Cauchy worked at the center of the mathematical world of his time and by 1820 was recognized as one of the great mathematicians. Hence it was Cauchy s role in starting the movement to rigorize mathematics that received most recognition and exerted the most influence.

柯西决定把微积分的逻辑建立在数之上。为什么以数为基础？追随牛顿的英国人曾试图用几何使微积分严谨化，却失败了。柯西清楚，几何不是适当基础。而且，追随莱布尼茨的欧洲大陆数学家，一直使用分析方法。此外，虽然到1820年，非欧几里得几何研究尚未广为人知，也许已知部分已足以使数学家对几何产生戒心。另一方面，在数的领域，直到哈密顿1843年创造四元数，才有某种创造使数学家不安；即使四元数，也没有挑战实数系的正确性。

Cauchy decided to build the logic of the calculus on number. Why build on number? The English, following Newton, had attempted to rigorize the calculus by using geometry and they failed. It was evident to Cauchy that geometry was not the proper base. Moreover, the Continentals, following Leibniz, had been using analytic methods. Also, though the work on non-Euclidean geometry had by 1820 not become widely known, perhaps enough was known to make mathematicians leery of geometry. On the other hand, in the realm of number no creation disturbed mathematicians until Hamilton produced quaternions in 1843, and even this did not challenge the correctness of the real number system.

柯西还明智地决定，把微积分建立在极限概念之上。正如数学中反复发生的那样，几位敏锐的头脑早已推荐这一正确方法。十七世纪的约翰·沃利斯在《无穷小算术》（1655）中、苏格兰教授詹姆斯·格雷戈里（1638—1675）在《圆和双曲线的真正求积》（1667）中，以及十八世纪的达朗贝尔，都十分确信极限概念才是恰当的。达朗贝尔的观点最有意义，因为他写作时，牛顿、莱布尼茨和欧拉的工作都已可见。在《百科全书》（1751—65）的“极限”条目中，达朗贝尔明确说：

Cauchy wisely also decided to found the calculus on the limit concept. As happens repeatedly in mathematics, this correct approach had already been recommended by several keen minds. John Wallis in his Arithmetic of Infinitesimals (1655) and the Scottish professor James Gregory (1638-1675) in his True Quadrature of the Circle and Hyperbola (1667) in the seventeenth century, and d’Alembert in the eighteenth were very certain that the limit concept was the proper one. D’Alembert’s views are most significant because, by the time he wrote, Newton s, Leibniz’s, and Euler’s works were at hand. In his article “Limit” in the Encyclopedic (1751-65), d’Alembert was explicit:

当第二个量能够接近第一个量，接近程度超过任何给定的、可设想为任意小的量，而趋近的量又永不能超过它所趋近的量时，我们说，第一个量是第二个量的极限……。

One says that a quantity is the limit of another quantity, when the second can approach the first more closely than any given quantity as small as one can suppose, though the quantity which approaches can never surpass the quantity it approaches. . . .

极限理论是微分学真正形而上学的基础……。

The theory of limits is the base of the true metaphysics of the differential calculus. . . .

达朗贝尔还为《百科全书》撰写“微分”条目，讨论巴罗、牛顿、莱布尼茨、罗尔等人的工作。他说，微分（无穷小量）是无穷小或小于任何可指定的量的量。但他解释，使用这些词只是为了符合当时习惯。他说，这种术语简略而模糊，比想定义的东西还模糊一百倍。极限才是正确语言和方法。他批评牛顿用速度解释导数，因为瞬时速度没有清晰概念，而且引入了非数学观念——运动。在《杂集》（1767）中，达朗贝尔再次说：“一个量要么是某物，要么是零；如果是某物，就尚未消失；如果是零，就已完全消失。”他再次建议采用极限概念。然而，他没有具体实现这一概念在微积分本身中的应用，而同时代人也未能赏识他的建议。

D’Alembert also wrote the Encyclopedic article entitled “Differential” in which he discussed the work of Barrow, Newton, Leibniz, Rolle, and others, and he said a differential (infinitesimal) is a quantity infinitely small or less than any assignable quantity. But he explained that he used such words to conform to current usage. This terminology, he said, was abbreviated and obscure, one hundred times more obscure than that which one wished to define. Limits were the correct language and approach. He criticized Newton’s use of velocity to explain the derivative because there was no clear idea of velocity at an instant and it introduces a non-mathematical idea—motion. In his Melanges (1767), d’Alembert repeated that “A quantity is either something or nothing; if it is something it has not vanished; if it is nothing it has vanished completely.” He again suggested the limit concept. However, he did not work out the application of the concept to the calculus proper and his contemporaries failed to appreciate d’Alembert’s suggestion.

极限的思想也见于卡诺的《论无穷小分析的形而上学》、吕利耶1786年赢得柏林科学院竞赛的获奖论文，以及卡诺那篇虽未获奖却至少值得尊重的论文。柯西很可能受到这些著作影响。无论如何，在如今著名的《代数分析教程》（Cours d’analyse algébrique，1821）引言中，他明确说：“关于方法，我力求赋予它们数学所能要求的全部严谨性。”

Ideas on limits are also to be found in Carnot’s Reflections, in L’Huillier’s prize paper of 1786 which won the competition of the Berlin Academy, and in Carnot’s paper which, though it did not win the prize, was at least respectable. It is very likely that Cauchy was influenced by these writings. In any case in the Introduction to his now famous work, Corns d’analyse algebrique (Course on Algebraic Analysis, 1821), Cauchy was very explicit that, “As to methods I have sought to give them all the rigor that one can demand in mathematics.”

尽管书名含有“代数”一词，柯西反对当时依赖“代数的一般性”的做法。他指的是，同时代人假定：对实数为真的东西，对复数也为真；对收敛级数为真的东西，对发散级数也为真；对有限量为真的东西，对无穷小量也为真。因此，他仔细定义并确立了微积分基本概念——函数、极限、连续性、导数和积分——的性质。他也区分了在其规定意义上有和的无穷级数与没有和的无穷级数，即收敛级数与发散级数。他禁止使用后者。*1826年10月，阿贝尔可以写信告诉以前的老师霍尔姆博，柯西目前是唯一知道数学应当如何处理的人。阿贝尔也补充说，柯西是傻瓜和顽固的偏执者，但显然他认为，即使魔鬼也应得到应有的承认。

Despite the word “algebraic” in the title of his text, Cauchy objected to the current reliance upon the “generality of algebra.” What he meant was that his contemporaries assumed what was true for real numbers was true for complex numbers, what was true for convergent series was true for divergent ones, and what was true for finite quantities was also true for infinitesimals. He therefore defined carefully and established the properties of the basic notions of the calculus—function, limit, continuity, the derivative, and the integral. He also distinguished between infinite series which have a sum in the sense he specified and those which do not, that is, between convergent and divergent series. The latter he outlawed/' In October 1826, Abel could write to his former teacher Holmboe that Cauchy is at present the only one who knows how mathematics should be treated. Abel did add that Cauchy was a fool and a bigot but apparently he thought the devil should be given his due.

虽然柯西着手使分析严谨化，并在《教程》1829年修订版中宣称已把极致的严谨引入分析，但他处理的概念很微妙，因而犯了许多错误。他对函数、极限、连续性和导数的定义基本正确，所用语言却仍模糊而不精确。像同时代人一样，他相信连续性蕴含可微性（第七章），因此提出许多定理，在这些定理中，假设只要求连续性，证明中却使用可微性；即使有人提醒他的错误，他仍坚持。柯西仔细定义定积分，然后试图证明每个连续函数的定积分都有确定值。然而，他的证明是错的（因为没有认识到一致连续性的必要性）。虽然清楚区分了收敛级数和发散级数，他却继续对收敛级数作出错误的断言和证明。例如，他断言连续函数的无穷级数之和是连续的（若不要求一致收敛，这就是错误的）。他逐项积分无穷级数，并主张积分所得的级数表示原级数所代表函数的积分。在这里，他同样未认识到一致收敛的必要性。他给出了数列收敛的判据，今天仍称为柯西条件，却未能证明这个条件的充分性，因为证明需要实数系的知识，而柯西及同时代人都不具备。柯西相信，如果二元函数在每个变量分别趋近某点时具有极限，那么两个变量同时变化并趋近该点时，函数也必趋近一个极限。

Though Cauchy undertook to rigorize analysis and stated in the 1829 revision of his Cours that he had brought the ultimate in rigor into analysis, the concepts he tackled are subtle and he made many mistakes. His definitions of function, limit, continuity, and derivative were essentially correct but the language he used was nevertheless vague and imprecise. Like his contemporaries, he believed that continuity implied differentiability (Chapter VII) and so he stated many theorems in which the hypotheses called only for continuity, but where he used differentiability, and even after his attention was called to his mistake, he persisted. Cauchy defined the definite integral carefully and then proceeded to show that it has a precise value for every continuous function. His proof, however, was erroneous (because he did not recognize the need for uniform continuity). Though he distinguished clearly between convergent and divergent series, he proceeded to make assertions and proofs about convergent series that were false. For example, he asserted that the sum of an infinite series of continuous functions is continuous (which without the requirement of uniform convergence is false). He integrated an infinite series term-by-term and maintained that the integrated series represented the integral of the function represented by the original series. Here, too, he failed to recognize the need for uniform convergence. He gave a criterion for the convergence of a sequence, still known as the Cauchy condition, but failed to prove the sufficiency of this condition because the proof requires a knowledge of the real number system which neither Cauchy nor his contemporaries possessed. Cauchy believed that if a function of two variables possesses a limit at some point when each variable separately approaches that point, the function must approach a limit when both variables vary simultaneously and approach the point.

*我们不必追究柯西提出的技术性定义和定理。就我们的目的而言，重要的是：恰当的严谨化终于由柯西着手进行了。

"We need not pursue the technical definitions and theorems Cauchy advanced. For our purposes the fact that the proper rigorization was finally undertaken by Cauchy is the significant one.

从一开始，分析严谨化的工作就引起巨大震动。柯西在巴黎科学院的一次科学会议上报告了自己的级数收敛理论以后，拉普拉斯急忙回家，闭门不出，直到检查完《天体力学》中的级数。幸运的是，他发现每一个都收敛。

From the outset the work on the rigorization of analysis caused a considerable stir. After a scientific meeting of the Paris Academy of Sciences at which Cauchy presented his theory on the convergence of series, Laplace hastened home and remained in seclusion until he had examined the series in his Celestial Mechanics. Luckily he found every one to be convergent.

矛盾的是，柯西不愿被自己对严谨的关切束缚。虽然他写了三部主要旨在确立严谨性的教科书（1821、1823和1829），却继续在研究论文中忽略它。他定义了连续性的含义，却从未证明自己使用的任何函数连续。虽然强调级数和反常积分收敛性的重要性，却仿佛不存在收敛问题那样，运用级数、傅里叶变换和反常积分。他把导数定义为极限，却也提出像拉格朗日那样的纯形式方法（第六章）。他容许1 − 1 + 1 − 1 + ……之类半收敛（振荡）级数，也容许所谓条件收敛级数（某些含正负项的级数）的项重排。他还犯过其他“罪行”，但对什么是真的有可靠感觉，即使没有按照自己教科书的标准确立真理。

Paradoxically, Cauchy refused to be shackled by his own concern for rigor. Though he wrote three texts (1821, 1823, and 1829) which were aimed primarily at the establishment of rigor, he continued to write research papers in which he ignored it. He defined what continuity means but he never proved that any function he used was continuous. Though he had stressed the importance of convergence of series and improper integrals, he operated with series, Fourier transforms, and improper integrals as though there were no problems of convergence. He had defined the derivative as a limit but he also gave a purely formal approach such as Lagrange had given (Chapter VI). He admitted semi-convergent (oscillating) series such as 1 − 1 + 1 − 1 + ⋯ and rearrangements of the terms in what are called conditionally convergent series (some series with positive and negative terms). He committed other “crimes” but he had a sure feeling for what was true even though he did not establish the truth by the standards of his own texts.

柯西的工作激发了对分析严谨化的许多贡献。不过，主要功劳属于另一位大师卡尔·魏尔斯特拉斯（1815—1897）。通过他的工作，分析基本内容的严谨化完成了。他开始在1858—59年柏林大学的讲课中介绍基础理论。最早的记录，是 H. A. 施瓦茨1861年春所作的笔记。魏尔斯特拉斯的工作，终于使分析摆脱对运动、直观理解和几何观念的一切依赖；这些依赖在他的时代当然已受到怀疑。

Numerous contributions to the rigorization of analysis were inspired by Cauchy s work. But the chief credit belongs to another master, Karl Weierstrass (1815-1897). With his work the rigorization of the fundamentals of analysis was completed. He began to present his foundations in his lectures of 1858-59 at the University of Berlin. The earliest record is the notes taken by H. A. Schwarz in the spring of 1861. Weierstrass’s work finally freed analysis from all dependence upon motion, intuitive understanding, and geometric notions which were certainly suspect by Weierstrass’s time.

到1861年，魏尔斯特拉斯已清楚，连续性不蕴含可微性。鉴于人们长期深信相反观点（第七章），当他于1872年向柏林科学院提出一个处处连续却处处无导数的实函数例子时，整个数学世界都震惊了。保罗·杜布瓦-雷蒙于1875年代他发表了这个例子。（更早的例子有波尔查诺1830年以几何形式给出的、却未发表的例子，以及夏尔·塞勒里耶约1830年给出的、直到1890年才发表的例子。因此，两者都未产生影响。）

Weierstrass was clear by 1861 that continuity does not imply differentiability. In view of the long held conviction to the contrary (Chapter VII), the world was shocked when Weierstrass presented to the Berlin Academy in 1872 (published for him by Paul du Bois-Reymond in 1875) an example of a function which is continuous for all real values of x but has no derivative at any value x. (There were earlier examples by Bolzano in 1830 in geometric form but not published, and by Charles Cellerier about 1830 but not published until 1890. Hence neither of these exerted any influence.)

从某方面看，魏尔斯特拉斯的例子在微积分发展较晚时才出现，倒是幸运的。因为正如埃米尔·皮卡1905年所说：“如果牛顿和莱布尼茨知道连续函数未必有导数，微分学就永远不会被创造出来。”严谨思考可能成为创造的障碍。

In one respect it was fortunate that Weierstrass’s example came late in the development of the calculus, for, as Emile Picard said in 1905, “If Newton and Leibniz had known that continuous functions need not necessarily have a derivative, the differential calculus would never have been created. ’ Rigorous thinking can be an obstacle to creativity.

柯西，甚至魏尔斯特拉斯在分析严谨化工作的开端，也都把实数系和复数系的一切性质视为当然。为实数和复数提供逻辑基础的第一步，是由四元数的创立者哈密顿在1837年迈出的。哈密顿知道复数可以表示同一平面中的向量，并寻求（第四章）能表示空间向量的三单位数。因此，他研究复数性质，以求推广。其工作的一项成果，载于《代数数偶；附时间初论》，是复数的逻辑基础，但仍假定实数具有熟悉的性质。哈密顿引入实数的有序对(a, b)，代替复数 a + b−1，并定义这些数偶的运算，使所得结果与运算 a + b−1 形式的复数相同。值得注意的是，哈密顿之所以寻求复数新理论，是因为像所有前人一样，他无法接受 −1，甚至无法接受负数。

Cauchy and even Weierstrass at the outset of his work on the rigorization of analysis took for granted all the properties of the real and complex number systems. The first step in supplying the logical basis for real and complex numbers was made in 1837 by Hamilton, the inventor of quaternions. Hamilton knew that complex numbers could be used to represent vectors in one plane, and he sought (Chapter IV) three-unit numbers which could represent vectors in space. He therefore studied the properties of complex numbers with a view to generalizing them. One product of his work, contained in his paper “Algebraic Couples; with a Preliminary Essay on Time,” was a logical basis for complex numbers which, however, assumed that the real numbers possessed the familiar properties. In place of complex numbers (a + b −1), Hamilton introduced ordered couples {a,b) of real numbers and he defined the operations with these couples so that one obtained the same results as when operating with the complex numbers in the form a + b −1. It is noteworthy that Hamilton was impelled to seek a new theory of complex numbers because, like all his predecessors, he could not reconcile himself to −1 or even to negative numbers.

在论文稍后的地方，他说：现在发表数偶理论，是为了使［复数的］这一隐藏意义显现出来，并通过这一显著例子表明，那些按通常看法似乎只是符号、完全不能解释的表达式，可以进入思想世界，获得实在性和意义。

Later in the paper he said: The present Theory of Couples is published to make manifest that hidden meaning [of complex numbers], and to show, by this remarkable instance, that expressions which seem according to common views to be merely symbolical, and quite incapable of being interpreted, may pass into the world of thoughts, and acquire reality and significance.

他在这篇论文中进一步说：

He said further in this paper:

在单数理论中，符号 −1 是荒谬的［哈密顿的斜体］，表示不可能的开方，或仅仅是虚数；但在数偶理论中，同一个符号 −1 是有意义的，表示可能的开方，或实在的数偶，即（如刚才所见）数偶(−1, 0)的主平方根。因此，在后一理论中——而非前一理论中——可以恰当地使用 −1 这个符号；若愿意，对于任意数偶(a1, a2)，我们都可以写成

In the Theory of Single Numbers, the symbol −1 is absurd [Hamilton’s italics] and denotes an Impossible Extraction or a merely Imaginary Number; but in the Theory of Couples, the same symbol −1 is significant and denotes a Possible Extraction or a Real Couple, namely, (as we have just now seen) the principal square root of the couples (-1, 0). In the latter theory, therefore, though not in the former, this sign −1 may properly be employed; and we may write, if we choose, for any couple (a1,a2) whatever,

(a1,a2)=a1+a2−1

(a1,a2)=a1+a2−1

并把这个表达式中的 −1，解释为第二单位，即纯第二数偶(0, 1)。

and interpreting the symbol −1 in the same expression, as denoting the secondary unit or pure secondary couple (0,1).

这样，哈密顿消除了复数系中他所谓的“形而上学绊脚石”。

Thus, Hamilton removed what he called the ‘ metaphysical stumbling-blocks” in the complex number system.

哈密顿的数偶理论预先依赖实数性质。他在1837年的文章中确实试图对实数系作逻辑发展。从时间概念，他导出正整数性质，再把这种发展扩展到有理数（正负整数和分数）及无理数。但其发展在逻辑上很差，尤其在处理无理数时失败。这项工作不仅不清楚，而且错误，被数学界忽视。哈密顿自己对实数和复数基础的关切有限。他的目标是四元数。因此，像当时大多数人一样，他在分析工作中毫不犹豫地自由使用实数和复数的性质。

Hamilton presupposed in his theory of couples the properties of the real numbers. He did try in his essay of 1837 to give a logical development of the real number system. From the concept of time, he derived properties of the positive whole numbers and then extended this development to rational numbers (positive and negative whole numbers and fractions) and irrational numbers. But the development was logically poor and foundered especially in the treatment of irrational numbers. This work was not only unclear but incorrect. It was ignored by the mathematical community. Hamilton’s own concern for the foundations of the real and complex numbers was limited. His objective was quaternions. Hence, like most men of his time when he worked in analysis he did not hesitate to use freely the properties of real and complex numbers.

魏尔斯特拉斯最先认识到，不更好地理解实数系，就无法完成分析的严谨化；他也最先以有理数的熟悉性质为基础，给出无理数的严谨定义并推导其性质。他在十九世纪四十年代进行过部分工作，但当时没有发表。这些工作通过十九世纪六十年代在柏林大学的讲课为人所知。

Weierstrass was the first to realize that the rigorization of analysis could not be completed without a better understanding of the real number system, and he was the first to offer a rigorous definition and derivation of the properties of irrational numbers on the basis of the familiar properties of the rationals. He undertook some of this work in the 1840s but did not publish it at that time. It became known through his lectures delivered at the University of Berlin in the 1860s.

其他几个人，尤其是理查德·戴德金和格奥尔格·康托尔，也把有理数性质视为当然，正确地定义无理数并确立其性质。他们的工作发表于十九世纪七十年代。戴德金与魏尔斯特拉斯很相似，是在教微积分时认识到需要清晰的无理数理论。他在《连续性与无理数》（1872）中写道，从1858年起，“他比以往任何时候都更加深切地感到，算术缺乏严谨基础”。康托尔在研究分析定理时认识到无理数理论的必要性（第九章）。因此，通过魏尔斯特拉斯、戴德金和康托尔的工作，数学终于能够证明 2 · 3 = 6。

Several other men, notably Richard Dedekind and Georg Cantor, also taking for granted the properties of the rational numbers, correctly defined the irrational numbers and established their properties. Their work was published in the 1870s. Dedekind, much like Weierstrass, realized the need for a clear theory of irrationals while teaching the calculus. He wrote, in Continuity and Irrational Numbers (1872), that from 1858 on, “He felt more keenly than ever the lack of a rigorous foundation for arithmetic.” Cantor recognized the need for a theory of irrational numbers in his work on theorems of analysis (Chapter IX). Thus, through the work of Weierstrass, Dedekind, and Cantor mathematics could finally prove that 2 3 = 6.

有理数的逻辑仍然缺失。戴德金意识到这一点，在《数的本质与意义》（1888）中，描述了可用于对有理数作公理化处理的基本性质。朱塞佩·皮亚诺（1858—1932）利用戴德金的思想及赫尔曼·格拉斯曼《算术教科书》（1861）中的一些思想，在《算术原理》（1889）中，成功地从关于正整数的公理出发发展有理数。这样，实数系和复数系的逻辑结构终于具备了。

The logic of the rational numbers was still missing. Dedekind realized this and, in The Nature and Meaning of Numbers (1888), he described the basic properties that one might use for an axiomatic approach to the rationals. Giuseppe Peano (1858-1932), utilizing Dedekind’s ideas and some ideas in Hermann Grassmann’s Textbook on Arithmetic (1861) succeeded in Principles of Arithmetic (1889) in producing a development of the rational numbers from axioms about the positive whole numbers. Thus, finally, the logical structure of the real and complex number systems was at hand.

作为副产品，数系基础的建立也解决了熟悉的代数的基础问题。为什么像字母代表正整数那样自由运算，用任何实数或复数代入字母时，结果仍同样适用？答案是，其他类型的数具有与正整数相同的形式性质。粗略地说，不仅2 · 3 = 3 · 2，而且 2 · 3 = 3 · 2；所以，把 ab 换成 ba，不论 a 和 b 代表正整数还是无理数，都正确。

As a by-product, the erection of the foundations of the number system also resolved the problem of the foundations of the familiar algebra. Why is it that, when letters are manipulated freely as though they stood for positive integers, the results apply equally well when any kind of real or complex numbers are substituted for the letters? The answer is that the other types of numbers possess the same formal properties as the positive integers. To put the matter somewhat loosely, not only is it true that 2 • 3 = 3 • 2 but also 23 = 32, so that if ab is replaced by ba, the replacement is correct whether a and b stand for positive integers or irrational numbers.

事件的顺序值得注意。数学家不是从整数和分数开始，再处理无理数、复数、代数和微积分，而是按相反顺序处理这些学科。他们仿佛不愿碰那些看来已清楚理解、完全可以放着不管的东西；只有使某学科逻辑化的需要迫在眉睫，才着手去做。无论如何，到约1890年，也就是埃及人和巴比伦人开始使用整数、分数和无理数仅仅六千年之后，数学家终于能证明2 + 2 = 4。看来，即使伟大的数学家，也必须被迫才考虑严谨。

The sequence of events is noteworthy. Instead of starting with the whole numbers and fractions, then taking up the irrational numbers, the complex numbers, algebra, and the calculus, the mathematicians tackled these subjects in reverse order. They acted as though they were reluctant to tackle what could well be left alone as clearly understood and only when the need to logicize a subject was imperative did they undertake to do so. At any rate by about 1890, only six thousand years after the Egyptians and Babylonians began to work with whole numbers, fractions, and irrational numbers, the mathematicians could finally prove that 2 + 2 = 4. It would appear that even the great mathematicians must be forced to consider rigor.

十九世纪后期，另一个突出问题得到解决。大约六十年间，从高斯表示确信自己的非欧几里得几何一致之时——大概因为他确信它可以是物理世界的几何——到约1870年高斯关于该学科的工作和黎曼取得编外讲师资格的演讲发表之时，大多数数学家都未认真对待非欧几里得几何（第四章）。其含义太激烈，令人难以面对。这些数学家宁愿相信并希望，总有一天，各种非欧几里得几何中会发现矛盾，从而可以把这些创造斥为无稽之谈。

During the latter part of the nineteenth century, another outstanding problem was resolved. For roughly sixty years, from the time that Gauss expressed confidence that his non-Euclidean geometry was consistent, probably because he was certain it can be the geometry of the physical world, to about 1870 when Gauss’s work on the subject and Riemann’s qualifying lecture for privatdozent were published, most mathematicians had not taken non-Euclidean geometry seriously (Chapter IV). Its implications were too drastic to be faced. These mathematicians preferred to believe and hope that some day contradictions would be discovered in each of the several non-Euclidean geometries so that these creations could be dismissed as nonsense.

幸运的是，所有初等非欧几里得几何的一致性问题终于得到回答。方法值得考察，尤其联系后来发生的事情来看。黎曼1854年论文（第四章）所启示的双椭圆几何，是几种非欧几里得几何之一，在根本方面不同于欧几里得几何。没有平行线；任何两条直线相交于两点；三角形内角和大于180°；还有许多定理不同于欧几里得几何。欧金尼奥·贝尔特拉米（1835—1900）在1868年指出，如果把双椭圆几何中的直线解释为球面上的大圆（圆心就是球心的圆，例如经线圈），这种平面双椭圆几何就适用于球面。

Fortunately, the question of the consistency of all the elementary non-Euclidean geometries was finally answered. The method warrants examination, especially in the light of what happened later. One of the several non-Euclidean geometries, the double elliptic geometry suggested by Riemann’s 1854 paper (Chapter IV), differs from Euclidean geometry in essential respects. There are no parallel lines; any two lines meet in two points; the sum of the angles of a triangle is greater than 180°; and many other theorems differ from those in Euclidean geometry. Eugenio Beltrami (1835-1900) pointed out in 1868 that this double elliptic geometry of the plane applies to the surface of a sphere, provided that the lines in the double elliptic geometry are interpreted as great circles on the sphere (circles whose center is the center of the sphere such as circles of longitude).

这种解释似乎不被允许。所有非欧几里得几何的创始者，都打算让其中的直线与欧几里得几何中的直线相同。然而，我们可以回想（第五章），欧几里得对直线及其他概念的定义是多余的。正如亚里士多德强调的，任何数学分支中必有未定义的术语；对这些直线所能要求的，只是满足公理。而球面上的大圆确实满足双椭圆几何的公理。只要双椭圆几何的公理适用于球面大圆，它的定理也必适用，因为定理是逻辑推论。

This interpretation may not seem allowable. The creators of all the non-Euclidean geometries meant their straight lines to be the same as the lines of Euclidean geometry. However, we may recall (Chapter V) that Euclid’s definitions of line and other concepts were superfluous. There must be undefined terms in any branch of mathematics, as Aristotle had stressed, and all that one can require of these lines is that they satisfy the axioms. But great circles on a sphere do satisfy the axioms of double elliptic geometry. As long as the axioms of the double elliptic geometry apply to the great circles on the sphere, the theorems of the geometry must also apply, because the theorems are logical consequences.

承认把直线解释为大圆以后，双椭圆几何的一致性便如下确立：如果双椭圆几何中有相互矛盾的定理，那么关于球面几何也会有相互矛盾的定理。而球属于欧几里得几何。因此，如果欧几里得几何一致，那么双椭圆几何也必一致。

Granted the interpretation of line as great circle, the consistency of double elliptic geometry is established as follows. If there should be contradictory theorems in double elliptic geometry, then there would be contradictory theorems about the geometry of the surface of the sphere. Now the sphere is part of Euclidean geometry. Hence, if Euclidean geometry is consistent, then double elliptic geometry must also be so.

双曲几何的一致性（第四章）不能如此简单地论证。不过，正如用球面作为模型确立了双椭圆几何的一致性，使用欧几里得几何中稍复杂的构形，也确立了双曲几何的一致性。我们不必考察它。但应注意，双曲几何一致，还意味着欧几里得平行公理独立于其他欧几里得公理。因为，如果它不独立——即能由其他公理推导——它就会成为双曲几何的定理，因为除平行公理外，双曲几何的其他公理与欧几里得几何相同。但这条欧几里得“定理”会与双曲几何的平行公理矛盾，双曲几何便不一致。因此，历代从其他欧几里得公理推导平行公理的努力，注定失败。

The case for the consistency of hyperbolic geometry (Chapter IV) cannot be made so simply. However, just as the consistency of double elliptic geometry was established by using the spherical surface as a model, so the consistency of hyperbolic geometry was established by using a somewhat more involved configuration of Euclidean geometry. We need not examine it. However, we should note that the fact that hyperbolic geometry is consistent means also that the Euclidean parallel axiom is independent of the other Euclidean axioms. For, if the Euclidean parallel axiom were not independent of the other Euclidean axioms that is, if it were derivable from them—it would be a theorem of hyperbolic geometry since, aside from the parallel axiom, the other axioms of hyperbolic geometry are the same as those of Euclidean geometry. But this Euclidean “theorem” would contradict the parallel axiom of hyperbolic geometry and hyperbolic geometry would then be inconsistent. Thus, the age-long efforts to deduce the Euclidean parallel axiom from the other Euclidean axioms were doomed to failure.

非欧几里得几何本来意在让直线具有通常意义，却竟可适用于完全不同于原意的图形，这一惊人事实有重大后果。如已解释的，任何公理化发展都必有未定义术语，因此完全不同的解释是可能的。这些解释称为模型。因此，我们看到，为表达某种物理意义而创造的数学分支，可能适用于完全不同的物理或数学情形。

The surprising fact that the non-Euclidean geometries, which were intended as geometries in which line had the usual meaning, could apply to figures totally different from the ones intended has weighty consequences. As we have explained, totally different interpretations are possible because undefined terms are necessarily present in any axiomatic development. These interpretations are called models. Thus, what we have seen is that a branch of mathematics created with one physical meaning intended may apply to an entirely different physical or mathematical situation.

非欧几里得几何的一致性，是在假定欧几里得几何一致的基础上确立的。对十九世纪七十、八十年代的数学家而言，欧几里得几何的一致性几乎不容置疑。尽管有高斯、罗巴切夫斯基、鲍耶和黎曼，欧几里得几何仍被接受为物理世界必然的几何，而物理世界的几何中会有任何相互矛盾的性质，是不可想象的。然而，欧几里得几何一致，并没有逻辑证明。

The consistency of the non-Euclidean geometries was established on the assumption that Euclidean geometry is consistent. To the mathematicians of the 1870s and 1880s the consistency of Euclidean geometry was hardly open to question. Despite Gauss, Lobatchevsky, Bolyai, and Riemann, Euclidean geometry was still accepted as the necessary geometry of the physical world and it was inconceivable that there could be any contradictory properties in the geometry of the physical world. However, there was no logical proof that Euclidean geometry was consistent.

许多几乎蔑视非欧几里得几何的数学家，还因另一个理由欢迎这些一致性证明。证明给了非欧几里得几何意义，但仅仅是作为欧几里得几何内部的模型。因此，可以在这个意义上接受它们，却不必把它们接受为可能适用于物理世界、且直线具有通常意义的几何。当然，这与高斯、罗巴切夫斯基和黎曼的观点相反。

To many mathematicians who had almost scorned non-Euclidean geometry, these consistency proofs were welcomed for another reason. The proofs gave meaning to the non-Euclidean geometries but only as models within Euclidean geometry. Hence, one could accept them in this sense but need not as geometries that might apply to the physical world with the usual meaning of straight line. Of course this was contrary to the views of Gauss, Lobatchevsky, and Riemann.

严谨化只剩一个主要问题。欧几里得几何的基础已被发现有缺陷。但与分析的情形不同，几何的性质及其概念都清楚。因此，确定未定义术语、精确化定义、补充缺失公理并完成证明，是比较简单的任务。莫里茨·帕施（1843—1930）、朱塞佩·韦罗内塞（1854—1917）和马里奥·皮耶里（1860—1904）分别独立完成了这项工作。戴维·希尔伯特（1862—1943）承认帕施的贡献，给出了今天最常用的版本。几乎与此同时，兰伯特、高斯、罗巴切夫斯基和鲍耶所创造的非欧几里得几何的基础，以及十九世纪创造的其他几何，尤其是射影几何的基础，也得到建立。

Only one major problem of rigorization remained. The foundations of Euclidean geometry had been found to be defective. However, unlike the situation in analysis, the nature of geometry and its concepts were clear. Hence, it was a relatively simple task to fix on the undefined terms, sharpen the definitions, supply the missing axioms, and complete the proofs. This was done independently by'Moritz Pasch (1843-1930), Giuseppe Veronese (1854-1917), and Mario Pieri (1860-1904). David Hilbert (1862-1943), who acknowledged Pasch’s contributions, gave the version most commonly used today. Almost in the same breath, the foundations of the non-Euclidean geometry created by Lambert, Gauss, Lobatchevsky, and Bolyai and the foundations of other geometries created in the nineteenth century, notably projective geometry, were supplied.

到1900年，算术、代数和分析（以整数公理为基础），以及几何（以点、线和其他几何概念的公理为基础），都已严谨化。许多数学家赞成更进一步，把全部几何建立在数之上，这可以通过解析几何做到。几何本身仍受怀疑。非欧几里得几何的一个教训，即曾被视为严谨典范的欧几里得几何实际上有缺陷，仍使数学家耿耿于怀。不过，到1900年，全部几何归结为数的工作尚未实际完成。尽管如此，当时多数数学家谈论数学的算术化，虽然说分析的算术化才更准确。因此，1900年在巴黎举行的第二届国际数学家大会上，庞加莱断言：“今天，分析中只剩整数，以及有限和无限的整数系统，由相等或不等关系的网络相互联系。正如我们所说，数学已经算术化。”帕斯卡曾说：“Tout ce qui passe la Géométrie nous passe.”*1900年，数学家更愿说：“Tout ce qui passe l’Arithmétique nous passe.”——凡超出算术的，也超出我们的理解。

By 1900, arithmetic, algebra, and analysis (on the basis of axioms for the whole numbers) and geometry (on the basis of axioms about points, lines, and other geometric concepts) had been rigorized. Many mathematicians favored going further and building up all of geometry on the basis of number, which could be done through analytic geometry. Geometry per se was still suspect. One lesson of non-Euclidean geometry, namely, that Euclidean geometry, which had been regarded as the model of rigor, had actually been defective, still rankled in the minds of mathematicians. However, the reduction of all of geometry to number was not actually carried out by 1900. Nevertheless, most mathematicians of that time spoke of the arithmetization of mathematics though it would have been more accurate to speak of the arithmetization of analysis. Thus, at the Second International Congress of Mathematicians, which was held in Paris in 1900, Poincare asserted, “Today there remain in analysis only integers and finite and infinite systems of integers, interrelated by a net of relations of equality or inequality. Mathematics, as we say, has been arithmetized.” Pascal had said, “Tout ce qui passe la Geometrie nous passe.”v In 1900, mathematicians preferred to say, “Tout ce qui passe l’Arithmetique nous passe.”

起初目标有限的运动，随着吸引越来越多的拥护者，往往倾向于纳入、甚至吞没更多超出原计划的问题。数学基础的批判运动也关注了逻辑，即从一个数学步骤推导另一个步骤时所使用的推理原则。

Movements initially limited in their objectives often tend, as they enlist more and more adherents, to embrace and even engulf many more issues than originally planned. The critical movement in the foundations of mathematics fastened also on logic, the principles of reasoning used in deducing one mathematical step from another.

*凡超出几何的，都超出我们的理解。

'AH that transcends geometry transcends our comprehension.

逻辑科学由亚里士多德在《工具论》（Organon，［推理的］工具，约公元前300年）中创立。他明确说，他注意到数学家使用的推理原则，把它们抽象出来，认识到它们适用于一切推理。因此，基本原则之一是排中律：每个有意义的陈述，不是真，就是假。他也许从“每个整数不是奇数就是非奇数”这类数学陈述中抽象出它。总体而言，亚里士多德的逻辑由三段论法则组成。

The science of logic was founded by Aristotle in his Organon (Instrument [of reasoning], c. 300 b.c.). He said explicitly that he noted the principles of reasoning used by the mathematicians, abstracted them, and recognized them to be principles applicable to all reasoning. Thus one of the fundamental principles is the law of excluded middle, which states that every meaningful statement is either true or false. This he may have abstracted from a mathematical statement such as every integer is odd or non-odd. In the main, Aristotle’s logic consisted of the laws of syllogisms.

两千多年来，包括数学家在内的知识界接受了亚里士多德的逻辑。诚然，质疑一切信念和学说的笛卡尔确实问过，我们怎么知道逻辑原则正确。他的回答是，上帝不会欺骗我们。因此在他看来，我们对这些原则正确性的确信获得了依据。

For over two thousand years, the intellectual world, of which mathematicians are a part, accepted Aristotle’s logic. It is true that Descartes, who questioned all beliefs and doctrines, did raise the question of how we know that the principles of logic are correct. His answer was that God would not deceive us. The assurance we possess of the correctness of these principles was thereby justified to him.

笛卡尔和莱布尼茨想把逻辑法则扩展为适用于一切思想领域的普遍推理科学，即普遍的推理演算；他们设想像代数一样使用符号，以使推理法则的应用更精确、更便捷。笛卡尔谈到数学方法时说：“它是比人类传给我们的任何其他工具都更强大的知识工具，因为它是一切其他工具的来源。”

Descartes and Leibniz thought of broadening the laws of logic into a universal science of reasoning that would be applicable to all fields of thought, a universal calculus of reasoning, and they had the idea of using symbolism, such as algebra does, to sharpen and facilitate the use of the laws of reasoning. Descartes said of mathematical method, It is a more powerful instrument of knowledge than any other that has been bequeathed to us by human agency as being the source of all others.

莱布尼茨的普遍逻辑计划比笛卡尔更具体，要求三个主要组成部分。第一是普遍表意语言（characteristica universalis）——一种部分或大体采用符号、适用于一切通过推理获得的真理的普遍科学语言。第二是逻辑推理形式的完全集合——推理演算（calculus ratiocinator），使人能从最初原理作出任何可能的演绎。第三是组合术（ars combinatoria）——一组基本概念，其他一切概念都可由它们定义；这是一套思想字母表，为每个简单观念指定符号，并通过这些符号的组合和运算，表达和处理更复杂的概念。

Leibniz’s plan for a universal logic, somewhat more specific than Descartes’s, called for three main elements. The first was to be a cbarac-teristica universalis—a universal scientific language which could be partly or largely symbolic and apply to all truths derived by reasoning. The second component was to be an exhaustive collection of logical forms of reasoning—a calculus ratiocinator which would permit any possible deductions from initial principles. The third an ars combina-toria—was to be a collection of basic concepts in terms of which all other concepts could be defined, an alphabet of thought which would assign a symbol to every simple idea and permit the expression and treatment of more complicated concepts by combinations and operations with these symbols.

基本原则例如同一律，即 A 是 A，A 不是非 A。从这类原则，可以推导全部理性真理，包括数学真理。此外还有事实真理，但它们的成立有赖于他所谓的充足理由律的支持，即它们不可能是别的样子。莱布尼茨是符号逻辑的创始者，但这方面的工作直到1901年才为人所知。

The fundamental principles would be, for example, the law of identity, namely, that A is A and A is not not-A. From such principles, all the truths of reason, including those of mathematics, would be derivable. There were, in addition, truths of fact but these were contingent on support by what he called the principle of sufficient reason, that they could not be otherwise. Leibniz was the founder of symbolic logic, but his work in this area was not known until 1901.

笛卡尔和莱布尼茨都没有发展出符号化的推理演算，只写下零碎片段。因此，直到十九世纪，亚里士多德逻辑仍占支配地位。1797年，康德在《纯粹理性批判》第二版中说，逻辑是“封闭而完备的学说体系”。直到约1900年，多数数学家仍按照非形式的、用文字表达的亚里士多德原则推理，但也使用亚里士多德从未考虑过的其他原则。他们没有仔细审查自己的逻辑原则，以为自己使用了充分的演绎逻辑。实际使用的却是直观上合理、但不明确属于逻辑的原则。

Neither Descartes nor Leibniz developed a symbolic calculus of reasoning. They wrote only fragments. Thus, until the nineteenth century, Aristotelian logic held sway. In 1797, in the second edition of his Critique of Pure Reason, Kant said logic was “a closed and complete body of doctrine. Though until about 1900 most mathematicians continued to reason in accordance with informal and verbally expressed Aristotelian principles, they also used others never entertained by Aristotle. They did not examine their own logical principles closely and were under the impression that they were using adequate deductive logic. Actually they were using intuitively reasonable but not explicitly logical principles.

大多数数学家集中精力使数学本身严谨化时，少数人研究了正在使用的逻辑。下一项主要发展来自乔治·布尔（1815—1864），他是爱尔兰科克女王学院的数学教授。

While most mathematicians were concentrating on the rigorization of mathematics proper, a few took up the subject of the logic being used. The next major development was due to George Boole (1815-1864), a professor of mathematics at Queens College in Cork, Ireland.

布尔工作的启发，无疑来自皮科克、格雷戈里和德·摩根所拥护的代数观点（第七章）。虽然他们的形式永久性原理，并没有真正证明用代表实数和复数的字母系数进行代数运算的合理性，却也许无意中提出了一种代数新观：符号和运算可以代表任何对象。而哈密顿的四元数工作（1843）确实表明，其他代数是可能的。布尔自己在1844年曾写出一种代数推理的推广，称为算子演算。因此，他注意到，代数不必只处理数，代数法则也不必是实数和复数的法则。他在《逻辑的数学分析》（1847）开头谈及这一点，然后提出逻辑代数。他的杰作是《思维规律的研究》（1854）。布尔的主要思想不像莱布尼茨那么宏大，而更接近莱布尼茨的推理演算：现有推理法则可以用符号形式表达，从而使现有逻辑的应用更精确、更迅速。他在书中说：

The inspiration for Boole’s work was undoubtedly the view of algebra espoused by Peacock, Gregory, and De Morgan (Chapter VII). Though their principle of permanence of form did not really justify the operations of algebra with literal coefficients representing real and complex numbers, they perhaps unintentionally espoused a new view of algebra as symbols and operations that could represent any objects. And Hamilton’s work on quaternions (1843) did indeed show that other algebras were possible. Boole had himself written in 1844 a generalization of algebraic reasoning in what is called the calculus of operators. Hence, he was alerted to the idea that algebra need not treat just number and that the laws of algebra need not be those of real and complex numbers. He referred to this in the beginning of his Mathematical Analysis of Logic (1847) and then proposed an algebra of logic. His masterpiece was An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854). Boole’s main idea, less ambitious than Leibniz’s and more in tune with Leibniz’s calculus ratiocinator, was that the existing laws of reasoning could be expressed in symbolic form and thereby one could sharpen and expedite the application of the existing logic. He said in this book:

本论著的宗旨，是研究心灵借以进行推理的那些运作的基本规律，用演算的符号语言表达它们，并在这个基础上建立逻辑科学，构造其方法。

The design of the following treatise is to investigate the fundamental laws of those operations of the mind by which reasoning is performed, to give expression to them in the symbolic language of a calculus, and upon this foundation to establish the science of logic and construct its method.

布尔还考虑具体应用，例如应用于概率法则。

Boole also had specific applications in mind, for example, to the laws of probability.

符号的优点很多。在论证过程中，人们可能无意间引入非原意的含义，或者使用错误的演绎原则。例如，讨论作为光学现象的 light 时，提到“seeing the light”（豁然开朗）或某物的“light weight”（轻重量），可能造成混淆。但如果用 ℓ 表示物理的光，随后对 ℓ 的一切符号处理就只能指光学现象。此外，一切证明都由符号集合按符号变换规则转成新的集合，这些规则取代以文字表达的逻辑法则。规则以明确且易于应用的方式表达正确原则。

The advantages of symbolism are numerous. One might in the course of an argument unintentionally make the mistake of introducing meanings that are not intended or use incorrect deductive principles. Thus, in a discussion of light as an optical phenomenon, a reference to seeing the light” or the “light weight” of an object might be confusing. But if one uses ℓ for physical light, all further symbolic treatment of ℓ can refer only to the optical phenomenon. Moreover, all proofs consist in transforming collections of symbols into new collections by rules for the transformation of symbols that replace the verbal laws of logic. The rules express the correct principles in a sharp and readily applied manner.

为对布尔的逻辑代数有所了解，我们看几个思想。设符号 x 和 y 表示对象的类，例如狗类和红色动物类。那么 xy 表示同时属于 x 和 y 的对象的类。在狗和红色动物的例子中，xy 就是红色狗的类。对任意 x 和 y，xy = yx 成立。如果 z 表示白色对象，而且 x = y，那么 zx = zy。从 xy 的含义本身，还得出 xx = x。

Just to get some appreciation of Boole’s algebra of logic, let us note a few of his ideas. Suppose the symbols x and y stand for classes of objects, for example, the class of dogs and the class of red animals. Then xy stands for the class of objects that are in both x and y. In the case of dogs and red animals, xy would be the class of red dogs. For any x and y, it is true that xy = yx. If z now stands for white objects and if x = y, then zx = zy. It also follows from the very meaning of xy that xx = x.

符号 x + y 表示在 x 中、在 y 中，或同时在两者中的对象的类。（这是威廉·斯坦利·杰文斯［1835—1882］后来对布尔的修改。）因此，若 x 是男人类，y 是选民类，x + y 就是男人和选民的类（其中包括女选民）。于是，若 z 表示年龄超过35岁的人，就可以论证：

The symbolism x + y means the class of objects in x or in y or in both. (This is a later modification of Boole by William Stanley Jevons (1835-1882)). Thus, if x is the class of men and y the class of voters, x + y is the class of men and voters (which would include women voters). One could then argue that, if z stands for people over age 35,

z(x+y)=zx+zy.

z(x+y)=zx+zy.

如果 x 是一个类，那么1 − x或 −x 就是不在 x 中的所有对象的集合。因此，若1表示所有对象，x 表示狗，1 − x或 −x 就表示不是狗的对象。于是 −(−x) 表示狗的集合。方程

If x is a class, then 1 - x or -x is the set of all objects not in x. Thus if 1 stands for all objects and x represents dogs, 1 — x or —x stands for objects that are not dogs. Then —(—x) means the set of dogs. The equation

x+(1−x)=1

x+(1−x)=1

说的是，一切东西不是狗，就是非狗。这是类的排中律。布尔说明，怎样用这种纯代数运算在各种领域进行推理。

says that everything is either a dog or not a dog. This is the law of excluded middle for classes. Boole showed how to carry out reasoning in various fields by means of such purely algebraic operations.

布尔还引入了所谓命题逻辑，虽然逻辑的这种用法可追溯到斯多葛学派（公元前四世纪）。在这种解释中，p 例如代表“约翰是男人”，断言 p，就是说“约翰是男人”为真。那么1 − p（或 −p）表示“约翰是男人”不真。而 −(−p) 表示“约翰不是男人”不真，即约翰是男人。命题排中律断言任何命题不是真就是假，布尔把它表达为 p + (−p) = 1，其中1代表真。乘积 pq 表示命题 p 和 q 都真，而 p + q 表示 p 或 q 真，或两者都真。

Boole also introduced what is called the logic of propositions, though the beginning of this use of logic can be traced back to the Stoics (fourth century b.c.). In this interpretation, p would stand for, say, “John is a man, and to assert p is to say that “John is a man” is true. Then 1 —p (or -p) means that “John is a man” is not true. Also -(-p) means it is not true that John is not a man, or John is a man. The law of excluded middle for propositions, which affirms that any proposition is either true or false, was expressed by Boole as p + (-p) = 1, where 1 represented truth. The product pq means both propositions p and q are true, whereas p + q means either p or q or both are true.

德·摩根作出另一项创新。在主要著作《形式逻辑》（1847）中，他提出，逻辑必须处理一般关系。亚里士多德的逻辑处理动词“是”的关系，经典例子是“所有人都会死”。德·摩根说，亚里士多德逻辑不能证明从“马是动物”推导“马的头是动物的头”的合理性。还需要加上“一切动物都有头”的前提。亚里士多德确实写过关系逻辑，但很模糊，也不广泛。而且，到十七世纪，亚里士多德许多著作及中世纪学者所作的扩展，都已被忽视。

Another innovation was made by De Morgan. In his chief work, Formal Logic (1847), De Morgan introduced the idea that logic must deal with relations in general. Aristotle’s logic deals with the relation of the verb “to be.” The classic example is “All men are mortal.” As De Morgan put it, Aristotelian logic could not justify deducing from A horse is an animal” that “A horse’s head is an animal’s head.” One needs in addition the premise that all animals have heads. Aristotle did write on the logic of relations although vaguely and not extensively. Moreover, many of Aristotle’s writings and the extensions made by medieval scholars were lost sight of by the seventeenth century.

关系逻辑的必要性很容易看出。例如，仅根据“是”这一关系的论证，即

The need for a logic of relations is readily seen. Thus, an argument based only on the relation “to be,” namely,

A 是一个 p；B 是一个 p；

A is a p;B is a p;

因此 A 和 B 是 p，

Hence A and B are p’s,

很容易看出是错的。因为论证

is readily seen to be false. For the argument

约翰是某人的兄弟；

John is a brother;

彼得是某人的兄弟；因此约翰和彼得是（彼此的）兄弟，

Peter is a brother; Hence John and Peter are brothers (of each other),

显然可能不正确。同样，

can obviously be incorrect. Likewise

苹果是酸的；酸是一种味道；

An apple is sour; Sour is a taste;

因此苹果是一种味道，

Hence an apple is a taste,

也是不正确的结论。未发展关系逻辑，是亚里士多德逻辑的主要缺陷，莱布尼茨也注意到这一点。

is also an incorrect conclusion. The failure to develop a logic of relations is the main defect of Aristotelian logic, a defect which Leibniz also noted.

关系通常不能转换成主词和谓词，而谓词仅表示主词属于谓词指定的类。因此，必须考虑陈述关系的命题，例如2小于3，或者点 Q 在 P 和 R 之间。必须考虑这类命题的否定、逆命题、联合断言及其他联系各指什么。

Relations cannot usually be translated into a subject and predicate in which the predicate merely says that the subject is included in a class specified by the predicate. Hence, one must consider propositions which state relationships such as 2 is less than 3 or the point Q is between P and R. One must consider for such propositions what one means by their denial, converse, joint assertion, and other connections.

查尔斯·桑德斯·皮尔士（1839—1914）在1870至1893年的多篇论文中扩展关系逻辑，恩斯特·施罗德（1841—1902）使之系统化。皮尔士引入特殊符号，表示表达关系的命题。例如 ℓij 表示 i 爱 j。实际上，他的关系代数复杂而不太有用。我们后面将看到现代符号逻辑如何处理关系。

The logic of relations was expanded by Charles Sanders Peirce (1839— 1914) in various papers from 1870 to 1893 and systematized by Ernst Schroder (1841-1902). Peirce introduced special symbolism to denote propositions expressing relationships. Thus ℓij expresses that i loves j. Actually, his algebra of relationships was complicated and not very useful. We shall see later how relations are treated in modern symbolic logic.

逻辑科学的另一补充，布尔曾简要涉及，而皮尔士有效地引入了它。他强调命题函数概念。正如数学处理 y = 2x 之类函数，而不只是10 = 2 · 5之类关于常数的陈述，“约翰是男人”是命题，“x 是男人”却是命题函数，其中 x 是变量。命题函数可含两个或更多变量，例如 x 爱 y。借助皮尔士的贡献，推理可以扩展到命题函数。

Another addition to the science of logic, briefly touched on by Boole, was effectively introduced by Peirce. He emphasized the notion of propositional functions. Just as mathematics deals with functions such as y = 2x as opposed to statements about constants such as 10 = 2 • 5, so John is a man” is a proposition, but “x is a man” is a propositional function wherein x is a variable. Propositional functions can include two or more variables as in x loves y. With Peirce’s contribution reasoning could be extended to propositional functions.

皮尔士还引入了所谓量词。普通语言在量词方面含糊。两个陈述：

Peirce also introduced what are called quantifiers. Ordinary language is ambiguous as to quantifiers. The two statements:

一个美国人领导了独立战争。一个美国人相信民主。

An American led the War of Independence. An American believes in democracy.

在两种意义上使用“一个美国人”。第一句指特定的美国人乔治·华盛顿；第二句指每一个美国人。通常，这种歧义可参照语境消除。但严谨的逻辑思考不能容忍这种歧义。陈述本身必须清楚。解决办法是使用量词。人们可能要断言，某个命题函数对某类中的所有个体都真，例如美国的人。如果断言“对所有 x，x 是男人”，便表示美国的所有人都是男人。“对所有 x”这个短语是量词。另一方面，人们可能要说，美国至少存在一个 x，使 x 是男人。在这种情况下，“至少存在一个 x，使得”是量词。两者分别用符号 ∀x 和 ∃x 表示。

use the term an American in two different senses. The first refers to a particular American, George Washington. The second refers to every American. Usually this ambiguity can be resolved by reference to the context in which the phrase is used. But this ambiguity cannot be tolerated in rigorous logical thinking. The statements must be clear in and for themselves. The resolution is the use of quantifiers. One might wish to assert that a propositional function is true for all individuals of some class, say, the people in the United States. If one then asserts that for all x, x is a man, he means that all people in the United States are men. The phrase “for all x” is a quantifier. On the other hand one might wish to say that there is at least one x such that x is a man in the United States. In this case, “There is at least one x such that” is the quantifier. These two are denoted respectively by the symbols ∀x and ∃x.

把逻辑扩展到关系、命题函数和量词，包含了数学中所用的推理类型，从而使逻辑更加充分。

The extension of logic to relations, to propositional functions, and to quantifiers embraces the types of reasoning used in mathematics and thereby makes logic more adequate.

十九世纪把逻辑数学化的最后一步，来自耶拿数学教授戈特洛布·弗雷格（1848—1925）。弗雷格写了几部主要著作：《概念文字》（1879）、《算术基础》（1884）和《算术基本规律》（第一卷1893；第二卷1903）。他吸收命题逻辑、含关系的命题、命题函数和量词的思想，也作出自己的若干贡献。他区分仅仅陈述命题与断言命题为真，断言以在命题前放置 ⊢ 符号表示。他区分对象 x 与仅包含 x 的集合{x}，也区分对象属于集合与一个集合包含于另一个集合。

The final nineteenth-century step in the direction of mathematizing logic was made by Gottlob Frege (1848-1925), a professor of mathematics at Jena. Frege wrote several major works, Concept-Writing (1879), The Foundations of Arithmetic (1884), and The Fundamental Laws of Arithmetic (vol. I, 1893; vol. II, 1903). He took over the ideas of a logic of propositions, propositions involving relations, propositional functions, and quantifiers. He also made several contributions of his own. He introduced the distinction between the mere statement of a proposition and the assertion that it is true. The assertion is denoted by placing the symbol b in front of the proposition. He distinguished between an object x and the set {x} containing just x and between an object belonging to a set and the inclusion of one set in another.

弗雷格把称为实质蕴涵的更广泛蕴涵概念形式化，虽然其文字表述可追溯到麦加拉的斐洛（约公元前300年）。逻辑处理关于命题和命题函数的推理，在此过程中，蕴涵最重要。例如，知道约翰聪明，且聪明人长寿，就能推导出约翰将长寿这一蕴涵。

Frege formalized a broader concept of implication called material implication, though its expression in verbal form can be traced back to Philo of Megara (c. 300 B.C.). Logic deals with reasoning about propositions and propositional functions and in this process implication is most important. Thus, if we know that John is wise and that wise men live long, we deduce the implication that John will live long.

实质蕴涵与通常使用的蕴涵略有不同。例如，断言“如果下雨，我就去看电影”，两个命题之间不仅有某种关系，还意味着前件“如果下雨”成立时，后件“我去看电影”必然随之而来。但实质蕴涵允许前件 p 和后件 q 是任何命题。两命题不必有因果关系，甚至不必有任何关系。同样可以处理“如果 x 是偶数，我就去看电影”。而且，实质蕴涵允许即使“x 是偶数”为假，后件仍成立。因此，“如果 x 不是偶数，我就去看电影”。它还允许蕴涵“如果 x 不是偶数，我就不去看电影”。只有 x 是偶数而我不去看电影时，这个蕴涵才为假。

Material implication is somewhat different from the one commonly used. When we assert, for example, that “If it rains, I shall go to the movies,” there is not only some relation between the two propositions, but the implication that, if the antecedent “if it rains” holds, the consequent “I shall go to the movies” necessarily follows. However, the notion of material implication allows p and q, the antecedent and the consequent, to be any propositions. There need be no causal relationship or even any relationship of the propositions to each other. One can as well deal with “If x is an even number, I shall go to the movies.” Moreover, material implication allows that even if it is false that x is an even number, then the consequent holds. Thus, “If x is not an even number, I shall go to the movies.” Moreover, it allows the implication “If x is not an even number, I shall not go to the movies.” The implication is false only in the case where x is an even number and I do not go to the movies.

更形式地说，若 p 和 q 是命题，且 p 为真，“p 蕴涵 q”当然表示 q 为真。但实质蕴涵允许即使 p 为假，无论 q 为真或假，仍把“p 蕴涵 q”视为真。只有 p 真而 q 假时，蕴涵才假。这是对通常含义的扩展，却无害，因为我们只在知道 p 为真时使用“p 蕴涵 q”。而且，实质蕴涵也多少符合普通用法。考虑“如果哈罗德今天领到工资，他就会购买食物”。这里 p 是“哈罗德今天领到工资”，q 是“他会购买食物”。即使今天没领工资，他仍可能购买食物。因此，可以把 p 假而 q 真的情况包括为正当蕴涵。结论当然不假。同样，“如果哈罗德今天没领到工资，他就不买食物”，当然也不是假陈述。作为最后一种情况的另一个、也许更好的例子，可以考虑“如果木材是金属，那么木材就有延展性”。我们知道两个陈述都假，但蕴涵却真。因此，也把 p 假、q 假的情况包括为“p 蕴涵 q”的正确情况。这个概念的重要用途，是由 p 为真及 p 蕴涵 q 推出 q。扩展到 p 为假的情况，在符号逻辑中很方便，也是现有的最佳处理。

Put more formally, if p and q are propositions and if p is true, the implication “p implies q” certainly means that q is true. However, material implication allows that even if p is false, then whether or not q is true or false, we still regard the implication p implies q as true. Only in the case where p is true and q is false is the implication false. This notion of implication is an extension of the usual meaning. The extension, however, does no harm because we use “p implies q” only when we know p is true. Moreover, material implication is even somewhat in keeping with ordinary usage. Consider the statement If Harold is paid today, he will purchase food.” Here the p is Harold is paid today, and the q is he will purchase food. Now he may still purchase food even if he is not paid today. Hence, we can include the case where p is false and q is true as a legitimate implication. Certainly the conclusion is not false. Similarly, “If Harold is not paid today, he will not buy food” is certainly not a false statement. As another, perhaps better example of the last case, we might consider “If wood were a metal, then wood would be malleable.” We know that both statements are false, and yet the implication is true. Hence, we include this case of implication, wherein p is false and q is false, as a correct case of p implies q. The important use of the concept is to conclude q from the truth of p and from the implication p implies q. The extension to the cases where p is false is convenient in symbolic logic and the best available.

然而，因为 p 假时，无论 q 真或假都蕴涵 q，实质蕴涵允许假命题蕴涵任何命题。对此缺点，可以反驳说，在正确的逻辑和数学体系中，不应出现假命题。尽管如此，实质蕴涵概念仍受到反对。例如，庞加莱用学生考试中从错误方程出发却得出正确结论的情形来嘲笑它。不过，虽有人努力改进这一概念，实质蕴涵如今仍是标准，至少在作为数学基础的符号逻辑中如此。

However, since the falsity of p implies q whether or not q is true or false, material implication allows a false proposition to imply any proposition. To this failing one could rebut that in a correct system of logic and mathematics, false propositions should not occur. Nevertheless there have been objections to the concept of material implication. Poincare, for example, mocked it by citing the case of students who on examinations start with false equations and then draw true conclusions. However, despite efforts to improve upon the concept, material implication is now standard, at least in the symbolic logic used as a basis for mathematics.

弗雷格还有一项贡献，后来变得极其重要。逻辑包含许多推理原则，它们可以与欧几里得几何关于三角形、矩形、圆及其他图形的众多断言相比。十九世纪末其他数学分支重组之际，几何中的众多断言也从少数基本断言，即公理，推导出来。弗雷格对逻辑所做的正是如此。他的符号和公理复杂，因此我们只用文字说明逻辑公理化发展的方法。（亦见第十章。）人们当然会放心把“p 蕴涵 p 或 q”作为公理，因为“p 或 q”的意义是 p 或 q 至少一个为真。如果起初 p 为真，那么 p 和 q 两者中当然有一个为真。

Frege made one more contribution which assumed great importance later. Logic contains many principles of reasoning. These may be compared to the numerous assertions which Euclidean geometry makes about triangles, rectangles, circles, and other figures. In geometry as a consequence of the late nineteenth-century reorganization of other branches of mathematics, the many assertions are derived from a few fundamental ones, the axioms. Frege did precisely this for logic. His notation and axioms were complicated, and so we shall merely indicate verbally the approach to an axiomatic development of logic. (See also Chapter X.) One would certainly feel secure in adopting as an axiom the assertion “p implies p or q”, for the meaning of p or q is that at least one, p or q, is true. But if we start with p being true, then surely one of the two, p and q, is true.

人们也采用这样一条公理：如果用 A 表示的某命题（或命题组合）为真，而且 A 蕴涵 B，其中 B 是另一个命题（或组合），那么可以单独断言 B。这条称为推理规则的公理，使我们能推导并断言新命题。

One also uses as an axiom that if some proposition (or combination of propositions) denoted by A is true and if A implies B, where B is another proposition (or combination), then we may assert B separately. This axiom, called a rule of inference, enables us to deduce and assert new propositions.

例如，从上述公理可以推导：

From axioms such as the above we can deduce, for example,

p 为真，或 p 为假。

p is true or p is false.

这一推论构成排中律。

This deduction constitutes the law of excluded middle.

也可以推导矛盾律，文字表述是：p 与非 p 同时为真是不真的，所以两种可能只能有一种成立。数学中的所谓间接证明使用矛盾律：若假定 p 真，却推导出它假，就有 p 和非 p。但两者不能同时成立，因此 p 必假。间接方法常采用另一形式：假定 p，并证明它蕴涵 q，但已知 q 假，于是由逻辑法则，p 必假。许多其他常用逻辑法则也可由公理推导。这种逻辑的演绎组织，由弗雷格在《概念文字》中开始，并在《算术基本规律》中继续。

One can also deduce the law of contradiction, which in verbal form states that it is not true that p and not p are both true, and so only one of the two possibilities can hold. The law of contradiction is used in what are called indirect proofs in mathematics. Therein if we suppose p is true and deduce that it is false, then we have p and not p. But both cannot hold. Hence p must be false. The indirect method often takes another form. We assume p and show it implies q. But q is known to be false. Hence, by a law of logic, p must be false. Many other commonly used laws of logic can be deduced from the axioms. This deductive organization of logic was begun by Frege in his Concept-Writing and continued in his Fundamental Laws.

弗雷格还有更加雄心勃勃的目标，我们将在后面一章详谈（第十章）。暂且简要说，他在逻辑工作中寻求为数、代数和分析建立新基础，比十九世纪最后几十年批判运动产生的基础更加严谨。

Frege had a still more ambitious objective about which we shall say more in a later chapter (Chapter X). Briefly put for the moment, he sought in his work on logic to institute a new basis for number, algebra, and analysis, a basis still more rigorous than the critical movement was producing during the last few decades of the nineteenth century.

用符号逻辑改进数学严谨性的另一关键人物，是朱塞佩·皮亚诺。像戴德金一样，他在教学中发现现有严谨性不足，便毕生致力于改进逻辑基础。他不仅把符号逻辑用于逻辑原则，也用于表达数学公理，并用符号逻辑原则操纵符号公理，推导定理。他明确而坚定地认为，必须摒弃直觉；只有使用符号，让意义不能在数学本身中发挥作用，才能做到这一点。符号避免了诉诸普通词语所带直观联想的危险。

Another pivotal figure in the use of symbolic logic to improve the rigor of mathematics was Giuseppe Peano. Like Dedekind, he found in his teaching that the existing rigor was inadequate and he devoted his life to improving the logical foundations. He applied symbolic logic not only to the principles of logic but also to the expression of mathematical axioms and to the deduction of theorems by using symbolic logical principles to manipulate symbolic axioms. He was explicit and firm that we must renounce intuition, and this could be done only by working with symbols so that meaning could not play a role in mathematics proper. Symbols avoid the danger of appealing to the intuitive associations attached to common words.

皮亚诺引入自己的符号，表示概念、量词，以及“且”“或”“非”等联结词。他的符号逻辑相当初步，影响却很大。他编辑的《数学评论》（Rivista di Matematica，1891年创刊，出版至1906年）和五卷本《数学公式汇编》（1894—1908），都是主要贡献。他正是在《公式汇编》中给出了前述整数公理。皮亚诺创立了逻辑学派，而皮尔士和弗雷格的工作大体不受注意，直到罗素1901年发现弗雷格的工作。罗素1900年已了解皮亚诺的工作，而且比起弗雷格的符号，他更喜欢皮亚诺的符号。

Peano introduced his own symbolism for concepts, quantifiers, and connectives such as “and,” “or,” and “not.” His own symbolic logic was rather rudimentary but his influence was great. The journal he edited, Rivista di Matematica (Mathematical Review, founded in 1891 and published until 1906) and the five-volume Formulary of Mathematics (1894- 1908) are major contributions. It was in the Formulary that he gave the axioms for the whole numbers referred to earlier. Peano founded a school of logicians whereas Peirce’s and Frege’s work went largely unnoticed until Bertrand Russell discovered Frege’s work in 1901. Russell had learned about Peano’s work in 1900 and preferred Peano’s symbolism to Frege’s.

从布尔到施罗德、皮尔士和弗雷格，逻辑创新都包括数学方法的应用：使用符号，以及从逻辑公理演绎证明逻辑原则。所有这些形式逻辑或符号逻辑的工作，都吸引逻辑学家和许多数学家，因为符号使用避免了心理学、认识论和形而上学的意义与含义。

From Boole to Schroder, Peirce, and Frege, the innovations in logic consisted of the application of mathematical method: symbolism and deductive proof of logical principles from logical axioms. All of this work on formal logic or symbolic logic appealed to logicians and many mathematicians because the use of symbols avoids psychological, epistemological, and metaphysical meanings and connotations.

包含命题函数、“x 爱 y”或“A 在 B 与 C 之间”之类关系，以及量词的逻辑体系，如今通常称为一阶谓词演算或一阶逻辑。虽然一些逻辑学家认为，它不能涵盖数学中的一切推理，例如数学归纳法，却是现代逻辑学家最青睐的体系。*

The system of logic which includes prepositional functions, relationships such as “* loves y” or “A is between B and C,” and quantifiers is now generally described as the first order predicate calculus or first order logic. Though according to some logicians it does not cover all the reasoning used in mathematics, for example, mathematical induction, it is the system most favored by modern logicians.’'''

逻辑领域扩展到涵盖数学中使用的所有推理类型，命题与命题函数的区分使陈述更精确，以及量词的使用，无疑增强了数学家在十九世纪寻求确立的严谨性。逻辑的公理化，更加符合时代运动。

The extension of the realm of logic to cover all types of reasoning used in mathematics, the greater precision given to statements by the distinction between propositions and propositional functions, and the use of quantifiers certainly added to the rigor mathematicians were seeking to institute in the nineteenth century. The axiomatization of logic was all the more in line with the movement of the times.

鉴于后面将谈到数学的逻辑结构，这里要强调：数学本身与逻辑的严谨化，是使用欧几里得首先采用的公理方法实现的。十九世纪的公理化运动使这一方法的若干特征更加清楚。我们来回顾它们。

In view of what we shall have to say later about the logical structure of mathematics, let us emphasize here that the rigorization of mathematics proper and logic was achieved by using the axiomatic approach first employed by Euclid. Several features of this method became clearer during the nineteenth-century axiomatization movement. Let us review them.

*为涵盖数学中使用的一切推理，有些逻辑学家要求所谓二阶逻辑，这要求把量词用于谓词。因此，要表达 x = y，我们要断言，适用于 x 的所有谓词也适用于 y，必须加入“对所有谓词”来量化谓词，或者用符号写成 x = y ↔ (F)(F(x) ↔ F(y))。

vTo encompass all the reasoning used in mathematics some logicians require what is called second order logic and this calls for applying quantifiers to predicates. Thus, to express that x = y, we wish to assert that all predicates that apply to x apply to y and we must quantify the predicate by including for all predicates” or in symbols x = y ↔ (F)(F(x) ↔ F(y)).

第一是未定义术语的必要性。数学独立于其他学科，因此定义必须用其他数学概念表达。这样会导致定义的无穷倒退。解决办法是让基本概念不定义。那么，如何使用它们？怎样知道能断言关于它们的哪些事实？答案是，公理对未定义（和已定义）概念作出断言，因此告诉我们可以断言什么。例如，点和线若未定义，“两点确定唯一的直线”及“三点确定一个平面”的公理，便提供可用于推导点、线、平面的其他结果的断言。虽然亚里士多德在《工具论》、帕斯卡在《论几何精神》、莱布尼茨在《单子论》中都强调未定义术语的必要性，数学家却奇怪地忽视此事，给出无意义的定义。十九世纪初，约瑟夫-迪亚兹·热尔岗（1771—1859）指出，公理告诉我们可以对未定义术语断言什么，给予它们所谓隐定义。直到莫里茨·帕施1882年重申未定义术语的必要性，数学家才认真看待。

The first concerns the necessity for undefined terms. Since mathematics is independent of other subjects, a definition must be in terms of other mathematical concepts. Such a process would lead to an infinite regress of definitions. The resolution of this difficulty is that the basic concepts must be undefined. How then can they be used? How does one know what facts about them can be asserted? The answer is that the axioms make assertions about the undefined (and defined) concepts and so the axioms tell us what can be asserted. Thus, if point and line are undefined, the axiom that two points determine a unique line and the axiom that three points determine a plane furnish assertions that can be used to deduce further results about point, line, and plane. Though Aristotle in the Organon, Pascal in Treatise on the Geometrical Spirit, and Leibniz in Monadology had emphasized the need for undefined terms, mathematicians peculiarly overlooked this fact and consequently gave definitions that were meaningless. Joseph-Diaz Gergonne (1771-1859) in the early nineteenth century pointed out that the axioms tell us what we may assert about the undefined terms; they give what may be called an implicit definition. It was not until Moritz Pasch reaffirmed the need for undefined terms in 1882 that mathematicians took this matter seriously.

任何演绎体系都必有未定义术语，而它们可被解释为满足公理的任何事物；这一事实把新的抽象层次引入数学。赫尔曼·格拉斯曼在《线性扩张论》（1844）中较早认识到这一点，指出必须区分几何与物理空间研究。几何是纯数学结构，可以适用于物理空间，却不限于这一解释。后来研究公理化的帕施、皮亚诺和希尔伯特，都强调抽象性。帕施虽清楚存在未定义术语，且只有公理限制其意义，却仍想着几何。了解帕施工作的皮亚诺，在1889年的文章中更明确指出，可能还有许多其他解释。希尔伯特在《几何基础》（1899）中说，虽然使用点、线、平面等术语，它们也可以是啤酒杯、椅子或任何其他对象，只须服从所涉及的公理。演绎体系可有多种解释，的确可能有益，因为能允许更多应用；但我们将发现（第十二章），它也有令人不安的后果。

The fact that any deductive system must contain undefined terms that can be interpreted to be anything that satisfies the axioms, introduced into mathematics a new level of abstraction. This was recognized rather early by Hermann Grassman in his Theory of Linear Extension (1844), who pointed out that geometry must be distinguished from the study of physical space. Geometry is a purely mathematical structure which can apply to physical space but is not limited to that interpretation. The later workers in axiomatics, Pasch, Peano, and Hilbert, emphasized the abstraction. Though Pasch was clear that there are undefined terms and that only the axioms limit their meaning, he did have geometry in mind. Peano, who knew Pasch s work, was clearer in his article of 1889 that many other interpretations may be possible. Hilbert, in the Foundations of Geometry (1899), said that though the terms used were point, line, plane, etc., they could be beer mugs, chairs, or any other objects, provided merely that they obey the axioms involved. The possibility of multiple interpretations of a deductive system may indeed be a boon because it may permit more applications, but we shall find (Chapter XII) that it also has disturbing consequences.

帕施很好地理解现代公理方法。他提出，任何一组公理的一致性，即不会导致相互矛盾的定理，必须确立。十九世纪末人们当然未充分理解这一点的重要性。非欧几里得几何曾提出一致性问题，而问题在那里得到满意解决。但非欧几里得几何是陌生的。对于整数或欧几里得几何等基本分支，任何一致性疑问似乎只是学究问题。尽管如此，帕施认为仍应确立这些公理体系的一致性。弗雷格支持他，在《算术基础》（1884）中写道：

Pasch had a fine understanding of modern axiomatics. He made the point, whose import was certainly not appreciated in the late nineteenth century, that the consistency of any set of axioms, that is, that they do not lead to contradictory theorems, must be established. The question of consistency had arisen with respect to the non-Euclidean geometries and for these the issue was satisfactorily settled. However, non-Euclidean geometry was strange. For the basic branches, such as the whole numbers or Euclidean geometry, any doubts about consistency seemed academic. Nevertheless, Pasch thought that the consistency of these systems of axioms should be established. In this matter he was seconded by Frege, who wrote in Foundations of Arithmetic (1884):

通常的做法，好像仅仅提出一个假设，就等于实现了它。我们假定一切情况下都能进行减法、除法或开方，便以为做得够了。但为什么不假定任何三点都能画一条直线？为什么不假定加法和乘法的一切法则，在三维复数系中像在实数中一样继续成立？因为这个假设含有矛盾。那么，首先必须证明，我们的其他假设不含任何矛盾。在做到这一点以前，无论怎样努力，一切严谨都不过是空话。

It is common to proceed as if a mere postulation were equivalent to its own fulfillment. We postulate that it shall be possible in all cases to carry out the operation of subtraction, or of division, or of root extraction, and suppose that with that we have done enough. But why do we not postulate that through any three points it shall be possible to draw a straight line? Why do we not postulate that all the laws of addition and multiplication shall continue to hold for a three-dimensional complex number system just as they do for real numbers? Because this postulate contains a contradiction. Very well, then, what we have to do first is to prove that these other postulates of ours do not contain any contradiction. Until we have done that, all rigor, strive for it as we will, is so much moonshine.

皮亚诺及其学派在十九世纪九十年代，也开始多少认真看待一致性问题。皮亚诺相信，很容易找到确立它的方法。

Peano and his school also began in the 1890s to take somewhat seriously the question of consistency. Peano believed that ways of establishing it would readily be found.

希腊时代本来就可以质疑数学的一致性。为什么它到十九世纪末才突出？我们已指出，非欧几里得几何的创造迫使人认识到，数学是人为的，只近似描述现实世界中发生的事情。描述异常成功，却不是表达宇宙内在结构意义上的真理，因此未必一致。事实上，十九世纪末的公理化运动，使数学家认识到数学与现实世界之间的鸿沟。每个公理体系都有未定义术语，其性质仅由公理规定。即使直观上想着数、点或线，这些术语的意义也未固定。公理当然应规定性质，使这些术语确实具有我们直观赋予的性质。但能确信我们做到了吗？能确信没有容许不希望的、实际上可能导致矛盾的某种性质或含义进入吗？

The consistency of mathematics might well have been questioned in Greek times. Why did it come to the fore in the late nineteenth century? We have already noted that the creation of non-Euclidean geometry had forced the realization that mathematics is man-made and describes only approximately what happens in the real world. The description is remarkably successful, but it is not truth in the sense of representing the inherent structure of the universe and therefore not necessarily consistent. Indeed, the axiomatic movement of the late nineteenth century made mathematicians realize the gulf that separated mathematics from the real world. Every axiom system contains undefined terms whose properties are specified only by the axioms. The meaning of these terms is not fixed, even though intuitively we have numbers or points or lines in mind. To be sure, the axioms are supposed to fix properties so that these terms do indeed possess the properties that we intuitively associate with them. But can we be sure that we have done so and can we be sure that we have not allowed some property or implication to enter which we do not desire and which in fact may lead to a contradiction?

帕施还指出公理方法的另一个特征。数学任一分支的公理最好独立，即不能从该分支的其他公理推导任何一个公理，否则可推导的公理就是定理。确立公理独立性的方法，是对其他公理给出一种解释或模型，使这些公理满足，而待考察的公理不满足。（这种解释不必与待考察公理的否定相一致。）例如，要确立欧几里得平行公理独立于其他公理，可以使用双曲非欧几里得几何的解释，其中除平行公理外的一切欧几里得公理都满足，而欧几里得平行公理不满足。同时满足待考察公理和与之矛盾公理的解释，不会一致。因此，在用解释或模型证明公理独立以前，必须知道模型一致。所以，正如前述，欧几里得平行公理的独立性，是通过在欧几里得几何内部提供双曲非欧几里得几何模型来确立的。

One more feature of the axiomatic method was also pointed out by Pasch. Preferably the axioms of any one branch of mathematics should be independent, that is, it should not be possible to derive any one of the axioms from the others of that branch, for if this can be done, the derivable axiom is a theorem. The method of establishing the independence of an axiom is to give an interpretation or model of the other axioms wherein these axioms are satisfied but the one in question is not. (The interpretation need not be consistent with the negation of the axiom in question.) Thus, to establish the independence of the parallel axiom of Euclidean geometry from the other axioms of that geometry, one can use the interpretation of hyperbolic non-Euclidean geometry in which all the Euclidean axioms other than the parallel axiom are satisfied but the Euclidean parallel axiom is not. An interpretation that satisfies the axiom in question and also satisfies a contradictory axiom would not be consistent. Hence, before one uses an interpretation or model to prove the independence of an axiom, one must know that the model is consistent. Thus, as we noted earlier, the independence of the Euclidean parallel axiom was established by providing a model of hyperbolic non-Euclidean geometry within Euclidean geometry.

虽然随后历史的大部分将涉及数学公理化提出的疑问、不足和深刻问题，二十世纪初，公理方法却被赞为理想。赞扬最甚的，是当时世界领先的数学家希尔伯特。他在《公理化思维》（1918年发表）中宣称：

Though much of our subsequent history will concern doubts, inadequacies, and deep problems raised by the axiomatization of mathematics, in the early part of the twentieth century the axiomatic method was hailed as the ideal. No one praised it more than Hilbert, who was by that time the world’s leading mathematician. In his article on “Axiomatic Thinking” (published in 1918), he declared:

凡能成为数学思考对象的东西，只要建立理论的时机成熟，就进入公理方法，从而直接进入数学。不断深入更深层的公理……，能使我们更深刻理解科学思考，认识知识的统一性。尤其凭借公理方法，数学似乎肩负着在一切知识中发挥领导作用的使命。

Everything that can be the object of mathematical thinking, as soon as the erection of a theory is ripe, falls into the axiomatic method and thereby directly into mathematics. By pressing to ever deeper layers of axioms ... we can obtain deeper insights into the scientific thinking and learn the unity of our knowledge. By virtue especially of the axiomatic method mathematics appears called upon to play a leading role in all knowledge.

1922年，他再次断言：

In 1922 he asserted again:

公理方法的确是、并始终是任何领域一切精确研究精神所需要的、适当而不可缺少的助力；它在逻辑上无可攻击，同时富有成果，因此保证研究的完全自由。在此意义上，按公理方法进行，不过就是清楚自己在做什么地思考。以前没有公理方法，人们天真地把某些关系当作教条相信；公理方法消除这种天真，却仍保留信念的好处。

The axiomatic method is indeed and remains the one suitable and indispensable aid to the spirit of every exact investigation no matter in what domain; it is logically unassailable and at the same time fruitful; it guarantees thereby complete freedom of investigation. To proceed axiomatically means in this sense nothing else than to think with knowledge of what one is about. While earlier without the axiomatic method one proceeded naively in that one believed in certain relationships as dogma, the axiomatic approach removes this naivete and yet permits the advantages of belief.

人们会以为，数学家欢迎学科建立在坚实严谨的基础上。但数学家很有人性。无理数、连续性、积分和导数等基本概念的精确表述，并非受到所有数学家的热情欢迎。许多人不懂新的技术语言，把精确定义看作时髦，对理解数学，甚至严谨证明，都不必要。他们认为直觉已经够好，尽管出现了无导数的连续函数及其他逻辑正确却违反直觉的创造。埃米尔·皮卡（1856—1941）1904年谈到偏微分方程中的严谨时说：“真正的严谨富有成果，区别于另一种纯形式而令人厌烦的严谨；后者使所触及的问题蒙上阴影。”夏尔·埃尔米特（1822—1901）在1893年5月20日给托马斯·扬·斯蒂尔切斯的信中说：“面对连续却没有导数的函数这种可悲的恶，我恐惧而厌恶地退缩。”庞加莱（1854—1912）抱怨：“以前引入新函数，是为了应用它们。今天却相反，人们构造函数，是为了反驳前人的结论，而且永远不能把它们用于任何其他目的。”他的数学哲学将在后面一章考察。

One would think that mathematicians would welcome the establishment of their subject on a firm, rigorous basis. But mathematicians are very human. The precise formulation of basic concepts such as irrational numbers, continuity, integral, and derivative was not greeted enthusiastically by all mathematicians. Many did not understand the new technical language and regarded the precise definitions as fads, unnecessary for the comprehension of mathematics or even for rigorous proof. These men felt that intuition was good enough, despite the surprises of continuous functions without derivatives, and other logically correct but non-intuitive creations. Emile Picard (1856-1941) said in 1904 apropos of the rigor in partial differential equations, “True rigor is productive, being distinguished in this from another rigor which is purely formal and tiresome, casting a shadow over the problems it touches.” Charles Hermite (1822-1901), in a letter to Thomas Jan Stieltjes of May 20, 1893, said, “I recoil with fear and loathing from that deplorable evil, continuous functions with no derivative.” Poincare (1854-1912), whose philosophy of mathematics will be examined in a later chapter, complained: “When earlier, new functions were introduced, the purpose was to apply them. Today, on the contrary, one constructs functions to contradict the conclusions of our predecessors and one will never be able to apply them for any other purpose.”

许多人的定义和证明如今被发现有错，他们却坚持，自己的原意正是严谨化产生的内容。甚至大师埃米尔·博雷尔也如此辩护。另一些人反对所谓吹毛求疵。戈弗雷·H. 哈代在1934年一篇文章中说，严谨是例行事务。还有人不理解严谨，因而防御性地贬低它。有些人谈论数学中的无政府状态。新思想——在这里是有助于数学严谨化的思想——在数学家中被接受时，并不比在其他任何人群中受到更开放的对待。

Many men whose definitions and proofs were now seen to be faulty maintained that they meant exactly what the rigorization produced. Even the master Emile Borel defended himself in this manner. Others objected to what they called nit-picking. Godfrey H. Hardy in an article of 1934 said rigor was a matter of routine. Still others did not understand the rigor and so defensively deprecated it. Some spoke of anarchy in mathematics. New ideas, in the present case those contributing to the rigorization of mathematics, are not more open-mindedly received by mathematicians than by any other group of people.

严谨化揭示了数学创造的另一面。严谨满足十九世纪的需要，但最终结果也使我们认识到数学发展的某些东西。新建立的严谨结构据说保证数学可靠，但这种保证几乎是多余的。算术、代数或欧几里得几何，没有一个定理因此改变；分析的定理也只是必须表述得更仔细。因此，若要使用连续函数的导数，必须增加函数可微的假设。事实上，新公理结构和严谨所做的，只是证实数学家知道必然如此的东西。公理确实必须产生现有定理，而不是其他定理，因为定理总体上正确。这一切表明，数学依靠的不是逻辑，而是可靠直觉。正如雅克·阿达马指出的，严谨只是认可直觉的征服；或者正如赫尔曼·外尔所说，逻辑是数学家为使思想健康有力而实行的卫生保健。

The rigorization revealed another aspect of mathematical creation. Rigor filled a nineteenth-century need but the end result also teaches us something about the development of mathematics. The newly founded rigorous structures presumably guaranteed the soundness of mathematics but the guarantee was almost gratuitous. Not a theorem of arithmetic, algebra, or Euclidean geometry was changed as a consequence, and the theorems of analysis had only to be more carefully formulated. Thus, if one wishes to use the derivative of a continuous function, he must add the hypothesis that the function is differentiable. In fact, all that the new axiomatic structures and rigor did was to substantiate what mathematicians knew had to be the case. Indeed, the axioms had to yield the existing theorems rather than different ones because the theorems were on the whole correct. All of which means that mathematics rests not on logic but on sound intuitions. Rigor, as Jacques Hadamard pointed out, merely sanctions the conquests of the intuition; or, as Hermann Weyl stated, logic is the hygiene which the mathematician practices to keep his ideas healthy and strong.

无论如何，到1900年，严谨重新确立了在数学中的作用，虽然姗姗来迟，却使许多世纪的发现得到保障。数学家可以宣称，已履行希腊人设定标准所要求的义务；知道除相对小的修正外，凭经验或直观建起的庞大内容已获得逻辑认可，他们可以更安心。事实上，他们欢欣，甚至自满。回顾无理数、微积分、非欧几里得几何和四元数这几次危机，他们庆贺自己克服了每种创造提出的问题。
