In his Development of Mathematics in the Nineteenth Century (1925), he recalled Fourier’s interest in solving practical problems with the best mathematics available and contrasted this with the purely mathematical refinement of tools and abstraction of concrete ideas. He then said:

当今数学仿佛和平时期的一座大兵工厂。橱窗摆满阅兵用的武器，其巧妙、熟练而赏心悦目的制作吸引着鉴赏家。这些物件原本的动机与目的，即与敌人战斗并征服敌人，已退到意识的背景中，乃至被遗忘。

The mathematics of our day seems to be like a great weapons factory in peace time. The show window is filled with parade pieces whose ingenious, skillful, eye-appealing execution attracts the connoisseur. The proper motivation for and purpose of these objects, to battle and conquer the enemy, has receded to the background of consciousness to the extent of having been forgotten.

理查德·柯朗继克莱因之后领导哥廷根的数学工作，随后主持纽约大学后来命名为柯朗数学科学研究所的机构。他也痛惜对纯数学的强调。在1924年写成的柯朗与希尔伯特合著《数学物理方法》第一版序言中，柯朗开头就指出：

Richard Courant, who succeeded Klein in the leadership of mathematics at Gottingen and subsequently headed what has since been named the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences of New York University, also deplored the emphasis on pure mathematics. In the Preface to the first edition of Courant’s and Hilbert’s Methods of Mathematical Physics, written in 1924, Courant opened with the observation:

自古以来，数学从分析的问题和方法与物理的直觉观念之间的密切关系中，获得了强有力的刺激。过去几十年，这种联系松弛了，因为数学研究在很大程度上脱离直觉起点，尤其在分析中，主要关注方法的精炼与概念的明确。于是，许多分析领域的领袖，失去了关于其学科与物理及其他领域相联系的知识；另一方面，物理学家也失去了对数学家的问题和方法，甚至对他们整个兴趣范围与语言的理解。毫无疑问，这一倾向威胁着全部科学。科学发展的潮流有不断分岔、涓涓流散直至干涸的危险。为避免这一命运，我们必须把大量力量用于重新联合分离的东西，在共同观点下阐明纷繁事实的内在联系。只有这样，学生才能有效掌握材料，研究者才能为有机发展做好准备。

From olden times onward mathematics won powerful stimuli from the close relations which existed between the problems and methods of analysis and the intuitive ideas of physics. The last few decades have witnessed a loosening of this connection in that mathematical research has severed itself a great deal from the intuitive starting points and especially in analysis has mostly concerned itself with the refinement of its methods and the sharpening of its concepts. Thus it has come about that many leaders of analysis have lost the knowledge of the connection between their discipline and physics as well as other domains, while on the other side the understanding by physicists of the problems and methods of the mathematicians and even of their entire spheres of interest and language has been lost. Without doubt there lies in this tendency a threat to all of science. The current of scientific development is in danger of further and further ramification, trickling away and drying up. To escape this fate we must direct a great deal of our power to uniting what is separated in that we lay clear under a common viewpoint the inner connections of the manifold facts. Only in this way will the student master an effective control of the material and the researcher be prepared for an organic development.

1939年，柯朗又写道：

Again in 1939 Courant wrote:

断言数学只不过是从定义和公设推导出的结论体系，而这些定义和公设只须一致，除此之外可以由数学家自由意志创造，这就暗含对科学生命本身的严重威胁。如果这种描述准确，数学就无法吸引任何聪明人。它将是一种没有动机或目标的定义、规则和三段论游戏。认为理智能随心所欲创造有意义的公设体系，是一种骗人的半真理。只有在对有机整体负责的约束下，只有以内在必然性为指引，自由的心灵才能取得具有科学价值的结果。

A serious threat to the very life of science is implied in the assertion that mathematics is nothing but a system of conclusions drawn from the definitions and postulates that must be consistent but otherwise may be created by the free will of mathematicians. If this description were accurate, mathematics could not attract any intelligent person. It would be a game with definitions, rules, and syllogisms without motivation or goal. The notion that the intellect can create meaningful postulational systems at its whim is a deceptive half-truth. Only under the discipline of responsibility to the organic whole, only guided by intrinsic necessity, can the free mind achieve results of scientific value.

当时美国最杰出的数学家乔治·戴维·伯克霍夫（1884—1944），在《美国科学家》

George David Birkhoff (1884-1944), the leading United States mathematician of his day, made the same point in the American Scientist

1943年刊物中提出相同观点：

of 1943:

希望未来有越来越多的理论物理学家深刻掌握数学原理；也希望数学家不再如此专一地把自己限制于数学抽象的审美发展。

It is to be hoped that in the future more and more theoretical physicists will command a deep knowledge of mathematical principles; and also that mathematicians will no longer limit themselves so exclusively to the aesthetic development of mathematical abstractions.

约翰·L.辛格——诚然，他是一位数学物理学家——在1944年一篇技术文章的萧伯纳式序言中，颇为详细地描述了这一局面：

John L. Synge, admittedly a mathematical physicist, described the situation in 1944 at some length in a Shavian preface to a technical article:

大多数数学家研究那些按照共同认可，明确属于数学的观念。他们组成一个封闭的行会。入会者宣誓摒弃世间事务，一般也遵守誓言。只有少数数学家走出门去，从其他科学领域直接产生的问题中寻求数学养料。在1744年或1844年，第二类几乎包括全部数学家。到1944年，它只占全体的一小部分，以至有必要提醒多数人注意少数人的存在，并解释他们的观点。

Most mathematicians work with ideas which, by common consent, belong definitely to mathematics. They form a closed guild. The initiate foreswears the things of the world, and generally keeps his oath. Only a few mathematicians roam abroad and seek mathematical sustenance in problems arising directly out of other fields of science. In 1744 or 1844 this second class included almost the whole body of mathematicians. In 1944 it is such a small fraction of the whole that it becomes necessary to remind the majority of the existence of the minority, and to explain its point of view.

少数人不希望被贴上“物理学家”或“工程师”的标签，因为他们遵循的是绵延二十多个世纪、包括欧几里得、阿基米德、牛顿、拉格朗日、哈密顿、高斯和庞加莱这些名字的数学传统。少数人不想以任何方式贬低多数人的工作，却确实担心，一种只以自身为食的数学，终将耗尽自身的趣味。

The minority does not wish to be labelled “physicist” or “engineer,” for it is following a mathematical tradition extending through more than twenty centuries and including the names Euclid, Archimedes, Newton, Lagrange, Hamilton, Gauss, Poincare. The minority does not wish to belittle in any way the work of the majority, but it does fear that a mathematics which feeds solely on itself will in time exhaust its interest.

除了影响数学本身的未来，数学家的孤立还剥夺了其他科学在以往所有时代都曾倚赖的支持……自然研究产生了（而且极可能继续产生）比数学家在自身观念圈子内构造的问题困难得多的问题。科学家一直依靠数学家投入精力来攻克这些问题。他们知道，数学家不只是某些现成工具的熟练使用者——他们自己也能相当熟练地使用这些工具。他们期待的，是数学家特有的品质——逻辑洞察力，以及在特殊中看到一般、在一般中看到特殊的能力……

Apart from its effect on the future of mathematics proper, the isolation of mathematicians has robbed the rest of science of a support on which it counted in all previous epochs. . . . Out of the study of nature there have originated (and in all probability will continue to originate) problems far more difficult than those constructed by mathematicians within the circle of their own ideas. Scientists have relied on the mathematician to throw his energies against these problems. They know that the mathematician is not merely a skilled user of certain tools already made—they can use those tools with no inconsiderable skill themselves. Rather they look to the qualities peculiar to the mathematician—his logical penetration and capacity to see the general in the particular and the particular in the general. . . .

在所有这些事情中，数学家曾是引导和规范的力量。他给科学提供计算方法——对数、微积分、微分方程等等——但给予的远不止这些。他还给科学提供蓝图。他坚持思想必须合乎逻辑。每当一门新科学兴起，他就给予它——或者试图给予它——欧几里得曾给予埃及土地测量的那种坚实逻辑结构。一门学科来到他手上时，是一块拖着无关杂草的粗石；离开他手时，却成为磨光的宝石。

In all this the mathematician was the directing and disciplining force. He gave science its methods of calculation—logarithms, calculus, differential equations, and so on—but he gave it much more than this. He gave it a blue-print. He insisted that thought be logical. As each new science came up, he gave it—or tried to give it—the firm logical structure that Euclid gave to Egyptian land surveying. A subject came to his hands a rough stone, trailing irrelevant weeds; it left his hands a polished gem.

目前，科学以前所未有的繁忙运转着。没有明显的衰败迹象。只有最敏锐的人注意到，守夜人已经离岗。他没有睡觉，仍像以往一样努力工作，但如今只为自己工作……

At present science is humming as it never hummed before. There are no obvious signs of decay. Only the most observant have noticed that the watchman has gone off duty. He has not gone to sleep. He is working as hard as ever, but now he is working solely for himself. . . .

简言之，聚会已经结束——它持续时确实令人兴奋……自然会抛出巨大的问题，却永远到不了数学家那里。他可以坐在象牙塔里，备着一整库枪炮等待敌人，但敌人不会来找他。自然不会把已经表述好的问题送上门。这些问题必须用镐和铲挖出来；不肯弄脏双手的人永远看不到它们。

In brief, the party is over—it was exciting while it lasted. . . . Nature will throw out mighty problems, but they will never reach the mathematician. He may sit in his ivory tower waiting for the enemy with an arsenal of guns, but the enemy will never come to him. Nature does not offer her problems ready formulated. They must be dug up with pick and shovel, and he who will not soil his hands will never see them.

观念世界的变化与死亡，和人间事务的变化与死亡一样不可避免。爱真理的数学家，当然不应在它们正在发生时假装没有发生。智力动机的深层源泉，不可能人为刺激。某种东西或者激发想象，或者不激发；若不激发，就没有火焰。如果数学家真的失去了昔日广泛涉猎的本领——如果事实上，他们在精确逻辑的精炼中，比在星辰运动中更真切地看到上帝之手——那么，任何诱使他们回到旧日领域的尝试，不仅无用，而且否定个人思想自由的权利。但每个形成自己哲学的青年数学家——人人都会如此——都应在充分掌握事实后作出决定。他应当认识到，如果遵循现代数学的模式，他虽然是伟大传统的继承人，却只是部分继承人。其余遗产将落入他人之手，他永远无法取回……

Change and death in the world of ideas are as inevitable as change and death in human affairs. It is certainly not the part of a truth-loving mathematician to pretend that they are not occurring when they are. It is impossible to stimulate artificially the deep sources of intellectual motivation. Something catches the imagination or it does not, and, if it does not, there is no fire. If mathematicians have really lost their old universal touch—if, in fact, they see the hand of God more truly in the refinement of precise logic than in the motion of the stars—then any attempt to lure them back to their old haunts would not only be useless—it would be denial of the right of the individual to intellectual freedom. But each young mathematician who formulates his own philosophy and all do—should make his decision in full possession of the facts. He should realize that if he follows the pattern of modern mathematics he is heir to a great tradition, but only part heir. The rest of the legacy will have gone to other hands, and he will never get it back. . . .

我们的科学始于数学，如果数学退出科学，科学也肯定会在不久之后终结。一个世纪之后，将有更大、更好的实验室，用来大量生产事实。这些事实仍仅仅是事实，还是成为科学，将取决于它们在多大程度上与数学精神接触。

Our science started with mathematics and will surely end not long after mathematics is withdrawn from it (if it is withdrawn). A century hence there will be bigger and better laboratories for the mass-production of facts. Whether these facts remain mere facts or become science will depend on the extent to which they are brought into contact with the spirit of mathematics.

约翰·冯·诺伊曼已足够警觉，以至发出警告。在常被引用、却很少得到重视的文章《数学家》（1947年）中，他说：

John von Neumann was sufficiently alarmed to issue a warning. In the often quoted but little heeded essay “The Mathematician” (1947), he stated:

当一门数学学科远离经验源泉，或者更甚，当它成为仅间接受到“现实”启发的第二、第三代学科时，就面临非常严重的危险。它越来越成为纯粹的审美，越来越纯粹地“为艺术而艺术”。如果周围还有与经验联系较紧密的相关学科，或者该学科受品味极其高明的人影响，这未必不好。但严重危险在于，学科可能沿阻力最小的方向发展；远离源头的溪流可能分成无数无关紧要的支流；学科可能成为一堆杂乱的细节与复杂性。换句话说，一门数学学科在远离经验源泉，或经过大量抽象的近亲繁殖之后，就有退化的危险。起初，其风格通常是古典的；当它出现巴洛克化迹象时，危险信号就亮起了……无论如何，每当达到这一阶段，在我看来，唯一的补救似乎是回归源头，使它返老还童：重新注入或多或少直接来自经验的观念。我确信，这是保持学科新鲜与活力的必要条件，未来也同样如此。

As a mathematical discipline travels far from its empirical source, or still more, if it is a second and third generation only indirectly inspired from “reality” it is beset with very grave dangers. It becomes more and more pure aestheticizing, more and more purely I’art pour I’art. This need not be bad if the field is surrounded by correlated subjects which still have closer empirical connections, or if the discipline is under the influence of men with exceptionally well-developed taste. But there is a grave danger that the subject will develop along the line of least resistance, that the stream so far from its source will separate into a multitude of insignificant branches, and that the discipline will become a disorganized mass of details and complexities. In other words, at a great distance from its empirical source, or after much abstract inbreeding, a mathematical subject is in danger of degeneration. At the inception the style is usually classical; when it shows signs of becoming baroque, the danger signal is up. . . . In any event, whenever this stage is reached, the only remedy seems to me to be the rejuvenating return to the source: the reinjection of more or less directly empirical ideas. I am convinced that this was a necessary condition to conserve the freshness and vitality of the subject and that this will remain equally true in the future.

但纯粹创造的趋势并未被遏止。数学家继续脱离科学，走自己的道路。也许为了安抚良心，他们倾向于把应用数学家看作低下的绘图员。他们抱怨，纯数学的甜美音乐被技术的号角淹没。不过，他们也觉得有必要回应上述这类批评。那些直言不讳的人，要么不懂历史，要么故意歪曲历史，现在声称，过去许多主要创造的动机只是智力兴趣，后来却被证明对应用极其重要。我们来看看这些纯数学家从历史中举出的例子。他们所称的纯数学究竟有多纯？

But the trend to pure creations has not been stemmed. Mathematicians have continued to break away from science and to pursue their own course. Perhaps to placate their own consciences, they have tended to look down on the applied mathematicians as lowly draftsmen. They complain that the sweet music of pure mathematics is being drowned out by the trumpets of technology. However, they have also felt the need to counter the criticisms such as those reproduced above. The outspoken ones, either ignorant of or deliberately distorting the history, now argue that many of the major creations of the past were motivated solely by intellectual interest and yet proved to be immensely important for applications later. Let us look at some of the examples these pure mathematicians adduce from history. How pure was the mathematics they describe as pure?

最常举的例子，是希腊人关于抛物线、椭圆和双曲线的工作。纯数学家的论点是，希腊人，尤其阿波罗尼奥斯，研究这些曲线仅为满足数学兴趣；然而一千八百年后，开普勒发现椭圆正是描述行星绕太阳运动所需要的曲线。虽然圆锥曲线最早的历史我们并不清楚，但权威史家奥托·诺伊格鲍尔提出的一种理论认为，它们产生于日晷构造的工作。使用圆锥曲线的古代日晷是已知的。此外，圆锥曲线可以聚光这一事实，早在阿波罗尼奥斯撰写该课题的经典著作之前就已知道（第一章）。因此，圆锥曲线在光学中的物理用途，肯定激发了一部分研究；希腊人曾对光学投入相当多的时间和精力。

The commonest example offered is the Greek work on the parabola, ellipse, and hyperbola. The argument of the pure mathematicians is that these curves were investigated by the Greeks, notably Apollonius, simply to satisfy a mathematical interest. Yet eighteen hundred years later the ellipse was found by Kepler to be just the curve he needed to describe the motions of the planets around the sun. Though we do not know the very early history of the conic sections, one theory, proposed by the authoritative historian Otto Neugebauer, is that they arose in work on the construction of sundials. Ancient sundials using conics are known. Moreover, the fact that the conic sections can be used to focus light was known long before Apollonius devoted his classic work to that subject (Chapter I). Hence the physical uses of the conic sections for optics, a subject to which the Greeks devoted considerable time and effort, certainly motivated some of the work on the conic sections.

早在阿波罗尼奥斯之前，人们还研究圆锥曲线，以解决构造一个体积为给定立方体两倍的新立方体的边长问题。这对希腊几何很重要，因为构造是证明存在的方法。

The conic sections were also investigated long before Apollonius’s time to solve the problem of constructing the side of a cube whose volume was double that of a given cube, a problem of importance to Greek geometry for which construction was the method of proving existence.

阿波罗尼奥斯也证明了数百个既无直接应用、也无潜在应用的圆锥曲线定理，这无疑是真的。在这种工作中，他与现代人并无不同：发现一个有实质内容的课题后，继续加以详究，或是基于上述理由，更多了解重要学科，或是出于智力挑战等理由。

That Apollonius also proved hundreds of theorems about the conics that have no application immediate or potential is undoubtedly true. In this work he did not differ from moderns who have found a substantial theme and proceed to elaborate on it either for the reasons cited above of learning more about a vital subject or for reasons such as intellectual challenge.

后来发现可应用的纯数学例子中，第二个最常被引用的是非欧几里得几何。据说，数学家只是猜测改变欧几里得平行公理会产生什么，就创建了非欧几里得几何。这一断言忽略了两千年历史。欧几里得公理曾被视为关于物理空间的自明真理（第一章）。但平行公理被欧几里得刻意而特别地措辞，以避免直接假定平行线，它不如其他公理自明。因此，寻找更可接受版本的许多努力，最终使人认识到，平行公理未必为真；关于平行线的另一条公理，从而一种非欧几里得几何，也可以同样好地表示物理空间。关键是，确保欧几里得平行公理真理性的努力，不是“思辨头脑的消遣”，而是试图保证几何的真理性；几何是数学本身和应用数学中数千个定理的基础。

The second most often cited example of pure mathematics later found to be applicable is non-Euchdean geometry. Presumably mathematicians merely speculating about what would result from changing the parallel axiom of Euclid created non-Euclidean geometry. This assertion ignores two thousand years of history. Euclid’s axioms were taken to be self-evident truths about physical space (Chapter I). However, the parallel axiom, rather deliberately and peculiarly worded by Euclid to avoid the outright assumption of parallel lines, was not as self-evident as the other axioms. Hence the many efforts to find a more acceptable version led ultimately to the realization that the parallel axiom was not necessarily true and that a differing axiom on parallels—and consequently a non-Euclidean geometry—could be as good a representation of physical space. The main point is that the efforts to guarantee the truth of Euclid’s parallel axiom were not the “amusement of speculative brains” but an attempt to secure the truth of geometry which underlies thousands of theorems of mathematics proper and of applied mathematics.

纯数学家常引用黎曼的工作。他推广当时已知的非欧几里得几何，引入大量不同的非欧几里得几何，现在称为黎曼几何。在这里，纯数学家也声称，黎曼创造这些几何只是为了看看能够做些什么。这种叙述是错误的。如刚才所说，数学家为了使欧几里得几何在物理上的可靠性无可置疑而努力，最终创造了一种非欧几里得几何；它在表示物理空间性质方面，被证明与欧几里得几何同样有用。这一意外事实引出问题：既然两种几何不同，我们究竟确信物理空间的哪些东西是真的？这正是黎曼明确的出发点；他在1854年的论文中回答它时（第四章），创造了更一般的几何。鉴于我们物理知识有限，这些几何在表示物理空间方面，可能与欧几里得几何同样有用。事实上，黎曼预见到，空间与物质必须一起考虑。那么，爱因斯坦发现某种黎曼几何有用，有什么奇怪呢？黎曼对于这种几何相关性的先见，并不减损爱因斯坦巧妙使用它的功绩；它的适宜性，来自数学家曾处理的最根本的物理问题，即物理空间的性质。

The pure mathematicians often cite the work of Riemann, who generalized on the non-Euclidean geometry known in his time and introduced a large variety of non-Euclidean geometries, now known as Riemannian geometries. Here, too, the pure mathematicians contend that Riemann created his geometries merely to see what could be done. Their account is false. The efforts of mathematicians to put beyond question the physical soundness of Euclidean geometry culminated, as we have just noted, in the creation of a non-Euclidean geometry which proved as useful in representing the properties of physical space as Euclidean geometry was. This unexpected fact gave rise to the question, since these two geometries differ, what are we really sure is true about physical space? This question was Riemann’s explicit point of departure and in answering it in his paper of 1854 (Chapter IV) he created more general geometries. In view of our limited physical knowledge, these could be as useful in representing physical space as Euclidean geometry. In fact, Riemann foresaw that space and matter would have to be considered together. Is it to be wondered then that Einstein found a Riemannian geometry useful? Riemann’s foresight concerning the relevance of this geometry does not detract from the ingenious use which Einstein made of it; its suitability was the consequence of work on the most fundamental physical problem which mathematicians have ever tackled, the nature of physical space.

也许还应考虑一个例子。现代数学中研究极活跃的学科是群论；纯数学家声称，人们研究它是出于其内在趣味。群论主要由埃瓦里斯特·伽罗瓦（1811—1832）创造，尽管此前有拉格朗日和保罗·鲁菲尼的工作。伽罗瓦所处理的问题，本质上是全部数学最简单、最实际的问题，即简单多项式方程的可解性，例如二次方程

Perhaps one more example should be considered. A subject very actively studied in modern mathematics is group theory, which, the pure mathematicians contend, was tackled for its intrinsic interest. Group theory was created primarily by Evariste Galois (1811-1832), though there was preceding work by Lagrange and Paolo Ruffini. The problem Galois tackled was in essence the simplest and most practical problem of all mathematics, namely, the solvability of simple polynomial equations such as the second degree equation

3x2+5x+7=0,

3x2+5x+7=0,

三次方程

the third degree equation

4x3+6x2−5x+9=0,

4x3+6x2−5x+9=0,

以及更高次方程。这类方程出现在数以千计的物理问题中。到伽罗瓦时代，数学家已经成功展示如何解一至四次一般方程；尼尔斯·亨里克·阿贝尔（1802—1829）已经表明，五次及更高次的一般方程不可能用代数方法求解，例如ax5+bx4+cx3+dx2+ex+f=0，其中a、b、c、d、e、f可以是任意实数（或复数）。于是，伽罗瓦着手说明，为什么五次及以上的一般方程不能用代数方法求解，以及哪些特殊方程可能可解。在这项工作中，他创建了群论。从多项式方程求解这样基本的问题产生的学科，能够应用于许多其他数学和物理问题，难道值得奇怪吗？群论显然不是脱离真实问题而受到启发的。

and higher degree equations. Such equations arise in thousands of physical problems. Mathematicians had succeeded by Galois’s time in showing how to solve the general equations from the first to the fourth degree, and Niels Henrik Abel (1802-1829) had shown that it is impossible to solve algebraically general equations of the fifth and higher degree such as ax5 + bx4 + cx3 + dx2 + ex + f = 0 where a, b, c, d, e, and f can be any real (or complex) numbers. Galois thereupon set out to show why such general equations of degree five or higher are not solvable algebraically and which special ones may be solvable. In his work he created the theory of groups. Is it any wonder that a subject derived from so basic a problem as the solution of polynomial equations should be applicable to many other mathematical and physical problems? Certainly group theory was not inspired independently of real problems.

此外，群论的动机并不只来自伽罗瓦的工作。纯数学家似乎忽略了奥古斯特·布拉维（1811—1863）关于石英、金刚石和岩石等晶体结构的工作。这些物质由不同原子按某种模式排列而成，这个模式在整个晶体中重复。此外，盐和普通矿物等晶体，具有非常特殊的原子排列类型。例如，在最简单情况下，原子虽彼此相邻，却可以看作位于立方体顶点。1848年起，布拉维研究一些可能的变换，允许将晶体绕某轴旋转，或平移、关于某轴反射，使晶体变换为自身。这些变换构成各种类型的群。卡米耶·若尔当（1838—1922）注意到布拉维的工作，在1868年的论文中加以扩展，并在其影响极大的《Traité des substitutions》（《置换论》，1870年）中，将它列为研究有限群的动机之一。

Moreover, the motivation for group theory does not rest solely on Galois’s work. The pure mathematicians seem to overlook the work of Auguste Bravais (1811-1863) on the structure of crystals such as quartz, diamonds, and rocks. These substances are composed of different atoms arranged in a pattern that repeats itself throughout the crystal. Moreover, crystals such as salt and common minerals have very special types of atomic arrangements. For example, in the simplest case, the atoms though contiguous may be thought of as located at the vertices of a cube. Bravais studied, from 1848 on, the possible transformations that permit one to rotate a crystal about some axis or to translate or reflect the crystal about some axis so that the crystal is transformed into itself. These transformations form various types of groups. Camille Jordan (1838-1922) noted this work of Bravais, extended it himself in a paper of 1868, and included it among other motivations for the study of finite groups in his most influential Traite des substitutions (Treatise on Substitutions, 1870).

布拉维的工作也启发若尔当研究无限群——平移群和旋转群。费利克斯·克莱因1872年的演讲与论文，使无限群受到重视；他用各种几何中可能的运动群，以及在这些运动下保持不变的东西，区分当时已知的不同几何。例如，欧几里得几何的特征，是研究图形在旋转、平移和相似变换下不变的性质。1872年，区分各种已知几何的问题，以及哪种几何符合物理空间的问题——当时数学家最关心的问题——很难被视为纯数学而置之不理。在19世纪90年代形成现代抽象群概念之前，还有许多涉及无限连续群与不连续群、用以刻画微分方程求解方法的工作进入数学。*

Bravais’s work also suggested to Jordan the study of infinite groups— groups of translations and rotations. The subject of infinite groups was brought into prominence by Felix Klein’s talk and paper of 1872 in which he distinguished the different geometries known in his time by the groups of movements possible in those geometries and by what remains invariant under these movements. Thus Euclidean geometry is characterized by the fact that it studies properties of figures that are invariant under rotations, translations, and similarity transformations. The problem in 1872 of distinguishing the various known geometries and the problem of which geometry fits physical space—then uppermost in the minds of mathematicians—can hardly be dismissed as pure mathematics. Many more works involving infinite continuous and discontinuous groups to characterize methods of solving differential equations had yet to enter mathematics before the modern notion of an abstract group was formulated in the 1890s.*

考察其他被声称为纯数学产物的学科，如矩阵、张量分析和拓扑学，会揭示相同的故事。例如，全部现代抽象代数的起源，都归于哈密顿创建四元数（第四章）。动机直接或间接来自物理，参与者都高度关注数学的用途。换句话说，那些据说作为纯数学创建、后来才发现可应用的学科，就历史事实而言，是在研究真实的物理问题，或与物理问题直接相关的问题时创建的。经常发生的是，最初由物理问题激发的优秀数学，找到此前未预见的新应用。数学由此偿还对科学的债务。这类用途本来就应当预期。锤子也许最初为碎石而发明，却也能把钉子打进木头，我们会惊讶吗？数学理论意外的科学用途之所以出现，是因为理论从一开始就具有物理基础，绝不是因为无所不知、只与自身灵魂搏斗的数学家具有预言性的洞察。持续成功使用这些创造，绝非偶然。

An investigation of other subjects claimed to be the product of pure mathematics, such as matrices, tensor analysis, and topology, would reveal the same story. For example, all of modern abstract algebra owes its origins to Hamilton’s creation of quaternions (Chapter IV). The motivations were either directly or indirectly physical and the men involved were vitally concerned with the uses of mathematics. In other words, the subjects purportedly created as pure mathematics and found to be applicable later were, as a matter of historical fact, created in the study of real physical problems or those bearing directly on physical problems. What does often happen is that good mathematics, originally motivated by physical problems, finds new applications that were not foreseen. Thereby mathematics pays its debt to science. Such uses are to be expected. Are we surprised to find that the hammer, which may have been invented originally to crush rocks, may also be used to drive nails into wood? The unexpected scientific uses of mathematical theories arise because the theories are physically grounded to start with and are by no means due to the prophetic insight of all-wise mathematicians who wrestle solely with their souls. The continuing successful use of these creations is by no means fortuitous.

*阿瑟·凯莱确实在1849年和1854年的论文中提出过抽象群的定义。但抽象概念的意义，直到上述许多更具体的用途出现之后，才受到重视。

^Arthur Cayley did suggest a definition of an abstract group in papers of 1849 and 1854. But the significance of an abstract concept was not appreciated until the many more concrete uses described above had been made.

据说，英国最主要的数学家之一戈弗雷·H.哈代（1877—1947）曾祝酒道：“为纯数学干杯！愿它永远没有任何用途。”芝加哥大学的权威伦纳德·尤金·迪克森（1874—1954）常说：“感谢上帝，数论没有受到任何应用的玷污。”

Godfrey H. Hardy (1877-1947), one of Britain’s leading mathematicians, is reported to have made the toast: “Here’s to pure mathematics! May it never have any use.” Leonard Eugene Dickson (1874-1954), an authority at the University of Chicago, used to say: “Thank God that number theory is unsullied by any applications.”

哈代在一篇关于战时数学的文章（1940年）中说：我最好立即说明，我所谓“数学”，指真正的数学，即费马、欧拉、高斯和阿贝尔的数学，而不是工程实验室中冒充数学的东西。我想到的不只是“纯”数学（虽然它自然是我的首要关切）；我也把麦克斯韦、爱因斯坦、爱丁顿和狄拉克算作“真正的”数学家。

In an article on mathematics in wartime (1940), Hardy said: I had better say at once that by “mathematics” I mean real mathematics, the mathematics of Fermat and Euler and Gauss and Abel, and not the stuff that passes for mathematics in an engineering laboratory. I am not thinking only of “pure” mathematics (though naturally that is my first concern); I count Maxwell and Einstein and Eddington and Dirac among “real” mathematicians.

从这段哈代在《一个数学家的辩白》（1967年版）中重复的引文，人们可能以为，他至少愿意接受某些应用数学。但随后他继续说：

One would believe from this quotation, which Hardy repeated in A Mathematician's Apology (1967 edition), that Hardy was willing to accept some at least of applied mathematics. But then he went on:

我包括的是全部具有永久审美价值的数学知识整体，例如最优秀的希腊数学。这样的数学是永恒的，因为其中最好的部分，可以像最优秀的文学一样，在数千年之后，仍继续给数千人带来情感上的满足。

I am including the whole body of mathematical knowledge which has permanent aesthetic value; as for example, the best Greek mathematics has, the mathematics which is eternal because the best of it may, like the best literature, continue to cause emotional satisfaction to thousands of people after thousands of years.

哈代和迪克森可以安息，因为历史给了他们保证。他们的纯数学，像一切为数学自身而创造的数学一样，几乎肯定不会有任何用途。不过，这种可能性并非完全不存在。随意往画布上涂颜料的孩子，可能比肩米开朗琪罗（尽管更可能像现代艺术）；正如阿瑟·斯坦利·爱丁顿指出的，随意打字的猴子可能写出莎士比亚水准的戏剧。事实上，数千名纯数学家在工作，偶尔可能出现与有用数学相关的结果。在街上寻找金币的人，可能找到五分和十分硬币。但不受现实锤炼的智力努力，几乎肯定不会结果。正如乔治·戴维·伯克霍夫所说：“经由物理启发的数学新发现，很可能永远最重要，因为从一开始，自然就在引路，建立数学——自然的语言——必须遵循的模式。”不过，自然从不大声宣扬她的秘密，而总是低声耳语。数学家必须认真倾听，然后尝试放大并宣布它们。

Hardy and Dickson can rest in peace because they have the assurance of history. Their pure mathematics, like all mathematics created for its own sake, will almost certainly not have any use. However, the possibility is not out of the question. A child who dabs paint at random on a canvas may rival Michelangelo (though more likely modern art) and, as Arthur Stanley Eddington pointed out, a monkey who types letters at random may produce a play of Shakespearean quality. As a matter of fact, with thousands of pure mathematicians at work, an occasional result bearing on useful mathematics can appear. A man who looks for gold coins in the street may find nickels and dimes. But intellectual efforts not tempered by reality are almost sure to prove sterile. As George David Birkhoff remarked, “It will probably be the new mathematical discoveries suggested through physics that will always be the most important, for from the beginning Nature has led the way and established the pattern which mathematics, the language of Nature, must follow.” However, nature never blazons her secrets with a loud voice but always whispers them. And the mathematician must listen attentively and then attempt to amplify and proclaim them.

尽管有历史证据，一些数学家仍断言纯数学未来会有适用性，甚至宣称独立于科学将改善前景。曾任哈佛、耶鲁和芝加哥大学教授的马歇尔·斯通，不久前的1961年再次肯定这个论点。他在题为《数学中的革命》的文章开头，赞颂数学对科学的重要性，随后继续说道：

Despite the evidence of history, some mathematicians still assert the future applicability of pure mathematics and in fact declare that independence from science will improve the prospects. This thesis was reaffirmed not too long ago (in 1961) by Marshall Stone, a professor at Harvard, Yale, and Chicago. Though he begins his article entitled “The Revolution in Mathematics” with a tribute to the importance of mathematics in science, Stone continues:

1900年以来，我们关于数学的概念或观点虽发生几项重要变化，但真正涉及观念革命的，是发现数学完全独立于物理世界……现在看来，数学与物理世界并无必然联系，除了“思考发生于大脑中”这一陈述所暗含的那种含糊而令人困惑的联系。毫不夸张地说，发现事情确实如此，标志着数学史上最重要的思想进步之一……

While several important changes have taken place since 1900 in our conception of mathematics or in our points of view concerning it, the one which truly involves a revolution in ideas is the discovery that mathematics is entirely independent of the physical world. . . . Mathematics is now seen to have no necessary connection with the physical world beyond the vague and mystifying one implicit in the statement that thinking takes place in the brain. The discovery that this is so may be said without exaggeration to mark one of the most significant intellectual advances in the history of mathematics. . . .

停下来将当今数学与19世纪末的数学比较，我们很可能惊讶于数学在数量和复杂性上的迅速增长；但也不应忽视，这一发展与强调抽象，以及日益关注广泛数学模式的认识和分析，联系多么紧密。事实上，仔细考察就会看到，只有数学脱离应用才可能出现的这种新方向，才是本世纪数学巨大活力与增长的真正源泉……

When we stop to compare the mathematics of today with mathematics as it was at the close of the nineteenth century we may well be amazed to note how rapidly our mathematics has grown in quantity and complexity, but we should also not fail to observe how closely this development has been involved with an emphasis on abstraction and an increasing concern with the perception and analysis of broad mathematical patterns. Indeed, upon closer examination we see that this new orientation, made possible only by the divorce of mathematics from its applications, has been the true source of its tremendous vitality and growth during the present century. . . .

现代数学家更愿意正面地把自己的学科界定为一般抽象体系的研究，每个体系都是由指定的抽象元素构建的建筑，其结构由元素之间任意、但明确规定的关系赋予……他会坚持认为，这些体系以及逻辑提供的研究其结构性质的手段，与物理世界都没有直接、即时或必然的联系……因为只有数学摆脱过去把它系于现实特定方面的束缚，才能成为极其灵活而强大的工具，使我们得以进入知识范围以外的领域。支持这一论点的例子已经很多……

A modern mathematician would prefer the positive characterization of his subject as the study of general abstract systems, each one of which is an edifice built of specified abstract elements and structured by the presence of arbitrary but unambiguously specified relations among them. . . . He would maintain that neither these systems nor the means provided by logic for studying their structural properties have any directly immediate or necessary connection with the physical world. . . . For it is only to the extent that mathematics is freed from the bonds which have attached it in the past to particular aspects of reality that it can become the extremely flexible and powerful instrument we need to break into areas beyond our ken. The examples which buttress this argument are already numerous. . . .

接着斯通提到遗传学、博弈论和通信的数学理论。实际上，这些例子很难为其论点辩护。它们都是应用可靠的古典数学而产生的。

Then Stone mentions genetics, game theory, and the mathematical theory of communication. Actually these are a poor defense of his thesis. They have come about by applying sound classical mathematics.

柯朗在1962年《SIAM评论》［工业与应用数学学会］发表的一篇文章中，反驳了斯通的论点：*

In an article which appeared in the SIAM Review [Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics] of 1962, Courant rebutted Stone’s thesis:*

这篇［斯通的］文章断言，我们生活在数学取得巨大成功的时代，远远超过自古至今的一切成就。“现代数学”的胜利归功于一个根本原则：抽象，以及数学有意识地脱离物理及其他实质内容。于是，数学心灵摆脱压舱物，能够翱翔高空，从那里完美地观察并驾驭地面的现实。

The article [by Stone] asserts that we live in an era of great mathematical successes, which outdistance everything achieved from antiquity until now. The triumph of “modern mathematics” is credited to one fundamental principle: abstraction and conscious detachment of mathematics from physical and other substance. Thus, the mathematical mind, freed from ballast, may soar to heights from which reality on the ground can be perfectly observed and mastered.

我不愿歪曲或贬低这位杰出作者的陈述及教育结论。但作为一种笼统主张，作为试图为研究、尤其为教育规定路线的尝试，这篇文章似乎是一个危险信号，而且肯定需要补充。狂热抽象主义的危险，又因这种风尚并非提倡胡说，而只是推销半真理这一事实而加剧。不能让片面的半真理扫除平衡的完整真理的重要方面。

I do not want to distort or belittle the statements and the pedagogical conclusions of the distinguished author. But as a sweeping claim, as an attempt to lay down a line for research and before all for education, the article seems a danger signal, and certainly in need of supplementation. The danger of enthusiastic abstractionism is compounded by the fact that this fashion does not at all advocate nonsense, but merely promotes a half truth. One-sided half truths must not be allowed to sweep aside the vital aspects of the balanced whole truth.

*经许可转载自《SIAM评论》，1962年10月，第297—320页。版权归SIAM所有，1962年。

“Reprinted with permission from SIAM Review, October 1962, pp. 297-320. Copyright by SIAM, 1962.

数学思想当然通过抽象运作；数学观念需要逐步进行抽象的精炼、公理化和结晶。确实，达到更高的结构洞见平台后，重要的简化就成为可能。当然也是真的——而且早已明确强调过——如果放弃把数学概念看作某种实体性现实的描述这一形而上学偏见，数学中的基本困难就会消失。

Certainly mathematical thought operates by abstraction; mathematical ideas are in need of abstract progressive refinement, axiomatization, crystallization. It is true indeed that important simplification becomes possible when a higher plateau of structural insight is reached. Certainly it is true—and has been clearly emphasized for a long time—that basic difficulties in mathematics disappear if one gives up the metaphysical prejudice of mathematical concepts as descriptions of a somehow substantive reality.

然而，我们科学的生命之血通过根系上升；根系不断分岔，深入可称为现实的东西，不论这种“现实”是力学、物理、生物形态、经济行为、大地测量，还是已属熟悉领域的其他数学实质。抽象和推广对数学的重要性，并不超过现象的个别性，尤其不超过归纳直觉。只有这些力量的相互作用与综合，才能使数学保持生命，防止它干枯成死骨架。我们必须反对把发展片面推向这一赋予生命的对立关系的一极。

Yet, the life blood of our science rises through its roots; these roots reach down in endless ramification deep into what might be called reality, whether this “reality” is mechanics, physics, biological form, economic behavior, geodesy, or, for that matter, other mathematical substance already in the realm of the familiar. Abstraction and generalization are not more vital for mathematics than individuality of phenomena and, before all, not more than inductive intuition. Only the interplay between these forces and their synthesis can keep mathematics alive and prevent its drying out into a dead skeleton. We must fight against attempts to push the development one-sidedly towards the one pole of the life-spending antinomy.

我们不能接受数学科学最终的正当理由是“人类心灵的荣耀”这种古老而亵渎的胡说。不能让数学分裂为“纯粹”和“应用”两种。它必须继续作为科学宽广洪流中一股统一而有活力的水流，并得到加强；必须防止它成为可能消失于沙中的小支流。

We must not accept the old blasphemous nonsense that the ultimate justification of mathematical science is “the glory of the human mind.” Mathematics must not be allowed to split and to diverge towards a “pure” and an “applied” variety. It must remain, and be strengthened as, a unified vital strand in the broad stream of science and must be prevented from becoming a little side brook that might disappear in the sand.

分化倾向内在于数学，却又构成始终存在的危险。孤立主义抽象派的狂热者确实危险。但不区分空洞的装腔作势与专注的追求的保守反动者，也同样危险。

The divergent tendencies are immanent in mathematics and yet prove an ever-present danger. Fanatics of isolationist abstractionism are dangerous indeed. But so are conservative reactionaries who do not discriminate between hollow pretense and dedicated aspirations.

柯朗并不否定抽象的价值。不过，他在1964年的文章中说，数学必须从具体、明确的实质内容中获得动机，并瞄准现实的某一层面。如果有必要飞入抽象，那也必须不只是逃避。重新返回地面不可或缺，即使同一位飞行员不能操纵航程的所有阶段。

Courant did not deny the value of abstraction. However, he said in an article of 1964 that mathematics must take its motivation from concrete specific substance and aim at some layer of reality. If a flight into abstraction is necessary, it must be something more than an escape. Re-entry to the ground is indispensable, even if the same pilot cannot handle all phases of the trajectory.

数学常被比作一棵根深而牢固地扎在肥沃自然土壤中的树。中央树干是数和几何图形，从树干长出的众多枝条代表许多发展。有些枝条粗壮，滋养许多富有生命的分枝。其他枝条产生细小分枝，对整个结构的规模和力量贡献不大。还有些枝条已经枯死。但最重要的是，树扎根于坚实大地。每根枝条都通过根和树干吸取现实。近来试图完全移除土壤，却仍维持整棵树、树根、树干及上部结构的努力，不可能成功。只有根系更深入肥沃土壤，众多枝条才能繁盛。试图嫁接不从现实获得养料的新枝的人，制造的是永远不会获得生命的死胎茎秆。充分努力之后，这些貌似枝条的东西可以做得像真枝，可以与活枝缠绕，仿佛从树干长出，但它们仍是死的，剪去也丝毫不损害活的生长。

Mathematics has often been compared with a tree whose roots are firmly and deeply grounded in rich natural soil. The central trunk is number and geometrical figure, and the outgrowths from this trunk of the multiplicity of branches represent the many developments. Some are stout and nourish many vital offshoots. Other branches have given rise to minor offshoots which contribute little to the size and strength of the entire structure. Still others are dead. But what is most relevant is that the tree is rooted in solid earth. Each branch draws on that reality through the roots and trunk. Recent efforts to remove the soil entirely and still sustain the tree, roots, trunk, and superstructure, can not succeed. The many branches will thrive only as the roots go deeper into fertile soil. Those who would graft on new branches having no nourishment in reality produce still-born stalks that will never acquire life. These would-be branches may, with enough effort, be made to look like real ones and may be made to intertwine with the live branches and seem to grow out of the trunk but they are nonetheless dead and can be lopped off with not the slightest harm to the live growth.

还有一些论点似乎削弱斯通的主张：自由研究纯数学，会增强应用数学并提供新方案。研究纯数学，不论其精深程度或研究者多么杰出，必定减弱一个人把数学推理用于实际情境的能力。如果把时间精力投入抽象数学，就不可避免地受到其氛围，以及成功从事它所必需的心态的影响。他了解应用需要、打造处理工具的时间也会减少。应用数学家注意抽象数学家正在做什么、取得了什么，是有益的；但过多关注会有害地分散资源。忽视应用导致孤立，并可能导致整个数学萎缩。

There are other arguments which seem to undermine Stone’s claim that the freedom to pursue pure mathematics will strengthen and contribute new approaches to applied mathematics. The pursuit of pure mathematics, no matter what the level of sophistication or how eminent the practitioner, must diminish a man’s power to apply mathematical reasoning to practical situations. If he spends time and energy on abstract mathematics, he will inevitably be influenced by its atmosphere and by the attitudes of mind necessary to its successful practice. He will also have less time to learn about the needs in applications and to fashion the tools for handling them. The applied mathematicians can usefully take note of what the abstract mathematicians are up to and what they achieve; but too much attention is a harmful diversion of resources. Disregard for applications leads to isolation and possibly to the atrophy of mathematics as a whole.

根据历史证据判断，斯通无疑错了。正如冯·诺伊曼在《数学家》（1947年）中指出的：

Judged by historical evidence, Stone is certainly wrong. As von Neumann pointed out in his essay “The Mathematician” (1947):

不可否认，数学中某些最好的灵感——甚至在那些纯粹程度达到人们想象极限的部分——来自自然科学……在我看来，数学最重要的特征事实，是它与自然科学，或者更一般地，与任何在高于纯描述层次上解释经验的科学之间，那种十分独特的关系。

It is undeniable that some of the best inspirations in mathematics— in those parts of it which are as pure mathematics as one can imagine—have come from the natural sciences. . . . The most vitally characteristic fact about mathematics is, in my opinion, its quite peculiar relationship to the natural sciences, or, more generally, to any science which interprets experience on a higher than purely descriptive level.

法国著名数学家洛朗·施瓦茨毫不犹豫地说，当今最活跃的领域，抽象代数和代数拓扑，没有应用。有些论文用这些领域的语言和概念装饰具体应用，却没有推进应用问题的解决。

Laurent Schwartz, a leading French mathematician, did not hesitate to say that today’s most active fields, abstract algebra and algebraic topology, have no application. Some papers dress up concrete applications in the language and concepts of these fields but make no advance in the solution of applied problems.

不过，纯粹抽象数学的倡导者并未让步。主要分析学家让·迪厄多内教授，在1964年的文章中，反对一种只以自身为食的数学会因缺乏养料而死亡的说法：

ITowever, the proponents of pure, abstract mathematics have not yielded. Professor Jean Dieudonne, a leading analyst, in an article of 1964 rejected the contention that a mathematics which feeds on itself will die for lack of nourishment:

我想强调，近来的历史多么不愿顺从那些灾难预言家的虔诚陈词滥调；他们定期警告，数学切断对其他科学的应用联系，必将承担可怕后果。我并非说，与理论物理等其他领域密切接触，对各方无益；但完全清楚的是，我谈到的所有惊人进展，除了广义函数理论可能是例外，没有一项与物理应用有关；甚至在偏微分方程理论中，如今的重点也更在于“内部”和结构问题，而非具有直接物理意义的问题。即使强行使数学与人类努力的所有其他渠道分离，我们科学内部仍待解决的大问题，也足以供数百年的思考之用。

I would like to stress how little recent history has been willing to conform to the pious platitudes of the prophets of doom, who regularly warn us of the dire consequences mathematics is bound to incur by cutting itself off from the applications to other sciences. I do not intend to say that close contact with other fields, such as theoretical physics, is not beneficial to all parties concerned; but it is perfectly clear that of all the striking progress I have been talking about, not a single one, with the possible exception of distribution theory, had anything to do with physical applications; and even in the theory of partial differential equations, the emphasis is now much more on “internal” and structural problems than on questions having a direct physical significance. Even if mathematics were to be forcibly separated from all other channels of human endeavor, there would remain food for centuries of thought in big problems we still have to solve within our science.

虽然迪厄多内看到纯数学中无穷无尽的问题，但为了公正对待他，必须补充，他并未吞下任何纯数学创造最终都会有用的论据。他列举许多纯数学研究，尤其是数论研究，并说：“无法想象这样的结果可能应用于任何物理问题。”此外，虽然他总体为纯数学辩护，却也论证，数学家夸耀其纯数学对科学的价值，是“一种温和的骗局”。他指出，纯数学家会费尽心力证明问题解的唯一性，却不尝试找出解。物理学家知道有唯一解——地球不会沿两条不同轨道运动——但他要的是实际轨道。

Though Dieudonne could see unending problems of pure mathematics, to be fair to the man one must add that he did not swallow the argument that any creation of pure mathematics will ultimately be useful. He cited many investigations of pure mathematics, particularly in the theory of numbers, of which he said, “It is inconceivable that such results might be applied to any physical problem.” Moreover, though he defended pure mathematics generally, he also argued that the boasting by mathematicians of the value of their pure mathematics to science is “a mild kind of swindle.” Pure mathematicians, he pointed out, will take great trouble to prove the uniqueness of a solution to a problem but won’t try to find the solution. The physicist knows there is a unique solution—the earth does not move on two different paths—but he wants the actual path.

对于应研究哪种数学及其价值，一位同样卓越、从事纯数学的人物更切合实际。1958年国际数学家大会上，拉尔斯·戈丁坦率地说：

More realistic about the value of the kind of mathematics that should be pursued is a man of equal stature who has worked in pure mathematics. At the International Congress of Mathematicians in 1958, he was frank. Said Lars Garding:

这里我无法讨论这个学科的许多重要部分，如差分方程、系统理论以及对量子力学和微分几何的应用。我的课题是偏微分算子的一般理论。它从古典物理中成长起来，却没有对物理真正重要的应用。不过，物理仍是它有趣问题的主要源泉。我感觉，我所作的这类一般性报告，也许不如定期综述物理中那些似乎需要新数学技术的未决问题有用。这些综述对专家当然不是新闻，却会给许多数学家提供值得研究的问题。有计划地促进物理与数学相互作用的努力很少，它们应当成为国际数学大会的主要关切之一。

I cannot go here into many important parts of the subject like difference equations, the theory of systems and applications to quantum mechanics and differential geometry. My subject has been the general theory of partial differential operators. It has grown out of classical physics, but has no really important applications to it. Still physics remains its main source of interesting problems. I have the feeling that general talks of the kind I have given are perhaps less useful than periodical surveys of unsolved problems in physics which seem to require new mathematical techniques. Such surveys will of course not be news to specialists, but they will provide many mathematicians with worthwhile problems. Planned efforts to further the interaction between physics and mathematics have been rare. They ought to be one of the major concerns of the international mathematical congresses.

那些夸耀创造不受物理世界玷污的数学，并在压力下坚持说，他人有朝一日会为他们目前无意义的努力找到正当理由的人，可以任其在自己的思想轨道上工作。但他们违背整个历史进程。他们相信，数学摆脱科学的束缚，会产生更丰富、更多样、更有成果的课题，适用范围远超旧数学；这种信心除了言辞，没有任何支持。

Those who boast of creating mathematics untainted by the physical world and maintain under pressure that others will some day find justification for their currently pointless endeavors may be left to work in their own mental grooves. But they contradict the entire course of history. Their confidence that a mathematics freed from bondage to science will produce richer, more varied, and more fruitful themes that will be applicable to far more than the older mathematics is not backed by anything but words.

纯数学的倡导者可以、也确实为其工作提出其他价值主张，即内在美和智力挑战。不能否认存在这些价值。不过，它们能否为纯数学的巨大产量辩护，确实可以质疑。无论对这些问题作何判断，这些价值都无助于数学历来最主要的重要性，即自然研究。美和智力挑战，是为数学自身而作的数学。诚然，这些内在价值值得更充分的认可，超出当前关于数学孤立的讨论所容许的范围。

The proponents of pure mathematics can and do make other claims for the value of their work, namely, intrinsic beauty and intellectual challenge. That there are such values cannot be denied. However, that they justify the enormous output of pure mathematics can indeed be challenged. Regardless of any judgments in these matters, these values do not contribute to what has been the major importance of mathematics, namely, the study of nature. Beauty and intellectual challenge are mathematics for mathematics’ sake. Admittedly the worth of these intrinsic values warrants more recognition than the present discussion of the isolation of mathematics permits.

纯数学的捍卫者和批评者显然彼此不和。任何争论都会引出幽默或讽刺的话。应用数学家不关心严格证明；他们最关心的是推论与物理事件相符。奥利弗·亥维赛是典型人物，他使用在纯数学家看来毫无依据、离奇古怪的技术，因此受到严厉批评。亥维赛蔑视他所谓的逻辑咬文嚼字者，回答说：“逻辑可以耐心等待，因为它是永恒的。”稍后，他更让纯数学家困惑。当时，所谓发散级数遭到禁止。亥维赛谈到一个特定级数时说：“哈，级数发散了；现在我们可以拿它做点事情。”结果，亥维赛的技术全部得到严密化，甚至提供了新数学课题。为了惹恼纯粹派，应用数学家说，纯数学家能在任何解答中找到困难，而应用数学家能为任何困难找到解答。

The defenders and critics of pure mathematics are clearly at odds with each other. All controversies prompt some humorous or sarcastic remarks. The applied mathematicians are not concerned with rigorous proof. For them agreement of their deductions with physical events is the chief concern. Typical of these men was Oliver Heaviside, who used what seemed to the pure mathematicians to be totally unjustified and outlandish techniques. Consequently, he was severely criticized. Heaviside was contemptuous of what he called the logic-choppers. He replied, “Logic can be patient for it is eternal.” Somewhat later he confounded the pure mathematicians still more. At that time, what are called divergent series were outlawed. Heaviside said of a particular one, “Ha, the series diverges; now we can do something with it.” It turns out that Heaviside’s techniques have all been rigorized and even have supplied new mathematical themes. To nettle the purists, the applied mathematicians have remarked that the pure mathematicians can find the difficulty in any solution, but the applied men can find the solution to any difficulty.

应用数学家又嘲讽纯粹派：应用问题由物理现象规定，相关数学家必须解决，而纯数学家可以自己创造问题。应用派说，后者就像在黑暗街道丢了钥匙的人，却转到路灯下寻找，因为那里光更亮。

The applied mathematicians make another gibe at the purists. Applied problems are set by physical phenomena and the mathematicians concerned are obliged to solve them while the pure mathematicians can create their own problems. The latter, the applied people say, are like a man who, searching for a key lost in some dark street, moves to search for it under a street lamp because there is more light there.

为进一步贬低对手，应用数学家还讲另一个故事。一个人有一包待洗衣服，到处寻找洗衣店。他发现一家商店，橱窗的牌子写着“本店洗衣”，便进去把包放在柜台上。店主有些惊讶，问：“这是什么？”那人回答：“我把这些衣服拿来洗。”“但我们这里不洗衣服，”店主答道。这回吃惊的是准顾客。他指着牌子问：“那牌子怎么回事？”“哦，”店主说，“我们只是制作牌子。”

To further belittle their opponents, the applied mathematicians tell another tale. A man has a bundle of clothes to be laundered and looks around for a laundry. He finds a store with a sign in the window, “Laundry Done Here,” enters, and puts his bundle on the counter. The storekeeper looks a little astonished and asks, “What is this?” The man answers, “I brought these clothes in to be laundered.” “But we don’t launder clothes here,” the storekeeper replies. This time it is the would-be customer who is astonished. He points to the sign and asks, “What about that sign?” “Oh,” says the storekeeper, “we just make the signs.”

纯数学家与应用数学家的争论继续着；既然现在纯数学家掌权，他们就能俯视误入歧途的兄弟，甚至责备他们。正如克利福德·E.特鲁斯德尔教授指出的：“‘应用数学’，是那些自称‘纯’数学家的人，向他们认为不纯的人发出的侮辱……但‘纯’数学若成为否认自身源于人的感知的弑父式任性，成为排斥不纯者的口令，就是上个世纪发明的一种疾病……”它成为自身的目的，不考虑能为任何目标服务。它本身并非一种至福状态。数学旨在发现值得知道的东西。如今，研究产生研究，研究又产生研究。在今天数学的殿堂中，人们不敢询问意义与目的。数学不许被现实玷污。常春藤长得如此茂密，里面的研究者再看不到外部世界。这些隔绝的心灵对孤立感到满足。

The controversy between pure and applied mathematicians continues, and since the pure mathematicians now rule the roost, they can look down at their misguided brethren and even reprove them. As Professor Clifford E. Truesdell has noted, “‘Applied mathematics’ is an insult directed by those who consider themselves ‘pure’ mathematicians at those whom they take for impure. . . . but ‘pure’ mathematics as a parricide tantrum denying growth from human sensation, as a shibboleth to cast out the impure, is a disease invented in the last century. . . .” It has become an end in itself with no thought of what objective it might serve. It is not, in itself, a state of beatitude. Mathematics aims to discover something worth knowing. As matters stand now, research begets research, which begets research. In the halls of mathematics today, one dare not ask for meaning and purpose. Mathematics must not be tainted by reality. The ivy has grown so thick that the researchers within can no longer see the world outside. These sequestered minds are content in their isolation.

数学家可以彼此争执，但物理学家及其他科学家只能痛惜自己被弃之不顾。听听直到不久前仍在麻省理工学院任杰出教授的约翰·C.斯莱特怎么说：

Mathematicians may disagree among themselves, but physicists and other scientists can only deplore that they have been left in the lurch. Let us listen to Professor John C. Slater, a distinguished professor until recently at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology:

物理学家从数学家那里得到的帮助很少。每有一位像冯·诺伊曼那样认识到［前述］问题、并实际作出贡献的数学家，就有二十位对此毫无兴趣，要么在与物理关系遥远的领域工作，要么强调数学物理中较旧、较熟悉的部分。在这种情况下，物理学家望着数学家，觉得他们偏离了使数学过去伟大的道路，并认为除非他们再次坚决进入数学物理进步的主流——过去引导数学取得最丰硕发展的主流——否则无法重回正轨，难道奇怪吗？……物理学家坚信，这是当今数学家能够达到伟大的唯一道路。

The physicist finds very little help from the mathematician. For every mathematician like von Neumann who realizes these problems [described earlier], and contributes practically to them, there are twenty who have no interest in them, who either work in fields of remote interest to physics, or who stress the older and more familiar parts of mathematical physics. Is it any wonder that in such a situation the physicist, looking at the mathematicians, feels that they have strayed from the path which has led to the past greatness of mathematics, and feels that they will not regain this path until they again resolutely enter the main current of progress of mathematical physics, the current which in the past has led to the most fruitful development of mathematics. . . . That, the physicist firmly feels, is the only path through which the mathematician of the present can achieve greatness.

1972年，弗里曼·J.戴森教授向数学家所作的一次重要演讲，以忽视科学为主题。戴森是一位诺贝尔物理学奖得主，他指出过去和现在数学家有机会研究一些重大而突出的科学问题，却未着手研究。其中某些问题或片段，不知怎样渗入数学，但数学家不知道其起源和物理意义，因此沿任意方向前进，或看不出自己取得了什么。用戴森的话说，数学与物理的婚姻以离婚告终。

The neglect of science was the subject of a major lecture by Professor Freeman J. Dyson to mathematicians in 1972. Dyson, a Nobel prize-winner in physics, pointed out opportunities, past and present, for mathematicians to take up significant and outstanding problems of science, but which they failed to take up. Some of these problems or fragments of them have somehow seeped into mathematics, but the mathematicians do not know their origin and physical significance. Hence they head in arbitrary directions or do not perceive what they have accomplished. As Dyson puts it, the marriage of mathematics and physics has ended in divorce.

本世纪，脱离科学的进程加速了。如今，经常听到和读到数学家独立于科学的宣言。数学家不再犹豫，公开说自己只对数学本身感兴趣，对科学漠不关心。虽没有精确统计，但当今活跃数学家约百分之九十不懂科学，而且相当满足于保持这种幸福状态。尽管有历史和一些反对，转向抽象、为推广而推广、研究任意选取问题的趋势继续着。为了更多了解具体情形而研究整类问题，以及为了把握问题本质而进行抽象，这些合理需要，已经成为为一般性和抽象本身而研究它们的借口。

The break from science has been accelerated during this century. Today it is common to hear and read mathematicians’ declarations of independence from science. Mathematicians no longer hesitate to speak freely of their interest solely in mathematics proper and their indifference to science. Though no precise statistics are available, about ninety percent of the mathematicians active today are ignorant of science and are quite content to remain in that blissful state. Despite the history and some opposition, the trend to abstraction, to generalization for the sake of generalization, and to the pursuit of arbitrarily chosen problems has continued. The reasonable need for study of an entire class of problems in order to learn more about concrete cases and for abstraction in order to get at the essence of a problem has become an excuse for tackling generalities and abstractions in and for themselves.

数百年来，人类创造了欧几里得几何、托勒密理论、日心说、牛顿力学、电磁理论，以及近来的相对论和量子理论等宏伟结构。如今我们知道，在这些以及其他重要而强大的科学体系中，数学都是构造方法、框架，甚至实质。数学理论使我们得以了解一些自然，把看似不同的多种现象纳入全面而可理解的叙述。数学理论揭示了人类在自然中发现的一切秩序和设计，使我们能够驾驭、或部分驾驭广大领域。

Over the centuries man created such grand structures as Euclidean geometry, the Ptolemaic theory, the heliocentric theory, Newtonian mechanics, electromagnetic theory, and in recent times relativity and quantum theory. In all of these and in other significant and powerful bodies of science, mathematics as we now know is the method of construction, the framework, and indeed the essence. Mathematical theories have enabled us to know something of nature, to embrace in comprehensive intelligible accounts varieties of seemingly diverse phenomena. Mathematical theories have revealed whatever order and plan man has found in nature and have given us mastery or partial mastery over vast domains.

但大多数数学家已经抛弃传统和遗产。自然传给感官的丰富讯息，如今遇到的是紧闭的眼睛和不留意的耳朵。数学家依靠前人赢得的声誉生活，仍期望获得旧工作所值得的赞誉和支持。纯数学家更进一步，把应用数学家逐出兄弟会，期望垄断数学家这一光荣称号，独享给予前人的荣耀。他们丢弃了丰富的观念源泉，如今正在耗费先前积累的财富。他们追随一道微光，被引出这个世界。诚然，有些人知道过去激励数学研究、使牛顿和高斯等人获得荣誉的崇高传统，仍声称其数学工作对科学有潜在价值。他们谈论为科学创造模型，但其实并不关心这个目标。事实上，大多数现代数学家不懂科学，不可能在创造模型。他们宁愿保持处子之身，也不愿与科学同床。总体而言，数学如今转向内部，以自身为食；若根据过去发生的事情判断，现代数学研究的大部分极不可能推进科学，数学可能注定在黑暗中摸索。数学现在几乎完全自成一体，沿自身相关性与卓越性标准所决定的方向前进，甚至为独立于外部问题、动机和灵感而自豪。它不再有统一性和目的。

But most mathematicians have abandoned their traditions and heritage. The pregnant messages that nature sends to the senses now fall on closed eyes and inattentive ears. Mathematicians are living on the reputation earned by their predecessors and still expect the acclaim and support that the older work warranted. The pure mathematicians have gone further. They have expelled the applied mathematicians from their fraternity in the hope that by cornering the honorable title of mathematician they alone will gain the glory accorded to their predecessors. They have thrown away their rich source of ideas and are now spending their previously accumulated wealth. They have followed a gleam that has led them out of this world. It is true that some, aware of the noble tradition that motivated mathematical research in the past and warranted the honor accorded to the Newtons and Gausses, still claim potential value of their mathematical work for science. They speak of creating models for science. But in truth they are not concerned with this goal. In fact, since most modern mathematicians know no science, they can’t be creating models. They prefer to remain virgins rather than to bed with science. On the whole mathematics is now turned inward; it feeds on itself; and it is extremely unlikely, if one may judge by what happened in the past, that most of the modern mathematical research will ever contribute to the advancement of science; mathematics may be doomed to grope in darkness. Mathematics is now an almost entirely self-contained enterprise. Moving in directions determined by its own criteria of relevance and excellence, it is even proud of its independence from outside problems, motivations, and inspirations. It no longer has unity and purpose.

当今大多数数学家的孤立，由于许多原因而令人痛惜。数学在科学和技术中的用途正以巨大速度扩展。直到不久前，笛卡尔的愿景——数学代表人类理智的最高成就、理性对经验主义的胜利，以及以数学为基础的方法最终渗透科学所有领域——似乎更接近实现。但就在数学方法向许多领域扩展时，数学家却缩到角落里。一百年前及更早，数学与物理科学密切交织（当然以柏拉图主义为基础），此后却分离了，分离在当代已十分明显。数学之所以有价值，是因为有助于理解和驾驭自然，这一事实已被遗忘。大多数当代数学家希望使学科孤立，只提供超然研究。一方坚守古老而光荣的数学活动动机，那些动机过去提供最富成果的课题；另一方顺风而行、研究心血来潮的东西，双方分裂明显。一个世纪越来越纯的数学使大多数数学家蒙蔽了双眼，失去阅读自然之书的能力和意愿。他们转向抽象代数、拓扑等领域，转向泛函分析这样的抽象与推广，转向远离应用的微分方程存在性证明，转向各种思想体系的公理化，以及枯燥的脑力游戏。只有少数仍尝试解决更具体的问题，尤其在微分方程及相关领域。

The isolation of most mathematicians today is deplorable for many reasons. The scientific and technological uses of mathematics are expanding at an enormous rate. Until recently, the vision of Descartes that mathematics represents the supreme achievement of the human intellect, the triumph of reason over empiricism, and the eventual pervasion of all fields of science by mathematically-based methodologies seemed closer to realization. But just when the mathematical approach to so many fields was spreading, the mathematicians withdrew into a corner. Whereas one hundred years ago and farther back mathematics and the physical sciences were intimately involved with each other (on a Platonic basis of course), since that time they have separated, and the separation has become marked in our time. The fact that mathematics is valuable because it contributes to the understanding and mastery of nature has been lost sight of. Most present-day mathematicians wish to isolate their subject and offer only an aloof study. The schism between those who would cleave to the ancient and honorable motivations for mathematical activity, the motivations that in the past supplied the most fruitful themes, and those who, sailing with the wind, investigate what strikes their fancy is pronounced. Blinded by a century of ever purer mathematics, most mathematicians have lost the skill and the will to read the book of nature. They have turned to fields such as abstract algebra and topology, to abstractions and generalizations such as functional analysis, to existence proofs for differential equations that are remote from applications, to axiomatizations of various bodies of thought, and to arid brain games. Only a few still attempt to solve the more concrete problems, notably in differential equations and allied fields.

大多数数学家放弃科学，是否意味着科学将被剥夺数学？完全不是。少数有识之士注意到，未来的牛顿、拉普拉斯和哈密顿，将像过去一样，创造自己需要的数学。这些人虽以数学家之名受到尊敬，却是物理学家。理查德·柯朗在1957年为弗朗茨·雷利希写的讣文中说，如果当前趋势继续，“就有这样的危险：未来的‘应用’数学由物理学家和工程师发展，著名的专业数学家将与新发展毫无联系。”柯朗把“应用”加上引号，因为他真正指的是所有重要的数学。他不区分纯数学与应用数学。

Does the abandonment of science by most mathematicians mean that science will be deprived of mathematics? Not at all. A few discerning mathematicians have noted that the Newtons, Laplaces, and Hamiltons of the future will create the mathematics they will need just as they have in the past. These men, though honored as mathematicians, were physicists. In an obituary of Franz Rellich that Richard Courant wrote in 1957, he said that if present trends continue, “There exists the danger that the ‘applied’ mathematics of the future will be developed by physicists and engineers, and the professional mathematicians of rank will have no connection with the new development.” Courant put quotes around the word applied because he really meant all significant mathematics. Fie did not distinguish pure and applied mathematics.

柯朗的预言正在实现。数学界的当权者偏爱纯数学，因此最好的应用工作，如今由电气工程、计算机科学、生物、物理、化学和天文学中的科学家完成。纯粹派就像格列佛去拉普他旅行时遇到的数学家，生活在悬于大地上空的岛上。他们把大地上的社会问题留给别人。这些数学家还能在过去数学家为学科提供的气氛中生活一阵，但最终注定在真空中死去。

Courant’s prophesy is being fulfilled. Because the establishment in the mathematical community favors pure mathematics, the best applied work is now being done by scientists in electrical engineering, computer science, biology, physics, chemistry, and astronomy. Like the mathematicians Gulliver met on his voyage to Laputa, the purists live on an island suspended in the air above the earth. They leave to others the problems of society on the earth itself. These mathematicians will live for a while in the atmosphere which mathematicians of the past supplied to the subject but they are doomed ultimately to expire in a vacuum.

塔列朗曾说，理想主义者若不是现实主义者，就无法长久存在；现实主义者若不是理想主义者，也无法长久存在。用于数学，这一观察说明，需要把真实问题理想化，并抽象研究；但也说明，忽视现实的理想主义者的工作不会存续。数学应当脚踏大地，头入云端。抽象与具体问题的相互作用，产生有生命、有活力、有意义的数学。数学家或许喜欢飞入抽象思想的云层，但像鸟一样，他们必须返回大地觅食。纯数学可能像餐后蛋糕，满足食欲，也多少滋养身体；但若无真实问题提供肉和土豆式的基本养料，身体无法只靠蛋糕生存。

Talleyrand once remarked that an idealist cannot last long unless he is a realist and a realist cannot last long unless he is an idealist. When applied to mathematics, this observation speaks for the need to idealize real problems and to study them abstractly but it also says that the work of the idealist who ignores reality will not survive. Mathematics should have its feet on the ground and its head in the clouds. It is the interplay between abstraction and concrete problems that produces live, vital, significant mathematics. Mathematicians may like to soar into the clouds of abstract thought, but like birds they must return to earth for food. Pure mathematics may be like cake for dessert. It pleases the appetite and even nourishes the system somewhat, but the body cannot survive on cake without the meat and potatoes of real problems for basic nourishment.

危险在于过多关注人为问题。如果当前强调纯数学的趋势继续，未来数学虽仍同名，却不再是过去受到我们珍视的学科。数学是一项奇妙发明，但奇妙之处在于，人的心灵能够为复杂而似乎不可理解的自然现象构造可理解的模型，从而给予人一些启示与力量。

The danger lies in too much attention to artificial questions. If the present emphasis on pure mathematics continues, the mathematics of the future will not be the subject we have valued in the past, though it bears the same name. Mathematics is a marvelous invention, but the marvel lies in the human mind’s capacity to construct understandable models of complex and seemingly inscrutable natural phenomena and thereby give man some enlightenment and power.

不过，个人必须有选择自己道路的自由。荷马在《奥德赛》中说：“不同的人喜欢不同的行动。”荷马之后的世纪，诗人阿尔基洛科斯说：“每个人必须以自己的方式使心灵欢悦。”歌德表达相同思想：“个人仍有自由，去从事吸引他、使他愉快、在他看来可能有用的事情。”不过，歌德补充：“人类应当研究的是人。”就我们的目的，可以改述为：数学家应当研究的是自然。正如弗朗西斯·培根在《Novum organon》（《新工具》［推理的新工具］）中所说：“科学真正而合法的目标，是赋予人类生活新的发明与财富。”

However, the individual must be free to choose his own course. Homer said in the Odyssey, “Different men take delight in different actions,” and in the century after Homer the poet Archilochus put it, “Each man must have his heart cheered in his own way.” Goethe expressed the same thought: “To the individual remains the freedom to occupy himself with what attracts him, what gives him pleasure, what seems to him likely to be useful.” However, Goethe added, “the proper study of mankind is man.” For our purposes we might paraphrase, the proper study of mathematicians is nature. As Francis Bacon put it in his Novum organon (New Instrument [of reasoning]). “But the real and legitimate goal of the sciences is the endowment of human life with new inventions and riches.”

归根结底，必须由健全判断决定什么研究值得追求。数学界应关注的区分，不是纯数学与应用数学，而是具有合理目标的数学与满足个人目标和心血来潮的数学，有所指向与毫无意义的数学，重要与不重要的数学，富有生命与毫无生气的数学。

In the final analysis, sound judgment must decide what research is worth pursuing. The distinction with which the mathematical world should be concerned is not between pure and applied mathematics but between mathematics that is undertaken with sound objectives and mathematics that satisfies personal goals and whims, between pointed mathematics and pointless mathematics, between significant and insignificant mathematics, and between vital and bloodless mathematics.

第十四章 数学何去何从？

XIV. Whither Mathematics?

谦卑下来吧，无能的理性！

Humble thyself, impotent reason!

帕斯卡

Pascal

我们详细叙述了数学家为确定什么是可靠数学、创造新数学应采用什么基础，而面临的日益增加的困惑，揭示了当前的困境。甚至数学家从工作中获得的一项慰藉，即数学应用于科学时惊人的有效性，也不再能安慰他们，因为大多数数学家已经放弃应用。数学家怎样回应这种两难，又能期待什么？数学的实质是什么？

Our lengthy account of the successively increasing perplexities which mathematicians confronted in attempting to determine what sound mathematics is and what foundation they should adopt in pursuing the creation of new mathematics has revealed the current plight. Even the one solace mathematicians derived from their work, namely, its remarkably effective applicability to science, can no longer be a comfort because most mathematicians have abandoned applications. How do mathematicians react to their dilemma and to what can they look forward? What is the essence of mathematics?

先回顾数学怎样陷入当前困境，以及根本问题究竟是什么。最先开始构建数学的埃及和巴比伦数学家，根本无法预见将建成怎样的结构，因此没有打下深厚基础，而直接在地表上建造。当时，大地似乎提供了可靠基底，他们用以开始建造的材料，即关于数和几何图形的事实，取自简单的尘世经验。我们至今使用geometry，即土地测量这个词，标示着数学的这一历史起源。

Let us first review how mathematics became involved in its present plight and just what the fundamental issues are. The Egyptian and Babylonian mathematicians, who first began building mathematics, were not at all able to foresee what kind of structure they would erect. Hence they did not lay a deep foundation. Rather they built directly on the surface of the earth. At that time the earth seemed to offer a secure base, and the material with which they commenced construction, facts about numbers and geometrical figures, was taken from simple earthly experiences. This historical origin of mathematics is signalized by our continuing use of the word geometry, the measurement of land.

但结构开始高出地面后，显然摇摇欲坠，继续加建可能危及它。古典时期的希腊人不仅看出危险，还提供必要的重建。他们采取两项措施。首先，选择坚实的地带，沿其建造墙壁。这些地带就是关于空间与整数的自明真理。其次，把钢材放进框架。钢材就是对结构中每一新增部分的演绎证明。

But as the structure began to rise above the ground it became obvious that it was shaky and that further additions might imperil it. The Greeks of the classical period not only saw the danger but supplied the necessary rebuilding. They adopted two measures. The first was to select firm strips of ground along which one could run the walls. These strips were the self-evident truths about space and the whole numbers. The second was to put steel into the framework. The steel was deductive proof of each addition to the structure.

就希腊时代发展的数学而言，主要由欧几里得几何构成的结构，被证明是稳定的。但一个缺陷显露了：某些线段，例如两直角边各长1单位的等腰直角三角形的斜边，必须具有2单位的长度。希腊人只承认普通整数，因此不接受2这样的实体。他们排斥这些无理“数”，并放弃给线段、面积和体积赋予数值的观念，从而解决困境。因此，除整数及可纳入几何结构的内容外，他们没有为算术和代数加建。诚然，有些亚历山大里亚的希腊人，尤其阿基米德，确实使用无理数运算，但没有把它们纳入数学的逻辑结构。

Insofar as mathematics was developed in Greek times, the structure, consisting mainly of Euclidean geometry, proved to be stable. One fault did show up, namely, that certain line segments—such as the diagonal of an isosceles right triangle whose arms are 1 unit long—would have to have a length of 2 units. Since the only numbers the Greeks recognized were the ordinary whole numbers, they would not accept such entities as 2. They resolved the dilemma by ostracizing these irrational “numbers,” and abandoning the idea of assigning numerical lengths to line segments, areas, and volumes. Hence, they built no additions to arithmetic and algebra beyond the whole numbers and what could be incorporated into the structure of geometry. It is true that some Alexandrian Greeks, notably Archimedes, did operate with irrational numbers, but these were not incorporated into the logical structure of mathematics.

印度人和阿拉伯人在建筑上加盖楼层，却不太关心稳定性。首先，约公元600年，印度人引入负数。随后，印度人和阿拉伯人不像希腊人那样挑剔，不仅接受无理数，还制定了其运算规则。文艺复兴时期的欧洲人接受希腊、印度和阿拉伯数学，最初却不愿接受这些异质元素。然而，科学需要占了上风，欧洲人克服了对数学逻辑可靠性的顾虑。

The Hindus and Arabs piled new floors on to the building with little concern for stability. First of all, about the year a.d. 600 the Hindus introduced negative numbers. Then the Hindus and Arabs, less fastidious than the Greeks, not only accepted irrational numbers but even developed rules for operating with them. The Renaissance Europeans, who adopted the mathematics of the Greeks, Hindus, and Arabs, at first balked at accepting these foreign elements. However, the needs of science prevailed and the Europeans overcame their concern for the logical soundness of mathematics.

通过扩展数的数学，印度人、阿拉伯人和欧洲人一层层加盖：复数、更多代数、微积分、微分方程、微分几何，以及许多其他学科。但他们不用钢材，而用直觉和物理论证构成的木柱与木梁。这些支撑却不堪重负，墙壁开始出现裂缝。到1800年，结构再次面临危险，数学家急忙以钢材替换木材。

By expanding the mathematics of number, the Hindus, Arabs, and Europeans added floor after floor: complex numbers, more algebra, the calculus, differential equations, differential geometry, and many more subjects. However, in place of steel they used wooden columns and beams composed of intuitive and physical arguments. But these supports proved unequal to their load and cracks began to show in the walls. By 1800, the structure was once again in peril and mathematicians hastened to replace the wood with steel.

加固上层结构之际，墙下的地基——希腊人选择的公理——塌陷了。非欧几里得几何的创建表明，欧几里得几何的公理并非真正坚实的地带，只是表面观察时显得如此。非欧几里得几何的公理也不是更坚固的地基。数学家相信心灵可靠地支持自己的认识，视为自然现实的东西，却被证明是不可靠的感官资料。更添烦恼的是，新代数的创建迫使数学家认识到，数的性质在现实中的根基，并不比几何的性质更牢固。因此，整个数学结构，几何、算术及其延伸出的代数与分析，都处于严重危险中。这座已然高耸的建筑，面临崩塌并陷入泥潭的危险。

While the superstructure was being strengthened, the ground—the axioms chosen by the Greeks—caved in under the walls. The creation of non-Euclidean geometry revealed that the axioms of Euclidean geometry were not truly solid strips of earth but only seemed so on superficial inspection. Nor were the axioms of the non-Euclidean geometries a firmer ground. What the mathematicians took to be the reality of nature, believing that their minds gave unfailing support for this cognition, proved to be unreliable sense data. To add to their troubles, the creation of new algebras forced the mathematicians to realize that the properties of number were no more firmly grounded in reality than those of geometry. Thus, the entire structure of mathematics, geometry, and arithmetic with its extentions to algebra and analysis, was in grave peril. The by now lofty building was in danger of collapsing and sinking into a quagmire.

维持数学结构需要有力措施，数学家迎接了挑战。显然，没有坚实的大地可为数学奠基，因为自然那似乎牢固的地面已证明具有欺骗性。但也许通过建造另一类坚实基础，可以使结构稳定。这将由措辞明确的定义、完整的公理组，以及对所有结果的明确证明组成，不论结果在直觉上多么明显。此外，逻辑一致性将取代真理。定理须精心交织，使整个结构牢固（第七章）。通过19世纪末的公理化活动，数学家似乎实现了结构的牢固。因此，数学虽失去现实根基，数学史上的又一次危机却解决了。

To maintain the structure of mathematics called for strong measures, and the mathematicians rose to the challenge. It was clear that there was no solid earth on which to base mathematics, for the seemingly firm ground of nature had proved to be deceptive. But perhaps the structure could be made stable by erecting a solid foundation of another kind. This would consist of sharply worded definitions, complete sets of axioms, and explicit proof of all results no matter how obvious they might seem to the intuition. Moreover, in place of truth there was to be logical consistency. The theorems were to be carefully interwoven, so that the entire structure would be solid (Chapter VII). Through the axiomatic activity of the late nineteenth century, the mathematicians seemingly achieved the solidity of the structure. And so, though mathematics lost its grounding in reality, another crisis in the history of mathematics was resolved.

不幸的是，新结构地基中使用的水泥没有适当凝固。建造者没有保证其一致性；集合论矛盾出现时，数学家认识到，更严重的危机威胁着他们的作品。当然，他们不会坐看数百年努力化为废墟。既然一致性依赖推理所选的基础，显然只有重建整个数学基础才够。重建数学赖以立足的基底，即逻辑公理与数学公理，必须加固，因此工作者决定挖得更深。不幸的是，他们对怎样以及在哪里加固基础意见不一；每人都声称能确保牢固，却各自以自己的方式重建。所得结构不是高大而根基牢固，而是摊铺开来且不稳固；每一翼都声称自己是唯一的数学殿堂，各自收藏它所认为的数学思想瑰宝。

Unfortunately, the cement used in the foundation of the new structure did not harden properly. Its consistency had not been guaranteed by the builders, and when the contradictions of set theory appeared, mathematicians realized that an even graver crisis threatened their handiwork. Of course, they were not going to sit by and see centuries of effort crumble into ruins. Since consistency was dependent on the bases chosen for the reasoning, it seemed clear that only a reconstruction of the entire foundation of mathematics would suffice. The base on which the reconstructed mathematics rested, the logical and mathematical axioms, had to be strengthened, and so the workers decided to dig more deeply. Unfortunately, they disagreed about how and where to strengthen the foundations and so, while each maintained that he would ensure solidity, each set about rebuilding in his own way. The resulting structure was not tall and firmly grounded but sprawling and insecure, with each wing claiming to be the sole temple of mathematics and each housing what it regarded as the gems of mathematical thought.

我们年轻时无疑都读过七个盲人摸象的故事。每个人触摸大象不同部位，对大象是什么得出自己的结论。同样，数学也许是比大象更优雅的结构，却对从不同观点考察它的基础研究者代表不同的知识整体。

When we were young, all of us undoubtedly read the story of the seven blind men and the elephant. Each man touched a different part of the elephant and drew his own conclusions about what the elephant was. So mathematics, perhaps a more graceful structure than an elephant, represents different bodies of knowledge to the foundationalists who contemplated it from different points of view.

于是数学进入这样一个阶段：人们对于什么才可恰当地称为数学，持有冲突的观点——逻辑主义、直觉主义、形式主义和集合论。而且每种建构内部，又有略为分歧的上层结构。直觉主义者对于哪些是根本而可靠的直觉有分歧：只接受整数，还是也接受某些无理数；排中律只用于有限集合，还是用于可数集合；以及构造方法的概念。逻辑主义者只依赖逻辑，却对可归约性、选择和无穷公理有疑虑。集合论者可以沿几个不同方向中的任何一个前进，取决于接受还是否定选择公理和连续统假设。甚至形式主义者也能走许多道路。有些人对确立一致性应使用的元数学原则有分歧。希尔伯特倡导的有穷原则，甚至不足以证明一阶谓词逻辑的完备性，当然也不足以确立其形式数学体系的一致性。因此，人们使用了非有穷方法（第十二章）。此外，哥德尔表明，在希尔伯特规定的限制下，任何重要的形式体系都包含不可判定命题，即独立于公理的命题。人们于是可以把这样的命题或其否定作为附加公理。但作出选择后，根据哥德尔的结果，扩大的体系也必须包含不可判定命题，于是又可选择。这个过程实际上无穷无尽。

Thus mathematics reached the stage where men held conflicting views of what may properly be designated mathematics—logicism, intuitionism, formalism, and set theory. Moreover within each construction there are somewhat diverging superstructures. Thus intuitionists differ in what they accept as fundamental, sound intuitions—the whole numbers only or also some irrationals, the law of excluded middle applied to finite sets only or to countable sets, and concepts of constructive methods. The logicists rely solely on logic and yet have misgivings about the axioms of reducibility, choice, and infinity. The set-theorists can proceed in any one of several distinct directions, depending on their acceptance or rejection of the axiom of choice and the continuum hypothesis. Even the formalists can pursue many paths. Some differ on the principles of metamathematics that should be used to establish consistency. The finit-istic principles advocated by Hilbert do not suffice to prove the completeness of even the predicate (first order) logic, and certainly do not suffice to establish the consistency of Hilbert’s formal mathematical systems. Hence non-finitistic methods have been used (Chapter XII). Further, under the limitations imposed by Hilbert, Godel showed that any significant formal system contains undecidable propositions, propositions that are independent of the axioms. One could then take either such a proposition or its denial as an additional axiom. However, after this choice, the enlarged system must, according to Godel’s result, also contain undecidable propositions and so a choice again becomes possible. The process is in fact unending.

逻辑主义者、形式主义者和集合论者依赖公理基础。本世纪头几十年，这种基础被赞颂为构建数学的最佳基底。但哥德尔定理表明，任何一个公理体系都不能涵盖属于一个结构的全部真理；勒文海姆－斯科伦定理则表明，每个体系都包含超出原意的内容。只有直觉主义者能对公理方案提出的问题无动于衷。

The logicists, formalists, and set-theorists rely on axiomatic foundations. In the first few decades of this century this type of foundation was hailed as the choice basis on which to build mathematics. But Godel’s theorem showed that no one system of axioms embraces all of the truths that belong to any one structure, and the Lowenheim-Skolem theorem showed that each embraces more than was intended. Only the intuitionists can be indifferent to the problems posed by the axiomatic approach.

除了关于哪种基础最好的一切分歧与不确定性，缺乏一致性证明仍像达摩克利斯之剑悬在所有数学家头上。不论采用哪种数学哲学，前进时都冒着得到矛盾的风险。

To top all the disagreements and uncertainties about which foundation is the best, the lack of a proof of consistency still hangs over the heads of all mathematicians like the sword of Damocles. No matter which philosophy of mathematics one adopts, one proceeds at the risk of arriving at a contradiction.

几种互相冲突的数学方案揭示的主要事实，是并非只有一个数学整体，而是有许多个。mathematics应按复数意义理解，也许每一种方案都该称为mathematic。哲学家乔治·桑塔亚纳曾说：“没有上帝，而玛利亚是祂的母亲。”今天可以说，没有普遍接受的数学整体，而希腊人是它的创始者。实际上，数学家如今可作选择之多，可以用雪莱的话描述：

The major fact that emerges from the several conflicting approaches to mathematics is that there is not one body of mathematics but many. The word mathematics should be understood in the plural sense and perhaps mathematic should be used for any one approach. The philosopher George Santayana once said, “There is no God and Mary is His mother.” One might say today, there is no universally accepted body of mathematics and the Greeks were its founder. In fact, the multiplicity of choices mathematicians can now make can well be described in the words of Shelley:

……这里，在这无尽的诸世界荒野中，其浩瀚，甚至让高飞的想象也踉跄。

. . . Here In this interminable wilderness Of worlds, at whose immensity Even soaring fancy staggers.

看来，我们将不得不生活在没有标准判定何种数学本身的研究方案可取的状态中，至少在可预见的未来肯定如此。

Apparently we shall have to live, certainly for the foreseeable future, with no criterion for the desirable approach to mathematics proper.

调和何为正确数学、至少何为数学适当道路的不同观点，任何希望都寄托于认识迫使数学家采用不同观点的问题。根本问题是什么是证明；主要由于对此意见不同，何为合法数学也就有分歧。

Any hope of reconciling the divergent views on what is correct mathematics—or at least the proper course for mathematics—rests on recognizing the issues that oblige mathematicians to adopt different views. The basic issue is what is proof and, primarily as a consequence of differences of opinion on this issue, there are differences on what legitimate mathematics is.

据说数学证明一向是清晰、无可争议的过程。诚然，它曾被忽视数百年（第五至第八章），但数学家总体上知道这一事实。概念一直存在，作为典范和标准，数学家或多或少自觉地遵守它。

Mathematical proof had supposedly always been a clear, indisputable process. True, it had been ignored for centuries (Chapters V-VIII), but mathematicians were on the whole conscious of this fact. The concept was there and served as the paradigm and standard to which mathematicians more or less conscientiously adhered.

什么导致了关于证明的忧虑甚至冲突？旧逻辑观认为，亚里士多德整理的原则是绝对真理，这一观点被接受了两千年。长期而似乎可靠的使用，增强了对它们的信心。但数学家认识到，逻辑原则像欧几里得几何公理一样，是经验的产物。因此，对于哪些原则可靠，产生了一些不安。于是，直觉主义者觉得限制排中律的应用是有理由的。如果逻辑原则过去并非不可改变，现在可接受的原则未来还可能同样可接受吗？

What has caused concern and even conflict about proof? The older view of logic, that its principles as codified by Aristotle are absolute truths, was accepted for two thousand years. Confidence in them had been bolstered by long and seemingly reliable usage. But mathematicians came to the realization that the principles of logic were as much a product of experience as the axioms of Euclidean geometry. Hence some uneasiness about what the sound principles are did develop. Thus the intuitionists felt justified in restricting the application of the law of excluded middle. If the principles of logic have not proved to be immutable in the past, are we likely to find that principles acceptable now will be so in the future?

逻辑主义学派建立时，出现了有关证明的第二个问题：逻辑原则涵盖什么？罗素和怀特海在《数学原理》第一版中，虽毫不犹豫地引入无穷公理和选择公理，后来却确实后退了；他们不仅承认基本逻辑规律不是绝对真理，也认识到这两条公理不是逻辑公理。在《数学原理》第二版中，开头不再列出这些公理，而在证明某些定理需要它们的地方明确说明。

A second issue concerning proof, which arose when the logistic school was founded, is what do the principles of logic embrace. Although Russell and Whitehead had no hesitation in introducing the axioms of infinity and choice in the first edition of their Pvincipia Muthemcxticci, they certainly backtracked later, not only in acknowledging that the primary laws of logic were not absolute truths but also in recognizing that these two axioms are not axioms of logic. In the second edition of their Principia, these axioms were not listed at the outset and their use where needed to prove certain theorems was specifically mentioned.

除对于哪些逻辑原则可接受的分歧外，逻辑本身能发挥多大作用，也有分歧。我们知道，逻辑主义者主张逻辑足以建立全部数学，尽管如刚才所述，他们后来对无穷公理和选择公理含糊其辞。形式主义者认为，仅有逻辑不够，要为数学奠基，必须在逻辑公理之外加入数学公理。集合论者对逻辑原则相当随意，有些人并不明确规定。直觉主义者原则上不用逻辑。

Beyond any differences on what are acceptable principles of logic, there are differences on how far logic itself can serve. As we know, the logicists contend that it suffices for all of mathematics, though, as just noted, they did later equivocate on the axioms of infinity and choice. The formalists believe that logic alone does not suffice and axioms of mathematics must be added to axioms of logic in order to found mathematics.
