The set-theorists are rather casual about logical principles and some do not specify them. The intuitionists in principle dispense with logic.

另一个问题是存在概念。例如，证明每个多项式方程至少有一个根，就是确立存在性定理。逻辑主义者、形式主义者和集合论者接受任何一致的证明。但即使不使用排中律，证明也可能没有提供计算所存在对象的方法。因此，直觉主义者不接受这种存在性证明。直觉主义者不愿接受超限基数和序数，因为它们对人的直觉不清楚，而且按他们所理解的构造或可计算性，无法构造得到；这是对于什么构成存在具有不同标准的另一个例子。不只是方程的根之类个别实体，连全部数学究竟在什么意义上存在，都是一个重大问题，本章稍后还将讨论。

Another issue is the concept of existence. For example, a proof that every polynomial equation must have at least one root establishes an existence theorem. Any proof, if consistent, is acceptable to the logicists, formalists, and set-theorists. However, even if a proof does not employ the law of excluded middle, the proof may give no method for calculating the existent object. Hence such existence proofs are unacceptable to the intuitionists. The unwillingness of intuitionists to accept transfinite cardinals and ordinals—because these are not clear to human intuition and cannot be constructively arrived at in the intuitionists’ sense of construction or calculability—is another example of different standards of what constitutes existence. The issue, in what sense not only individual entities such as a root of an equation but all of mathematics exists, is a major one, and we shall say more about it later in this chapter.

对于何为适当数学的忧虑，还来自另一源头：什么数学公理可接受？一个突出例子是能否使用选择公理。数学家在此陷入两难。不使用或否定它，就意味着放弃数学的广大部分。使用它，则如我们所见，不导致矛盾，却导致直觉上不合理的结论（第十二章）。

Concern about what proper mathematics is arises from still another source. What are acceptable mathematical axioms? An outstanding example is whether one can use the axiom of choice. Here mathematicians are caught on the horns of a dilemma. Not to use it or to deny it means to forgo large portions of mathematics. To use it leads, as we have seen, not to contradictions but to intuitively unreasonable conclusions (Chapter XII).

数学家无法证明数学一致性，玷污了整个数学理想。矛盾出现于未曾预料的地方。虽然以多少可以接受的方式得到解决，但可能发现新矛盾的危险，确实使一些数学家怀疑为严密性付出巨大努力是否值得。

Sullying the whole ideal of mathematics is the mathematicians’ inability to prove its consistency. Contradictions appeared where they were unexpected. Though they have been resolved in more or less acceptable fashion, the danger that new ones may be discovered certainly has made some mathematicians skeptical of the extraordinary efforts required for rigor.

那么，数学若不是唯一、严密的逻辑结构，究竟是什么？它是一系列伟大的直觉，经过人们在任何时期愿意且能够应用的逻辑，仔细筛选、精炼和组织。人们越努力精炼概念、使数学演绎结构系统化，数学的直觉就越精深。但数学依赖某些直觉，它们可能是我们的感官、大脑和外部世界的性质的产物。数学是人的建构，任何为它寻找绝对基础的尝试，很可能注定失败。

What then is mathematics if it is not a unique, rigorous, logical structure? It is a series of great intuitions carefully sifted, refined, and organized by the logic men are willing and able to apply at any time. The more they attempt to refine the concepts and systematize the deductive structure of mathematics, the more sophisticated are its intuitions. But mathematics rests upon certain intuitions that may be the product of what our sense organs, brains, and the external world are like. It is a human construction and any attempt to find an absolute basis for it is probably doomed to failure.

数学通过一系列伟大的直觉进展成长；这些进展后来并非一步确立，而是通过一连串对疏漏和错误的纠正，直到证明达到当时接受的证明水平。没有证明是最终的。新反例推翻旧证明，证明于是被修订，并被错误地认为永远成立。但历史告诉我们，这只是意味着，对证明进行批判检验的时机尚未到来。这种检验常被故意推迟。发现错误不仅没有荣耀，而且可能有理由怀疑某定理证明的数学家，或许想引用它来支持自己的工作。数学家远更关心确立自己的定理，而不是寻找现有结果的缺陷。

Mathematics grows through a series of great intuitive advances, which are later established not in one step but by a series of corrections of oversights and errors until the proof reaches the level of accepted proof for that time. No proof is final. New counterexamples undermine old proofs. The proofs are then revised and mistakenly considered proven for all time. But history tells us that this merely means that the time has not yet come for a critical examination of the proof. Such an examination is often willfully delayed. Not only is there no glory in finding errors but the mathematician who could have reason to question the proof of a theorem may want to cite it in behalf of his own work. Mathematicians are far more concerned with establishing their own theorems than with finding flaws in existing results.

几个学派试图把数学圈在人类逻辑的界限内。但直觉不容被封装进逻辑。在可靠基础上构建安全、无可怀疑、不会出错的数学整体的观念，当然源于古典希腊人的梦想，体现在欧几里得的工作中。这一理想引导数学家思考二十多个世纪。但看来，数学家被“邪恶天才”欧几里得误导了。

Several of the schools have tried to enclose mathematics within the confines of man’s logic. But intuition defies encapsulation in logic. The concept of a safe, indubitable, and infallible body of mathematics built upon a sound foundation stems of course from the dream of the classical Greeks, embodied in the work of Euclid. This ideal guided the thinking of mathematicians for more than twenty centuries. But apparently mathematicians were misled by the “evil genius” Euclid.

实际上，数学家并不像通常认为的那样依赖严格证明。他的创造在任何形式化之前，对他已有意义；这种意义本身就赋予创造以存在或现实性。试图从公理结构中推导结果，以确定其精确界限，或许在某些方面有帮助，却并不真正提高结果的地位。

Actually the mathematician does not rely upon rigorous proof to the extent that is normally supposed. His creations have a meaning for him that precedes any formalization, and this meaning gives the creations an existence or reality ipso facto. The attempt to determine precise metes and bounds of a result by deriving it from an axiomatic structure may help in some ways but does not actually enhance its status.

直觉甚至比逻辑更令人满足或安心。数学家自问某结果为什么成立时，寻求的答案是某种直觉理解。事实上，如果结果在直觉上说不通，严格证明对他就毫无意义。若说不通，他会极其严格地检验证明。若证明似乎正确，他就努力找出自己的直觉哪里错了。数学家希望知道一系列三段论成功的内在原因。庞加莱说：“一个较长的论证导致简单而惊人的结果时，只有表明，即使不能预见全部结果，至少也可以预见其主要特征，我们才会满足。”

Intuition can be even more satisfying or reassuring than logic. When a mathematician asks himself why some result should hold, the answer he seeks is some intuitive understanding. In fact, a rigorous proof means nothing to him if the result doesn’t make sense intuitively. If it doesn t, he will examine the proof very critically. If the proof seems right, he will then try hard to find what is wrong with his intuition. Mathematicians wish to know the inner reason for the success of a series of syllogisms. Poincare said: “When a somewhat long argument leads us to a simple and striking result, we are not satisfied until we have shown that we could have foreseen, if not the entire result, at least its principal features.”

许多数学家更依赖直觉。哲学家阿瑟·叔本华表达过这种态度：“要改进数学方法，首先必须要求放弃一种成见，即相信经论证的真理优于直觉知识。”帕斯卡创造了esprit de géométrie和esprit de finesse两个词。前者指心灵的力量与正直，如强有力逻辑推理所显示的；后者指心灵的广博，能更深入、更有洞见地观察的能力。对帕斯卡而言，即使在科学中，精微精神也是高于并超越逻辑、与逻辑不可通约的思想层次。甚至理性不能理解的东西，仍可能为真。

Many mathematicians have placed far more reliance upon intuition. The philosopher Arthur Schopenhauer expressed this attitude: “To improve the method in mathematics it is necessary to demand above all that one abandon the preconception that consists in believing that demonstrated truth is superior to intuitive knowledge.” Pascal coined the phrases esprit de geometrie and esprit de finesse. By the former, Pascal meant force and rectitude of mind such as those exhibited by powerful logical reasoning. By the latter, he meant amplitude of mind, the capacity to see more deeply and insightfully. To Pascal, even in science esprit de finesse is a level of thought above and beyond logic and incommensurable with it. Even what is incomprehensible to reason may nonetheless be true.

很早以前，其他数学家也断言，直觉确信胜过逻辑，犹如太阳光辉胜过苍白月光。笛卡尔依赖基本直觉，谈逻辑时说：“我发现，至于逻辑，它的三段论和大多数规则，更适合用来传达我们已经知道的东西，或……不加判断地谈论一无所知的事。”不过，他愿意用演绎推理补充直觉（第二章）。

Long ago other mathematicians also asserted that intuitive conviction surpasses logic as the brilliance of the sun surpasses the pale light of the moon. Descartes relied upon fundamental intuitions and apropos of logic remarked: “I have found that, as for Logic, its syllogisms and the majority of its precepts are useful rather in the communication of what we already know or ... in speaking without judgment about things of which one is ignorant.” However, he was willing to supplement intuition with deductive reasoning (Chapter II).

伟大的数学家在逻辑证明尚未写成之前，就知道定理必真，有时只提示证明就满足了。事实上，费马在广博而经典的数论工作中，牛顿在三次曲线的工作中，连提示也没给。无疑，数学创造最受推动，来自直觉能力出众的人，而非以制作严格证明的能力见长的人。

Great mathematicians know before a logical proof is ever composed that a theorem must be true, and they sometimes are content with no more than an indication of a proof. In fact, Lermat in his vast and classic work on the theory of numbers and Newton in his work on third degree curves gave not even indications. Certainly, mathematical creation is furthered most by men who are distinguished by their power of intuition rather than by their capacity to make rigorous proofs.

因此，证明概念虽然在公众心目中和数学家的出版物中占据显著地位，却未发挥通常假定的作用。互相冲突的数学哲学兴起，各自坚持自身的证明标准，助长了对证明价值的怀疑；甚至在各哲学明确界定、冲突观点广泛传播之前，就开始出现对证明观念的攻击。早在1928年，戈弗雷·H.哈代就以惯常的直率说道：

The concept of proof then, large as it has loomed in the public mind and in the publications of mathematicians, has not played the role commonly assumed. The rise of conflicting philosophies of mathematics, each insisting on its own standards of proof, has fomented much skepticism about the value of proof, and attacks on the notion of proof began to appear even before the several philosophies had been clearly defined and their conflicting views were widespread. As far back as 1928, Godfrey H. Hardy spoke out with his usual bluntness:

严格说来，没有数学证明这种东西……归根结底，我们只能指点……证明是利特尔伍德和我所谓的空话，是为影响心理而设计的修辞花样，是讲课时黑板上的图画，是刺激学生想象的手段。

There is strictly speaking no such thing as mathematical proof; . . . we can, in the last analysis, do nothing but point; . . . proofs are what Littlewood and I call gas, rhetorical flourishes designed to affect psychology, pictures on the board in lectures, devices to stimulate the imagination of pupils.

对哈代而言，证明是数学结构的门面，而非支撑柱。

To Hardy, proofs were a facade rather than the supporting columns of the mathematical structure.

1944年，美国著名数学家雷蒙德·L.怀尔德更有理由降低证明的地位。他说，证明不过是

In 1944 with all the more justification, the prominent American mathematician Raymond L. Wilder downgraded the status of proof. Proof, he said, is no more than the

检验我们直觉的产物……显然，我们没有、也许永远不会有任何独立于时间、待证事物、或使用它的个人和思想学派的证明标准。在这些条件下，明智的做法似乎是承认，一般而言，数学中没有绝对真理［证明］这种东西，不论公众怎样想。

testing of the products of our intuition. . . . Obviously we don’t possess, and probably will never possess, any standard of proof that is independent of time, the thing to be proved, or the person or school of thought using it. And under these conditions, the sensible thing to do seems to be to admit that there is no such thing, generally, as absolute truth [proof] in mathematics, whatever the public may think.

怀特海在题为《不朽》的演讲中，抨击证明的价值：

The value of proof was attacked by Whitehead in a lecture entitled “Immortality”:

结论是，若把逻辑视为对思想进展的充分分析，它就是赝品。逻辑是一件极好的工具，却需要常识背景……我的意思是，哲学思想的最终观点，不能建立在构成专门科学基础的精确陈述之上。这种精确性是假的。

The conclusion is that Logic, conceived as an adequate analysis of the advance of thought, is a fake. It is a superb instrument, but it requires a background of common sense. . . . My point is that the final outlook of philosophic thought cannot be based upon the exact statements which form the basis of special sciences. The exactness is a fake.

证明、绝对严密性及其同类，是鬼火，是“在数学世界中没有自然栖息地”的理想概念。没有关于严密性的严密定义。一个证明得到当时主要专家的认可，或采用当时流行的原则，就会被接受。但今天没有普遍接受的标准。这不是数学严密性最光辉的时刻。先前公认的数学特征，即从明确公理得出不容质疑的证明，现在看来无疑已过时。逻辑具有一切限制人类心灵的易错性和不确定性。我们不禁怀疑，数学中究竟有多少基本假定，被我们习惯性地作出，却从未察觉。

Proof, absolute rigor, and their ilk are will-o’-the wisps, ideal concepts, “with no natural habitat in the mathematical world.” There is no rigorous definition of rigor. A proof is accepted if it obtains the endorse-ment of the leading specialists of the time or employs the principles that are fashionable at the moment. But no standard is universally acceptable today. This is not the finest hour of mathematical rigor. Certainly the previously accepted feature of mathematics, unquestionable proof from explicit axioms, now seems passe. Logic has all the fallibility and uncertainty that limit human minds. One must wonder how many fundamental assumptions we are habitually making in mathematics without ever recognizing them.

哲学家尼采曾说：“笑话是情感的墓志铭。”数学家为缓解沮丧，开始拿学科的逻辑打趣：“逻辑证明的优点不在于强迫相信，而在于引起疑问。证明告诉我们，应在哪里集中怀疑。”“尊重数学证明，但也怀疑它。”“我们不能再希望合乎逻辑；最好的希望是不违反逻辑。”“多些活力，少些严密。”直觉主义数学家亨利·勒贝格在1928年说：“逻辑能使我们拒绝某些证明，却不能使我们相信任何证明。”1941年的文章中，他补充，逻辑不能说服、不能产生信心。我们相信符合直觉的东西。勒贝格确实承认，随着数学知识增加，这种直觉变得更精深。

The philosopher Nietzsche once said that “jokes are the epitaphs of emotions.” To relieve their dejection, mathematicians have resorted to joshing about the logic of their subject. “The virtue of a logical proof is not that it compels belief but that it suggests doubts. The proof tells us where to concentrate our doubts.” “Respect but suspect mathematical proof.” “We can no longer hope to be logical; the best we can hope for is not to be illogical.” “More vigor and less rigor.” The mathematician Henri Lebesgue, an intuitionist, said in 1928, “Logic can make us reject certain proofs but it cannot make us believe any proof.” In an article of 1941, he added that logic does not serve to convince, to create confidence. We have confidence in what accords with our intuition. Lebesgue did grant that this intuition becomes more sophisticated as we learn more about mathematics.

甚至伯特兰·罗素，尽管有彻底的逻辑主义纲领，也忍不住对逻辑作尖刻评论。他在《数学原则》（1903年）中写道：“证明的主要优点之一，是让人对被证明的结果产生某种怀疑。”他在同一著作中还说，试图把数学建立在未定义概念和原始命题体系之上的尝试，其本性就意味着，发现矛盾可以否证结果，却永远不能证明结果。最终一切都依赖直接感知。稍后的1906年，他因当时悖论而不安，说出比以后更真实的话。当二律背反表明当时逻辑证明并非不会出错时，他说：“不确定的因素必须始终存在，正如天文学中也存在。它可能随时间大幅减少；但凡人并无不犯错误的天赋……”

Even Bertrand Russell, despite his thoroughly logistic program, could not refrain from a caustic remark about logic. In his Principles of Mathematics (1903), he wrote, “It is one of the chief merits of proofs that they instill a certain skepticism about the result proved.” He also said in his Principles of 1903 that it follows from the very nature of an attempt to base mathematics on a system of undefined concepts and primitive propositions that results can be disproved by the discovery of a contradiction but can never be proved. All depends in the end upon immediate perception. Somewhat later in his work (1906), disturbed by the current paradoxes, he spoke more truly than he did in after years. When the antinomies had shown that the logical proof of the time was not infallible, he said, “An element of uncertainty must always remain, just as it remains in astronomy. It may with time be immensely diminished; but infallibility is not granted to mortals. . . .”

对于这些嘲讽证明的话，还可以加上数学逻辑的重要研究者卡尔·波普尔的话：“理解证明有三个层次。最低层次，是感觉愉快，自以为已经理解论证；第二层次，是能复述它；第三或最高层次，是能驳倒它。”

To these gibes at proof we may add the words of a leading student of the logic of mathematics, Karl Popper: “There are three levels of understanding of a proof. The lowest is the pleasant feeling of having grasped the argument; the second is the ability to repeat it; and the third or top level is that of being able to refute it.”

奥利弗·亥维赛蔑视数学家对严密性的关切，却提出一个颇具讽刺意味的反驳：“逻辑不可战胜，因为必须用逻辑来击败逻辑。”

Rather ironic is the counterargument made by Oliver Heaviside, who was contemptuous about the mathematicians’ concern for rigor: “Logic is invincible because one must use logic to defeat logic.”

费利克斯·克莱因在本世纪头四分之一时期，领导当时世界数学中心哥廷根大学的数学工作，虽主要不关注基础问题，却看出了数学成长的一点特征，至少迄今历史已证实它。他在《高观点下的初等数学》（1908年）中这样描述数学的成长：

Though Felix Klein, the head of mathematics during the first quarter of this century at what was then the world center for mathematics, the University of Gottingen, was not primarily concerned with the foundational problems, he perceived something about the growth of mathematics that has, thus far at least, been borne out by history. In his Elementary Mathematics from an Advanced Standpoint (1908), Klein described the growth of mathematics thus:

事实上，数学像树一样成长；树并不是从最细小的根须开始，只往上长，而是在枝叶向上扩展的同时，以相同速度使根越扎越深……因此，就数学的基础研究而言，没有最终的结束，相应也没有最初的开端。

In fact, mathematics [has] grown like a tree, which does not start at its tiniest rootlets and grow merely upward, but rather sends its roots deeper and deeper at the same time and rate that its branches and leaves are spreading upward. . . . We see, then, that as regards the fundamental investigation in mathematics, there is no final ending, and therefore on the other hand, no first beginning.

庞加莱虽在略有不同的语境中，也表达类似观点：没有已经解决的问题，只有多少得到解决的问题。

Though in a somewhat different connection, Poincare expressed a similar view: there are no solved problems; there are only problems more or less solved.

数学家一直崇拜一头金牛犊——严密、普遍可接受、在一切可能世界中为真的证明——以为它就是上帝。现在他们认识到它是假神。但真神拒绝显现，如今他们必须问上帝是否存在。能够传达神言的摩西尚未出现。我们有理由质疑理性。

Mathematicians have been worshipping a golden calf—rigorous, universally acceptable proof, true in all possible worlds—in the belief that it was God. They now realize it was a false god. But the true god refuses to reveal himself, and now they must question whether God exists. The Moses who might relay the word has yet to appear. There is reason to question reason.

有些健全的基础批评者，对这些数学基础研究者作出的精细区分更加不耐烦。他们说，若数学最终依赖直觉，那么引用伊姆雷·拉卡托斯（1922—1974）的话，为什么我们越探越深？

There are sound critics of the foundations who are even more impatient with the fine distinctions these mathematical foundationists make. If, they say, mathematics rests ultimately on intuitions, then to cite Imre Lakatos (1922-1974), why do we probe deeper and deeper?

那么，为什么不早一点停下来，为什么不说“一个方法是否可用于算术，最终检验当然应是它是否在直觉上令人信服”……为什么不诚实承认数学的易错性，努力捍卫可错知识的尊严，使其免遭犬儒式怀疑主义，而要自欺地以为，能够不留痕迹地修补我们“最终”直觉织物上最新的裂口？

Why then don’t we stop earlier, why not say that “the ultimate test whether a method is admissible in arithmetic must of course be whether it is intuitively convincing.” . . . Why not honestly admit mathematical fallibility, and try to defend the dignity of fallible knowledge from cynical scepticism, rather than delude ourselves that we can invisibly mend the latest tear in the fabric of our “ultimate” intuitions?

一个故事很好地描述了直觉相对于证明的价值。一位物理学家在实验室门上挂了马蹄铁。访客惊讶地问，它是否给他和工作带来好运。“不，”物理学家回答，“我不信迷信，但它似乎仍然管用。”

The value of intuition vis-a-vis proof is aptly described by a story. A physicist had a horseshoe hanging on the door of his laboratory. A visitor taken aback asked him whether this brought luck to him and his work. “No,” the physicist answered, “I don’t believe in superstition. But it seems to work nevertheless.”

阿瑟·斯坦利·爱丁顿曾说：“证明是数学家在其面前折磨自己的偶像。”为什么还要继续？如果数学家不再知道学科是一致的，尤其不再对何为正确证明达成一致，那么他们强调推理究竟取得什么，我们完全可以这样问。他们是否该对严密性漠不关心，摊开双手，说数学作为牢固确立的知识整体只是一种幻觉？是否该放弃演绎证明，只采用令人信服、直觉上可靠的论证？毕竟，物理科学就使用这类论证，即使使用数学，也不太关心数学家对严密性的热情。放弃不是可取的道路。任何考察过数学对人类思想贡献的人，都不会牺牲证明概念。

Arthur Stanley Eddington once said, “Proof is an idol before whom the mathematician tortures himself.” Why should they continue to do so? We might well ask what mathematicians accomplish with their stress on reasoning if they no longer know that their subject is consistent and if, especially, they no longer agree on what correct proof is. Should they rather become indifferent to rigor, throw up their hands and say that mathematics as a soundly established body of knowledge is an illusion? Should they abandon deductive proof and resort merely to convincing, intuitively sound arguments? After all, the physical sciences use such arguments, and even where they use mathematics they are not too concerned with the mathematician’s passion for rigor. Abandonment is not the advisable path. Anyone who has looked into the contributions of mathematics to human thought would not sacrifice the concept of proof.

必须承认逻辑发挥作用。如果直觉是主人、逻辑是仆人，仆人对主人也有一定权力。它限制不受约束的直觉。直觉虽发挥主要作用，却可能导致过分一般的断言。逻辑施加适当的限制条件。直觉把谨慎抛诸脑后，逻辑却教人节制。诚然，遵守逻辑涉及附有许多假设的冗长断言，通常需要许多定理和证明，一小步一小步地达到强大直觉常能一举征服的东西。但直觉大胆占领的桥头堡，必须通过彻底搜剿可能包围并摧毁它的敌对队伍，得到巩固。

One must grant that logic plays a part. If intuition is master and logic the servant, the servant has some power over the master. It restricts unbridled intuition. Though intuition does play the major role, it can lead to assertions that are far too general. The proper limiting conditions are imposed by logic. Intuition throws caution to the winds but logic teaches restraint. It is true that the adherence to logic involves long assertions qualified by many hypotheses and usually requires many theorems and proofs, in mincing steps, to arrive at what a powerful intuition often conquers in one swoop. But the bold bridgeheads seized by intuition must be secured by thorough scouring for hostile bands that might surround and destroy the bridgeheads.

直觉可能骗人。19世纪大部分时期，数学家，包括严密性的奠基人柯西，相信连续函数必有导数。但魏尔斯特拉斯展示一个处处不可导的连续函数，震惊了数学界。这种函数过去和现在都无法由直觉把握。数学推理不仅补充直觉，证实或纠正它，偶尔甚至超越它。

Intuition can be deceptive. Throughout most of the nineteenth century, mathematicians, including Cauchy, the founder of rigor, believed that a continuous function must have a derivative. But Weierstrass astonished the mathematical world by exhibiting a continuous function that does not have a derivative at any point. Such a function was not and is not accessible to intuition. Mathematical reasoning not only supplements intuition to confirm or correct it, but even occasionally surpasses it.

一个类比或许更能说明数学通过推理取得什么。假定农夫接手荒野的一片土地，准备耕种。他清理一块地，却发现周围林地潜伏野兽，随时可能攻击他。因此，他决定清理那片区域。他做了，但野兽转到另一片区域，他又清理那里。野兽又转到新清地外围的另一处。过程无限继续。农夫清理越来越多土地，野兽却仍在边缘。他得到了什么？清理区域越大，野兽就被迫退得越远，农夫也越安全，至少在清理区内部工作时如此。野兽一直存在，有一天可能突袭并毁灭他，但随着清地扩大，农夫的相对安全增加。同样，应用逻辑澄清一个又一个基础问题，我们使用数学核心整体的安全性也增加。换句话说，证明给我们相对保证。如果依据关于数或几何图形的相当可靠陈述来证明一个定理，而这些陈述在直觉上比待证定理更可接受，我们就相当相信它正确。用雷蒙德·L.怀尔德的话说，证明是应用于直觉所提示思想的检验过程。

What mathematics accomplishes with its reasoning may be more evident from an analogy. Suppose a farmer takes over a tract of land in a wilderness with a view to farming it. He clears a piece of ground but notices wild beasts lurking in a wooded area surrounding the clearing who may attack him at any time. He decides therefore to clear that area. He does so but the beasts move to another area. He therefore clears this one. And the beasts move to still another spot just outside the new clearing. The process goes on indefinitely. The farmer clears away more and more land but the beasts remain on the fringe. What has the farmer gained? As the cleared area gets larger the beasts are compelled to move farther back and the farmer becomes more and more secure at least as long as he works in the interior of his cleared area. The beasts are always there and one day they may surprise and destroy him but the farmer’s relative security increases as he clears more land. So, too, the security with which we use the central body of mathematics increases as logic is applied to clear up one or another of the foundational problems. Proof, in other words, gives us relative assurance. We become quite convinced that a theorem is correct if we prove it on the basis of reasonably sound statements about numbers or geometrical figures which are intuitively more acceptable than the one we prove. In the words of Raymond L. Wilder, proof is a testing process that we apply to the thoughts suggested by our intuition.

不幸的是，一代人的证明成为下一代人的谬误。美国杰出数学家E.H.穆尔早在1903年说：“所有科学，包括逻辑和数学，都是时代的函数——理想和成就皆如此。”“一天有一天足够的严密性。”如今，证明概念还取决于所信奉的思想学派。怀尔德本人会满足于一个在可见范围内不含矛盾、并且数学上有用的证明。例如，他会把连续统假设作为公理。他降低证明的重要性，批评各思想学派的分裂。他们坚持某个学派、排斥另一个，岂不像宗教狂热者，自称代表真神，拒绝一切其他教派？

Unfortunately, the proofs of one generation are the fallacies of the next. As E. H. Moore, a foremost American mathematician, put it as far back as 1903, “All science, logic and mathematics included, is a function of the epoch—all science in the ideals as well as its achievements.” “Sufficient unto the day is the rigor thereof.” Today the concept of proof depends also on the school of thought to which one adheres. Wilder himself would be satisfied with a proof that, as far as one can see, does not involve a contradiction and is mathematically useful. He would, for example, use the continuum hypothesis as an axiom. Downgrading the importance of proof, he criticizes the divisiveness of the various schools of thought. Is not their insistence on one school rather than another like the fanaticism of religionists who claim to represent the true God and reject all other sects?

如今我们不得不接受，没有绝对证明或普遍可接受证明这种东西。我们知道，若质疑凭直觉接受的陈述，就只有凭直觉接受其他陈述，才能证明前者。我们也不能把这些最终直觉探究得过远，否则会遇到悖论或其他未解决困难，有些就在逻辑本身的领域。约1900年，法国著名数学家雅克·阿达马说：“数学严密性的目标，只是批准直觉的征服，使之合法。”我们不能再接受这一判断。赫尔曼·外尔的话更恰当：“逻辑是数学家为保持思想健康强壮而实行的卫生措施。”证明确实发挥作用，尽量减少矛盾的风险。

We are now compelled to accept the fact that there is no such thing as an absolute proof or a universally acceptable proof. We know that, if we question the statements we accept on an intuitive basis, we shall be able to prove them only if we accept others on an intuitive basis. Nor can we probe these ultimate intuitions too far without running into paradoxes or other unresolved difficulties, some lying in the realm of logic itself. Sometime about 1900, the famous French mathematician Jacques Hadamard said, “The object of mathematical rigor has been only to sanction and legitimatize the conquests of intuition.” We can no longer accept this judgment. It is more appropriate to say with Hermann Weyl, “Logic is the hygiene which the mathematician practices to keep his ideas healthy and strong.” Proof does play a role; it minimizes the risk of contradictions.

必须认识到，绝对证明不是现实，而是目标；值得追求，却极可能永远无法达到。它也许只是幻影，不断被追逐，却永远难以捕捉。我们应不断努力加强已有东西，却不期望使之完美。证明史的寓意是，即使追求不可达到的目标，仍可能产生数学过去提供的美好价值。因此，如果重新调整对数学的态度，即使幻灭，也会更满足于继续研究。

We must recognize that absolute proof is not an actuality but a goal, a goal to be sought but very likely never to be attained. It may be no more than a phantom, constantly pursued but forever elusive. We should make constant efforts to strengthen what we have without ever expecting to perfect it. The moral of the history of proof is that even though we pursue an unattainable goal, we may still produce the wonderful values that mathematics has furnished in the past. If then we reorient our attitude toward mathematics, we shall be more content to pursue the subject despite our disillusionment.

认识到直觉在确保数学真理中发挥根本作用，而证明只作支撑，意味着在更广意义上，数学转了一整圈。它始于直觉和经验基础。证明在希腊人那里成为目标；虽直到19世纪人们更多违背而非遵守它，19世纪末似乎已实现。但把严密性追求到极致的努力，导致僵局，逻辑像追自己尾巴的狗一样击败逻辑。正如帕斯卡在《思想录》中说：“理性的最后一步，是认识到有无穷多事物超出它的范围。”

The recognition that intuition plays a fundamental role in securing mathematical truths and that proof plays only a supporting role suggests that, in a larger sense, mathematics has turned full circle. The subject started on an intuitive and empirical basis. Proof became a goal with the Greeks and, though honored in the breach until the nineteenth century, it seemed late in that century to be achieved. But the efforts to pursue rigor to the utmost have led to an impasse in which, like a dog chasing its tail, logic has defeated logic. As Pascal put it in his Pensees, “Reason’s last step is the recognition that there are an infinite number of things that are beyond it.”

康德也认识到理性的局限。在《纯粹理性批判》中，他承认：

Kant, too, recognized the limitations of reason. In his Critique of Pure Reason he acknowledged:

我们的理性具有一种特殊命运：就某一类知识而言，它总被一些问题困扰；这些问题不能忽视，因为源于理性自身的本性，又不能回答，因为超出人类理性的力量。

Our reason has this peculiar fate that, with reference to one class of its knowledge, it is always troubled with questions that cannot be ignored, because they spring from the very nature of reason, and that cannot be answered, because they transcend the power of human reason.

或者，如米格尔·德·乌纳穆诺在《生命的悲剧意识》中说：“理性的最高胜利，是怀疑自身的有效性。”

Or as Miguel de Unamuno stated in The Tragic Sense of Life, “The supreme triumph of reason is to cast doubt on its own validity.”

外尔对逻辑作用更悲观。1940年，他说：“尽管、或正因为我们具有批判洞察力，今天对数学赖以立足的最终基础，我们比以往任何时候都更不确定。”1944年，他进一步说：

More pessimistic about the role of logic was Weyl. In 1940 he said, “In spite, or because, of our disposed critical insight, we are today less sure than at any previous time of the ultimate foundations on which mathematics rests.” In 1944 he elaborated:

数学最终基础与最终意义的问题仍未解决；不知道它将沿什么方向找到最终答案，甚至不知道究竟能否期待最终的客观答案。“数学化”很可能像语言或音乐一样，是人的创造活动，具有原初独创性，其历史抉择无法完全客观地合理化。

The question of the ultimate foundations and the ultimate meaning of mathematics remains open; we do not know in what direction it will find its final solution or even whether a final objective answer can be expected at all. “Mathematizing” may well be a creative activity of man, like language or music, of primary originality, whose historical decisions defy complete objective rationalization.

正如外尔所说，数学是一种思想活动，不是一组精确知识，最好从历史角度看待。对基础的理性建构与重建，如今看来只是对历史的歪曲。

As Weyl stated, mathematics is an activity of thought, not a body of exact knowledge. It is best viewed historically. The rational constructions and reconstructions of the foundations appear now only as a travesty of the history.

著名科学哲学家卡尔·波普尔在《科学发现的逻辑》中表达最极端的观点。数学推理永不可验证，只可证伪。数学定理没有任何保证。没有更好理论时，可以继续使用现有理论，就像牛顿力学在相对论前用了两百年，或欧几里得几何在黎曼几何前那样。但正确性的保证不可获得。

The most extreme view was expressed by Karl Popper, a notable philosopher of science, in The Logic of Scientific Discovery. Mathematical reasoning is never verifiable but only falsifiable. Mathematical theorems are not guaranteed in any way. One may continue to use the existent theory in the absence of a better one, just as Newton’s theory of mechanics was used for two hundred years before relativity, or as Euclidean geometry was before Riemannian geometry. But assurance of correctness is not attainable.

历史支持这样的观点：没有固定、客观、唯一的数学整体。此外，若历史可作指引，数学将出现新内容，要求新基础。在这方面，数学像任何物理科学。新观察或新实验结果与已有理论冲突、迫使形成新理论时，理论必须修改。不可能对数学真理作超越时间的说明。把数学建立在不可动摇基础上的尝试，已经失败。从欧几里得，经魏尔斯特拉斯，到现代基础学派，接连提供坚实基础的尝试，没有显示任何有望最终成功的演化进步迹象。

History supports the view that there is no fixed, objective, unique body of mathematics. Moreover, if history is any guide, there will be new additions to mathematics that will call for new foundations. In this respect, mathematics is like any one of the physical sciences. Theories must be modified as new observations or new experimental results conflict with previously established theories and compel formulation of new ones. No timeless account of mathematical truth is possible. The attempts to erect mathematics on an unshakable foundation have ended in failure. The successive attempts to provide a solid foundation, from Euclid through Weierstrass to the modern foundational schools, do not give any indication of an evolutionary advance which promises eventual success.

上述关于直觉和证明作用的叙述，代表当今数学的前景，却不反映对未来的所有意见。以尼古拉·布尔巴基为笔名写作的数学家团体，重新肯定了逻辑的理由。在《数学原本》第一卷导言中，他们指出：

This account of the roles of intuition and proof represents the outlook for mathematics today. But it does not reflect all opinions about the future. The case for logic has been reaffirmed by the group of mathematicians who write under the pseudonym of Nicolas Bourbaki. In the introduction to the first volume of their Elements of Mathematics, they observe:

从历史上说，数学没有矛盾当然完全不真实；无矛盾性表现为待实现的目标，而非上帝一劳永逸赐予我们的品质。自最早时代，对整个数学或其任何分支原则的批判修订，几乎总是在不确定时期之后发生；那时出现矛盾，必须解决……数学家纠正错误，看到科学因此丰富而非贫乏的实践，至今已有二十五个世纪；这使他们有权平静地看待未来。

Historically speaking, it is of course quite untrue that mathematics is free from contradiction; non-contradiction appears as a goal to be achieved, not as a God-given quality that has been granted to us once for all. Since the earliest times, all critical revisions of the principles of mathematics as a whole, or of any branch of it, have almost invariably followed periods of uncertainty, where contradictions did appear and had to be resolved. . . . There are now twenty-five centuries during which the mathematicians have had the practice of correcting their errors and thereby seeing their science enriched, not impoverished; this gives them the right to view the future with serenity.

诉诸历史或许有些安慰，但历史也告诉我们，会出现新危机。然而，这一前景并未减弱布尔巴基的乐观。

There may be some comfort in this appeal to history, but history also tells us that new crises will appear. However, this prospect does not diminish Bourbaki’s optimism.

法国主要数学家之一、布尔巴基学派成员让·迪厄多内，相信出现的逻辑问题总能解决：

Jean Dieudonne, one of the leading French mathematicians and a Bourbakist, is confident that problems of logic that arise will always be resolved:

还可以补充，若有一天证明数学有矛盾，我们很可能知道应归因于哪条规则，并通过删去或适当修改这条规则避免矛盾。简言之，数学会改变方向，却不会作为科学消失。这并非纯属猜测；发现无理数之后，发生的事情几乎就是如此。我们今天非但不痛惜它揭示毕达哥拉斯数学的矛盾，反而把它视为人类精神的伟大胜利之一。

One may add that if some day it will be shown that mathematics is contradictory, it is probable that we shall know which rule to attribute the result to, and that the contradiction will be avoided by leaving this rule out or modifying it suitably. In short, mathematics will take a change in direction but will not disappear as a science. This is not entirely a speculation; it is almost what happened after the discovery of irrationals. Far from deploring it as having revealed a contradiction in Pythagorean mathematics, we consider it today as one of the great victories of the human spirit.

迪厄多内完全可以再加上莱布尼茨微积分方案的例子（第七章）。18世纪，它遭受种种批评；后来一种新表述，即非标准分析（第十二章），在与逻辑主义、形式主义和集合论基础一致的基础上，使它严密化。

Dieudonne might well have added the case of Leibniz’s approach to the calculus (Chapter VII). After all the criticism it received in the eighteenth century, a new formulation—non-standard analysis (Chapter XII)—has rigorized it on a basis consistent with the logicist, formalist, and set-theoretic foundations.

除了布尔巴基等人对数学逻辑可调整的信心，还有数学家相信，存在一个唯一、正确、永恒的数学整体，尽管它可能适用、也可能不适用于物理世界。这一永存的观念整体，未必全为人知，却仍存在。他们主张，证明的分歧和不确定性，只源于人类理性的局限。此外，人当前的分歧只是暂时障碍，将逐步克服。

Beyond the confidence which men such as the Bourbakists profess about adjustments to the logic of mathematics, there are mathematicians who believe that there is a unique, correct, eternally existing body of mathematics, though it may or may not apply to the physical world. Not all of this eternally existing body of ideas may be known to man, but it nevertheless exists. Their contention is that the disagreements and uncertainties of proof are due only to the limitations of man’s reason. Moreover, man’s current differences are merely a temporary obstacle that will gradually be overcome.

其中一些人在这方面是康德主义者，认为数学深嵌于人的理性，何者必然正确毫无疑问。例如，威廉·罗恩·哈密顿虽发明了导致人们质疑算术物理真理性的四元数，1836年却坚持一种很像笛卡尔的立场：

Some of these men, Kantians in this respect, see mathematics as so deeply embedded in human reason that there can be no question of what must be correct. For example, William Rowan Hamilton, though he invented the very objects—quaternions—that led to the questioning of the physical truth of arithmetic, maintained in 1836 a position very much like Descartes’s:

代数和几何这些纯数学科学，是纯粹理性的科学，不从实验获得分量与帮助，与一切外部、偶然现象隔绝，或至少可以隔绝……然而，它们是一些似乎如此生于我们内部的观念，拥有它们的任何可想象程度，都只是发展原有能力，展开我们本有的人性。

Those purely mathematical sciences of algebra and geometry are sciences of the pure reason, deriving no weight and assistance from experiment, and isolated or at least isolable from all outward and accidental phenomena. . . . They are, however, ideas which seem so far born within us that the possession of them in any conceivable degree is only the development of our original power, the unfolding of our proper humanity.

19世纪主要代数学家之一阿瑟·凯莱，在1883年向英国科学促进协会演讲时说：“我们……拥有先验知识，不是独立于这种或那种经验，而是绝对独立于一切经验……这些知识是心灵对解释经验的贡献。”

Arthur Cayley, one of the leading nineteenth-century algebraists, said in an address to the British Association for the Advancement of Science (1883) that “We are ... in possession of cognitions a priori, independent, not of this or that experience, but absolutely so of all experience. . . . These cognitions are a contribution of the mind to the interpretation of experience.”

哈密顿和凯莱等人把数学看作嵌入人的心灵，另一些人则认为它存在于人之外的世界。1900年前，人们相信有一个独立于人的、唯一客观的数学真理世界，这当然可以理解。这一信念可追溯至柏拉图（第一章），多次得到重申，尤其是莱布尼茨区分理性真理与事实真理，前者在一切可能世界成立。甚至最先理解非欧几里得几何意义的高斯，也坚持数与分析的真理性（第四章）。

Whereas men such as Hamilton and Cayley saw mathematics as embedded in man’s mind, others see it existing in a world outside of man. That the belief in a unique objective world of mathematical truths independent of man should have been held prior to 1900 is certainly understandable. The belief goes back to Plato (Chapter I) and was reaffirmed many times, notably by Leibniz, who distinguished between truths of reason and truths of fact, the former holding in all possible worlds. Even Gauss, who first appreciated the significance of non-Euclidean geometry, maintained the truth of number and analysis (Chapter IV).

19世纪杰出的分析学家夏尔·埃尔米特（1822—1901），也相信有客观真实的数学世界。他在给数学家托马斯·扬·斯蒂尔切斯的信中说：

The fine nineteenth-century analyst Charles Hermite (1822-1901) also expressed a belief that there is an objective real world of mathematics. He said in a letter to the mathematician Thomas Jan Stieltjes:

我相信，分析中的数和函数不是我们精神的任意产物；我相信它们存在于我们之外，具有与客观现实对象相同的必然性质；我们寻找或发现它们，像物理学家、化学家和动物学家那样研究它们。

I believe that the numbers and functions of analysis are not the arbitrary product of our spirits; I believe that they exist outside of us with the same character of necessity as the objects of objective reality; and we find or discover them and study them as do the physicists, chemists, and zoologists.

另一次，他说：“在数学中，我们是仆人而非主人。”

On another occasion he said, “We are servants rather than masters in mathematics.”

尽管基础存在争论，许多20世纪人物仍持相同立场。集合与超限数理论的创造者格奥尔格·康托尔，相信数学家不是发明，而是发现概念和定理。它们独立于人的思想存在。康托尔把自己视为报道者和秘书。戈弗雷·H.哈代虽怀疑人的证明，却在1929年的文章中说：

Despite the controversies on the foundations, many twentieth-century men maintained the same position. Georg Cantor, the creator of the theory of sets and transfinite numbers, believed that the mathematician does not invent but discovers concepts and theorems. They exist independently of human thoughts. Cantor regarded himself as a reporter and secretary. Though Godfrey H. Hardy was skeptical of man’s proof, he said in an article of 1929:

在我看来，任何哲学若不以某种方式承认数学真理的不变性与无条件有效性，就不可能得到数学家的认同。数学定理非真即假；其真伪绝对独立于我们对它们的知识。在某种意义上，数学真理是客观现实的一部分。

It seems to me that no philosophy can possibly be sympathetic to a mathematician which does not admit, in one manner or other, the immutability and unconditional validity of mathematical truth. Mathematical theorems are true or false; their truth or falsity is absolutely independent of our knowledge of them. In some sense, mathematical truth is part of objective reality.

他在《一个数学家的辩白》中表达相同观点：

He expressed the same view in his book A Mathematician’s Apology:

为避免小误解，我将断然陈述自己的立场。我相信，数学现实存在于我们之外，我们的作用是发现或观察它；我们证明的定理，被冠冕堂皇地称作自己的“创造”，只不过是观察笔记。

I will state my own position dogmatically in order to avoid minor misapprehensions. I believe that mathematical reality lies outside us, that our function is to discover or observe it, and that the theorems which we prove, and which we describe grandiloquently as our “creations,” are simply our notes of our observations.

本世纪法国主要数学家雅克·阿达马（1865—1963），在《数学领域中发明的心理学》中断言：“虽然真理还不为我们所知，它已预先存在，不可避免地向我们规定必须遵循的道路。”

The leading French mathematician of this century, Jacques Hadamard (1865-1963), affirmed in his Psychology of Invention in the Mathematical Field: “Although the truth is not yet known to us, it pre-exists, and inescapably imposes on us the path we must follow.”

哥德尔也坚持存在一个超越的数学世界。谈到集合论，他肯定把所有集合视为真实对象是合法的：

Godel, too, maintained that there is a transcendent world of mathematics. Apropos of set theory, he affirmed that it is legitimate to consider all sets as real objects:

在我看来，假定这类对象存在，与假定物理对象存在同样合法，也有同样充分的理由相信它们存在。为了获得令人满意的数学理论，它们是必需的，正如物理物体对于令人满意的感知理论是必需的；两种情况下，都不可能把我们希望对这些实体作出的命题，解释成关于“资料”的命题，即在后一情况下，关于实际发生的感知的命题。

It seems to me that the assumption of such objects is quite as legitimate as the assumption of physical objects and there is quite as much reason to believe in their existence. They are in the same sense necessary to obtain a satisfactory theory of mathematics as physical bodies are necessary for a satisfactory theory of our sense perceptions and in both cases it is impossible to interpret the propositions one wants to assert about these entities as propositions about the “data,” i.e., in the latter case the actually occurring sense perceptions.

这些肯定中，有一些来自不太关心、甚至全不关心基础的20世纪人物。令人惊讶的是，甚至某些基础工作的领袖——希尔伯特、阿隆佐·丘奇和布尔巴基学派成员——也肯定数学概念和性质在某种客观意义上存在，并能被人的心灵把握。因此，数学真理是发现而非发明的。演变的不是数学，而是人关于数学的知识。

Some of these affirmations come from twentieth-century men who were not much if at all concerned with foundations. What is surprising is that even some of the leaders in the work on foundations—Hilbert, Alonzo Church, and the members of the Bourbaki school—affirm that the mathematical concepts and properties exist in some objective sense and that they can be apprehended by hum^n minds. Thus mathematical truth is discovered not invented. What evolves is not mathematics but man’s knowledge of mathematics.

持这些观点的人常被称为柏拉图主义者。柏拉图确实相信，数学存在于独立于人的某种理想世界，但他的学说包含许多不适用于当前观点的内容，因此“柏拉图主义者”这一名称，与其说有帮助，不如说不恰当。

The men who hold these views are often called Platonists. Though Plato did believe that mathematics exists in some ideal world independent of human beings, his doctrines included much that does not apply to the current views, and the use of the appellation Platonist is more unsuitable than helpful.

这些关于客观、唯一数学整体存在的断言，没有解释数学在哪里。它们只是说，数学存在于某个人之外的世界、一座空中楼阁，只是被人察觉。公理和定理并非纯粹人的创造，而像矿藏中的财富，必须耐心挖掘，带到地面。但它们的存在，像行星看起来那样，独立于人。

These assertions about the existence of an objective, unique body of mathematics do not explain where mathematics resides. They say merely that mathematics exists in some extra-human world, a castle in the air, and is merely detected by man. The axioms and theorems are not purely human creations, rather they are like riches in a mine which have to be brought to the surface by patient digging. But their existence is as independent of man as the planets appear to be.

那么，数学是藏在宇宙深处、逐渐挖出的钻石，还是人制造的合成宝石，却仍如此灿烂，使那些已因自豪于自身创造而部分蒙蔽的数学家眼花缭乱？

Is then mathematics a collection of diamonds hidden in the depths of the universe and gradually unearthed, or is it a collection of synthetic stones manufactured by man, yet so brilliant nevertheless that they bedazzle those mathematicians who are already partially blinded by pride in their own creations?

此外，如果存在一个超感官而先验绝对的实体世界，如果逻辑与数学命题只是对这些实体的观察记录，那么矛盾和假命题，岂不与真命题在完全相同意义上存在？虚假与不一致的毒草，可能与善、真、美并肩繁茂。也许魔鬼与真理之神一同播种、收获。柏拉图主义者当然可以反驳，假命题与矛盾，只因为人把握真理的努力不足而产生。

Moreover, if there is a world of entities that are supra-sensible and transcendentally absolute, and if our propositions in logic and mathematics are mere registers of observations of these entities, then do not the contradictions and false propositions exist in exactly the same sense as true propositions? The noxious weeds of falsehood and inconsistency may flourish side by side with the good, the true, and the beautiful. Perhaps the Devil sows his seeds and raises his harvest along with the God of truth. The Platonists can of course retort that false propositions and contradictions arise only because man’s efforts to grasp the truth are inadequate.

第二种观点，即数学完全是人类思想的产物，当然由直觉主义者持有，并可追溯至亚里士多德。不过，有些人断言心灵保证真理，另一些人则主张，数学是会犯错的心灵的创造，而非固定的知识整体。早在现代争论出现前，帕斯卡在《思想录》中就作过经典表述：“真理是如此细微的尖点，我们的工具太钝，无法准确触及。触到它时，就压碎尖点，压在周围，落在假上的部分多于真。”主要直觉主义者阿伦德·海廷肯定，今天没人能谈真正的数学，即作为正确、唯一知识整体意义上的真。

The second view—that mathematics is entirely a product of human thought—is of course held by the intuitionists and can be traced back to Aristotle. However, whereas some assert that truth is guaranteed by the mind, others maintain that mathematics is the creation of fallible human minds rather than a fixed body of knowledge. A classic statement to this effect was made by Pascal in his Pensees long before the modern controversies arose. “Truth is so subtle a point that our instruments are too blunt to touch it exactly. When they do reach it, they crush the point and bear down around it, more on the false than on the true.” Arend Heyting, a leading intuitionist, affirmed that no one today can speak of the true mathematics, that is, true in the sense of a correct, unique body of knowledge.

赫尔曼·汉克尔、理查德·戴德金和卡尔·魏尔斯特拉斯都相信数学是人的创造。戴德金在给海因里希·韦伯的信中肯定：“我还建议，我们所谓数，不应指类本身，而应指某种新东西……由心灵创造。我们属于神圣种族，拥有……创造的力量。”魏尔斯特拉斯用“真正的数学家是诗人”赞同这一思想。罗素的学生、本身也是权威的路德维希·维特根斯坦（1889—1951），相信数学家是发明者而非发现者。这些人及其他人都认为，数学远远超出经验发现或理性推演的束缚。支持其立场的事实是，无理数和负数等初等概念，既非由经验发现推出，也不是明显存在于某个外部世界的实体。

Hermann Hankel, Richard Dedekind, and Karl Weierstrass all believed that mathematics is a human creation. Dedekind in a letter to Heinrich Weber affirmed: “I advise moreover that we understand by number not the class itself, but something new . . . which the mind creates. We are of a divine race and we possess ... the power to create.” Weierstrass endorsed this thought with the words, “The true mathematician is a poet.” And Ludwig Wittgenstein (1889-1951), a student of Russell and an authority in his own right, believed that the mathematician is an inventor not a discoverer. All these men and others conceive of mathematics as something far beyond bondage to empirical findings or rational deductions. In favor of their position is the fact that such elementary concepts as irrational numbers and negative numbers are neither deductions from empirical findings nor entities obviously existing in some external world.

赫尔曼·外尔也颇为讽刺永恒真理。他在《数学与自然科学的哲学》中说：

Hermann Weyl, too, was rather ironic about eternal truths. In his Philosophy of Mathematics and Natural Science, he said:

哥德尔对超越逻辑抱有根本信任，喜欢认为，我们的逻辑光学只是稍微失焦，希望稍作校正就能看清，然后人人都会同意我们看得正确。但不分享这种信任的人，会为Z［策梅洛］这样的体系，甚至希尔伯特体系中的高度任意性而不安……没有哪个希尔伯特能永远保证一致性；如果一个简单数学公理体系迄今经受住我们精细数学实验的检验，就必须满足。以后出现不相符的地方时，再改变基础也不迟。

Godel, with his basic trust in transcendental logic, likes to think that our logical optics is only slightly out of focus and hopes that after some minor correction of it we shall see sharp, and then everybody will agree that we see right. But he who does not share this trust will be disturbed by the high degree of arbitrariness in a system like Z [Zermelo’s], or even in Hilbert’s system. ... No Hilbert will be able to assure us of consistency forever; we must be content if a simple axiomatic system of mathematics has met the test of our elaborate mathematical experiments so far. It will be early enough to change the foundations when, at a later stage, discrepancies appear.

诺贝尔奖物理学家珀西·W.布里奇曼，在《现代物理的逻辑》（1946年）中断然拒绝任何客观数学世界。“数学是人的发明，这只是最平常的道理，不加雕琢的观察立即就能看清。”理论科学是一种数学假想游戏。这些人都主张，数学不仅人为，而且深受其发展所在文化的影响。它的“真理”像颜色感知或英语一样依赖人。也许只有数学相对普遍地被接受，不像政治、经济与宗教学说那样，才诱使我们相信，它是客观存在于人之外的真理整体。它可以独立于任何个人存在，却不能独立于个人所处文化。改述赫尔曼·外尔的话，数学不是孤立的技术成就，只是完整人类存在的一部分，并由此获得正当理由。

The Nobel prize-winning physicist Percy W. Bridgman, in The Logic of Modern Physics (1946), rejected flatly any objective world of mathematics. “It is the merest truism, evident at once to unsophisticated observation, that mathematics is a human invention.” Theoretical science is a game of mathematical make-believe. All these men contend that mathematics is not only man-made but very much influenced by the cultures in which it was developed. Its “truths” are as dependent on human beings as is the perception of color or the English language. Only the relatively universal acceptance of mathematics as opposed to political, economic, and religious doctrines may have lured us into believing that it is a body of truths existing objectively outside of man. It may exist independently of any one human but not of the culture in which he resides. To paraphrase Hermann Weyl, mathematics is not an isolated technical accomplishment but only a part of human existence in its totality, and thereby it finds its justification.

赞同数学人为观点的人，本质上是康德主义者，因为康德把数学源泉置于心灵的组织力量。但现代派说，数学并非源于心灵的形态或生理，而源于心灵活动。心灵用演化的方法组织。心灵的创造活动不断发展出更新、更高的思想形式。在数学中，人心能清楚看到，自己有自由创造感到有趣或有用的知识整体。而且创造领域并非封闭；适用于现有及新兴思想领域的观念将被创造。心灵能设计结构，容纳经验资料，提供安排它们的方式。数学的源泉是心灵本身的逐步发展。

The men who favor the view that mathematics is man-made are in essence Kantians, for he placed the source of mathematics in the organizing power of the mind. However, the modernists say that it is not in the morphology or physiology of the mind that mathematics originates; rather it is in the activity of the mind. It organizes by methods that are evolutionary. The creative activity of the mind constantly evolves newer and higher forms of thought. In mathematics the human mind is able to see clearly that it is free to create a body of knowledge that it finds interesting or useful. Moreover the field of creation is not a closed one. Notions that apply to existing and newly arising fields of thought will be created. The mind has the power to devise structures that will embrace the data of experience and provide a mode of arranging them. The source of mathematics is the progressive development of the mind itself.

当前关于数学本性的冲突，以及数学今天并非普遍接受、无可争议的知识整体这一事实，当然支持数学人为的观点。正如爱因斯坦说：“谁若试图把自己立为真理和知识领域的裁判，就会在诸神的笑声中覆舟。”

The present conflicts about the nature of mathematics itself and the fact that mathematics is not today a universally accepted, indisputable body of knowledge certainly favor the view that mathematics is man-made. As Einstein put it, “Whoever undertakes to set himself up as a judge in the field of Truth and Knowledge is shipwrecked by the laughter of the gods.”

理性时代的知识分子，把数学作为人的理性力量及获取真理能力的证据，自信断言理性会解决人的所有问题，颇具讽刺意味。20世纪知识分子中，有些人无论多么相信理性力量，也肯定不能把数学作为标准和典范。这种变化近乎思想灾难。数学仍是人类为实现精确而有效思考所作的最广泛、最深刻努力，其成就衡量人类心灵的能力，代表一切理性领域所能希望达到的上限。但今天，关于何为有效数学的混乱，不能给人多少安慰。这就是希尔伯特为何如此迫切地寻求恢复作为客观、无可攻击的推理意义上的真理。他在1925年《论无穷》中说：“如果连数学思维都失败，可靠性与真理还到哪里寻找？”

It is rather ironic that the intellectuals of the Age of Reason, pointing to mathematics as evidence of man’s rational powers and his ability to obtain truths, confidently asserted that reason would solve all of man’s problems. Intellectuals of the twentieth century, however confident some may be of the power of reason, certainly cannot point to mathematics as the standard and paradigm. This turn of events is not far short of an intellectual disaster. It is still true that mathematics is man’s most extensive and most profound effort to achieve precise and effective thinking and what it accomplishes measures the capacity of the human mind. It represents the upper limit of what we can hope to attain in all rational domains. But today one cannot derive much comfort from the current confusion about what valid mathematics is. This is why Hilbert sought so desperately to restore truth in the sense of objective, unassailable reasoning. As he put it in his paper of 1925 “On the Infinite”: “And where else would reliability and truth be found if even mathematical thinking fails?”

他在1928年博洛尼亚国际大会的演讲中，重复这一忧虑：

He repeated this concern in a talk he gave at the International Congress in Bologna (1928):

如果数学中没有真理，我们知识的真理性，以及科学的存在与进步，首先会怎样呢？今天，专业著述与公开演讲中，确实经常出现对知识的怀疑与沮丧；这是一种我认为有害的神秘主义。

For how would it be above all with the truth of our knowledge and with the existence and progress of science if there were no truth in mathematics? Indeed there often appears today in professional writings and public lectures skepticism and despondency about knowledge; this is a certain kind of occultism which I regard as damaging.

不断、无止境地寻求绝对，似乎次于真正获得绝对；但很早以前，歌德指出，这正是人的救赎：

A continual, never-ending search for absolutes may seem second best to actual attainment of absolutes, but a long time ago Goethe pointed out that this is man’s saving grace:

凡永远努力不懈的人，我们就能拯救。*

Wer immer strebend sicb bemiiht Den konnen wir erlosen.*

*凡不断奋斗者皆可获救。

* Whoever strives constantly can be saved.

当代主要数学家之一安德烈·韦伊，虽不那么确信绝对真理存在，却主张，即使数学不是人类理性的宏伟高塔，仍必须推进数学研究。他说：

Though not as confident of the existence of absolute truths, Andre Weil, one of the leading mathematicians of our time, maintains that the pursuit of mathematics must be furthered even though it is not the majestic tower of human reason. As he put it:

我们肩负希腊思想遗产，重压使双肩下垂，沿着文艺复兴英雄开辟的道路前行；对我们而言，没有数学的文明不可想象。像平行公设一样，数学会存续的公设，也已被剥去“自明性”；但前者已不再必需，后者却不可或缺。

For us, whose shoulders sag under the weight of the heritage of Greek thought and who walk in the paths traced out by the heroes of the Renaissance, a civilization without mathematics is unthinkable. Like the parallel postulate, the postulate that mathematics will survive has been stripped of its “evidence;” but, while the former is no longer necessary, we would not be able to get on without the latter.

数学未来从未如此充满希望，其本性也从未如此不清楚。对明显事物的细微分析，产生了无尽复杂性的螺旋。但数学家将继续与基础问题搏斗。正如笛卡尔所说：“我将坚持下去，直到找到确定的东西——或者至少，确定地发现没有任何东西是确定的。”

The future of mathematics has never been of greater promise; the nature of it has never been less clear. The subtle analysis of the obvious has produced a spiral of never-ending complications. But mathematicians will continue to struggle with foundational problems. As Descartes put it, “I shall persevere until I find something that is certain—or, at least, until I find for certain that nothing is certain.”

据荷马说，诸神判科林斯国王西西弗斯死后永远把大石头滚上山，每次接近山顶，石头又落回山脚。他不幻想劳作有朝一日结束。数学家拥有近乎本能的意志和勇气，去完善和巩固学科基础。他们的斗争也可能永远继续，他们也可能永不成功。但现代西西弗斯们会坚持。

According to Homer, the gods condemned Sisyphus, king of Corinth, after his death perpetually to roll a big rock uphill, only to see it fall back to the bottom each time he neared the summit. He had no illusion that some day his labors would end. Mathematicians have the will and the courage that comes almost instinctively to complete and solidify the foundations of their subject. Their struggle too may go on forever; they too may never succeed. But the modern Sisyphuses will persist.

第十五章 自然的权威

XV. The Authority of Nature

我作这样的祈祷，知道自然从未背叛，爱她的心……

And this prayer I make, Knowing that Nature never did betray The heart that loved her . . .

威廉·华兹华斯

William Wordsworth

数学家能沿许多互相冲突的方向推导新结果。没有内部标准偏爱某个方向、或为其辩护，选择就必须基于外部考虑。其中最重要的，当然是创造发展数学的传统理由，也是至今最有依据的理由：对科学的价值。如今显露的数学适当基础的不确定性，以及逻辑牢固性的问题，可以通过强调对自然的应用来抵挡，虽不能解决。用爱默生的话说，让我们“在物质中为心灵建家”。不能先验地确定，产生的数学定理是否必然直接适用，或与可靠物理原则结合时，从这些原则推出的结果是否在物理上正确。但应用确实提供实用检验。一次次产生正确结果的定理，可以越来越放心地使用。例如，若持续使用选择公理带来可靠物理结果，关于可接受性的疑虑至少会减轻。

Mathematicians can pursue many conflicting directions to derive new results. In the absence of internal criteria that favor or justify one direction rather than another, a choice must be based on external considerations. Of these, certainly the most important is the traditional and still most justifiable reason for the creation and development of mathematics, its value to the sciences. The uncertainties now evident about the proper foundation for mathematics and the questions about the solidity of its logic can be parried, though not resolved, by stressing application to nature. In the words of Emerson, let us “build in matter home for mind.” One cannot determine on a priori grounds whether mathematical theorems produced will necessarily apply directly, or whether, if used in conjunction with sound physical principles, the deductions from these principles will lead to physically correct results. However, application does provide a pragmatic test. The theorems that lead to correct results time after time may be used with increasing confidence. If continued use of the axiom of choice, for example, leads to sound physical results, then certainly doubts concerning its acceptability are at least diminished.

从历史看，诉诸应用并不像当代数学纯粹派觉得的那么激进。概念和公理来自观察物理世界。甚至逻辑规律现在也普遍被承认为经验产物。导致定理的问题，乃至关于证明方法的提示，都来自同一源头。至少直到约七十五年前，从公理推导的结果的价值或意义，都按它们对物理世界所肯定的东西判断。为何不根据数学能否继续很好地描述和预测物理事件，检验其正确性？当然，按适用性判断数学正确性，不会有绝对检验。定理可能适用于n个情况，却在第n+1个失败。一次不符就使定理失格。但修改可能带来、历史上也确实带来能够继续确保有用性的纠正。

From the historical standpoint, the appeal to applications is not as radical as it may seem to present-day mathematical purists. The concepts and axioms came from observation of the physical world. Even the laws of logic are now generally granted to be the product of experience. The problems which led to theorems and even suggestions about methods of proof came from this same source. And the value or significance of the results deduced from the axioms was judged, at least until seventy-five or so years ago, by what they affirmed about the physical world. Why not test correctness by how well mathematics continues to describe and predict physical happenings? Insofar as one judges the correctness of mathematics by its applicability, there can, of course, be no absolute test. A theorem may work in n cases and fail in the (n + 1)th case. One disagreement disqualifies the theorem. But modification may lead, and historically has led, to corrections that will continue to ensure usefulness.

约翰·斯图尔特·密尔（1806—1873）曾倡导数学的经验基础与检验。他承认，数学比各物理科学更一般。但为数学“辩护”的，是其命题比物理科学命题受到更广泛的检验和证实。因此，人们错误地认为，数学定理与其他科学分支中经确认的假说和理论有质的差别。定理被视为确定，物理理论却被视为极可能、或仅获经验支持。

An empirical foundation and test for mathematics had been advocated by John Stuart Mill (1806-1873). He admitted that mathematics is more general than the several physical sciences. But what “justifies” mathematics is that its propositions have been tested and confirmed to a greater extent than those of the physical sciences. Hence men came to think incorrectly of mathematical theorems as qualitatively different from confirmed hypotheses and theories of other branches of science. The theorems were taken as certain whereas physical theories were thought of as very probable or merely corroborated by experience.

密尔早在现代基础争论出现前，就从哲学理由提出主张。近来及当前许多基础研究者，更有理由转向实用主义。正如希尔伯特说：“凭他们的果实，就能认识他们。”1925年他又说：“在数学中，如同其他地方，成功是人人服从其裁决的最高法院。”

Mill based his assertions on philosophical grounds, long before the modern foundational controversies arose. With all the more reason many recent and current workers in the foundations have become pragmatic. As Hilbert remarked, “By their fruits shall ye know them.” Hilbert also said in 1925, “In mathematics as elsewhere success is the supreme court to whose decisions everyone submits.”

著名而活跃的基础研究者安杰伊·莫斯托夫斯基赞同。1953年在波兰举行的一次大会上，他说：

Andrzej Mostowski, one of the prominent and active workers in the foundations, agrees. At a congress held in Poland in 1953, he stated:

唯一一致、既符合健全人类理解也符合数学传统的观点，倒是这样一个假定：数概念——不只是自然数，也包括实数——的源泉与最终存在理由，在于经验及实际适用性。集合论概念在古典数学领域所需的范围内，也同样如此。

The only consistent point of view, which is in accord not only with healthy human understanding but also with mathematical tradition, is rather the assumption that the source and last raison d’etre of the number concept—not only the natural but also the real numbers—lie in experience and practical applicability. The same is true of the concepts of set theory insofar as they are needed in the classical domains of mathematics.

莫斯托夫斯基更进一步，说数学是自然科学。概念和方法源于经验，任何不顾数学在自然科学中的起源、应用乃至历史，而为数学奠基的尝试，都注定失败。

Mostowski goes further. He says that mathematics is a natural science. Its concepts and methods have their origin in experience, and any attempts to found mathematics without regard to its origin in the natural sciences, its applications, and even its history are doomed to fail.

也许更令人惊讶的是，直觉主义者外尔也同意，可以通过应用于物理世界判断可靠性。外尔对数学物理贡献很大，虽坚定支持直觉主义原则，却不愿顽固坚持这些原则而牺牲有用结果。他在《数学与自然科学的哲学》（1949年）中承认：

Perhaps more surprising is that Weyl, an intuitionist, also agreed that soundness may be judged by application to the physical world. Weyl had contributed much to mathematical physics and, firm as he was in support of the intuitionistic principles, he was not willing to sacrifice useful results by unyielding adherence to these principles. In his Philosophy of Mathematics and Natural Science (1949), he conceded:

爱因斯坦广义相对论，或海森堡－薛定谔量子力学中的启发性论证及随后系统建构，是多么更令人信服、更接近事实。真正现实的数学，应与物理一致，被理解为关于唯一真实世界的理论建构的一个分支；对基础的假设性扩展，应采用物理所表现的同样清醒谨慎的态度。

How much more convincing and closer to facts are the heuristic arguments and the subsequent systematic constructions in Einstein’s general relativity theory, or the Heisenberg-Schrodinger quantum mechanics. A truly realistic mathematics should be conceived, in line with physics, as a branch of the theoretical construction of the one real world, and should adopt the same sober and cautious attitude toward hypothetic extensions of its foundations as is exhibited by physics.

外尔无疑倡导把数学作为科学之一。其定理像物理定理一样，可能暂定且不稳固，可能必须改写；但与现实对应，是可靠性的一个确切检验。

Weyl is certainly advocating treating mathematics as one of the sciences. Its theorems, like those of physics, may be tentative and precarious. They may have to be recast but correspondence with reality is one sure test of soundness.

著名而活跃的形式主义者哈斯凯尔·B.柯里愿意走得更远。在《数理逻辑基础》（1963年）中，他论证：

Haskell B. Curry, a prominent and active formalist, is willing to go further. In his Foundations of Mathematical Logic (1963), he argued:

但数学需要绝对确定性，才能获得正当理由吗？尤其，为何使用一个理论之前，必须确信它一致，或能由关于纯粹时间的绝对确定直觉推出？其他科学都没有这种要求。在物理中，所有定理都是假设性的；只要理论作出有用预测，我们就采用它，一旦不能，就修改或抛弃。过去数学理论也是如此，发现矛盾导致修改截至发现时接受的数学学说。为何未来不能同样做？

But does mathematics need absolute certainty for its justification? In particular, why do we need to be sure a theory is consistent or that it can be derived by an absolutely certain intuition of pure time, before we use it? In no other science do we make such demands. In physics all theorems are hypothetical; we adopt a theory so long as it makes useful predictions and modify or discard it as soon as it does not. This is what happened to mathematical theories in the past, where the discovery of contradictions has led to modification in the mathematical doctrines accepted up to the time of that discovery. Why should we not do the same in the future?

活跃的逻辑主义者威拉德·范·奥曼·蒯因，曾多次尝试简化罗素－怀特海《数学原理》，却未成功；至少目前，他也愿意满足于物理可靠性。在1958年一篇收入《现代逻辑的哲学意义》的文章中，他说：

Willard Van Orman Quine, an active ldgicist who made many unsuccessful efforts to simplify the Russell-Whitehead Principia, has also been willing, at least for the present, to settle for physical soundness. In an article of 1958, part of the collection entitled The Philosophical Bearing of Modern Logic, he said:

更合理的是，把集合论及一般数学，大体像自然科学的理论部分一样看待：它们包含的真理或假说，其正当性与其说来自纯粹理性的光芒，不如说来自它们对组织自然科学经验资料所作的间接而系统的贡献。

We may more reasonably view set theory, and mathematics generally, in much the way in which we view theoretical portions of the natural sciences themselves; as comprising truths or hypotheses which are to be vindicated less by the light of pure reason than by the indirect systematic contribution which they make to the organizing of empirical data in the natural sciences.

对形式主义和集合论作出根本贡献的冯·诺伊曼，也愿意用相同方式越过当前僵局。在著名文章《数学家》（收于罗伯特·B.海伍德编《心灵的工作》，1947年）中，他论证，各基础学派虽未成功为古典数学辩护，大多数数学家仍使用它：

Von Neumann, who made fundamental contributions to formalism and to set theory, was also willing to surmount the present impasse in the same way. In a famous article “The Mathematician” (to be found in Robert B. Heywood’s The Works of the Mind, 1947), he argued that though the several foundational schools have not succeeded in justifying classical mathematics, most mathematicians use it anyway:

毕竟，古典数学产生优雅而有用的结果；虽再也不能绝对确信其可靠性，它的基础至少与比如电子的存在一样可靠。因此，若愿意接受科学，不妨也接受古典数学体系。

After all classical mathematics was producing results which were both elegant and useful, and, even though one could never again be absolutely certain of its reliability, it stood on at least as sound a foundation as, for example, the existence of the electron. Hence if one was willing to accept the sciences, one might as well accept the classical system of mathematics.

因此，数学的地位并不优于物理。

The status of mathematics, then, is no better than that of physics.

甚至罗素，1901年声称数学真理的逻辑及物理大厦仍不可动摇，却在1914年的文章中承认：“关于物理几何的知识是综合的，却非先验的。”它不能仅由逻辑推出。在《数学原理》第二版（1926年）中，他作更多让步：逻辑和数学像电磁理论的麦克斯韦方程一样，“之所以被相信，是因为观察到其某些逻辑后果为真”。

Even Russell, who in 1901 claimed that the edifice of mathematical truth, logical and physical, remained unshakable, admitted in an essay of 1914 that “our knowledge of physical geometry is synthetic but not a priori.” It is not deducible from logic alone. In the second edition of his Principia (1926), he conceded still more. Logic and mathematics like Maxwell’s equation of electromagnetic theory “are believed because of the observed truth of certain of their logical consequences.”

也许更令人惊讶的是，哥德尔1950年的陈述：

Perhaps more surprising is Godel’s statement of 1950 that

所谓“基础”的作用，倒更像物理理论中解释性假说的功能……所谓数论或任何其他牢固确立的数学理论的逻辑或集合论基础，是解释性的，而非奠基性的；正如物理中，公理的实际功能，是解释该体系定理所描述的现象，而非为这些定理提供真正基础。

the role of the alleged “foundations” is rather comparable to the function discharged, in physical theory, by explanatory hypotheses. . . . The so-called logical or set-theoretical foundation for number theory or of any other well established mathematical theory is explanatory, rather than foundational, exactly as in physics where the actual function of axioms is to explain the phenomena described by the theorems of this system rather than to provide a genuine foundation for such theorems.

这些领袖承认的是，确立普遍可接受、逻辑可靠的数学整体的尝试失败了。数学是人的活动，受人类一切弱点和脆弱性影响。任何形式逻辑的叙述，虽有理性成分，却是伪数学、虚构，甚至传说。

What these leaders are acknowledging is that the attempt to establish a universally acceptable, logically sound body of mathematics has failed. Mathematics is a human activity and is subject to all the foibles and frailties of humans. Any formal, logical account is a pseudomathematics, a fiction, even a legend, despite the element of reason.

许多其他著名基础研究者，也接受相同的可靠数学检验作为实际解决办法。数学可由适用性牢固、虽非绝对地得到保障，即使偶尔需要纠正。正如华兹华斯说：“永恒建造的心灵，信赖自然的坚实大地。”

Many other prominent workers in the foundations have accepted as a practical solution the same test of what sound mathematics is. Mathematics can be firmly, if not absolutely, secured by its applicability even if occasional corrections are required. As Wordsworth put it, “To the solid ground of nature trusts the Mind that builds for aye.”

基础研究者倡导实用检验，即数学对科学的适用性，似乎放弃了自己的原则与信念。但不论是否意识到，他们所肯定的，只是历来数学可靠性的检验。鉴于那些不合逻辑的发展（第五至第八章），那些世纪的数学家为何相信数学？他们未察觉证明有缺陷，以为已经证明一些结果。但肯定知道，负数、无理数、复数、代数和微积分，都没有逻辑支持。他们依赖适用性。

In urging the pragmatic test, the applicability of mathematics to science, the foundationalists may seem to be abandoning their own principles and convictions. But, whether they realized it or not, they were affirming only what had always been the test of mathematical soundness. In view of the illogical development (Chapters V-VIII), why did the mathematicians of those centuries believe in mathematics? Failing to recognize that their proofs were faulty, they thought that they had proved some results. But surely they knew that no logic supported negative, irrational, and complex numbers, or algebra, or the calculus. They relied upon applicability.

诉诸科学适用性，或者说经验证据，具有值得注意的含义。欧几里得理想预先假定，从真公理开始，以有效推理推出更多真理。依赖物理适用性，颠倒了整个数学观。如果推论适用，公理至少合理，虽未必是产生这些结论的唯一公理。在有用或可应用数学的意义上，真理并不是向上流动的。

The resort to scientific applicability, or, one can say, empirical evidence, has an implication that is worth noting. The Euclidean ideal presupposed that one starts with axioms that are truths and that from these axioms one deduces further truths by valid reasoning. Reliance upon physical applicability reverses the entire concept of mathematics. If the deductions apply, then the axioms are at least reasonable, though not necessarily the only ones which can give rise to the conclusions. Truth, in the sense of useful or applicable mathematics, does not flow upward.

实际上，基础学派的领袖，至少曾在长时期内搁置自己的信念。直觉主义学派奠基人之一克罗内克，做过一些不符合自身标准的优秀代数工作，因为正如庞加莱说，他忘了自己的哲学。布劳威尔也在1907年论文中宣布直觉主义哲学后，把随后十年用于拓扑研究和证明，忽视直觉主义学说。

Actually the leaders of foundational schools did at least for long periods of time put aside their own convictions. Thus Kronecker, one of the founders of the intuitionist school, did some fine work in algebra that did not conform to his own standards because, as Poincare remarked, Kronecker forgot his own philosophy. Brouwer, too, after proclaiming his philosophy of intuitionism in his thesis of 1907, spent the next decade on research and proofs in topology wherein he ignored the intuitionist doctrines.

这些观点的结果是，可靠数学不能由某个有朝一日可能被证明正确的基础决定。数学的“正确性”必须按它对物理世界的适用性判断。数学像牛顿力学一样，是经验科学，只在有效的范围内正确；无效时必须修改。虽然被如此看待两千年，它并非先验知识，也非绝对、不变的。

The upshot of these views is that sound mathematics must be determined not by any one foundation which may some day prove to be right. The “correctness” of mathematics must be judged by its applicability to the physical world. Mathematics is an empirical science much as Newtonian mechanics. It is correct only to the extent that it works and when it does not, it must be modified. It is not a priori knowledge even though it was so regarded for two thousand years. It is not absolute or unchangeable.

如果把数学作为科学之一，就必须充分了解科学如何运作。科学观察、实验，构建运动、光、声、热、电、化学结合等理论。理论是人为的，通过进一步观察实验检验预测。若预测至少在实验误差内得到证实，理论就保留。但它以后可能被推翻，始终必须视为理论，而非内在于物理世界设计中的真理。我们习惯这种科学理论观，因为已有许多旧理论被推翻、被新理论替代的例子。人不接受这种数学观的唯一原因，如密尔指出，是基本算术与欧几里得几何数百年有效，使人误当为真理。但现在必须看到，数学任何分支只提供一个有效理论。只要有效，就坚持；以后可能需要更好的。数学确实在人与自然、内心与外部世界之间作媒介，是我们与外部世界之间大胆而强有力的桥梁。不得不认识到桥梁既未牢固锚定现实，也未牢固锚定人心，是悲剧。

If mathematics is to be treated as one of the sciences, it is important to be fully aware of how science operates. It makes observations and experiments and constructs a theory, a theory of motion, or of light, sound, heat, electricity, chemical combinations, and so forth. These theories are man-made and are tested by checking their predictions with further observation and experiment. If the predictions are verified at least within experimental error, the theory is maintained. But it may be overthrown later and must always be regarded as a theory and not as truth imbedded in the design of the physical world. We are accustomed to this view of scientific theories because we have had many examples of scientific theories being overthrown and rejected for new ones. The only reason men did not accept this view of mathematics is, as Mill pointed out, that basic arithmetic and Euclidean geometry were effective for so many centuries that people mistook it for truth. But we must now see that any branch of mathematics offers only a theory that works. As long as it works we shall hold to it, but a better one may be needed later. Mathematics does mediate between man and nature, between his inner and outer worlds. It is a bold and formidable bridge between ourselves and the external world. It is tragic to have to recognize that the bridge is not firmly anchored in reality or in human minds.

理性只洞悉它按自身计划构建的东西；理性虽可提出方案率先行动，随后必须通过实验从自然引出这些方案是否明智的答案。有提出理论之时，也有依据自然表现决定理论命运之时。

Reason possesses insights only into that which reason itself constructs according to its own plan, and though reason may take the lead with its own proposals, it must then by experiment elicit from nature the wisdom of these proposals. There is a time for theory and a time to decide the disposition of that theory by nature’s behavior.

有一种性质使大部分数学区别于物理理论。科学理论曾发生根本变化，数学中大部分逻辑、数论和古典分析，却已运作数百年，过去和现在都适用。在这范围内，数学不同于其他科学。不论这些部分绝对可靠与否，它们一直很好地服务，可以称为准经验的。

There is one quality that distinguishes most of mathematics from physical theories. Whereas in science there have been radical changes in theories, in mathematics most of the logic, number theory, and classical analysis has functioned for centuries. They have been and still are applicable. To this extent mathematics differs from the other sciences. Whether or not these portions of mathematics are absolutely reliable, they have served well. They can be called quasi-empirical.

微积分史尤其支持这一观点。尽管微积分逻辑公开争论，它作为方法一直成功。讽刺的是，非标准分析（第十二章）为莱布尼茨无穷小理论辩护，却未为微积分全部技术辩护。

Support for this view can be drawn especially from the history of the calculus. Despite the open debates about the logic of the calculus, it has been successful as a methodology. Ironically non-standard analysis (Chapter XII) has justified Leibniz’s theory of infinitesimals but not all of the techniques of the calculus.

甚至选择公理也可受适用性检验。策梅洛在1908年论文中说：“皮亚诺怎样得到自己的基本原则……毕竟他也无法证明它们？显然，是分析历史上被认为有效的推理方式，并指出这些原则在直觉上明显、对科学必需……”策梅洛为使用选择公理辩护时，指出使用公理取得的成功。他在1908年论文中列举，选择公理即使到那时，已在超限数理论、戴德金有限数理论，以及更技术性的分析问题中非常有用。

One can apply the test of applicability even to the axiom of choice. As Zermelo himself said in his paper of 1908, “How does Peano arrive at his own fundamental principles . . . since after all he cannot prove them either? Evidently by analyzing the modes of inference that in the course of history came to be recognized as valid and by pointing out that the principles are intuitively evident and necessary for science. . . . Zermelo in defending his use of the axiom of choice pointed to the successes achieved by using the axiom. He cited in his 1908 paper how useful the axiom had been (even by then) in the theory of transfimte numbers, in Dedekind’s theory of finite numbers, and in more technical problems of analysis.

各位领袖建议，以对科学的应用作为指引和可靠性的检验，动机不只是想在几种基础之间选择。他们认识到，数学驾驭物理现象的力量大幅增加，不能在争论基础问题时，放弃对人类的服务。许多数学家约一百年前虽基于更多是浮华而非有价值的理由放弃科学，近代最伟大的领袖庞加莱、希尔伯特、冯·诺伊曼和外尔，却一直研究物理应用。

The recommendation of various leaders that applications to science be utilized as a guide and a test of what is reliable is motivated by more than a desire to choose among the several foundations. These men recognize that the power of mathematics to master physical phenomena has increased enormously and this service to mankind cannot be abandoned while foundational issues are thrashed out. Though many mathematicians, for reasons more meretricious than meritorious, did abandon science about one hundred years ago, the greatest of the recent leaders, Poincare, Hilbert, von Neumann, and Weyl, have constantly pursued physical applications.

不幸的是，当今大多数数学家不研究应用（第十三章），而以越来越快速度产生纯数学新结果。《数学评论》杂志简评新的、据说重要的结果，可据此了解当前纯数学和应用数学研究的规模。每期月刊约2500项，每年约30000项。

Unfortunately, most mathematicians today do not work on applications (Chapter XIII). Instead they continue to produce new results in pure mathematics at an ever increasing pace. Some indication of the current volume of research (pure and applied) may be gained from the journal Mathematical Reviews, which reviews briefly the new and presumably significant results. There are about 2500 in each monthly issue or about 30,000 per year.

人们会以为，当前关于何为正确数学、哪种思想学派最可靠，以及甚至一个学派内部也可沿多重方向发展的困境，会使纯数学家停下来，先集中研究基础问题，再创造可能在逻辑上错误的新数学。那么，他们怎能如此轻快地继续在无应用的领域产生新结果？

One would think that the present quandary concerning correct mathematics, which school of thought is soundest, and the multiple directions mathematics can pursue even within any one school of thought, would give pure mathematicians pause and move them to concentrate on foundational problems before creating new mathematics that may indeed prove to be logically incorrect. How then can they proceed so blithely to produce new results in areas of mathematics that are not applied?

这个问题有几个答案。许多数学家不了解基础工作。1900年以来数学家的工作方式，是人应对许多问题的典型方式。他们几乎都在高大数学建筑中设办公室。基础工作者越挖越深，以确保结构，住户却继续占用建筑、进行工作。基础工作者深入地下，完全不见踪影，住户不知道结构支撑有问题，或有倒塌危险。因此继续使用传统数学。他们不知道流行正统受到任何挑战，乐于在其中工作。

There are several answers to this question. Many mathematicians are ignorant of the work in foundations. The manner in which mathematicians have been working since 1900 is typical of the way in which human beings face many of their problems. Almost all of them maintain offices in the tall structure of mathematics. While the foundation workers dig farther and farther down to secure the structure, the tenants of the building continue to occupy it and do their work. The people working on the foundations delve so far below ground that they are completely out of sight and the tenants are not aware that there is any concern about the support of the structure or that there is a danger of collapse. Hence they continue to use the conventional mathematics. They do not know of any challenge to the prevailing orthodoxy and so are happy to work within it.

另一些当代数学家知道基础不确定，却对他们称为哲学、而非纯数学的问题采取超然态度。他们难以相信基础，或至少自己的数学活动，可能有严重问题。他们宁愿受过时信条哺育。对他们，不成文准则是：像过去七十五年什么都没发生一样继续。他们谈普遍接受意义上的证明，虽没有这种东西；写作发表，仿佛不确定性不存在。他们关心新出版物，越多越好。若尊重可靠基础，也只在星期日；那天或祈求宽恕，或暂停写新论文，阅读竞争者在做什么。个人进步是必须的——不论对错。

Other contemporary mathematicians are aware of the uncertainties in the foundations but prefer to take an aloof attitude toward what they characterize as philosophical (as opposed to purely mathematical) questions. They find it hard to believe that there can be any serious concern about the foundations, or at least about their own mathematical activity. They prefer to be suckled in a creed outworn. For these men the unwritten code states: Let us proceed as though nothing has happened in the last seventy-five years. They speak of proof in some universally accepted sense even though there is no such animal, and write and publish as if the uncertainties were non-existent. What matters for them is new publications, the more the better. If they respect sound foundations at all, it is only on Sundays and on that day they either pray for forgiveness or they desist from writing new papers in order to read what their competitors are doing. Personal progress is a must—right or wrong.

难道没有权威，能以基础问题待解为由要求克制？期刊编辑可以拒稿。但编辑和审稿人是同行，与广大数学家立场相同。因此，保持某种严密性外观，即1900年的严密性的论文，会被接受发表。如果皇帝无衣，朝廷也无衣，裸体就不再令人惊讶，也不引起尴尬。正如拉普拉斯曾写，人类理性取得进步，比研究自身更少困难。

Are there then no authorities who might urge restraint on the ground that foundational issues remain to be resolved? The editors of journals could refuse papers. But the editors and referees are peers who take the same position as mathematicians at large. Hence papers that maintain some semblance of rigor, the rigor of 1900, are accepted and published. If the emperor has no clothes and the court also has none, nudity is no longer astonishing, nor does it cause any embarrassment. As Laplace once wrote, human reason has less difficulty in making progress than in investigating itself.

无论如何，许多数学家把基础问题放逐到边陲。数理逻辑学家确实投入精力研究，但这个群体常被视为在数学本身之外。

In any case, foundational questions are relegated by many mathematicians to the hinterland. The mathematical logicians do devote their energies to the foundational problem, but this group is often regarded as outside the pale of mathematics proper.

不能谴责所有忽视基础问题、仿佛它们不存在而继续工作的数学家。有些认真关注数学的使用，援引历史支持这种生活方式。我们见过（第五、六章），数系及运算、微积分缺乏逻辑基础，争论热烈持续一个多世纪，数学家仍继续使用这些内容，产生确实有效的新结果。证明粗糙，甚至不存在。发现矛盾时，他们重新检验、修改推理。推理常被改进，却甚至按19世纪末标准仍不严密。若等到达到那标准，就不会有进步。埃米尔·皮卡说，牛顿和莱布尼茨若知道连续函数不一定可导，就永不会发明微积分。过去，大胆与谨慎共同产生重要进步。

One cannot condemn all of the mathematicians who ignore foundational problems and proceed as though they were non-existent. Some are seriously concerned with utilizing mathematics, and they call upon historical support for their modus vivendi. As we have seen (Chapters V and VI), despite the lack of logical foundations for the number system and operations with it and for the calculus, about which heated arguments took place for over a century, mathematicians proceeded to utilize the material and to produce new results which are certainly effective. The proofs were crude or even non-existent. When contradictions were discovered, mathematicians re-examined their reasoning and modified it. Often the reasoning was improved but was still not rigorous even by late-nineteenth-century standards. Had the mathematicians waited until they attained that standard, they would have made no progress. As Emile Picard remarked, if Newton and Leibniz had been aware that continuous functions were not necessarily differentiable, the calculus would never have been invented. In the past, audacity and prudence produced the important progress.

哲学家乔治·桑塔亚纳在《怀疑主义与动物信仰》中指出，怀疑对思考重要，动物信仰对行为重要。许多数学研究价值极高，要滋养这些价值，研究必须继续。动物信仰提供行动的信心。

The philosopher George Santayana in his book Skepticism and Animal Faith pointed out that while skepticism and doubt are important for thinking, animal faith is important for behavior. The values of much mathematical research are superb and if these values are to be nourished, research must go on. Animal faith supplies the confidence to act.

少数数学家表达了对质疑其工作的基础问题的忧虑。埃米尔·波莱尔、勒内·贝尔和亨利·勒贝格明确怀疑集合论方法的有效性，却继续使用，对所得结果的可靠性有所保留。波莱尔1905年说，他愿意参与康托尔超限数推理，因为有助于重要数学工作。但波莱尔等人采用这条道路，并不轻松。听听赫尔曼·外尔的话，他是现代数学家中最深刻、无疑也最博学的人之一：

A few mathematicians have expressed their concern about foundational issues that impugn their work. Emile Borel, Rene Baire, and Henri Lebesgue stated explicitly their doubts about the validity of set-theoretic methods but continued to use them with some reservation about the reliability of what they yielded. Borel said in 1905 that he was willing to indulge in reasoning about the Cantorian transfinite numbers because they are helpful in vital mathematical work. However, the course adopted by Borel and others has not been light-hearted. Let us listen to the words of Hermann Weyl, one of the deepest and certainly the most erudite of modern mathematicians:

我们对数学和逻辑的最终基础，比以往更不确定。像当今世界的所有人和一切事物，我们有自己的“危机”，已有近五十年［截至1946年］。表面上，它似乎不妨碍日常工作，但我承认，它对我的数学生活有相当实际的影响；它使兴趣转向自认为相对“安全”的领域，不断消耗研究的热情与决心。那些关心自己的科学努力在人的整个关怀与认知、受苦与创造性存在中意味着什么的数学家，可能也有这种经验。

We are less certain than ever about the ultimate foundations of mathematics and logic. Like everybody and everything in the world today, we have our “crisis.” We have had it for nearly fifty years [as of 1946]. Outwardly it does not seem to hamper our daily work, and yet I for one confess that it has had a considerable practical influence on my mathematical life; it directed my interests to fields I considered relatively “safe,” and has been a constant drain on the enthusiasm and determination with which I pursued my research work. This experience is probably shared by other mathematicians who are not indifferent to what their scientific endeavors mean in the context of man’s whole caring and knowing, suffering and creative existence in the world.
