按适用性检验数学可靠性，立即引出问题：数学有效到什么程度？对于1800年前创建并应用的数学，我们已有机会（第三章）通过几个例子展示，它如何出色地描述和预测物理世界实际发生的事。但19世纪，数学家引入一些概念理论，无论动机多么值得赞许，却不直接来自自然，甚至似乎与自然不符，如无穷级数、非欧几里得几何、复数、四元数、奇异代数、各种大小的无限集合，以及未讨论的其他创造。没有先验理由预期它们应该适用。先让我们确信，现代数学确实有效，而且极其有效。

To test the soundness of mathematics by its applicability immediately raises a question. How well does mathematics work? As for the mathematics created and applied before 1800, we have already had occasion (Chapter III) to demonstrate through several examples how remarkably well mathematics describes and predicts what does happen in the physical world. However, in the nineteenth century, mathematicians introduced concepts and theories that, however commendable the motivation, were not drawn directly from nature and even seemed at variance with nature, for example, infinite series, non-Euclidean geometries, complex numbers, quaternions, strange algebras, infinite sets of various sizes, and other creations we have not treated. On a priori grounds there is no reason to expect that these concepts and theories should apply. Let us first assure ourselves that this modern mathematics does work and indeed marvelously well.

过去百年最伟大的科学创造，是电磁理论、相对论和量子理论，都广泛使用现代数学。只考虑第一种，因为其适用性人人熟悉。19世纪上半叶，许多物理学家和数学家研究电和磁，得到几条关于两种现象行为的数学规律。19世纪60年代，詹姆斯·克拉克·麦克斯韦着手汇集这些规律、考察相容性。他发现，数学相容性要求给方程增加一项，称为位移电流。他能给这一项找到的唯一物理意义，是电源（大体为载流导线）必有电磁场或电磁波向空间扩展。这些波有各种频率，包括如今收音机和电视接收的波，以及X射线、光、红外线、紫外线。因此，麦克斯韦通过纯数学考虑，预测了此前未知的大量现象的存在，并正确得出光是电磁现象的结论。

The greatest scientific creations of the past hundred years are electromagnetic theory, the theory of relativity, and quantum theory, all of which employ modern mathematics extensively. We shall consider only the first of these because its applicability is familiar to all of us. During the first half of the nineteenth century, numerous investigations of electricity and magnetism were undertaken by a number of physicists and mathematicians, and a few mathematical laws about the behavior of the two phenomena were obtained. During the 1860s James Clerk Maxwell undertook to assemble these laws and to examine their compatibility. He found that mathematical compatibility required the addition to the equations of a term, which he called displacement current. The only physical meaning he could find for this term was that from a source of electricity (roughly a wire carrying current) an electromagnetic field or electromagnetic wave must spread out into space. These electromagnetic waves can be of various frequencies and include what we now receive over our radios and television sets, as well as X rays, light, infrared rays, and ultra-violet rays. Thus by purely mathematical considerations Maxwell predicted the existence of a great variety of phenomena unknown until then and rightly concluded that light is an electromagnetic phenomenon.

电磁波特别引人注目、也使人想起引力（第三章）的是，我们丝毫不知道电磁波的物理实质。只有数学保证其存在，只有数学使工程师能发明无线电和电视的奇迹。

What is especially remarkable about electromagnetic waves—and reminiscent of gravitation (Chapter III)—is that we have not the slightest physical knowledge of what electromagnetic waves are. Only mathematics vouches for their existence, and only mathematics enabled engineers to invent the marvels of radio and television.

同一观察适用于各种原子与核现象。数学家和理论物理学家谈引力场、电磁场、电子场等场，仿佛它们是向空间传播的物质波，像水波冲击船只与海岸那样发挥作用。但这些场是虚构。我们不知其物理性质。它们与光声感受、物体运动，以及如今也许太熟悉的无线电电视等可观察物，只有遥远联系。贝克莱曾把导数称为消失量的幽灵。现代物理理论是物质的幽灵。但把这些在现实中没有明显对应物的虚构场的规律数学化，推导其后果，所得结论经适当物理解释后，可以用感官知觉检验。

The same observation applies to all sorts of atomic and nuclear phenomena. Mathematicians and theoretical physicists speak of fields—the gravitational field, the electromagnetic field, the field of electrons, and others—as though they were material waves which spread out into space and exert their effects somewhat as water waves pound against ships and shores. But these fields are fictions. We know nothing of their physical nature. They are only distantly related to observables such as sensations of light, sound, motions of objects, and the now perhaps too familiar radio and television. Berkeley once described the derivative as the ghost of departed quantities. Modern physical theory is the ghost of matter. But by formulating mathematically the laws of these fictional fields, which have no apparent counterparts in reality, and by deducing consequences of these laws, we obtain conclusions, which when suitably interpreted in physical terms can be checked against sense perceptions.

爱因斯坦在1931年强调现代科学的虚构性质：

The modern fictional character of science was emphasized by Einstein in 1931:

根据牛顿体系，物理现实由空间、时间、质点和力（质点的相互作用）等概念刻画……

According to Newton’s system, physical reality is characterized by the concepts of space, time, material point, and force (reciprocal action of material points). . . .

麦克斯韦之后，人们把物理现实理解为由连续场表示，场不能以力学解释，受偏微分方程支配。这种现实观的改变，是牛顿以来物理中最深刻、最富成果的改变……

After Maxwell they conceived physical reality as represented by continuous fields, not mechanically explicable, which are subject to partial differential equations. This change in the conception of reality is the most profound and fruitful one that has come to physics since Newton. . . .

刚才概述的科学理论基础纯属虚构的观点，在18、19世纪绝非主流。但它不断取得地位，因为逻辑结构越简单——即支撑结构所需的逻辑独立概念元素越少——一方面的基本概念与规律，和另一方面必须与经验联系的结论，思想上的距离就越大。

The view I have just outlined of the purely fictitious character of the fundamentals of scientific theory was by no means the prevailing one in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. But it is steadily gaining ground from the fact that the distance in thought between the fundamental concepts and laws on one side and, on the other, the con-elusions which have to be brought into relation with our experience grows larger and larger, the simpler the logical structure becomes— that is to say, the smaller the number of logically independent conceptual elements which are found necessary to support the structure.

现代科学因提供自然现象的理性解释，消除体液、魔鬼、天使、恶魔、神秘力量和泛灵论而受赞誉。现在必须补充，现代科学逐步移除诉诸感官的直觉与物理内容，消除物质，使用场和电子等纯合成、理想概念，我们对它们所知只有数学规律。经过长链数学演绎，科学仅与感官知觉保持微小但关键的接触。科学是合理化的虚构，由数学使之合理化。

Modern science has been praised for eliminating humors, devils, angels, demons, mystic forces, and animism by providing rational explanations of natural phenomena. We must now add that modern science is gradually removing the intuitive and physical content, both of which appeal to the senses; it is eliminating matter; it is utilizing purely synthetic and ideal concepts such as fields and electrons about which all we know are mathematical laws. Science retains only a small but nevertheless vital contact with sense perceptions after long chains of mathematical deduction. Science is rationalized fiction, rationalized by mathematics.

伟大物理学家海因里希·赫兹，首先在实验中证实麦克斯韦关于电磁波可在空间传播的预言。他对数学力量印象极深，难抑热情：“不禁感到，这些数学公式具有独立存在和自身智慧，比我们聪明，甚至比发现者聪明；我们从中取得的，比最初放进去的更多。”

Heinrich Hertz, a great physicist and the man who first confirmed experimentally Maxwell’s prediction that electromagnetic waves can travel through space, was so impressed with the power of mathematics that he could not restrain his enthusiasm. “One cannot escape the feeling that these mathematical formulas have an independent existence and intelligence of their own, that they are wiser than we are, wiser even than their discoverers, that we get more out of them than was originally put into them.”

詹姆斯·金斯爵士（1877—1946）强调数学在自然研究中的作用。他在《神秘的宇宙》中肯定：“根本事实只是，科学现在描绘的所有自然图景，而且唯有这些图景似乎符合观察事实，都是数学图景……超越数学公式，风险自负。”为构建数学叙述，人们猜想物理概念和机制；随后矛盾的是，这些物理辅助物被发现几乎只是幻想，数学方程却仍是把握现象的唯一可靠方式。

Sir James Jeans (1877-1946) underscored the role of mathematics in the investigation of nature. In The Mysterious Universe he affirmed: “The essential fact is simply that all the pictures which science now draws of nature, and which alone seem capable of according with observational fact, are mathematical pictures. . . . We go beyond the mathematical formulas at our own risk.” Physical concepts and mechanisms are conjectured to construct the mathematical account and then, paradoxically, the physical aids are seen to be hardly more than fantasies, but the mathe matical equations remain as the only sure hold on the phenomena.

金斯在《物理学与哲学之间》中重申：自然的运作方式，不能通过感官可把握的模型或图景为人心理解。我们永不能理解事件是什么，只能限于用数学术语描述事件模式。物理的最终收获，永远是一批数学公式。物质的真实本质永不可知。

In Between Physics and Philosophy Jeans reaffirmed the thought. Nature does not function in a way that can be comprehensible to the human mind through models or pictures that the senses can grasp. We can never understand what events are, but must limit ourselves to describing the patterns of events in mathematical terms. The final harvest in physics will always be a collection of mathematical formulas. The real essence of material substance is forever unknowable.

因此，数学在现代科学中的作用，远不只是主要工具。常见描述是，数学用符号公式概括、系统化物理观察或实验确立的东西，再从公式推出观察实验无法取得、或更易取得的额外信息。但这种描述远未达到数学实际成就。数学是科学理论的实质；19、20世纪基于纯数学构造的应用，比以前数学家使用物理事件直接提示的概念时，更强大、更奇妙。现代科学的成就，如无线电、电视、飞机、电话、电报、高保真唱机和录音仪、X射线、晶体管、原子能（及原子弹），不能只归功于数学；但数学的作用比实验科学任何贡献，都更根本、更不可或缺。

Thus the role of mathematics in modern science is now seen to be far more than that of a major tool. The role has often been described as one of summarizing and systematizing in symbols and formulas what is physically observed or physically established by experimentation and then deducing from the formulas additional information that is not accessible to observation or experimentation nor to information more readily obtained. However, this account of the role of mathematics falls far short of what it achieves. Mathematics is the essence of scientific theories, and the applications made in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries on the basis of purely mathematical constructs are even more powerful and marvelous than those made earlier when mathematicians operated with concepts suggested directly by physical happenings. Though credit for the achievements of modern science—radio, television, airplanes, the telephone, the telegraph, high fidelity phonographs and recording instruments, X rays, transistors, atomic power (and bombs), to mention a few that are familiar—cannot be accorded only to mathematics, the role of mathematics is more fundamental and less dispensable than any contribution of experimental science.

17世纪弗朗西斯·培根怀疑哥白尼和开普勒等天文理论。他担心，理论由哲学或宗教信念塑造，如上帝偏爱简单、设计数学有序的自然，而非观察实验所要求。培根态度无疑合理，但现代数学理论支配物理科学，只因为极有效。当然，符合观察是接受任何科学数学理论的必要条件。

Francis Bacon in the seventeenth century was skeptical of theories such as the Copernican and Keplerian astronomical theories. He feared that they were fashioned by philosophic or religious beliefs—such as God’s predilection for simplicity or His design of a mathematically ordered nature rather than demanded by observation or experimentation. Bacon’s attitude was certainly reasonable, but modern mathematical theories have come to dominate physical science solely because they are so effective. Of course, conformity to observations is a requisite for the acceptance of any mathematical theory of science.

因此，问数学是否有效，可以响亮回答是。但为何有效，不那么容易回答。希腊时代及随后许多世纪，数学家相信明确知道去哪里找黄金——数学是物理世界的真理，逻辑原则也是真理——于是艰苦、奋力、热切地挖掘，辉煌成功。但如今知道，被当作黄金的不是黄金，却仍是贵金属。这贵金属继续极准确地描述自然运作。为何服务如此出色，值得分析。为什么预期独立、抽象、先验的“精确”思想整体，会与人的物理世界相关？

Hence any question about whether mathematics works can be answered with a resounding yes. But the question of why it works is not so readily answered. In Greek times and for many centuries thereafter, mathematicians believed that they had clear indications of where to search for gold—mathematics was truth about the physical world and the logical principles were also truths—and so they dug for it arduously, vigorously, and eagerly. They succeeded gloriously. But now we know that what was taken for gold was not gold but precious metal nevertheless. This precious metal has continued to describe the working of nature with remarkable accuracy. Why it has served so well warrants analysis. Why should one expect the construction of an independent, abstract, a priori body of “exact” thought to bear on man’s physical world?

可以回答，数学概念与公理由经验提示，甚至逻辑规律也已承认由经验提示，因而符合经验。但解释过分简单。它或许足以解释五十头牛加五十头牛是一百头牛。在数与几何领域，经验确实可能提示适当公理，所用逻辑也只是经验教给的。但人类在代数、微积分、微分方程等领域，创造了并非经验提示的数学概念和技术。

One might answer that mathematical concepts and axioms are suggested by experience. Even the laws of logic have been acknowledged to be suggested by and therefore in accord with experience. But such an explanation is far too simplistic. It may suffice to explain why fifty cows and fifty cows make one hundred cows. In the areas of number and geometry, experience may indeed suggest the proper axioms, and the logic employed may be no more than what experience has taught. But human beings have created mathematical concepts and techniques in algebra, the calculus, differential equations, and other fields that are not suggested by experience.

除这些非经验数学的例子，还应考虑，数学直线由不可数点集组成。微积分使用的时间概念，由像实数系一样“挤在一起”的瞬间组成。导数概念（第六章）可能由无穷小时段内速度的物理概念提示，但导数表示速度时，表示的是瞬间速度。各种无限集合当然并非经验提示，却用于数学推理，对满意的数学理论必不可少，像物理物体对感知必不可少。数学也提供电磁场等概念，其物理性质我们当然不知道。

Beyond these examples of non-empirical mathematics, we should take into account that the mathematical straight line consists of a non-denumerable set of points. The calculus uses a concept of time composed of instants that are “crowded together” like the numbers of the real number system. The notion of a derivative (Chapter VI) may be suggested by the physical concept of velocity at some infinitesimal period of time, but the derivative, when it represents velocity, represents it at an instant. The variety of infinite sets is certainly not suggested by experience but is used in mathematical reasoning and is as necessary for a satisfactory mathematical theory as physical bodies are for sense perceptions. Mathematics has also contributed concepts such as the electromagnetic field whose physical nature is certainly not known to us.

此外，即使逻辑规律与某些物理原则来自经验，在对有物理意义结论的漫长数学证明中，规律被使用数十次，证明仅靠逻辑。纯数学推理产生海王星存在等预言。那么，自然服从逻辑原则吗？换句话说，是否有一组逻辑，不论怎样获得，告诉我们自然必须怎样表现？涉及数百定理和数千关于抽象的推演的主要理论，仍像公理一样紧贴现实，说明数学表示预测真实现象的力量，其准确性不可思议。长链纯推理为何产生如此适用的结论？这是数学最大的悖论。

Moreover, even if the laws of logic and some physical principles are derived from experience, in the course of an extensive mathematical proof of a physically significant conclusion the laws are used dozens of times and the proof rests solely on logic. Purely mathematical reasoning led to predictions such as the existence of Neptune. Does nature then conform to logical principles? Is there in other words a body of logic, however obtained, which tells us how nature must behave? The fact that major theories which involve hundreds of theorems and thousands of deductions about abstractions still cleave as closely to reality as the axioms, speaks for a power of mathematics to represent and predict real phenomena with an accuracy which is incredible. Why should long chains of pure reasoning produce such remarkably applicable conclusions? This is the greatest paradox in mathematics.

因此，人面临双重奥秘。即使物理现象已用物理术语理解，为何从公理数百次推导得到的结果，仍像公理一样适用？在那些我们对物理现象只有猜测、几乎完全依靠数学描述的领域，数学为何仍有效？不能轻率忽视。科学技术太多依赖数学。学科曾在真理这无敌旗帜下战斗，却实际靠某种内部神秘力量获胜，是否其中有魔力？

Hence man is left with a twofold mystery. Why does mathematics work even where, although the physical phenomena are understood in physical terms, hundreds of deductions from axioms prove to be as applicable as the axioms themselves? And why does it work in domains where we have only mere conjectures about the physical phenomena but depend almost entirely upon mathematics to describe these phenomena? One cannot dismiss these questions lightheartedly. Far too much of our science and technology depends upon mathematics. Is there perhaps some magical power in the subject which, though it used to fight under the invincible banner of truth, has actually achieved its victories through some inner mysterious strength?

问题多次提出，尤其爱因斯坦在《相对论侧记》（1921年）中说：

The problem has been posed repeatedly, notably by Albert Einstein in his Sidelights on Relativity (1921):

这里出现困扰各时代科学家的谜题：数学是独立于经验的人类思想产物，怎能如此出色地适合物理现实对象？人的理性不靠经验，能通过纯思考发现真实事物的性质吗？……

Here arises a puzzle that has disturbed scientists of all periods. How is it possible that mathematics, a product of human thought that is independent of experience, fits so excellently the objects of physical reality? Can human reason without experience discover by pure thinking properties of real things? . . .

数学命题涉及现实之处，它们不确定；确定之处，它们不涉及现实。

As far as the propositions of mathematics refer to reality they are not certain; and as far as they are certain they do not refer to reality.

他继续解释，数学公理化明确了这一区别。爱因斯坦虽理解数学公理和逻辑原则源于经验，却问：独立于经验、涉及人心创造概念的漫长复杂纯推理，为何产生如此适用的结论？

He went on to explain that the axiomatization of mathematics made this distinction clear. Though Einstein understood that the axioms of mathematics and principles of logic derive from experience, he was questioning why long and intricate pure reasoning, which is independent of experience and involves concepts created by the human mind, can produce such remarkably applicable conclusions.

一种现代解释源于康德。康德主张（第四章），我们不认识、也不能认识自然，而有感官知觉。心灵具有既定的空间时间结构（康德称为直觉），按内置精神结构的要求组织知觉。因此按欧几里得几何规律组织空间知觉，因为心灵要求如此。这样组织后，空间知觉继续服从欧几里得规律。康德坚持欧几里得几何当然错了，但人心决定自然怎样表现这一点，提供部分解释。心灵塑造空间时间概念。在自然中，我们看到心灵预先决定让我们看到的东西。

One modern explanation stems from Kant. Kant maintained (Chapter IV) that we do not and cannot know nature. Rather we have sense perceptions. Our minds, endowed with established structures (intuitions in Kant’s terminology) of space and time, organize these perceptions in accordance with what these built-in mental structures dictate. Thus we organize spatial perceptions in accordance with the laws of Euclidean geometry because our minds require this. Being so organized, the spatial perceptions continue to obey the laws of Euclidean geometry. Of course, Kant was wrong in insisting upon Euclidean geometry, but his point that man’s mind determines how nature behaves is a partial explanation. The mind shapes our concepts of space and time. We see in nature what our minds predetermine for us to see.

当代伟大物理学家之一阿瑟·斯坦利·爱丁顿（1882—1944），倡导有些类似却超越康德的观点。按爱丁顿说法，人心决定自然必须怎样表现：

A view somewhat similar to Kant’s but extending beyond it was advocated by Arthur Stanley Eddington (1882-1944), one of the great physicists of our time. According to Eddington the human mind decides how nature must behave:

我们发现，在科学进步最远的地方，心灵只是从自然收回自己放进自然的东西。我们在未知的岸边发现奇怪脚印，一个接一个设计深刻理论解释其来源。终于成功重构留下脚印的生物。瞧！那就是我们自己。

We have found that where science has progressed the farthest, the mind has but regained from nature that which the mind has put into nature. We have found a strange footprint on the shores of the unknown. We have devised profound theories, one after another, to account for its origin. At last we have succeeded in reconstructing the creature that made the footprint. And Lo! It is our own.

近年，阿尔弗雷德·诺思·怀特海详细阐述康德式的数学为何有效的解释，甚至布劳威尔在1923年论文中也赞同。关键是，数学不是独立于外部世界现象、再应用于它们的东西，而是我们理解现象方式的一部分。自然世界并非客观给予，而是人根据感觉作出的解释或建构，数学是组织感觉的主要工具。因此，数学几乎自动描述人在所知范围内的外部世界。许多人接受相同数学组织，可解释为人心确实可能运作相同，或人生于某种文化语言中，被训练接受特定数学方案。欧几里得几何虽不是关于空间的最终答案，其支配地位支持后一观点。日心说也一样，因为它最初并非由观察与托勒密理论的不符激发。而且，若保留托勒密理论并精炼，使之符合较新观察，无疑同样有效，代价只是数学复杂性。

The Kantian explanation of why mathematics works has in recent years been elaborated at length by Alfred North Whitehead and espoused even by Brouwer in a paper of 1923. The key idea is that mathematics is not something independent of and applied to phenomena taking place in an external world but rather an element in our way of conceiving the phenomena. The natural world is not objectively given to us. It is man’s interpretation or construction based on his sensations, and mathematics is a major instrument for organizing the sensations. Almost automatically then mathematics describes the external world insofar as it is known to man. That many human beings accept the same mathemati cal organization is explained by the proposition that human minds may indeed function alike or by the fact that they are born into a culture and language that condition them to accept a particular mathematical scheme. The dominance of Euclidean geometry, though it is not the final word about space, supports the latter view. The same may be said of the heliocentric theory because it was not at the outset motivated by any discrepancies of observation with Ptolemaic theory. Moreover, if Ptolemaic theory had been retained and refined to agree with more recent observations, it would undoubtedly serve equally well at the expense only of mathematical complexity.

上述思想可这样表达：我们尝试从复杂现象抽象出一些简单体系，其性质可以数学描述。这种抽象能力，产生了数学对自然的惊人描述。而且，只看到数学“光学”让我们看到的东西。例如，哲学家威廉·詹姆斯在《实用主义讲演》中也说：“数学与物理科学的一切宏伟成就……源于我们不屈的愿望，要在心中把世界塑成比粗糙经验秩序投进心里的形状更合理的形状。”

The substance of the above thought may be expressed thus. We attempt to abstract from the complexity of phenomena some simple systems whose properties are susceptible of being described mathematically. This power of abstraction is responsible for the amazing mathematical description of nature. Moreover, we see only what our mathematical “optics” permits us to see. This thought was also expressed, for example, by the philosopher William James in his Lectures on Pragmatism: “All the magnificient achievements of mathematical and physical science . . . proceed from our indomitable desire to cast the world into a more rational shape in our minds than the shape into which it is thrown there by the crude order of our experience.”

一位近代作者用更诗意的语言说：“现实是所有交际花中最诱人的，因为她使自己变成你此刻希望她成为的样子；但她不是可锚定灵魂的岩石，因为她的实质是影子，不能在梦之外存在，常常只是你自己的思想照在自然面容上的反光。”

In the somewhat more poetic language of a recent writer: “Reality is the most alluring of all courtesans, for she makes herself what you would have her at the moment; but she is no rock on which to anchor your soul, for her substance is of the stuff of shadows; she has no existence outside your dreams and is often no more than the reflection of your own thoughts shining upon the face of nature.”

不过，康德式解释，即我们在自然中看到心灵预定让我们看到的东西，并未充分回答数学为何有效。康德以后的电磁理论等发展，很难是人心天赋或对感觉的组织。无线电电视之所以存在，并非因为心灵按某种内在结构组织感觉，使我们能把它们体验为心灵关于自然必须怎样表现的观念的后果。

However, this Kantian explanation that we see in nature what our minds predetermine for us to see does not fully answer the question of why mathematics works. Developments since Kant’s time such as electromagnetic theory can hardly be endowments of the human mind or the mind s organization of sensations. Radio and television do not exist because the mind organized some sensations in accordance with some internal structure which then enabled us to experience radio and television as consequences of the mind’s conception of how nature must behave.

有些数学家相信数学自主（第十四章）：公理不论是纯理性产物还是经验提示，此后整个数学独立于经验建立。在这种观点下，数学怎能适用于物理世界，尤其物理现象？有几个答案。一个是，数学公理使用未定义术语，它们可以不同解释以适合物理情境。一个小例子是，椭圆型非欧几里得几何既适用于通常意义的直线，也适用于球面几何，其中直线是大圆。

There are mathematicians who believe that mathematics is autonomous (Chapter XIV). That is, whether its axioms are the products of pure reason or suggested by experience, thereafter the entire body of mathematics is built up independently of experience. How then under this view can mathematics apply to the physical world and especially to physical phenomena? There are several answers. One is that mathematical axioms use undefined terms and these can be differently interpreted to suit the physical situation. Thus, as a minor example, elliptic non-Euclidean geometry applies to straight lines in the usual sense and it applies to the geometry of a sphere where straight lines are great circles.

庞加莱提出这种解释。他愿意承认，数学是纯演绎科学，只推出公理后果。人使用合理、也许由感觉提示的公理，构建欧几里得或非欧几里得几何。这些几何的公理定理既非经验真理，也非先验真理，既不真也不假，像选择极坐标而非直角坐标无所谓真伪。庞加莱称之为安排、度量物体的约定，或伪装的概念定义。我们使用最方便的几何。不过，他坚持将永远使用欧几里得几何，以绷紧细绳或尺边作为直线的通常解释，因为它最简单。为何推论仍适用？庞加莱回答，我们修改物理规律，使数学吻合。

This type of explanation was offered by Poincare. He was willing to grant that mathematics was a purely deductive science which merely deduced the implications of its axioms. Thus man, using plausible axioms, perhaps suggested by sensations, constructs Euclidean geometry or a non-Euclidean geometry. The axioms and theorems of these geometries are neither empirical nor a priori truths. They are neither true nor false any more than the use of polar coordinates rather than rectangular is true or false. Poincare called them conventions for ordering and measuring bodies, or disguised definitions of the concepts. We use the geometry that is most convenient. However, he insisted that we would always use Euclidean geometry with the usual interpretation of straight line, that is, the stretched string or the ruler’s edge, because it is simplest. Why then should the deductions still apply? Poincare’s answer is that we modify the physical laws to make the mathematics fit.

为说明庞加莱的论点，考察测量员怎样确定距离。首先选择方便的基线AB（图15.1），用卷尺实际测量长度。为了确定AC，测量员把望远镜置于A，瞄准C，再转向B，测出角A。经纬仪上的刻度显示望远镜转了多少，从而知道角A。同样测出角B。测量员假定，从C到A及B到A的光线沿两点间的直线（绷紧细绳）传播；欧几里得几何公理符合绷紧细绳，因此应用欧几里得几何或三角学计算AC和BC。但结果可能错误。为什么？从C到A的光可能沿图15.1的折线路径；A处测量员必须沿光线切向瞄准才能接收光。因此，虽在望远镜中看到C，实际瞄准C′。所以实际测的是∠C′AB，而非∠CAB。随后使用欧几里得几何，可能得出错误的AC和BC。

To illustrate Poincare’s thesis, let us consider how surveyors determine distances. They begin by adopting a convenient base line AB (Fig. 15.1) whose length is measured by actually applying a tape measure. To determine the distance AC, a surveyor measures angle A by sighting point C in his telescope stationed at A and then swings the telescope around until he sights point B. On his theodolite he has a scale which tells him how much he has rotated his telescope, and hence he knows angle A. In a similar manner, he measures angle B. The surveyor proceeds on the assumption that the light rays which travel,from C to A and from B to A follow the straight-line (stretched string) paths between those pairs of points, and, since the axioms of Euclidean geometry fit stretched strings, he applies Euclidean geometry or trigonometry to calculate AC and BC. However, the surveyor’s results may be wrong. Why? The light ray from C to A may have followed the broken-line path shown in Figure 15.1, and the surveyor at A would have to point his telescope tangentially to the light ray in order to receive the light. Hence the telescope would really be pointed to C' although the surveyor sees the point C in his telescope. Consequently, the angle he actually measures is C'AB and not CAB. Then the subsequent use of Euclidean geometry may have led to erroneous results for AC and BC.

图15.1

Figure 15.1

光线沿什么路径，有些疑问。有时真正沿直线，有时因大气折射而弯曲。假定测量员得到错误的AC、BC，即使没有理由相信光路弯曲，也应这样处理。随后可以纠正A、B处角度测量，再用欧几里得几何得到正确的AC、BC。

There is some question of what path the light rays followed. Sometimes the paths are truly straight-line; sometimes they are bent by the refractive effect of the atmosphere. Suppose the surveyor does get incorrect results for AC and BC. Even though he may have no reason to believe that the paths of the light rays are curved, he should treat them as such. He can then correct the measurements of the angles at A and B and apply Euclidean geometry to obtain the correct values of AC and BC.

庞加莱主张可使数学符合物理现实，另一个例子是地球是否自转。他说，应接受自转为物理事实，因为能设计更简单的数学天文理论。事实上，数学理论简单性，是哥白尼和开普勒支持日心说、反对旧托勒密理论的唯一论据。

As another example of Poincare’s thesis that mathematics can be made to fit physical reality, let us see what he had to say about the question of whether the earth rotates. He argued that we should accept rotation as a physical fact because it enables us to devise a simpler mathematical theory of astronomy. And in fact simplicity of the mathematical theory was the only argument Copernicus and Kepler could advance in favor of their heliocentric theory as opposed to the older Ptolemaic theory.

庞加莱的科学哲学有价值。我们确实尝试使用最简单数学，必要时改变物理规律，使推理符合物理事实。但当今数学家与科学家使用的标准，是整个数学与物理理论的简单性。若必须使用非欧几里得几何，像爱因斯坦相对论那样，才能产生最简单的结合理论，就使用它。

Poincare’s philosophy of science has merit. We do try to use the simplest mathematics and alter physical laws if necessary to make our reasoning conform to physical facts. However, the criterion used by mathematicians and scientists today is the simplicity of the whole of mathematical and physical theory. And if we must use a non-Euclidean geometry—as Einstein did in his theory of relativity—to produce the simplest combined theory, we do so.

庞加莱更明确解释怎样使数学有效，但也多少同意康德解释，相信数学与自然的符合由人心塑造。他在《科学的价值》中肯定：

Though Poincare was more explicit in explaining how mathematics is made to work, he did agree somewhat with the Kantian explanation in that he believed the accord between mathematics and nature is fashioned by human minds. In The Value of Science he affirmed:

人的理智自以为在自然中发现的和谐，独立于理智存在吗？肯定不。完全独立于理解、看见或感受它的精神的现实，不可能存在。如此外在的世界，即使存在，我们也永远无法接近。严格说来，“客观现实”是几个思考者共有、可能所有思考者共有的东西；我们将看到，这共同部分只能是数学规律所表达的和谐。

Does the harmony which human intelligence thinks it discovers in Nature exist apart from such intelligence? Assuredly no. A reality completely independent of the spirit that conceives it, sees it or feels it, is an impossibility. A world so external as that, even if it existed, would be forever inaccessible to us. What we call “objective reality” is, strictly speaking, that which is common to several thinking beings and might be common to all; this common part, we shall see, can only be the harmony expressed by mathematical laws.

还有一种略含糊、也许过分简单的数学为何有效的解释。按此观点，存在客观物理世界，人不断努力让数学符合它。应用揭示数学表述失真或明显错误时，就修改数学。希尔伯特在1900年第二届国际数学大会演讲中表达这种观点：

There is a somewhat vague, perhaps a too simplistic, explanation of why mathematics works. According to this view there is an objective physical world and man constantly strives to fit his mathematics to it. We modify the mathematics when applications reveal misrepresentation or downright errors in the mathematics. This view was expressed by Hilbert in his address at the Second International Congress of Mathematics (1900):

但纯思考的创造活动进行时，外部世界再次肯定自身有效性，通过发生的现象向我们提出新问题，开启数学知识新领域；努力使新领域受纯思考支配时，常找到重要未决问题的答案，同时最有效地推进旧理论。在我看来，数学家经常在不同知识领域的问题、方法、概念中察觉的众多惊人类比和仿佛预定的和谐，依赖这种不断重复的思想与经验的相互作用。

But even while this creative activity of pure thought is going on, the external world once again reasserts its validity, and by thrusting new questions upon us through the phenomena that occur, it opens up new domains of mathematical knowledge; and as we strive to bring these new domains under the dominion of pure thought we often find answers to outstanding unsolved problems, and thus at the same time we advance in the most effective way the earlier theories. On this ever-repeated interplay of thought and experience depend, it seems to me, the numerous and astonishing analogies and the apparently pre-established harmony that the mathematician so often perceives in the problems, methods, and concepts of diverse realms of knowledge.

更简单、当今更难相信的数学为何有效的解释，重复了数学家从希腊时代直到约1850年的信念。有些人仍相信自然的数学设计。他们可能承认，许多旧的物理现象数学理论不完善，却指出不断改进，不仅涵盖更多现象，也与观察更准确吻合。例如，牛顿力学代替亚里士多德力学，相对论改进牛顿力学。这段历史岂不意味着有设计，而人越来越接近真理？埃尔米特对数学与科学的符合提出这种解释：

Simpler explanations of why mathematics works, less credible in our day, repeat what mathematicians believed from Greek times until about 1850. Some men still believe in the mathematical design of nature. They may grant that many of the earlier mathematical theories of physical phenomena were imperfect, but they point to continuing improvements that not only embrace more phenomena but offer far more accurate agreement with observations. Thus Newtonian mechanics replaced Aristotelian mechanics, and the theory of relativity improved on Newtonian mechanics. Does not this history imply that there is design and that man is approaching closer and closer to the truth? Hermite offered this explanation of the accord between mathematics and science:

若我没有受骗，存在一个由数学真理汇集成的世界，只有通过理智能够接近，正如存在物理现实世界；两者独立于我们，都是神的创造，因为心灵软弱才显得不同，对更强大的思考方式却是同一回事。两者的综合，部分显露于抽象数学与物理各分支之间奇妙的对应。

There exists, if I am not deceived, a world which is the collection of mathematical truths, to which we have access only through our intellects, just as there is the world of physical reality; the one and the other independent of us, both of divine creation, which appear distinct because of the weakness of our minds, but for a more powerful mode of thinking are one and the same thing. The synthesis of the two is revealed partially in the marvelous correspondence between abstract mathematics on the one hand and all the branches of physics on the other.

埃尔米特在给利奥·柯尼斯贝格的信中补充：“这些分析概念在我们之外存在，构成一个仅部分向我们显现的整体；它虽神秘，却无可争辩地与通过感官知觉的另一个事物整体相联系。”

In a letter to Leo Konigsberger, Hermite added “that these notions of analysis have their existence apart from us, that they constitute a whole of which only a part is revealed to us, incontestably although mysteriously associated with that other totality of things which we perceive through the senses.”

詹姆斯·金斯爵士在《神秘的宇宙》中，也接受旧观点：“从其创造的内在证据看，宇宙的伟大建筑师如今开始像一位纯数学家。”但起初承认，人的数学“尚未接触最终现实”。书中后来更武断：

Sir James Jeans in The Mysterious Universe also accepted the older view that “from the intrinsic evidence of his creation, the Great Architect of the Universe now begins to appear as a pure mathematician.” However, at first he granted that man’s mathematics is “not yet in contact with ultimate reality.” But later in the book he became more dogmatic:

自然似乎非常熟悉纯数学规则；数学家在书斋中从内在意识形成这些规则，并未显著借助外部世界经验……无论如何，自然与我们有意识的数学心灵按相同规律工作，几乎无可争辩。

Nature seems very conversant with the rules of pure mathematics, as our mathematicians have formulated them in their studies, out of their own inner consciousness and without drawing to any appreciable extent on their experience of the outer world. ... In any event, it can hardly be disputed that nature and our conscious mathematical minds work according to the same laws.

爱丁顿晚年也确信自然由数学设计，在《基本理论》（1946年）中断然肯定，心灵能从先验知识建立纯粹自然科学。这是唯一可能的科学，其他任何一种会有逻辑矛盾。并非全部细节都能如此得到，一般规律却可以。例如，光必须以有限速度传播，可由心灵得出。甚至质子与电子质量之比等自然常数，也可先验确定。这种知识独立于宇宙实际观察，比实验知识更确定。

Later in life Eddington too became convinced that nature is mathematically designed and he affirmed categorically in Fundamental Theory (1946) that our minds can build up a pure science of nature from a priori knowledge. This science is the only one possible; any other one would contain logical inconsistencies. Not all details of science could be so obtained but general laws could be. Thus that light must travel at a finite velocity is obtainable by the mind. Even constants of nature—such as the ratio of the mass of a proton to the mass of an electron—can be determined a priori. This knowledge is independent of actual observation of the universe and more certain than experimental knowledge.

美国第一位伟大数学家乔治·戴维·伯克霍夫，在1941年毫不犹豫重复并支持爱丁顿的话：

George David Birkhoff, the first of the great mathematicians in the United States, did not hesitate to repeat and support in 1941 the words of Eddington:

……整个物理规律体系中，没有什么不能从认识论考虑明确推出。一个不熟悉宇宙、却熟悉人心解释感官经验内容的思想体系的理智，应能获得我们通过实验获得的全部物理知识……例如，能推知镭的存在与性质，却不能推知地球尺寸。

. . . There is nothing in the whole system of laws of physics that cannot be deduced unambiguously from epistemological considerations. An intelligence, unacquainted with our universe but acquainted with our system of thought by which the human mind interprets to itself the content of its sensory experience, should be able to attain all the knowledge of physics that we have attained by experiment. . . . For example, he would infer the existence and properties of radium, but not the dimensions of the Earth.

爱因斯坦较早的1918年，提出一种虽不充分却合理的数学为何符合现实的解释：

Earlier in life (1918), Einstein expressed a somewhat inadequate but reasonable explanation of why mathematics fits reality:

物理发展表明，任何给定时刻，所有可想象的建构中，总有一个明显优于其他。真正深入研究的人，都不会否认，实践中现象世界唯一地决定理论体系，尽管现象与理论原则之间没有逻辑桥梁；这就是莱布尼茨恰当地称为预定和谐的东西。

The development of physics has shown that at any given moment, out of all conceivable constructions, a single one has proved itself decidedly superior to all the rest. Nobody who has really gone deeply into the matter will deny that in practice the world of phenomena uniquely determines the theoretical system, in spite of the fact that there is no logical bridge between phenomena and their theoretical principles; this is what Leibniz described so happily as a pre-established harmony.”

在《我的世界观》（1934年）所陈述的成熟立场中，他断言：

In his mature position, presented in The World As I See It (1934), he asserted:

迄今经验使我们有理由相信，自然是可想象的最简单数学观念的实现。我确信，能够通过纯数学构造发现概念及连接它们的规律，提供理解自然现象的钥匙。经验可以提示适当数学概念，却绝不能从经验推出它们。当然，经验仍是数学构造效用的唯一标准。但创造原则在数学中。因此，在某种意义上，我相信纯思想能像古人梦想那样把握现实。

Our experience hitherto justifies us in believing that nature is the realization of the simplest conceivable mathematical ideas. I am convinced that we can discover by purely mathematical constructions the concepts and the laws connecting them with each other, which furnish the key to the understanding of natural phenomena. Experience may suggest the appropriate mathematical concepts, but they most certainly cannot be deduced from it. Experience remains, of course, the sole criterion of the utility of a mathematical construction. But the creative principle resides in mathematics. In a certain sense, therefore, I hold it true that pure thought can grasp reality as the ancients dreamed.

另一处，爱因斯坦用如今著名的关于上帝的话重申信念：“无论如何，我相信祂不掷骰子。”若祂掷，那么如拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生曾说：“上帝的骰子总是动过手脚的。”爱因斯坦并非肯定现有数学规律正确，而是肯定存在正确规律，可以希望越来越接近。正如他说：“上帝精妙，却不恶意。”

In another passage Einstein reaffirmed his belief through the now famous phrase about God: “I, at any rate, am convinced that He does not throw dice.” And if He does, then, as Ralph Waldo Emerson once suggested, “The dice of God are always loaded.” Einstein is not affirming here that the mathematical laws we now have are the correct ones but that there are such, and we can hope to come closer and closer to them. As he put it, “God is subtle; He is not malicious.”

伟大科学史家与哲学家皮埃尔·迪昂，像爱因斯坦一样，在《物理理论的目的与结构》中，从怀疑走向肯定。起初描述物理理论为“旨在逻辑概括和分类一组实验规律，而不声称解释这些规律的抽象体系”。理论近似、暂定，“剥去一切客观指涉”。科学只熟悉感官表象，应放弃以为理论在“撕去感官表象的面纱”的幻觉。天才科学家为混乱表象带来数学秩序与清晰，也只能牺牲相对可理解的概念，代以不揭示宇宙真实本性的符号抽象。但最后迪昂宣布：“我们不可能相信，［数学理论产生的］这种秩序与组织，不是真实秩序与组织的反映。”世界由伟大建筑师数学设计。上帝永恒地从事几何，人的数学描述这一设计。

Like Einstein, Pierre Duhem, one of the great historians and philosophers of science, in The Aim and Structure of Physical Theory passed through doubts to positive affirmation. He first described a physical theory as “an abstract system whose aim is to summarize and classify logically a group of experimental laws without claiming to explain these laws.” Theories are approximate, provisional, and “stripped of all objective references.” Science is acquainted only with sensible appearances, and we should shed the illusion that in theorizing we are “tearing the veil from these sensible appearances.” And when a scientist of genius brings mathematical order and clarity into the confusion of appearances, he achieves his aim only at the expense of replacing relatively intelligible concepts by symbolic abstractions which reveal nothing of the true nature of the universe. But Duhem ended by declaring that “It is impossible for us to believe that this order and this organization [produced by mathematical theory] are not the reflected image of a real order and organization.” The world is mathematically designed by a great architect. God does eternally geometrize and man’s mathematics describes that design.

赫尔曼·外尔确信数学反映自然秩序。他在演讲中说：

Hermann Weyl was sure that mathematics reflects the order of nature. In a talk he said:

自然内在地有隐藏和谐，以简单数学规律的形象反映于心中。这就是自然事件能通过观察与数学分析结合而预测的原因。物理史上，这种对自然和谐的信念，或者说梦想，一次又一次超出预期地得到实现。

There is inherent in nature a hidden harmony that reflects itself in our minds under the image of simple mathematical laws. That then is the reason why events in nature are predictable by a combination of observation and mathematical analysis. Again and again in the history of physics this conviction, or should I say this dream, of harmony in nature had found fulfillments beyond our expectation.

但也许愿望孕育思想，因为他在《数学与自然科学的哲学》中补充：

Perhaps, however, the wish was father to the thought, for, in his book Philosophy of Mathematics and Natural Science, he added:

然而，若没有对真理与现实的超越信仰支持，没有事实与建构同观念意象之间持续的相互作用，科学就会灭亡。

And yet science would perish without a supporting transcendental faith in truth and reality, and without the continuous interplay between its facts and constructions on the one hand and the imagery of ideas on the other.

不能轻率否定金斯、外尔、爱丁顿和爱因斯坦的观点，但他们关于数学与自然关系的观点并非主流。数学描述自然如此成功，解释似乎合理，正如许多世纪的数学家觉得欧几里得几何是不容怀疑的真理。但今天，相信自然的数学设计，似乎牵强。

Though one cannot dismiss lightly the views of Jeans, Weyl, Eddington, and Einstein, their views of the relation of mathematics and nature are not the dominant ones. It is true the successes of the mathematical description of nature have been so astounding that the explanations they offer seem to be reasonable, just as Euclidean geometry seemed to be indubitable truth to mathematicians of many centuries. But today the belief in the mathematical design of nature seems far-fetched.

还有一种关于数学与物理世界关系的说法，允许某种对应，却不是通常理解的对应。过去百年出现自然的统计观点。略为讽刺的是，它由拉普拉斯发起；他坚定相信自然严格按数学规律决定，但行为原因不总为人知，观察仅近似正确。因此应应用概率论，确定最可能的原因与最可能正确的资料。他的《概率的解析理论》（第三版，1820年）是经典。概率统计史漫长，也许不必在此纳入。但不到一个世纪，它导致自然行为并非决定而是混乱的观点。不过，有最可能的行为、平均行为，这就是观察到并称由数学规律决定的东西。像人能活到各种年龄，有些夭折、有些活到百岁，不仅男女有预期寿命，在任何给定年龄也有预期寿命。保险公司用这些资料建立非常成功的事业。近年来，量子力学的发展大力支持统计观点：不存在坚硬、离散、局域化的物质粒子。它们仅以一定概率存在于空间各处，但最可能在某处。

Still another account of the relationship of mathematics to the physical world allows for some correspondence but not the kind usually understood. In the past hundred years there has arisen the statistical view of nature. Somewhat ironically, it was initiated by Laplace who firmly believed that the behavior of nature is strictly determined in accordance with mathematical laws but that causes of the behavior of nature are not always known and observations are only approximately correct. Hence one should apply the theory of probability to determine the most likely causes and the data most likely to be correct. His Analytical Theory of Probability (3rd edition, 1820) is the classic on this subject. The history of probability and statistics is extensive and perhaps it is unnecessary to include it here. But in less than a century, it led to the view that the behavior of nature is not at all determined, but rather chaotic. However, there is a most probable behavior, an average behavior, and this is what we observe and say is determined by mathematical laws. Just as human beings live to all ages—some die as infants and some at a hundred—there is not only a life expectancy for all men and women but even a life expectancy at any given age. And by using these data, insurance companies build a very successful business. The statistical view of nature has received enormous support in recent years because of the development of quantum mechanics, according to which there are no rigid, discrete, localized particles of matter. They exist only with a certain probability in every part of space, but most probably in some one place.

无论如何，按统计观点，自然数学规律至多描述自然最可能怎样表现，却不排除地球突然游荡进太空。自然能自己拿主意，决定不做最可能的事。今天有些科学哲学家得出的结论，是数学无法解释的力量仍无法解释。哲学家查尔斯·桑德斯·皮尔士最先说：“这里很可能有某种秘密，尚待发现。”

At any rate, according to the statistical view, the mathematical laws of nature describe at best how nature will most probably behave, but they do not preclude that the earth may suddenly wander off into space. Nature can make up her own mind and decide not to do what is most probable. The conclusion which some philosophers of science adopt today is that the inexplicable power of mathematics remains inexplicable. This was first expressed by the philosopher Charles Sanders Peirce: “It is probable that there is some secret here which remains to be discovered.”

更近的1945年，埃尔温·薛定谔在《生命是什么》中说，人发现自然规律的奇迹，很可能超出人的理解。另一位物理学家、诺贝尔奖得主弗里曼·戴森同意：“我们大概还未接近理解物理世界与数学世界的关系。”可以加上爱因斯坦的话：“世界最不可理解之处，是它可以理解。”

More recently (1945) Erwin Schrodinger in What Is Life said that the miracle of man’s discovering laws of nature may well be beyond human understanding. Another physicist, the Nobel prize-winner Freeman Dyson agrees: “We are probably not close yet to understanding the relation between the physical and the mathematical worlds.” To which one can add Einstein’s remark, “The most incomprehensible thing about the world is that it is comprehensible.”

1960年，另一位诺贝尔物理学奖得主尤金·P.维格纳，在题为《数学在自然科学中不可思议的有效性》的文章中讨论这个问题，除了重述问题，未给更多解释：

In 1960 Eugene P. Wigner, another Nobel prize-winner in physics, discussed the problem of the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics in the natural sciences in an article with that very title and offered no more explanation than to restate the issue:

数学语言适于表述物理规律的奇迹，是美妙的礼物，我们既不理解，也不配得。应当感激它，希望未来研究仍有效，且不论好坏，给我们愉悦、也许也带来困惑地，扩展到广大学问分支。

The miracle of the appropriateness of the language of mathematics for the formulation of the laws of physics is a wonderful gift which we neither understand nor deserve. We should be grateful for it, and hope that it will remain valid in future research and that it will extend, for better or for worse, to our pleasure even though perhaps also to our bafflement, to wide branches of learning.

最后这几个“解释”是辩解性的。说得很少，虽常用印象深刻的语言，缓和承认不知道数学为何有效的尴尬。

These last few “explanations” are apologetic. They say rather little, though often in impressive language that tempers the admission that they have no answer to why mathematics is effective.

无论数学为何有效的解释多么满意或不满意，重要的是认识到，自然与自然的数学表示并不相同。差别不只是数学理想化。数学三角形无疑不是物理三角形，但数学偏离更远。公元前五世纪，埃利亚的芝诺提出若干悖论。不论目的为何，甚至第一个运动悖论，也说明数学概念化与经验的差别。它说，跑者永不能到跑道终点，因为先须走一半，再走剩余一半，再走剩余一半，如此继续。因此跑者必须走过

However satisfactory or unsatisfactory any explanation of why mathematics works may be, it is important to recognize that nature and the mathematical representation of nature are not the same. The difference is not merely that mathematics is an idealization. The mathematical triangle is assuredly not a physical triangle. But mathematics departs even further. In the fifth century B.C., Zeno of Elea posed a number of paradoxes. Whatever his purpose, even the first of his paradoxes on motion illustrates the difference between mathematical conceptualization and experience. Zeno’s first paradox states that a runner can never get to the end of a race-course because first he must cover Vi the distance, then Vi of the remaining distance, then Vi of the remaining distance, and so on. Hence the runner must cover

于是芝诺论证，走过无限多个距离所需时间必定无限。

Then, Zeno argued, the time required to cover an infinite number of distances must be infinite.

芝诺悖论的一种最明显的物理解法，是跑者以有限步数走完距离。但即使接受芝诺的数学分析，所需时间也可能是半分钟，加四分之一分钟，加八分之一分钟，等等；这些无限多个时段之和，恰为一分钟。这种分析偏离物理过程，结果却仍相符。

One physical resolution of Zeno’s paradox and the most obvious is that a runner will cover the distance in a finite number of steps. However, even if one accepts Zeno’s mathematical analysis, the time required may be 12 minute, plus 14 minute, plus 18 minute, and so forth, and the sum of all these infinite numbers of time intervals is just one minute. This analysis departs from the physical process, but the result agrees nevertheless.

也许人引入了有限、甚至人为的概念，只有这样才在自然中建立某种秩序。人的数学可能只是可行方案。自然本身可能复杂得多，或没有内在设计。但数学仍是研究、表示和驾驭自然的卓越方法。在有效领域，它是我们拥有的全部；若不是现实本身，也是我们最接近现实的方式。

It may be that man has introduced limited and even artificial concepts and only in this way has managed to institute some order in nature. Man’s mathematics may be no more than a workable scheme. Nature itself may be far more complex or have no» inherent design. Nevertheless, mathematics remains the method par excellence for the investigation, representation, and mastery of nature. In those domains where it is effective, it is all we have; if it is not reality itself, it is the closest to reality we can get.

数学虽纯为人创造，却让我们进入自然某些领域，使进步远超一切预期。远离现实的抽象取得如此多成就，确实矛盾。数学叙述或许人为，也许是童话，却有寓意。人的理性具有力量，即使不易解释。

Though it is a purely human creation, the access it has given us to some domains of nature enables us to progress far beyond all expectations. Indeed it is paradoxical that abstractions so remote from reality should achieve so much. Artificial the mathematical account may be; a fairy tale perhaps, but one with a moral. Human reason has a power even if it is not readily explained.

数学成功有代价，即按度量、质量、重量、持续时间等概念看世界。这种叙述不能完整表示丰富多样的经验，正如一个人的身高不等于这个人。数学至多描述自然某些过程，符号却不包含自然全部。

The mathematical successes are bought at a price, the price of viewing the world in terms of measure, mass, weight, duration, and other similar concepts. Such an account cannot be a complete representation of the rich and variegated experiences any more than a person’s height is the person. At best mathematics describes some processes of nature, but its symbols do not contain all of it.

此外，数学处理物理世界最简单的概念现象，不处理人，而处理无生命物质。物质行为重复，数学能描述。但在经济、政治理论、心理学及生物学中，数学远不那么有用。甚至物理领域，数学处理的简化只触及现实，像切线在一点触及曲线。地球绕太阳轨道是椭圆吗？不。只有视地球太阳为点、忽视宇宙所有其他物体才是。地球四季年复一年重复吗？很难说。只在最粗略方面重复，而人反正也大体只能察觉这些方面。

Moreover, mathematics deals with the simplest concepts and phenomena of the physical world. It does not deal with man but with inanimate matter. The behavior of matter is repetitive and mathematics can describe it. But in economics, political theory, psychology, as well as biology, mathematics is far less useful. Even in the physical realm, mathematics deals with simplifications which merely touch reality as a tangent touches a curve at one point. Is the path of the earth around the sun an ellipse? No. Only if the earth and sun are regarded as points and only if all other bodies in the universe are ignored. Do the four seasons on earth repeat themselves year after year? Hardly. Only in their grossest aspects, which are about all that man can perceive anyway, do they repeat.

应因不理解数学不可思议的有效性而拒绝它吗？亥维赛曾问：我应因不理解消化而拒绝晚餐吗？经验反驳怀疑者，自信者忽视理性解释。对宗教、社会科学和哲学应有尊重，也明确承认数学不处理生活那些方面；但事实是，数学在提供知识上成功得多得多。这知识不只基于声称正确，而每天在每台收音机、每座原子能电站的运转，在日月食预测、实验室及日常生活数千事件中受到检验。

Should we reject mathematics because we do not understand its unreasonable effectiveness? Heaviside once remarked: Should I refuse my dinner because I do not understand the process of digestion? Experience refutes the doubters. Rational explanations are disregarded by the confident. With all due respect to religion, social science, and philosophy and with explicit acknowledgment of the fact that mathematics does not treat those aspects of our lives, the fact is that mathematics is infinitely more successful in giving us knowledge. This knowledge is not based on mere assertions of its correctness. It is tested daily in the working of every radio set and atomic power plant, in the prediction of eclipses, and in thousands of events in the laboratory and in daily life.

数学也许处理较简单的问题——物理世界——但在自身范围内，是最成功的发展。人相信自己多少有意义的某些希望，来自通过数学获得的力量。数学驾驭自然，减轻人的负担，其胜利使我们振奋。

Mathematics may treat the simpler problems—the physical world— but in its sphere it is the most successful development. Some of the hope that man has any significance at all springs from the power he has acquired through mathematics. It has harnessed nature and lightened man’s burden. One can take heart from its victories.

数学为何有效并非纯学术问题。工程中，预测设计能在多大程度依靠数学？应使用涉及无限集合或选择公理的理论设计桥梁吗？桥会不会塌？幸运的是，有些工程采用过去经验充分支持的定理，可以放心使用。许多工程故意留出较大余量。桥梁用钢等材料，但材料强度知识不精确，所以工程师采用比理论要求更强的缆索和梁。但从未建造的新类型工程，必须关注数学可靠性；谨慎要求正式施工前使用缩尺模型或其他测试。

The question of why mathematics works is not solely academic. In the use of mathematics in engineering, to what extent can one rely upon mathematics to predict and design? Should one design a bridge using theory involving infinite sets or the axiom of choice? Might not the bridge collapse? Fortunately some engineering projects use theorems so well supported by past experience that the theorems may be used with confidence. Many engineering projects are deliberately over-designed. Thus a bridge uses materials such as steel, but our knowledge of the strength of materials is not accurate. Hence engineers use stronger cables and beams than theory calls for. However, in the case of a type of project that has never been built before, one must be concerned about the reliability of the mathematics used. In such cases, prudence would dictate the use of small-scale models or other tests before the construction proper is undertaken.

本章关心如何解决数学及数学家的困境。没有普遍接受的数学整体，各团体倡导的众多道路不可能全走，否则妨碍数学主要目标，即推进科学。因此我们倡导以该目标为标准，也讨论这条道路涉及的问题。

The concern of this chapter has been to seek some resolution of the quandary in which mathematics and mathematicians find themselves. There is no universally accepted body of mathematics and the multitude of paths that are advocated by various groups cannot all be pursued, for to do so would hinder the major goal of mathematics, namely, the advancement of science. Hence we have advocated using that goal as a standard. We have also discussed the problems and issues that this course entails.

强调科学应用虽似乎最明智，却不排除其他值得、甚至明智的数学研究。我们指出过（第十三章），应用数学也需要抽象、推广、严密化及方法改进等支持活动。此外，也可为不直接涉及科学研究中已有用数学的基础方案辩护。直觉主义者的构造主义纲领，虽意在替换无意义存在定理，却产生计算数量的方法，而纯存在定理只告诉我们数量存在。为简单起见，取旧例：欧几里得证明，任意圆面积与半径平方之比对所有圆相同。这比当然是π。因此他证明纯存在定理。但要计算给定圆面积，知道π值显然重要。幸运的是，阿基米德近似计算与后来几个级数展开，使我们早在直觉主义者挑战纯存在定理前就能计算π。计算π的能力当然重要。同样，其他目前只确立存在的量，也应计算。所以应推进构造主义纲领。

However, while emphasis on application to science does seem the wisest course, this program does not exclude other worthy and even wise pursuits in the realm of mathematics. We did point out (Chapter XIII) that even the pursuit of applied mathematics requires a variety of supporting activities, abstraction, generalization, rigorization, and improvements in methodology. Beyond these, one can justify the pursuit of foundational approaches that do not bear directly on the mathematics that has proved useful in scientific inquiries. The constructivist program of the intuitionists, though intended by them to replace meaningless existence theorems, does produce methods of calculating quantities which the pure existence theorems merely tell us exist. To use for the sake of simplicity an old example, Euclid proved that the ratio of the area of any circle to the square of its radius is the same for all circles. This ratio is of course π. Hence Euclid proved a pure existence theorem. But to know the value of π is obviously important if one is to calculate the area of any given circle. Fortunately Archimedes’ approximate calculation and several later series expansions enabled us to calculate π long before the challenge to pure existence theorems was posed by the intuitionists. Certainly the ability to calculate π was important. Similarly other quantities whose existence alone is now established should be calculated. And so the constructivist program should be pursued.

研究基础方案的另一个潜在价值，是可能得到矛盾。一致性尚未确立，所以发现矛盾或明显荒谬的定理，至少能排除一种目前吸收某些数学家时间精力的选择。

Another potential value in pursuing foundational approaches is the possibility of arriving at a contradiction. Consistency is not established, and so finding a contradiction or a patently absurd theorem would at least eliminate an alternative that now absorbs the time and energy of some mathematicians.

我们对数学地位的叙述无疑不令人安慰。数学被剥去真理，并非独立、安全、根基牢固的知识整体。大多数数学家放弃献身科学，这在任何历史时期都可悲，尤其当应用可能指引数学应走的可靠方向时。而已应用数学的惊人证实和力量，仍待解释。

Our account of the status of mathematics is certainly not a comforting one. Mathematics has been shorn of its truth; it is not an independent, secure, solidly grounded body of knowledge. Most mathematicians have renounced their devotion to science, an act that would be deplorable at any period of history but especially when applications might supply some guide to the sound direction mathematics should pursue. And the remarkable confirmation and power of what has been applied remains to be explained.

尽管缺陷与局限，数学能提供很多。它是人类最高智力成就、精神最独创的创造。音乐可激励或安抚灵魂，绘画悦目，诗歌动情，哲学满足心灵，工程改善物质生活。数学却提供所有这些价值。此外，在推理所能达到的方向上，数学家以人心所能做到的最大谨慎，确保结果可靠。数学精确性成为典范并非偶然。数学仍是最佳现有知识的范式。

Despite these defects and limitations mathematics has much to offer. It is man’s supreme intellectual achievement and the most original creation of the human spirit. Music may rouse or pacify the soul, painting may delight the eye, poetry may stir the emotions, philosophy may satisfy the mind, and engineering may improve the material life of man. But mathematics offers all these values. Moreover, in the direction of what reasoning can accomplish, mathematicians have exercised the greatest care that the human mind is capable of to secure the soundness of their results. It is not accidental that mathematical precision is a byword. Mathematics is still the paradigm of the best knowledge available.

数学成就是人心的成就；这种人类能力的证据，使人有勇气和信心处理一度似乎不可穿透的宇宙奥秘，战胜致命疾病，质疑并改进政治制度。在这些努力中，数学可能有效、也可能无效，但不可熄灭的成功希望源于数学。

The accomplishments of mathematics are the accomplishments of the human mind, and this evidence of what human beings can achieve has given man the courage and confidence to tackle the once seemingly impenetrable mysteries of the cosmos, to overcome fatal diseases to which man is subject, and to question and to improve the political systems under which man lives. In these endeavors mathematics may or may not be effective but our unquenchable hope for success derives from mathematics.

这些价值存在，至少与任何人类创造能提供的同样伟大。若并非全部容易或广泛被察觉、欣赏，幸而仍被使用。若攀登以达到它们比比如音乐更艰难，回报也更丰富，因为包含几乎一切人类创造能提供的智力、审美及情感价值。登高山可能比爬低丘费力，但顶峰视野伸向更远地平线。价值丰富，唯一可问的是重要性次序。但每人须自己回答，涉及个人判断、意见与品味。

The values are there, values at least as great as any human creation can offer. If all are not readily or widely perceptible or appreciated, fortunately they are utilized. If the climb to reach them is more arduous than in music, say, the rewards are richer, for they include almost all the intellectual, aesthetic, and emotional values that any human creation can offer. To ascend a high mountain may be more strenuous than to climb a low hill but the view from the top extends to far more distant horizons. Values there are in abundance and the only question one may raise is the order of importance. But this question each must answer for himself; individual judgments, opinions, and tastes enter.

就知识确定性而言，数学是理想，我们努力趋向，即使永不能达到。确定性可能只是不断追逐、永远难捕的幻影。但理想有力量与价值。正义、民主和上帝都是理想。诚然，人曾以上帝之名杀人，司法不公也臭名昭著。但这些理想是数千年文明的主要产物。数学也是，即使只是理想。也许思考理想，能使我们更清楚认识任何领域获取真理须走的方向。

Insofar as certainty of knowledge is concerned, mathematics serves as an ideal, an ideal toward which we shall strive, even though it may be one that we shall never attain. Certainty may be no more than a phantom constantly pursued and interminably elusive. However, ideals do have a force and a value. Justice, democracy, and God are ideals. It is true that people have murdered in the name of God and miscarriages of justice are notorious. Nevertheless, these ideals are the major product of thousands of years of civilization. So is mathematics, even if it is only an ideal. Perhaps contemplation of the ideal will make us more aware of the direction we must pursue to obtain truths in any field.

人的处境可怜。我们在浩瀚宇宙流浪，面对自然破坏无助，食物和必需品依赖自然，不知为何出生、应追求什么。人在冷漠陌生的宇宙孤独。凝视神秘、迅速变化、无尽的宇宙，为自身渺小而困惑、迷茫甚至恐惧。帕斯卡说：

The plight of man is pitiable. We are wanderers in a vast universe, helpless before the devastations of nature, dependent upon nature for food and other necessities, and uninformed about why we were born and what we should strive for. Man is alone in a cold and alien universe. He gazes upon this mysterious, rapidly changing, and endless universe and is confused, baffled, and even frightened by his own insignificance. As Pascal put it:

毕竟，人在自然中是什么？对于无穷是虚无，对于虚无是一切，处于虚无与一切之间的中心，却与理解二者无限遥远。事物的终点与开端，在不可穿透的秘密中牢牢向他隐藏。他同样不能看到自己从中产生的虚无，以及吞没自己的无穷。

For after all what is man in nature? A nothing in relation to infinity, all in relation to nothing, a central point between nothing and all and infinitely far from understanding either. The ends of things and their beginnings are impregnably concealed from him in an impenetrable secret. He is equally incapable of seeing the nothingness out of which he was drawn and the infinite in which he is engulfed.

蒙田和霍布斯用其他话说相同意思。人的生活孤独、贫困、肮脏、野蛮而短暂，是偶然事件的猎物。

Montaigne and Hobbes said the same thing in other words. The life of man is solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short. He is the prey of contingent happenings.

拥有有限的几个感官和大脑，人开始穿透周围奥秘。利用感官直接揭示、或从实验推知的东西，采用公理，运用推理力量。他追求秩序，目标是建立知识体系而非短暂感觉，形成解释模式，以帮助驾驭环境。其主要成就、自身理性的产物，是数学。它不是完美宝石，继续打磨可能不能除尽瑕疵。但数学是我们与感官知觉世界最有效的联系；承认基础不稳固令人不安，却仍是人心最珍贵的宝石，必须珍惜、善加保存。它一直在理性前列，即使更深入审视发现新缺陷，也无疑继续如此。阿尔弗雷德·诺思·怀特海曾写：“让我们承认，数学研究是人类精神的神圣疯狂。”也许疯狂，却确实神圣。

Endowed with a few limited senses and a brain, man began to pierce the mystery about him. By utilizing what the senses reveal immediately or what can be inferred from experiments, man adopted axioms and applied his reasoning powers. His quest was the quest for order; his goal, to build systems of knowledge as opposed to transient sensations, and to form patterns of explanation that might help him attain some mastery over his environment. His chief accomplishment, the product of man’s own reason, is mathematics. It is not a perfect gem and continued polishing will probably not remove all flaws. Nevertheless, mathematics has been our most effective link with the world of sense perceptions and though it is discomfiting to have to grant that its foundations are not secure, it is still the most precious jewel of the human mind and must be treasured and husbanded. It has been in the van of reason and no doubt will continue to be even if new flaws are discovered by more searching scrutiny. Alfred North Whitehead once wrote, “Let us grant that the pursuit of mathematics is a divine madness of the human spirit.” Madness, perhaps, but surely divine.
